source: Mochichao Design lane — game-lane coding of the 60 owner-confirmed concepts (124 stage entries). FUTURE CONSIDERED, NOT CANON: id is null and baseStats numbers are null by design until the owner's canon lock assigns roster numbers and stat numbers. Apparatus properties (footprint, silhouette, cry, discovery, statProfile, designBrief...) ride under the canon schema's additionalProperties allowance.

species.name: Pupparmor
species.dexText: Pupparmor is born with soft, overlapping plates that flex when it tumbles and stiffen when it is startled. It practises guarding by sitting very still in doorways, usually asleep within moments. A sleeping Pupparmor in a doorway is treated by everyone who lives there as a door that has earned its rest.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Line flag (source §5.5): the final stage's name was coined as Bastihound after an earlier draft name was dropped for echoing an existing source name — Bastihound is the settled name. No other ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.
species.lineConcept: A1 — a round-armoured puppy whose soft plates harden each stage; the final stands upright as a tower-shield hound.
species.sizeClass: Small — about the size of a plump household puppy, low to the ground.
species.temperament: Loyal, earnest, and sleepy; brave in intention long before it is brave in fact.
species.habitat: Region 2 settlements, farmyards, and garden paths — wherever there is a threshold it can appoint itself to.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats soft grains, roots, and whatever it is given for good guarding. Rolls rather than runs when excited; its plates clink faintly as it goes.
species.evolution: Becomes Shieldane as it grows and its soft plates harden into true armour through everyday guarding and play (growth class — no special trigger).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route grassland edges, village outskirts, and garden gates. Rarity: common. Method: grass walk, daytime. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets it close to home, often sitting in the middle of a path refusing to be a hazard.
species.cry: Source character: a round puppy yip with a faint metallic clink from its plates underneath. Pitch contour: short upward chirp, then a drop. Duration: very short. Rhythm: single yip, or two quick yips when excited. Variations — idle: soft sleepy huff-yips; call: repeated bright yips toward its Ranger; hurt: a sharp yelp and plate-clatter; faint: one low whine fading out; affection: muffled contented yips against a leg; evolution moment: yips deepening mid-sequence as the plates ring harder.
species.anatomyNotes: Quadruped puppy; short legs, no manipulators; small jaw with puppy teeth, mouth opens wide for yips but bite reads playful, not dangerous. Locomotion is a waddling trot and a sideways roll. Plates are segmented over the back and shoulders and must flex, not move as one shell.
species.paletteSeed: warm cream belly, soft slate-grey plates, tan ears, dull steel-blue plate rims.
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad print. Four toes plus a main pad per foot, claws usually not showing (soft puppy claws). Gait: alternating steps that wander and double back, with occasional round roll-marks where it has tumbled. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: a faint crescent scuff behind each pad print where a plate edge brushes the ground as it sits down mid-walk.
species.silhouette: Outline class: round quadruped, almost a ball on legs. Proportions: head large against the body, legs very short. Key masses: the domed plated back is the main mass, head second. Reads at sprite size as a round armoured ball with ears. Identifying negative space: the small notches between ear and plate dome, and the low belly arc barely clearing the ground between the short legs.
species.statProfile: sturdy for its size, slow, defence-leaning even this young. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A round puppy wearing its armour as a soft domed blanket of plates — the silhouette must read "puppy first, armour second." Key features: overlapping back plates, floppy ears, cream belly. Must never change: it stays quadruped and unmistakably a puppy; the plates are grown, rounded, and soft-edged, never spiked or bladed; no held items.

species.name: Shieldane
species.dexText: Shieldane's plates have hardened into a proper shield-back, and it has learned to brace. It positions itself between its companions and anything it judges rude, which includes storms, strangers, and large vegetables. Once braced, it is easier to walk around than to argue with.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Line flag (source §5.5): the final stage's name was coined as Bastihound after an earlier draft name was dropped for echoing an existing source name — Bastihound is the settled name. No other ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.
species.lineConcept: A1 — a round-armoured puppy whose soft plates harden each stage; the final stands upright as a tower-shield hound.
species.sizeClass: Medium — about the size of a sturdy herding dog, broad across the shoulders.
species.temperament: Dutiful and calm; stubborn once it has decided where to stand.
species.habitat: Region 2 roads, gate posts, and pasture edges; often found escorting slower creatures across open ground.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes on grains and tough roots, and crunches mineral grit that keeps its plates hard. Patrols a small territory in a slow, regular circuit.
species.evolution: Becomes Bastihound at full maturity, when the foreleg shield completes its growth and the dog takes its upright stance (growth class — the line's single body-plan break happens here, at the final stage).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region roads, pasture land, and checkpoint paths. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass walk, daytime; sometimes found already escorting wild Pupparmor. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one on the road, being politely but firmly inspected.
species.cry: Source character: a young hound's bark, rounded, with plate resonance like a tapped shield. Pitch contour: flat bark with a falling end. Duration: short. Rhythm: one or two measured barks, never a frenzy. Variations — idle: low huffs; call: two clear barks, spaced; hurt: a yelp cut into a growl; faint: a long low whine; affection: soft chuffing barks; evolution moment: barks slowing and deepening as the stance rises.
species.anatomyNotes: Quadruped; forelegs thickening, one foreleg visibly broader where the shield is growing. Jaw stronger, can carry and brace. Locomotion is a deliberate trot and a planted four-foot brace; shield-plant animations belong to the next stage, not this one.
species.paletteSeed: slate-grey hardened plates, cream chest, tan legs, polished steel-blue shield-foreleg.
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad print. Four toes and a main pad, claw marks now showing on the foreprints. Gait: steady alternating steps in straight patrol lines, with paired deep foreprints where it has braced. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: the brace mark — two foreprints pressed noticeably deeper, side by side, facing whatever it was guarding against.
species.silhouette: Outline class: solid quadruped, shield-backed. Proportions: head medium against a heavy body, legs medium-short and thick. Key masses: the plate dome over the shoulders, the broad chest. Reads at sprite size as a dog carrying a shield on its back. Identifying negative space: the wedge gap under the chest between forelegs, and the notch where the tail clears the back plate.
species.statProfile: slow, bulky, defence-first; attack modest. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: The same dog, grown: a quadruped hound whose back plates have fused toward a shield shape and whose one foreleg is becoming the shield it will plant as Bastihound. Must never change: still quadruped, still plainly the Pupparmor dog; the shield is grown from the foreleg, never strapped on or held; no weapons.

species.name: Bastihound
species.dexText: Bastihound stands upright and plants its shield-foreleg in the earth, and for as long as it stands there, nothing passes. Travellers shelter behind it in storms without asking, the way one shelters behind a wall. It does not consider this an imposition; it considers it the job finally being the right size.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Line flag (source §5.5): Bastihound was renamed in drafting from "Aegishound," which was dropped for echoing Aegislash — Bastihound is the settled, source-given name and is spelled as the source has it. No other ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5. ---
species.lineConcept: A1 — a round-armoured puppy whose soft plates harden each stage; the final stands upright as a tower-shield hound, one foreleg grown into a full shield it plants like a gate.
species.sizeClass: Large — stands about as tall as an adult person when upright, and wider with the shield planted.
species.temperament: Steadfast, gentle, and immovable; a guardian's patience rather than a fighter's temper.
species.habitat: Region 2 passes, gates, bridges, and exposed high roads — chokepoints it can make safe by standing in them.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats grains, roots, and mineral grit; spends long hours standing watch, dozing upright behind its shield. In a fight it advances slowly, shield first, and ends arguments by being in the way.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Shieldane at full maturity (growth class); the break is posture, not species — upright stance and the completed shield-foreleg are the line's single permitted body-plan break, per the Region 2 law.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region passes, gate roads, and exposed bridges. Rarity: rare in the wild; more often met as a long-raised partner's final form. Method: grass / road walk, daytime; occasionally found already standing watch over a wild crossing. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one at a place that feels safer the moment they see it.
species.cry: Source character: a deep hound bay with a low shield-boom resonance under it. Pitch contour: rises, holds, falls slowly. Duration: long for a cry. Rhythm: single bay, or a slow pair. Variations — idle: deep breathing huffs behind the shield; call: a bay that carries across a pass; hurt: a booming bark of outrage; faint: a low groan as the shield settles; affection: a soft, rumbling chuff; evolution moment: Shieldane's bark dropping into the bay as the shield plants for the first time.
species.anatomyNotes: Bipedal stance on hind legs; one foreleg is a full tower shield grown from the limb — it is planted, swung as a wall, and never detached or handed off. The other foreleg stays a normal paw-arm. Jaw is a hound's, used for barks and carrying, not a weapon read. Locomotion: slow upright stride, or dropping to all fours to run.
species.paletteSeed: deep slate plates, polished steel-blue shield face, cream chest and muzzle, tan tail and free paw.
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad print, two gaits. Upright: two large hind pad prints, alternating, with a repeated round shield-rim dent beside them where the shield is planted at each rest. On all fours: four prints as Shieldane's, larger. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the shield dent — a clean crescent pit next to the track line that no other Region 2 dog leaves.
species.silhouette: Outline class: upright tower — a wall with a dog's head. Proportions: body tall and narrow behind the shield, head small against the shield mass. Key masses: the tower shield is the dominant mass, shoulders second. Reads at sprite size as a shield with ears. Identifying negative space: the slim gap between shield edge and free foreleg, and the arch between its planted hind feet under the body's hem of plates.
species.statProfile: a wall — very high defence read, slow, steady physical presence, low speed. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: An upright hound behind a grown tower shield: the final form is a gate that is also a dog. Key features: shield-foreleg planted like a gate, plated shoulders, kind hound head above the shield rim. Must never change: still unmistakably the same dog as Pupparmor (source evolution note); the shield is grown from the foreleg and can never be removed, held in a hand, or sold; the read is guardian, never knight-with-equipment or menace.

species.name: Flickfin
species.dexText: Flickfin is a minnow with a needle for a nose, and it has not yet learned what the needle is for. It jabs at bubbles, falling leaves, and its own reflection, then darts away delighted. Whole schools practise on the same reed until the reed gives up and falls over.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: A2 — a minnow with a needle nose; the needle becomes a pike, then the whole fish becomes a halberd-headed drake that duels by fencing.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a minnow that fits the idea of a hand, all flicker and dart.
species.temperament: Daring, excitable, and easily distracted; brave at the size where bravery is cheap.
species.habitat: Region 2 shallow rivers, reed beds, and clear pond margins.
species.dietBehaviour: Snaps up water insects and tiny larvae, stabbing first and checking afterwards. Moves in flickering schools that turn as one fish.
species.evolution: Becomes Pikeperil as it grows and the needle nose lengthens into a true pike (growth class).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route rivers and ponds. Rarity: common. Method: water (shallows / fishing-class encounter), daytime. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets it in the first river they wade, needling their boot.
species.cry: Source character: underwater, a tiny ticking click made with the needle against the water; above water, a small wet pip. Pitch contour: flat and very high. Duration: extremely short. Rhythm: single clicks, or a rapid rattle when schooling. Variations — idle: occasional single clicks; call: a quick click-chorus with the school; hurt: one sharp tick and silence; faint: clicks slowing to a stop; affection: soft rapid ticking near a hand; evolution moment: clicks spacing out as the pike lengthens the sound.
species.anatomyNotes: True fish body; no limbs, no manipulators. The needle nose is the line's one idea and must be in every action — jabs, probes, and fencing beats all come from the snout. Mouth is tiny and behind the needle's base. Locomotion is darting swimming only; out of water it flops.
species.paletteSeed: silver-blue back, pale belly, bright steel needle, dark bead eye stripe.
species.footprint: Leaves no footprints. Trace spec: in shallow margins, fine needle-prick pits in soft mud where it has jabbed at things, in loose clusters; in water, a brief V-wake far too pointed for its size. Distinctive marker: the prick-pit clusters.
species.silhouette: Outline class: slim teardrop fish. Proportions: needle about as long again as the head, tail fin small. Key masses: the body is one small mass, the needle a single leading line. Reads at sprite size as a fish with a pin. Identifying negative space: the thin triangle between needle and lower jaw line, and the notch between tail-fin lobes.
species.statProfile: very fast, very frail; a needle, not yet a weapon. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A minnow whose whole design is one needle nose on a small silver fish. Must never change: the weapon grows from the snout and is part of the face at every stage (the line's one idea, per the source); no fins shaped as hands, no held items; the read stays quick and bright, not predatory-menacing.

species.name: Pikeperil
species.dexText: Pikeperil's needle has become a pike, and the fish has become serious about it. It holds formal duels with its own kind at dawn, pike to pike, in slow water where the light comes sideways. Losers retire to the reeds to practise; winners retire to the reeds to practise more.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: A2 — a minnow with a needle nose; the needle becomes a pike, then the whole fish becomes a halberd-headed drake that duels by fencing.
species.sizeClass: Medium — about the length of a person's arm, lean and fast.
species.temperament: Proud, disciplined, and touchy about honour; a duellist's manners in a fish.
species.habitat: Region 2 slow rivers, lake edges, and flooded meadows with open water for duelling.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts smaller fish and large water insects with a single pike-thrust. Spends its still hours holding a fencing guard, nose up-current.
species.evolution: Becomes Halberdrake at full maturity, when the pike broadens into a halberd head and the body takes its drake form (growth class into the line's single final-stage break).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region rivers and lakes. Rarity: uncommon. Method: water, dawn and daytime. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by disturbing a dawn duel — both fish will turn and consider the interruption together.
species.cry: Source character: a clean metallic *ting* as the pike cuts water, with a low fish croak beneath. Pitch contour: a struck rising note, then flat. Duration: short. Rhythm: single challenges; a measured pair before a duel. Variations — idle: rare single tings; call: two tings, spaced like an invitation; hurt: a harsh croak and thrash; faint: ting, croak, silence; affection: a surprisingly gentle single ting; evolution moment: the ting broadening into a ringing note as the pike becomes a halberd.
species.anatomyNotes: Fish body, longer and more muscular; no limbs. All attacks are snout-line actions — thrust, parry, riposte — animated on the whole body's lunge. Jaw can snap but the pike is the weapon. Locomotion: powerful cruising and sudden straight-line lunges.
species.paletteSeed: steel-blue back, silver flanks, chrome pike, pale gold eye.
species.footprint: Leaves no footprints. Trace spec: long single score-lines in mud at the water's edge where a duellist has beached its pike testing the bank, and paired parallel wakes on still water at dawn. Distinctive marker: the bank score-lines, always in duelling pairs.
species.silhouette: Outline class: long horizontal lance-fish. Proportions: pike a major fraction of total length, body slim, tail broad. Key masses: one long body mass with the pike as its extension. Reads at sprite size as an arrow. Identifying negative space: the narrow triangle between pike and belly line, and the deep tail notch.
species.statProfile: fast, precise, physical-leaning; still frail for its length. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A pike-fish that reads as a fencer mid-guard: lean body, formal posture, the snout grown into a true pike. Must never change: weapon stays grown from the snout; silhouette stays a fish — the drake break is reserved for the final stage only; no armour plating beyond the Chrome sheen of the pike itself.

species.name: Halberdrake
species.dexText: Halberdrake has traded the fish's shape for a drake's, and its snout for a halberd it was born wearing. It duels by fencing — measure, salute, exchange — and treats every fight as a formal occasion. Rivers where a Halberdrake holds court are noticeably politer places.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: A2 — a minnow with a needle nose; the needle becomes a pike, then the whole fish becomes a halberd-headed drake that duels by fencing.
species.sizeClass: Large — a drake about the length of a small boat, most of it presence.
species.temperament: Courtly, exacting, and fair; will salute an opponent before, and after, defeating them.
species.habitat: Region 2 wide rivers, estuaries, and deep lake channels; a drake holds one stretch of water as its hall.
species.dietBehaviour: Takes large fish in single clean lunges. Rests coiled in deep water with the halberd head breaking the surface like a standard planted in the current.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Pikeperil at full maturity (growth class); per the source, the final stage trades the fish silhouette for a drake's — this is the line's one permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region wide rivers and estuary channels. Rarity: rare in the wild; usually a raised partner's final form. Method: water (deep channel), dawn preferred. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by being saluted — the halberd dipping once above the surface before anything else happens.
species.cry: Source character: a ringing halberd-note, bell-clean, over a deep drake rumble. Pitch contour: struck high note falling into the rumble. Duration: medium. Rhythm: single formal notes; never chatter. Variations — idle: a rare low rumble; call: one ringing note across the water; hurt: a cracked bell-note and roar; faint: the ring fading into the rumble, then stillness; affection: a softened ring, almost a chime; evolution moment: Pikeperil's ting opening out into the full ringing salute.
species.anatomyNotes: Drake body — long neck and coiling body, limbs are drake limbs (clawed, weight-bearing), not arms holding anything. The halberd is the head/snout itself: blade and spike grown from the skull; fencing actions are whole-neck actions. Jaw sits under the halberd head and can open for bites and cries. Locomotion: swimming with serpentine coils, and hauling out to rear on the bank.
species.paletteSeed: deep steel-blue scales, chrome halberd head, silver belly plates, gold accents at the frill.
species.footprint: Leaves prints where it hauls out: four clawed drake footprints, alternating, with a central sinuous tail-drag groove and occasional halberd-tip pricks where it has tested the ground. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the tail-drag groove ending in a single neat halberd prick — its salute, left in mud.
species.silhouette: Outline class: coiled drake with a bladed head-profile. Proportions: neck long, head small against the halberd blade it carries as a snout, body heavy behind. Key masses: the coiled body and the halberd head. Reads at sprite size as a serpent with an axe for a face. Identifying negative space: the crescent gap inside its resting coil, and the notch between halberd blade and spike.
species.statProfile: strong, precise, physical-leaning, with real bulk at last; speed now in bursts. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A drake that fences with its own halberd head — formal, courtly, gleaming. Key features: halberd grown as the snout/head, long neck, coiled drake body. Must never change: the weapon is the head, grown, never held in a claw; the fish-to-drake trade happens only at this final stage; the read is duellist, not monster — no menace-spikes or horror detailing.

species.name: Seedquire
species.dexText: Seedquire is a seedling that has appointed itself squire to the first tall plant it met. It carries a twig everywhere, in earnest, the way other seedlings carry nothing at all. When the wind bows the grass, Seedquire bows back, assuming it has been greeted by knights.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source reconciliation (source wins, noted per instructions): the seed says Seedquire "carrying a twig" — reconciled to a grown shoot under the binding grown-gear rule, not a held/carried object. Design-distance note (source §Bucket A, A3): this line is deliberately *not* a turtle — Region 1's Flora chair (Sproutle's line) is a tortoise; this is the region-2 answer, a person. No ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A3 — a seedling squire carrying a twig; a bud-page with a leaf shield; a tall lance-bearing knight whose armour is bark and whose lance is a grown sunflower stalk.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a seedling that comes up to a person's ankle, twig and all.
species.temperament: Earnest, polite, and very serious about duties it invented itself.
species.habitat: Region 2 garden edges, hedgerows, and the feet of old trees it admires.
species.dietBehaviour: Drinks rainwater and feeds on sunlight and rich soil like any seedling. Practises twig-drills at dawn; guards anthills and fallen fruit with great ceremony.
species.evolution: Becomes Budguard as it grows, its bud opening into a page's leaf shield (growth class). Source reconciliation: the seed text says Seedquire "carries" a twig — under the Region 2 grown-gear law and this lane's rules, the twig is read as a grown shoot from its own stem, not a held object; see Flags.
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route gardens, hedgerows, and meadow margins. Rarity: common. Method: grass walk, morning and daytime. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets one at ankle height, being formally challenged to step around a puddle.
species.cry: Source character: a small leaf-rustle with a pip in it, like a seed husk popping. Pitch contour: quick rise, quick fall. Duration: very short. Rhythm: pip-pip when busy, single pips at rest. Variations — idle: soft rustle-pips; call: an eager pip-pip-pip toward its chosen tall plant or Ranger; hurt: one sharp husk-pop; faint: rustling settling flat; affection: gentle repeated pips while leaning on a boot; evolution moment: pips deepening into a bud-creak as the leaf shield unfolds.
species.anatomyNotes: Small bipedal seedling: a stem body, root-feet, two leaf-arms. One leaf-arm ends in the grown twig-shoot. Mouth is a small line under the seed cap; no jaw strength. Locomotion: toddling steps and hopeful hops; it overbalances backward when saluting.
species.paletteSeed: fresh seed green, pale cream seed cap, soft brown twig-shoot, bright leaf green.
species.footprint: Print shape class: root-toe print — two or three tiny splayed root toes, no claws. Gait: alternating toddling steps, close together, often veering toward tall plants. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: a tiny twig-drag tick beside every few prints, where the grown shoot brushes the soil as it walks.
species.silhouette: Outline class: sprout on a stem — a round seed head over a narrow body. Proportions: head (seed cap and first leaves) large against a short stem body, legs stubby. Key masses: the seed head and the twig-shoot line. Reads at sprite size as a sprout holding a stick upright. Identifying negative space: the V gap between its two first leaves, and the small triangle between twig-shoot and body.
species.statProfile: frail, slow, eager; heart far ahead of stats. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A seedling squire: round seed head, first leaves like a cap, one grown twig-shoot carried as a squire's blade. Must never change: plant body, never an animal in costume; the twig is grown from its own shoot (see Flags); the read is earnest pageantry at ankle height — cute first, chivalric second.

species.name: Budguard
species.dexText: Budguard's bud has opened into a broad leaf that it wears as a shield, and its twig has become a proper page's spear of green wood. It now guards things on behalf of others — paths, nests, younger Seedquire — and keeps a strict rota nobody assigned it. It is happiest standing between something small and something large.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Design-distance note (source §Bucket A, A3): deliberately *not* a turtle — Region 1's Flora chair (Sproutle's line) is a tortoise; this line is the region-2 answer, a person. Grown-gear reconciliation from stage 1 applies line-wide: the "leaf shield" and spear are grown anatomy. No ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A3 — a seedling squire carrying a twig; a bud-page with a leaf shield; a tall lance-bearing knight whose armour is bark and whose lance is a grown sunflower stalk.
species.sizeClass: Small — about knee-high on a person, bud held high.
species.temperament: Dutiful, courteous, and quietly proud; takes praise by standing straighter.
species.habitat: Region 2 garden terraces, orchard rows, and path junctions where guarding is useful.
species.dietBehaviour: Sunlight, water, and soil feeding as a growing plant; it rotates slowly through the day to keep its leaf shield to the light. Drills with other Budguard in pairs, leaf to leaf.
species.evolution: Becomes Verdilance at full growth, when the bud crowns open, bark armour plates the stem, and the sunflower lance comes into bloom (growth class into the line's single final-stage break).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region gardens, orchards, and kept paths. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass walk, daytime. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one on a kept path, standing aside with great formality to let them pass.
species.cry: Source character: leaf-rustle and a young woody creak, with a clearer pip at the centre. Pitch contour: rises and levels. Duration: short. Rhythm: measured single cries; a rustle-roll when drilling. Variations — idle: soft creak-rustles as it turns to the light; call: a bright pip-and-rustle salute; hurt: a sharp leaf-snap sound; faint: rustling folding down; affection: low contented creaks; evolution moment: a long rising creak as bark plates and the lance crown form.
species.anatomyNotes: Bipedal plant; stem legs longer, leaf-arms distinct — one arm's leaf is the shield (broad, veined, can be braced across the body), the other carries the grown spear-shoot. Head is a closed bud that nods and tilts but does not open until the final stage. Locomotion: a marching toddle; roots grip when bracing.
species.paletteSeed: leaf green shield, bud pink-green crown, cream stem, warm brown spear-shoot.
species.footprint: Print shape class: root-toe print, three splayed toes. Gait: regular alternating marching steps in noticeably straight lines, with paired planted prints where it has stood guard. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the guard stand — two deep side-by-side prints with a leaf-tip drag arc in front, where the shield leaf brushed down.
species.silhouette: Outline class: upright sprout with a shield disc. Proportions: bud head medium, body taller and slimmer than Seedquire, shield leaf a major side mass. Key masses: shield leaf and bud crown. Reads at sprite size as a plant holding a round leaf shield. Identifying negative space: the crescent between shield leaf and body, and the fork gap at the root-feet when marching.
species.statProfile: balanced, defence-leaning, still light; a page's promise. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A bud-page plant knight in training: leaf shield grown from one arm, spear-shoot grown from the other, closed bud for a head. Must never change: all equipment is grown plant matter; the bud stays closed until Verdilance; silhouette stays a plant person in the making, not a tortoise and not an animal (see line flag).

species.name: Verdilance
species.dexText: Verdilance is a knight grown, not made: armour of bark, a shield of layered leaf, and a lance that is a living sunflower stalk, blooming at its head. It keeps the old duties — paths, nests, the small and the slow — at a size where the duties finally fit. On bright mornings it tilts its flower toward the sun and calls that prayer, drill, and breakfast at once.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Design-distance note (source §Bucket A, A3): deliberately *not* a turtle — R1's Flora chair (Sproutle's line) is a tortoise; this is the region-2 answer, a person. Grown-gear reconciliation from stage 1 applies line-wide. No ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5. ---
species.lineConcept: A3 — a seedling squire carrying a twig; a bud-page with a leaf shield; a tall lance-bearing knight whose armour is bark and whose lance is a grown sunflower stalk.
species.sizeClass: Large — a tall plant knight, head and sunflower crown above a person's head height.
species.temperament: Gallant, patient, and ceremonious; gentle with everything smaller than itself.
species.habitat: Region 2 old gardens, sunlit clearings, and the approaches to kept places — anywhere a guard post becomes a landmark.
species.dietBehaviour: Feeds as a great plant: sunlight through the lance-flower and leaves, deep root-watering at rest. Stands long watches; in a fight it works like a fencer-planter, lance couched, shield leaf taking weather and blows alike.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Budguard at full growth (growth class); the tall humanoid knight is the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law — the sprout becomes a person-shaped plant.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region old gardens and sunlit clearings near kept settlements. Rarity: rare in the wild; usually a long-raised partner's final form. Method: grass walk, sunny daytime (it follows the light). Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one as a landmark — a flower over a wall that turns out to have been watching them kindly for some time.
species.cry: Source character: deep leaf-rustle, bark creak, and a low clear pip-note like a struck green stem. Pitch contour: slow rise, long level hold. Duration: medium-long. Rhythm: single formal cries; a rustle-roll for drill. Variations — idle: slow creaks as it turns with the sun; call: one clear stem-note across a garden; hurt: a bark-crack cry; faint: a great slow rustle as it folds to rest; affection: low creaking, flower bowed toward the Ranger; evolution moment: Budguard's creak rising into the stem-note as the sunflower opens.
species.anatomyNotes: Humanoid plant: long stem legs, bark-plated torso, leaf-arm shield on one side, the other arm grown into — and continuous with — the sunflower lance stalk; the lance is never gripped as a separate object, it flowers from the arm's line. Head is the opened crown with a face under the petals. Locomotion: slow stately strides; roots can anchor for a couched-lance brace.
species.paletteSeed: bark brown armour, deep leaf green, sunflower gold, cream petal accents.
species.footprint: Print shape class: root-toe print, broad three-toed root foot. Gait: long alternating strides, very straight, with anchor-splays where it has rooted to brace. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: fallen sunflower petals near the track on bright days, and the anchor-splay — toes dug and spread wider than the walking prints.
species.silhouette: Outline class: tall humanoid lance-knight. Proportions: legs long, torso bark-narrow, head small under a wide flower crown, lance a single tall vertical exceeding its height. Key masses: flower crown, shield leaf, lance line. Reads at sprite size as a flower-headed knight. Identifying negative space: the ring gap between flower crown and head, and the long triangle between lance stalk and body.
species.statProfile: balanced and durable, defence- and reach-leaning; a knight's even spread with no glass anywhere. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A tall plant knight whose armour is bark, whose shield is leaf, and whose lance is a blooming sunflower grown from its own arm. Must never change: every piece of gear is grown plant anatomy — nothing held, strapped, or metal; the humanoid break happens only at this final stage; explicitly not a tortoise in any read (Region 1's Flora chair is Sproutle's tortoise line — this is a person).

species.name: Ashimp
species.dexText: Ashimp is a sooty little imp that keeps one coal, always the same coal, and will not be parted from it. It warms its hands on it, sleeps curled around it, and offers to show it to strangers within seconds of meeting them. If the coal ever goes out, Ashimp sits down wherever it is and waits, quite certain the world has ended.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source reconciliation (source wins, noted per instructions): the seed says Ashimp "carries one coal." That wording is kept for behaviour, but the coal is not gear in the grown-gear sense — it is a kept treasure object in its hands at this stage only; from Embrute on, the fire is inside the body, per the source's own hand → belly → chest progression. Source drift note carried: the ladder is kept show-warm (mischief, never menace-theology). No ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A4 — a sooty imp that carries one coal; a brute with a furnace belly; a horned, grinning battler whose chest is an open furnace door.
species.sizeClass: Small — a sooty imp about the size of a garden cat, coal and all.
species.temperament: Mischievous, clingy, and theatrical; show-warm trouble, never real menace.
species.habitat: Region 2 hearthsides, kiln yards, campfire rings, and warm chimneysides in cool country.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats charcoal scraps, toasted grains, and anything slightly burnt. Hoards warmth: sun-warmed stones, other creatures' laps, the top of the stove. Source reconciliation: the seed says it "carries one coal" — read as cupped in its hands as its treasure, not as growing gear; see Flags.
species.evolution: Becomes Embrute as it grows and the coal is taken into the body — the fire moves from hand to belly (growth class; per the source, each stage's fire moves hand → belly → chest).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-to-mid hearth settlements, kiln yards, and campfire sites. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass / settlement walk, evening and night favoured (it gathers where fires are lit). Level band: early-route to mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one at a campfire, asking — in cries — to show them the coal.
species.cry: Source character: a cheeky chirping chitter with coal-hiss pops in it. Pitch contour: bouncing up-down, never level. Duration: short. Rhythm: chitter-bursts of three to five. Variations — idle: soft hiss-pops and muttering chitters to the coal; call: a loud chitter-burst to get attention for the coal; hurt: a startled squeak and hiss; faint: chitters slowing into a damp fizz; affection: warm purring hisses against a hand; evolution moment: chittering deepening as the hiss moves into its belly.
species.anatomyNotes: Small bipedal imp: oversized head, little horns just budding, thin arms with dexterous hands (it cups and juggles the coal), clawed feet, a thin tail. Mouth is a wide grin with small fangs — expression first, bite last. Locomotion: scampering, climbing, and sitting abruptly.
species.paletteSeed: soot black-grey, ember orange coal-glow, ash-white belly smudge, dull red horn tips.
species.footprint: Print shape class: clawed toe print — three front toes with claw ticks, small heel. Gait: bounding pairs and scampers that double back; prints cluster in circles around hearths. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: faint soot smudging inside the prints and the occasional round coal-rest scorch, a small dark circle where it set the coal down.
species.silhouette: Outline class: compact imp, head-heavy. Proportions: head large, body small, arms long for its size, tail a thin trailing line. Key masses: head and the glowing coal spot at its hands. Reads at sprite size as a soot blob holding a light. Identifying negative space: the arcs between its budding horns, and the gap between tail curve and legs.
species.statProfile: quick, frail, special-leaning even now; more spark than staying power. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A sooty imp whose whole world is one treasured coal. Key features: ash-smudged body, budding horns, grin, the coal's glow as the palette's hot point. Must never change: mischief, never menace-theology (source drift note) — the imp ladder stays show-warm at every stage; the fire's position is the line's story (hand here, belly next, chest last); no held weapons — the coal is a treasure, not a tool.

species.name: Embrute
species.dexText: Embrute swallowed the coal — on purpose, it insists — and now carries its fire in a furnace belly that glows through a grate of ribs. It is warmer, slower, and much prouder. Other Ashimp gather around it on cold nights, and Embrute pretends to mind, and moves closer so more of them fit.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source drift note carried (source §Bucket A, A4): Digimon's imp→devil escalation ladder, kept show-warm — mischief, never menace-theology. No ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A4 — a sooty imp that carries one coal; a brute with a furnace belly; a horned, grinning battler whose chest is an open furnace door.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a squat brute about as tall as a person's waist and nearly as wide.
species.temperament: Blustery and soft-hearted; a bully's silhouette with a stove's personality.
species.habitat: Region 2 kiln yards, forge outskirts, and warm caves near settlements.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats charcoal, coal lumps, and burnt offerings from friendly kitchens; the belly fire brightens as it digests. Sleeps sitting, glowing gently, and is used — with its permission — as a night landmark.
species.evolution: Becomes Diablaze at full maturity, when the furnace rises from belly to chest and opens as a door (growth class into the line's single final-stage break; fire's journey hand → belly → chest completes).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region kiln and forge country, warm caves. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass / cave walk, night favoured (its glow gives it away). Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by following a warm glow that turns out to be snoring.
species.cry: Source character: a bellows-breath growl with furnace pops and a low coal rumble. Pitch contour: low, rolling, rises when showing off. Duration: medium. Rhythm: growl-puff, growl-puff, like a small engine. Variations — idle: rhythmic snore-pops; call: a bellowing huff that flares the belly; hurt: a clanging growl; faint: pops slowing to embers; affection: a deep warm rumble, belly dimmed politely; evolution moment: the rumble climbing from belly to chest as the door forms.
species.anatomyNotes: Squat biped: huge belly is the furnace — a rib-grate front that glows, flexes with breathing, and vents heat shimmer. Arms thick, hands still dexterous. Horns grown longer; grin wider. Locomotion: heavy waddle and a planted sitting rest; it does not jump.
species.paletteSeed: soot black, furnace orange belly-glow, ash grey arms, red horn bands.
species.footprint: Print shape class: clawed toe print, three toes and a broad heel, deep. Gait: alternating heavy steps, short stride, with wide sitting-crush marks where it has rested and warmed the ground. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: scorched, dried earth inside resting marks — ground it sat on is baked noticeably harder than the soil around it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: belly-first brute, a stove with horns. Proportions: belly the dominant mass, head small on top of it, legs short. Key masses: furnace belly, horned head. Reads at sprite size as a glowing pot-bellied imp. Identifying negative space: the gaps between horn and head on each side, and the low arch between its short legs under the belly's glow-line.
species.statProfile: bulky, slow, special-leaning from the furnace; a stove that can shove. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A brute whose belly is a lit furnace, ribs as its grate. Must never change: the fire lives in the belly at this stage (not hands, not chest — that ordering is the line's spine); the glow is body light, never a held lantern; menace stays theatrical and warm, never theological or frightening.

species.name: Diablaze
species.dexText: Diablaze's furnace has risen to its chest and opened as a door, and the grin has risen with it. It is a battler now — theatrical, honourable in its own sooty way, and incapable of entering a fight quietly. Whole crowds have been warmed at a Diablaze standing in a winter square, door open, accepting applause as its due.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source drift note carried (source §Bucket A, A4): Digimon's imp→devil escalation ladder, kept show-warm — mischief, never menace-theology. No ⚠ sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5. ---
species.lineConcept: A4 — a sooty imp that carries one coal; a brute with a furnace belly; a horned, grinning battler whose chest is an open furnace door.
species.sizeClass: Large — a horned battler standing taller than a person, chest-door and all.
species.temperament: Showy, grinning, and big-hearted; a performer-battler who loves an audience and protects it.
species.habitat: Region 2 festival squares, forge districts, and volcanic foothills it visits like a tourist of its own element.
species.dietBehaviour: Feeds the chest furnace with coal and charcoal, taken through the door with great ceremony. Fights in open displays — chest flaring at the dramatic moments it chooses — and banks its fire low and kind at night for whoever is cold.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Embrute at full maturity (growth class); the horned upright battler with the open furnace chest is the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region festival squares and forge districts. Rarity: rare in the wild; usually a raised partner's final form. Method: settlement walk, evening and festival times favoured. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one holding court in a square, warming a crowd — and being applauded, correctly.
species.cry: Source character: a big ringing laugh-shape of a roar — bellows, furnace roar, and coal-pops in chorus. Pitch contour: starts low, flares up, settles into rumble. Duration: long. Rhythm: roar-puffs in showy bursts. Variations — idle: contented furnace rumbles; call: a door-flaring roar that carries across a square; hurt: a clanging roar of outrage; faint: the roar banking down to ember-pops; affection: a low warm rumble, door dimmed; evolution moment: Embrute's belly-rumble climbing and bursting open as the chest door.
species.anatomyNotes: Tall bipedal battler: horns full-grown and curved, arms long and strong, clawed hands. The chest is an open furnace door — a rib-framed opening with a door of bone and hide grown on a hinge of its own body; it opens, closes, and flares, and is anatomy, never equipment. Mouth is the wide grin, front and centre. Locomotion: striding, stamping display steps, planted roaring poses.
species.paletteSeed: soot black body, bright furnace orange chest, ember red horns, ash-white grin and claws.
species.footprint: Print shape class: clawed toe print, three toes, deep heel. Gait: long alternating strides with stamp-clusters where it has performed. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: a faint scorched halo in the soil of its standing prints on cold ground — the chest furnace dries and darkens the earth it stands over.
species.silhouette: Outline class: horned upright battler with a lit chest window. Proportions: chest broad and dominant, head medium with wide horn span, legs strong. Key masses: furnace chest and horn span. Reads at sprite size as a grinning horned figure with fire in its chest. Identifying negative space: the wide arc between the horns, and the triangle gaps between arm and torso when it poses.
species.statProfile: strong and bulky, special-leaning from the chest furnace; a showpiece bruiser, not fast. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A horned, grinning battler whose open chest is a furnace door — the imp, the brute, and the battler are one creature at three sizes of theatre. Must never change: the furnace sits in the chest and nowhere else at this stage; the door is grown anatomy; the grin and show-warmth are mandatory — this is a beloved crowd-warmer, never a demon in the menacing or theological sense (source drift note).

species.name: Polypup
species.dexText: Polypup is a coral polyp with a pup's enthusiasm, anchored to one stone it has chosen as the whole world. It waves its soft tentacles at passing fish and retracts into a pebble-tight ball at shadows. The stone it chooses first is rarely the stone it keeps; it migrates often, and calls each move an adventure.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: A5 — a coral polyp pup that budges into a reef-backed defender; the final is a walking atoll — a whole reef ecosystem on one creature.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a polyp pup that could sit in a cupped hand, if it approved of the hand.
species.temperament: Shy, curious, and home-proud; brave exactly one tentacle at a time.
species.habitat: Region 2 warm shallow reefs, rockpools, and sunlit harbour stones.
species.dietBehaviour: Filters plankton and sips mineral-rich water; its first hard coral buds grow from what it drinks. Bobs in the current when content; balls up when not.
species.evolution: Becomes Reefender as it grows and its coral buds harden into a true reef-back (growth class — it doesn't outgrow the reef, the reef begins outgrowing it).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route rockpools and shallow reef flats. Rarity: common. Method: water (rockpool / shallows), daytime, low-tide class conditions. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets one in a rockpool, being waved at by something the size of a thumb.
species.cry: Source character: tiny watery pops and a soft bubble-trill through its tentacles. Pitch contour: small rising bubbles of sound. Duration: very short. Rhythm: pop-pop-trill when curious; silence when balled. Variations — idle: occasional single pops; call: a quick bubble-trill toward food or a friend; hurt: one wet squeak, then balled silence; faint: pops trailing off; affection: gentle trilling against a fingertip; evolution moment: trills layering as new coral buds crack open with tiny clicks.
species.anatomyNotes: A polyp body: soft column, a crown of short tentacles around the mouth, no limbs, no jaw — the mouth is a small centre opening the tentacles serve. One nub foot anchors it to stone. Locomotion: inching on the foot, or balled rolling in a current; it cannot walk.
species.paletteSeed: soft coral pink, cream tentacle tips, pale stone grey foot, bright aqua eye-spots.
species.footprint: Leaves no footprints. Trace spec: a single small clean ring-mark on stone where its foot has anchored, and faint mineral crust at favourite stones. In sand, a tiny dragged comma where it has inched. Distinctive marker: the anchor ring — a pale perfect circle on harbour rock, thumb-sized.
species.silhouette: Outline class: small bulb on a stone — a button with a crown. Proportions: tentacle crown wide against a short body, foot narrow. Key masses: the round polyp body and its crown. Reads at sprite size as a pink pebble that waves. Identifying negative space: the gaps between tentacles in the crown, and the notch between body and chosen stone.
species.statProfile: frail and slow, defence in bud only; more reef-to-be than creature. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A coral polyp pup: one soft round body, a waving tentacle crown, its first hard buds showing like baby teeth of coral. Must never change: it is an anchored polyp, not a free-swimming animal — no fins, legs, or face beyond the mouth-crown and eye-spots; the reef grows *on* it from the very first hard bud.

species.name: Reefender
species.dexText: Reefender's back has become a reef in earnest — coral branches, shell ledges, and hollows where small fish have begun, uninvited and unwarned-against, to live. It moves slowly and announces turns early, for the tenants' sake. Anemones on its shoulders sting first and apologise never, and Reefender has stopped apologising for them.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: A5 — a coral polyp pup that budges into a reef-backed defender; the final is a walking atoll — a whole reef ecosystem on one creature.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a broad reef-backed creature about the size of a laden cart, most of it reef.
species.temperament: Patient, proprietorial, and quietly proud of its tenants.
species.habitat: Region 2 reef shelves and warm bays; it patrols a slow circuit of its feeding ground.
species.dietBehaviour: Filters plankton in quantity and grazes algae from its own lower branches, carefully, like a landlord eating the garden. In a fight it turns its reef to the threat and shelters everything small behind itself.
species.evolution: Becomes Atollossus at full growth, when the reef completes into a walking atoll with grown tube-sponge water cannons (growth class into the line's single final-stage break — habitat becomes body).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region reef shelves and warm bays. Rarity: uncommon. Method: water (reef), daytime. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by noticing a reef has politely moved out of their boat's way.
species.cry: Source character: a low watery groan through coral, with clicks and pops from the reef itself — tenant shrimp joining in. Pitch contour: low and rolling. Duration: medium. Rhythm: slow groan-and-click phrases. Variations — idle: ambient reef pops with soft groans; call: a groan the whole reef answers with clicks; hurt: a cracking coral groan; faint: groans subsiding into reef noise only; affection: a warm low groan, tentacles waving; evolution moment: groans deepening under a chorus of cracking, growing coral as the atoll forms.
species.anatomyNotes: Low quadruped-ish base body almost hidden under reef growth; stub limbs move the whole mass slowly. Mouth is low at the front, under an overhang. The reef-back is the animation problem: branches sway, tenants dart, and the whole back must read as one ecosystem, not decoration. No cannons yet — tube-sponges are still closed buds at this stage.
species.paletteSeed: coral pink and orange branches, cream sandstone base, aqua tenant fish accents, algae green shadows.
species.footprint: Print spec (on sand and mud at low tide): a broad dragged furrow rather than steps — the low body and stub limbs plough a wide channel with irregular limb-scrapes at its edges, and coral-grain shed in the trail. Print size class: medium-broad. Distinctive marker: living shed — tiny coral fragments and the occasional startled tenant left in the furrow, which rescues itself.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a reef mound that moves — jagged top, low base. Proportions: back reef is most of the height and mass, head low and small at the front. Key masses: the reef-back. Reads at sprite size as a walking piece of reef. Identifying negative space: the gaps and arches inside the coral branches, and the low slot between head-overhang and ground.
species.statProfile: slow, very bulky, defence-first; a shelter with opinions. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A defender whose back is a working reef with tenants, ledges, and anemone shoulders. Must never change: the reef is grown body, not cargo — nothing on the back can be taken off; tenants are part of the read at this stage; movement is slow landlord energy, never agility.

species.name: Atollossus
species.dexText: Atollossus is a reef that walks: a whole atoll ecosystem carried on one vast creature, tube-sponges grown as water cannons along its rim, small fish sheltering in its branches, birds — the brave ones — nesting high. Coastal people navigate by it, argue about its route at festivals, and leave it offerings of clean water. It accepts all of this as weather.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: A5 — a coral polyp pup that budges into a reef-backed defender; the final is a walking atoll — a whole reef ecosystem on one creature, tube-sponges grown as water cannons, small fish sheltering in its branches.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a walking atoll, a place as much as a creature; other creatures live out their whole lives on it.
species.temperament: Vast, calm, and communal; its moods are seasons, not moments.
species.habitat: Region 2 warm coasts and island shallows; it walks a slow migration between feeding grounds, and harbours form where it winters.
species.dietBehaviour: Filters enormous quantities of plankton; its tenants graze, shelter, and defend it in return — a moving mutual arrangement. In a fight it brings the tube-sponge cannons to bear like a coast answering an insult, then settles back to being a place.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Reefender at full growth (growth class); per the source, it doesn't outgrow the reef — the reef outgrows *it*. The walking-atoll form, with grown artillery, is the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region coasts and island shallows. Rarity: very rare in the wild — there are simply not many, and each is known by name to coastal people; usually a legend a Ranger finally catches up with. Method: water (coast), daytime; event-class first meetings are normal for this species. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one as a rumour that turns out to have tenants, a route, and a festival argument about it.
species.cry: Source character: a deep reef-chorus — its own low groan amplified by water moving through a hundred sponge tubes, with every tenant adding clicks and pops. Pitch contour: very low, slow swells. Duration: long. Rhythm: tidal phrases, minutes apart. Variations — idle: constant low reef ambience with a groan under it; call: a swell the whole coast hears underwater; hurt: a groaning crack across the reef, tenants scattering; faint: the chorus dimming to tenant noise alone (it does not truly fall silent); affection: a warm tidal swell when an old friend returns; evolution moment: Reefender's groan opening into the full chorus as the cannons and rim complete.
species.anatomyNotes: A place-body: massive low base, walking on great stub limbs mostly submerged; the back is a full atoll — rim, lagoon hollow, coral branches, and grown tube-sponge cannons that aim by the body's slow turning and fire water, never projectiles of any other kind. The original polyp mouth and crown sit low at the front, small against everything it became. Animation must keep tenants moving independently; a still Atollossus is a failed Atollossus.
species.paletteSeed: full reef spectrum anchored in coral pink-orange, lagoon aqua, sandstone cream, deep Chrome-grey sponge tubes.
species.footprint: Print spec: at low tide, a coastline event — a broad ploughed channel in sand with huge round limb-pits at its edges, coral-grain and shell shed throughout, and small pools left in the pits that tenants colonise within the hour. Print size class: huge. Distinctive marker: the trail is briefly an ecosystem — no other track in Region 2 acquires residents.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a horizon, not an animal — a jagged atoll rim on a low vast base. Proportions: the reef is nearly all of the silhouette; the creature's own head is a minor front feature. Key masses: the rim and branches, the cannon tubes as vertical accents. Reads at sprite size as an island with legs at the bottom edge. Identifying negative space: the lagoon hollow at the centre of the rim, and the arches between cannon tubes.
species.statProfile: enormous bulk and defence, very slow, special-leaning through the water cannons; a fortress that is also a postcode. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A walking atoll: one creature that is also a whole reef ecosystem, tube-sponges grown as water cannons, fish sheltering in living branches. Must never change: final stage is a place as much as a creature (source evolution note); the cannons are grown tube-sponges firing water, never mechanical artillery; the tenants stay — an empty Atollossus contradicts the concept.

species.name: Tunnlet
species.dexText: Tunnlet digs before it walks, and walks mostly to find new digging. Its mitts are soft — the claws come later — so its first tunnels are short, proud, and prone to collapse, which it treats as the tunnel asking to be dug again. A garden with a Tunnlet in it has excellent soil and no straight rows.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag (lane standard, from source §1's element note): "Terra" is a brainstorm working label, not one of canon's show elements as recorded in the source (canon's vocabulary as documented runs Aqua/Flame/Flora/Chrome/Umbral/Beast, with Earth-class battle types in data). The label is recorded exactly as the source gives it; reconciling it is owner/game-design class. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.
species.lineConcept: A6 — a tunnelling pup with soft mitts; an excavator-armed digger; a bipedal magma mole whose drill gauntlets glow at the tips because it digs *toward* the volcano.
species.sizeClass: Small — a round pup about the size of a small burrowing pet, mitts included.
species.temperament: Busy, cheerful, and single-minded; happiest mid-tunnel.
species.habitat: Region 2 soft hills, garden soil, riverbanks, and the loose earth at the foot of higher, stonier country.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats roots, tubers, and the grubs it excavates, in that order of surprise. Digs in bursts, surfaces to check the sky is still there, dives again.
species.evolution: Becomes Excavarm as it grows and the soft mitts harden into excavator arms (growth class).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route hills and farmland soil. Rarity: common. Method: grass walk; also found by following fresh spoil heaps. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets one head-first out of a flowerbed, blinking.
species.cry: Source character: a muffled pup-whine mixed with dirt-scuff sounds, brighter above ground. Pitch contour: small rising whines. Duration: short. Rhythm: whine-scuff-whine when digging; single yips above ground. Variations — idle: soft digging mutters underground; call: a yip that carries oddly through soil; hurt: a sharp squeak and a shower of digging; faint: whines fading under a final scuff; affection: happy muffled chuffs against a boot; evolution moment: whines deepening as the mitts harden with a stony crackle.
species.anatomyNotes: Quadruped pup-mole: blunt snout for rooting, small eyes, oversized soft forepaws (the mitts) that do all the digging animation; hind paws push spoil. Jaw small, for roots and grubs. Locomotion: scampering above ground, swimming through soil below it — dig cycles are the signature loop.
species.paletteSeed: warm brown fur, cream mitts and belly, pink-brown nose, dark soil-stained paw pads.
species.footprint: Print shape class: paw print with mitt character — broad forepaw ovals with toe beans, claw marks absent (soft mitts), hind prints smaller. Gait: alternating steps above ground, interrupted constantly by dig pits. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the trail ends in fresh spoil — a fan of loose earth with mitt-prints radiating into it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: round quadruped with oversized front mitts. Proportions: head medium, forepaws comically large against the body, tail short. Key masses: mitts and round rump. Reads at sprite size as a pup wearing mittens. Identifying negative space: the gap between mitt and ground in its digging pose, and the notch between tail and rump.
species.statProfile: sturdy and busy, neither fast nor frail; digging-leaning in every sense. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A tunnelling pup whose soft mitts are the whole promise of the line. Must never change: mitts are soft at this stage — the tools harden later, as anatomy; it reads pup first, mole second; no held digging tools of any kind.

species.name: Excavarm
species.dexText: Excavarm's mitts have become excavator arms — scoop and breaker grown as one tool on each side — and it has opinions about soil the way chefs have opinions about knives. It hires itself out by standing in fields and looking expectant, and is paid in roots, which it banks in a burrow it redesigned four times. Its tunnels now have corners, and regulars.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Terra" is a brainstorm working label (see stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.
species.lineConcept: A6 — a tunnelling pup with soft mitts; an excavator-armed digger; a bipedal magma mole whose drill gauntlets glow at the tips because it digs *toward* the volcano.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a low, powerful digger about the length of a laden wheelbarrow, arms first.
species.temperament: Professional, proud, and territorial about finished tunnels.
species.habitat: Region 2 quarries' edges, terraced farms, roadworks, and any hillside being honestly improved.
species.dietBehaviour: Roots, tubers, and mineral grit for the arms. Digs planned workings now: survey sniffs, a marked line of pawprints, then excavation at a pace that embarrasses machinery.
species.evolution: Becomes Magmole at full maturity, when it takes the upright stance and the arms complete as drill gauntlets (growth class into the line's single final-stage break), digging ever deeper — toward the volcano.
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region terrace and quarry country. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass / earth walk, daytime; spoil architecture gives it away. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by falling, gently, into a tunnel that has corners.
species.cry: Source character: a gruff bark-whine with stony grinding under it, like gravel in a cheerful throat. Pitch contour: low, bumpy. Duration: short-medium. Rhythm: work phrases — grunt, grind, grunt. Variations — idle: muttered grinds while surveying; call: a carrying bark down its own tunnel; hurt: a clanging yowl; faint: grinds slowing to rest; affection: a pleased gravelly chuff; evolution moment: the grind rising into a drill-whine as the gauntlets form.
species.anatomyNotes: Still quadruped, front-heavy: excavator fore-arms are the signature — one scoop-formed, one breaker-formed, both grown, both animated as digging tools with shoulder-driven power. Hindquarters push. Snout is a rooting shovel-nose; jaw strong. Locomotion: deliberate above ground, extremely fast in soil.
species.paletteSeed: deep brown fur, Chrome-grey excavator arms, cream belly, amber eye-shine.
species.footprint: Print shape class: mixed — broad fore-arm scoop scrapes (long parallel gouges) with hind paw prints between them. Gait: alternating push-steps; trails scored by excavation marks. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: surveyed lines — a row of neat marker pawprints laid out before the digging starts, like a plan left in the dirt.
species.silhouette: Outline class: front-heavy low digger, arms as architecture. Proportions: fore-arms huge, body long, head low. Key masses: excavator arms and shoulders. Reads at sprite size as a mole crossed with a digger, arms first. Identifying negative space: the scoop's inner curve gap, and the low slot between belly and ground.
species.statProfile: strong and bulky, physical-leaning, slow on the surface and quick beneath it. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: An excavator-armed digger whose fore-arms are grown tools — scoop and breaker. Must never change: the arms are anatomy, never machinery worn or held (in-world they are body, per the grown-gear law); the break to upright drill-gauntlets is reserved for the final stage; temperament stays professional-pup, not industrial menace.

species.name: Magmole
species.dexText: Magmole stands upright and digs downward, always downward — its drill gauntlets glow at the tips because it digs toward the volcano, and the deep rock answers with heat. Miners leave marks at tunnel mouths it has passed: a spiral, meaning the way down is open and the company is good. It belongs to Region 2 and visits the volcano country like a relative who lives in the walls.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Terra" is a brainstorm working label (see stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Design note carried from source: written to feel at home near R3's volcano country without belonging to it. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5. ---
species.lineConcept: A6 — a tunnelling pup with soft mitts; an excavator-armed digger; a bipedal magma mole whose drill gauntlets glow at the tips because it digs *toward* the volcano.
species.sizeClass: Large — an upright mole standing about a person's height, gauntlets glowing, presence considerably larger.
species.temperament: Driven, warm-hearted, and funny about everything except the digging.
species.habitat: Region 2 deep hills and the roots of mountains, on the long slope toward Region 3's volcano country — written (source) to feel at home near that country without belonging to it.
species.dietBehaviour: Deep roots, mineral lodes it cracks for the salts, and heat itself, basked in at magma seams. It digs pilgrim tunnels — long, spiralling, carefully shored — and emerges at festivals smelling of stone and celebration.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Excavarm at full maturity (growth class); the bipedal stance and drill gauntlets are the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region deep hills and mountain roots. Rarity: rare in the wild; usually a raised partner's final form, or met at tunnel mouths. Method: earth / cave walk; glow and spiral marks signal it. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one underground, in a tunnel lit at the far end by approaching good company.
species.cry: Source character: a deep drilling whine over a mole's chuff, with hot-stone ticks as the gauntlets cool. Pitch contour: rises into the whine, drops to chuffs. Duration: medium. Rhythm: work phrases — whine, chuff, tick-tick. Variations — idle: low chuffs and cooling ticks; call: a whine that carries through rock; hurt: a cracking yowl; faint: whine winding down to silence and ticks; affection: a warm rumbling chuff, gauntlets dimmed; evolution moment: Excavarm's grind spinning up into the full drill-whine as it stands for the first time.
species.anatomyNotes: Bipedal mole: drill gauntlets are the forearms themselves — conical, segmented, glowing at the tips from deep-rock heat; they spin for digging and still for company. Rooting snout retained; eyes small and bright; jaw strong. Locomotion: upright stride above ground, and a corkscrew full-body dig below it. The glow is body heat at the gauntlet tips, not a light device.
species.paletteSeed: dark umber fur, Chrome drill gauntlets, magma orange tip-glow, cream chest blaze.
species.footprint: Print shape class: upright — two broad mole-foot prints, heavy toe spread, with spiral drill-scores beside rest points and tunnel mouths. Gait: alternating strides, purposeful and straight, heading downslope and down in the world. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the spiral score — a neat drilled spiral in earth or soft rock where it has tested the way down.
species.silhouette: Outline class: upright mole with drill arms. Proportions: gauntlets long and heavy, body compact, head low-set with a strong snout. Key masses: drill gauntlets and shoulders. Reads at sprite size as a mole holding two drills — which are its arms. Identifying negative space: the V between gauntlet and body when at rest, and the arc gap under its snout.
species.statProfile: strong, bulky, physical-leaning; heat gives it a special edge at depth. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A bipedal magma mole whose drill gauntlets glow at the tips because it digs toward the volcano. Must never change: gauntlets are grown forearms, never held drills or machinery; the upright break is final-stage only; the line's geography is law — at home near Region 3's volcano country without belonging to it (source evolution note).

species.name: Foldchick
species.dexText: Foldchick hatches already folded, like a note someone meant kindly. Its wings are creased paper-soft, and it cannot yet fly so much as be posted — it rides breezes a few feet at a time and lands with a small paper *pap*. It sleeps folded flat under leaves, and more than one gardener has tried to read it.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag (lane standard, from source §1's element note): "Gale" is a brainstorm working label — canon's vocabulary as documented includes Aero/Wind-class types in data rather than a Gale show element. Recorded exactly as the source gives it; reconciliation is owner/game-design class. Source variety note (A7): the only A-line whose final is more graceful, not more armoured. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.
species.lineConcept: A7 — a chick folded like paper; a crane with crease-marked wings; a majestic final whose thousand paper feathers detach as blade-feathers and return.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a chick that fits the idea of two cupped hands, if the hands are gentle and the chick is folded.
species.temperament: Sweet, patient, and unbothered by being mistaken for stationery.
species.habitat: Region 2 paper-tree groves, garden shelters, and the lee sides of hills where breezes are kind.
species.dietBehaviour: Pecks seeds and sips dew from its own wing-creases. Practises unfolding each morning: wing, wing, tail, beak — always the same order, always a small ceremony.
species.evolution: Becomes Papercrane as it grows, its folds setting into crease-marked crane wings (growth class).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route groves and sheltered gardens. Rarity: common. Method: grass walk, morning (unfolding time). Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets one by almost stepping on a note that peeps.
species.cry: Source character: a paper-dry peep — a chick chirp with a rustle folded into it. Pitch contour: quick rise, papery fall. Duration: very short. Rhythm: peep-rustle pairs. Variations — idle: soft single peeps while unfolding; call: repeated peep-rustles toward the flock; hurt: a sharp crumple-chirp; faint: peeps flattening, literally, into rustle; affection: gentle peeps against a palm; evolution moment: peeps lengthening as the creases sharpen into a crane's call.
species.anatomyNotes: Chick body of soft paper-like feather plates, folded along visible crease lines; wings fold flat in origami planes, not bird-realistic feather fans. Beak is small and crisp-edged; legs are thin folds. Locomotion: hops, and short breeze-posted glides ending in a flat landing. All movement should have a fold-and-smooth quality.
species.paletteSeed: warm paper white, soft Flora green crease-lines, pale gold beak, blush pink cheek fold.
species.footprint: Print shape class: bird toe print — three thin front toes, no claw marks (paper feet). Gait: hopping pairs, close together, with flat rectangular body-prints beside them where it has landed or slept folded. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the flat fold-print — a neat paper-sized rectangle pressed into dust or dew beside its hops.
species.silhouette: Outline class: folded chick — a plump diamond with a beak. Proportions: body compact and angular-soft, wings invisible when folded, head barely separate. Key masses: the folded body diamond. Reads at sprite size as a paper chick. Identifying negative space: the small triangle under the beak, and the slit gap along its main back crease.
species.statProfile: frail and light, quick in hops and breezes; defence is being folded and overlooked. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A chick folded like paper — origami planes, crease lines, morning unfolding ritual. Must never change: the body reads as folded paper-feather, never ordinary chick fluff; it is the line's promise of elegance, so even at this stage the folds are crisp and deliberate; no ribbons or held ornaments.

species.name: Papercrane
species.dexText: Papercrane's wings carry their creases openly, like the lines on a palm, and it flies the way handwriting moves — in long, deliberate strokes. It delivers nothing and works for no one, but it is always arriving somewhere beautifully, and villages along its routes set their clocks by the courtesy of its passing. After rain it lands and shakes out each crease separately.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Gale" is a brainstorm working label (see stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Source variety note carried: the only A-line whose final is more graceful, not more armoured — variety is the point. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.
species.lineConcept: A7 — a chick folded like paper; a crane with crease-marked wings; a majestic final whose thousand paper feathers detach as blade-feathers and return.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a crane with a wingspan wider than a person is tall, body still slight.
species.temperament: Graceful, punctual, and quietly vain about its lines.
species.habitat: Region 2 wetlands, river flats, and the air above garden country it has flown since it was a chick.
species.dietBehaviour: Takes seeds, shoots, and small water plants while wading. Flies set routes at set hours; folds itself narrow to pass through storm gaps other birds wait out.
species.evolution: Becomes Thouswings at full growth, when its paper feathers multiply toward the thousand and learn to detach and return (growth class into the line's single final-stage break — majesty, not armour).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region wetlands and river flats. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass / water-edge walk, morning and evening flight hours. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by its shadow — a clean folded shape crossing the water before the bird does.
species.cry: Source character: a clear crane call with a paper-rustle undertow, like a page turned in a quiet room. Pitch contour: long level note, elegant fall. Duration: medium. Rhythm: single calls, or a spaced pair in flight. Variations — idle: soft rustle-calls while preening creases; call: one carrying note across the flats; hurt: a harsh tearing-rustle cry; faint: the call folding down into rustle; affection: a low rustling murmur, wings half-open; evolution moment: calls layering as feathers begin, briefly, to answer on their own.
species.anatomyNotes: True crane: long legs, long neck, beak a fine paper-knife line. Wings are the signature — broad paper planes with visible crease geometry that fold in stages, origami-fashion, not feather-by-feather. Flight is gliding strokes with folded adjustments. Mouth/beak never opens wide; cries come with a lifted bill.
species.paletteSeed: paper white, green crease-lines deepening, gold beak and legs, one red fold-mark at the crown.
