species.footprint: Print shape class: bird toe print — three long front toes, elegant, no webbing. Gait: alternating wading strides, widely spaced, with take-off clusters where hops become wingbeats. Print size class: medium (long toes). Distinctive marker: a single shed crease-feather impression — sometimes the feather itself, flat and crisp as a bookmark, left at the water's edge.
species.silhouette: Outline class: crane in profile — vertical neck, horizontal body, long wing planes. Proportions: neck and legs long, body slim, wings the largest surfaces. Key masses: folded wings on the back. Reads at sprite size as a white crane with ruled lines. Identifying negative space: the long triangle between neck and folded wing, and the gap between its stilt legs.
species.statProfile: fast in the air, frail, special-leaning; elegance as evasion. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A crane with crease-marked paper wings, flying in calligraphy strokes. Must never change: creases stay visible and structural — the wings fold like paper, not like ordinary feathers; the line's direction is grace, never armour (source variety note); no tassels, ribbons, or held items.

species.name: Thouswings
species.dexText: Thouswings wears a thousand paper feathers, and every one of them can leave — fanning out as blade-feathers in a slow bright halo — and every one returns. It fights the way calligraphy argues: nothing wasted, everything placed. Elders say a Thouswings shedding and regathering its feathers over water is the closest the coast has to a second sunrise.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Gale" is a brainstorm working label (see stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Source variety note carried: the only A-line whose final is more graceful, not more armoured. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5. ---
species.lineConcept: A7 — a chick folded like paper; a crane with crease-marked wings; a majestic final whose thousand paper feathers detach as blade-feathers and return.
species.sizeClass: Large — a majestic crane, wings like a ceremony; the detached feather-cloud makes it read larger still.
species.temperament: Serene, majestic, and precise; kind in the distant way of beautiful weather.
species.habitat: Region 2 high wetlands, estuary skies, and the cliff air above the coast it patrols at dawn.
species.dietBehaviour: Wades and takes seeds, shoots, and small fish with a beak like a brushstroke. At rest it refolds its thousand feathers one section at a time, a nightly inventory that younger Papercrane watch in silence.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Papercrane at full growth (growth class); the thousand detaching blade-feathers are the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law — weaponised plumage as grown anatomy, in Digimon's ornament-as-arsenal read (source drift marker), kept elegant.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region estuaries and cliff coasts. Rarity: rare in the wild; usually a raised partner's final form or a dawn sighting. Method: water-edge / cliff walk, dawn. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one as falling bright feathers that stop, turn, and fly back up.
species.cry: Source character: a great clear crane call with a thousand-paper rustle moving under it like a turning library. Pitch contour: a long rising note that opens out. Duration: long. Rhythm: single ceremonious calls; in display, calls answered by the feather-cloud's rustle. Variations — idle: soft section-by-section rustles; call: one vast note across an estuary; hurt: a tearing chorus-cry, feathers scattering; faint: the call folding away as feathers settle home early; affection: a low murmur with the halo half-open, offered; evolution moment: Papercrane's call blooming into the full rustle-chorus as the first feathers detach and return.
species.anatomyNotes: Majestic crane; the animation signature is the feather system — a thousand paper blade-feathers that detach, array as a halo or a fanned wing of blades, strike or shield, and return to exact places. Feathers are grown plumage, never thrown objects that stay thrown. Beak and neck keep the calligraphy line; legs long and still. Flight can be borne partly on the detached cloud.
species.paletteSeed: radiant paper white, deep green creases, gold edging on blade-feathers, crown red fold-mark.
species.footprint: Print shape class: bird toe print, three long toes, as Papercrane's but grander, with a scatter of flat blade-feather impressions around standing places. Gait: stately alternating strides. Print size class: large for a bird. Distinctive marker: perfect paper feathers left flat on water or stone after a display — shed, never the detached blades themselves, which always return.
species.silhouette: Outline class: crane with a halo — a slim bird inside a fan of feathers. Proportions: body slim against an enormous feather array, neck a single fine line. Key masses: the wings and detached halo. Reads at sprite size as a white bird in a sunburst of paper. Identifying negative space: the ring gap between body and halo, and the fine slots between arrayed blade-feathers.
species.statProfile: fast, special-leaning, frail in the body and formidable in the feathers; a glass calligrapher. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A majestic paper crane whose thousand feathers detach as blade-feathers and return — ornament as arsenal, executed as grace. Must never change: feathers are grown plumage that always returns (never ammunition, never merchandise); this final stage gets *more graceful, not more armoured* (source evolution note — the bucket's deliberate variety); no metal blades — every edge is paper.

species.name: Snowpup
species.dexText: Snowpup is born in the first snow it will ever see and considers all later snow a personal sequel. Its breath frosts in small perfect puffs, and it practises its hunter's stalk on snowflakes, drifts, and its own tail. The first faint rune-lines in its back fur appear the first winter it survives — one for the season, though Snowpup cannot read them yet.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag (lane standard, from source §1's element note): "Frost" is a brainstorm working label, recorded in the source as a working element label outside canon's core show elements. Recorded exactly as given; reconciliation is owner/game-design class. Inspiration note (source §Bucket A, A8): the Fenrir myth, name re-coined (Fenrir + rune) — inspiration only, no source design carried. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A8 — a snow pup; a frost-fanged hunter; a great wolf with runes grown as ice along its spine and an ice blade grown from one shoulder.
species.sizeClass: Small — a round snow pup about the size of a winter housecat, mostly fluff.
species.temperament: Bold, joyful, and cold-proof; a pup that thinks winter is a friend.
species.habitat: Region 2 snowy foothills, winter pine forest, and frost meadows at the region's cold edge.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats winter berries, roots dug from frost-softened soil, and whatever a pup can catch, which is mostly snow. Digs snow dens and defends them against weather.
species.evolution: Becomes Frosfang as it grows through its winters, fangs frosting over and the rune-lines deepening (growth class — the line's diary is written by seasons survived).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-to-mid cold country: snowy foothills and pine edges. Rarity: uncommon. Method: grass / snow walk, winter season class; daytime. Level band: early-route to mid-region (cold route). A Ranger first meets one as a puff of frost-breath moving through a drift, pup attached.
species.cry: Source character: a bright pup yip with a crystalline frost-chime inside it. Pitch contour: quick rise, sparkling fall. Duration: very short. Rhythm: yip-chime singles; excited bursts when snow falls. Variations — idle: soft huff-yips, each frosted; call: a yip-chime that carries across snow; hurt: a sharp yelp and chime-crack; faint: yips muffling into snowfall quiet; affection: warm chuffs that frost a hand gently; evolution moment: yips dropping and chiming deeper as the fangs ice over.
species.anatomyNotes: Round quadruped pup: thick double coat, small ears, short muzzle with baby fangs just showing frost. No manipulators. Locomotion: bounding through snow — it swims drifts as much as walks them — plus the classic pup stalk-and-pounce. Faint rune-lines sit in the spine fur as a texture, not yet ice.
species.paletteSeed: snow white, pale ice blue shading, frost-pink nose, dark pine-green eye.
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad print — four toes and main pad, clear in snow, its home medium. Gait: bounding pairs, pup-wide, with belly-drag lines through deep drifts. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: prints stay rimmed with unfused frost crystals longer than other tracks — its cold lingers in its own footprints.
species.silhouette: Outline class: round fluff quadruped. Proportions: head large, coat making the body a near-circle, legs short. Key masses: the fluff body. Reads at sprite size as a snowball with ears. Identifying negative space: tiny notches between ear-tips and coat dome, and the shallow belly arc in its bounding pose.
species.statProfile: quick and sturdy for a pup, cold-leaning; balanced beginnings. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A snow pup with frost in its breath and the first unread rune-lines in its spine fur. Must never change: the runes begin as *this* line's diary (see final stage — a map of everywhere it has wintered); pup read stays warm and round; no ice armour or blade at this stage — only hints in fur and fang.

species.name: Frosfang
species.dexText: Frosfang hunts the cold months like a profession. Its fangs carry permanent frost, its breath stills the air before it, and the rune-lines along its spine have hardened into shallow ice — one stretch for every wintering ground it has learned. Other hunters follow its old tracks in spring to find where the winter game sheltered.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Frost" is a brainstorm working label (see stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Inspiration note (source §Bucket A, A8): Fenrir myth, name re-coined, no source design carried. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A8 — a snow pup; a frost-fanged hunter; a great wolf with runes grown as ice along its spine and an ice blade grown from one shoulder.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a lean hunter about the size of a large herding dog, all winter angles.
species.temperament: Focused, solitary, and fair; it hunts what it needs and guards what it has hunted past.
species.habitat: Region 2 deep pine forest, frozen lakes' edges, and high frost meadows.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts winter game and caches food in snow vaults it marks with breath-frost. Ranges alone across a wide circuit of wintering grounds, adding to the map on its back each season.
species.evolution: Becomes Fenrirune at full maturity, when the spine runes complete as grown ice and the shoulder blade comes in (growth class into the line's single final-stage break — mythic escalation).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-to-late cold country: deep forest and frozen lake country. Rarity: uncommon to rare. Method: snow walk, winter season class; dawn and dusk hunting hours. Level band: mid-region to late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one across a frozen lake, both of them deciding the other is worth watching.
species.cry: Source character: a young wolf's howl edged with ice-chime, breath audible as frost-crackle. Pitch contour: rising howl, chiming fall. Duration: medium. Rhythm: single howls; a short two-note answer pattern to distant kin. Variations — idle: low frost-crackle breaths; call: a howl that draws a map of the valley by echo; hurt: a snarling crackle-cry; faint: the howl thinning into cold air; affection: a soft chuffing howl-note, close and low; evolution moment: the howl deepening as spine-ice sings with it.
species.anatomyNotes: Lean quadruped wolf: long legs for snow, frosted fangs are the jaw's whole read — mouth animations carry ice breath. Spine has raised ice rune-lines (texture becoming structure). No blade yet; the shoulder where it will grow is marked by a pad of clear ice. Locomotion: loping snow-gait, silent placement, sudden straight hunts.
species.paletteSeed: white and ice-blue coat, deep frost blue fangs and spine-ice, dark grey paws, amber eye.
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad print with claw marks — a hunter's track. Gait: alternating lopes in long straight ranging lines between wintering grounds. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: frost-rims in the prints (as Snowpup, stronger) and occasional single fang-test pricks in lake ice at the track's pauses.
species.silhouette: Outline class: lean wolf, long lines. Proportions: legs long, body narrow, head a clean wedge, spine-ice a raised dashed line. Key masses: chest and haunches, spine line as accent. Reads at sprite size as a white wolf with an icy spine. Identifying negative space: the long gap under the belly between snow legs, and the notch between ear and spine-ice start.
species.statProfile: fast, precise, physical-leaning; a hunter's glass edge — quick, not bulky. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A frost-fanged hunting wolf whose spine is becoming an ice-written diary. Must never change: runes are grown ice along the spine recording its winterings (source evolution note) — never carved, tattooed, or decorative script from any real writing system presented as such; no shoulder blade yet — that growth is the final stage's; hunter read stays noble, not savage.

species.name: Fenrirune
species.dexText: Fenrirune is a great wolf that carries its life on its back: runes grown as ice along its spine, one for everywhere it has wintered, legible — elders insist — to anyone who has wintered honestly themselves. From one shoulder grows a blade of clear ice, drawn in battle the way other wolves bare fangs: as a fact, stated once. In deep winter its howl is answered by wolves that are not there, in places it has been.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Frost" is a brainstorm working label (see stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Inspiration note (source §Bucket A, A8): the Fenrir myth, name re-coined (Fenrir + rune), no source design carried over. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5. ---
species.lineConcept: A8 — a snow pup; a frost-fanged hunter; a great wolf with runes grown as ice along its spine and an ice blade grown from one shoulder.
species.sizeClass: Large — a great wolf, shoulder about at a person's shoulder height, blade above that.
species.temperament: Mythic, patient, and self-possessed; a creature that has become a story while still alive.
species.habitat: Region 2 highest frost country — glacier edges, summit pines, and the wintering grounds of its whole life, revisited in a grand circuit.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts great winter game sparingly and keeps the old caches of its middle years. It walks its circuit each deep winter, reading its own back by memory at every ground it made.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Frosfang at full maturity (growth class); the mythic escalation — full rune-spine and grown shoulder greatsword of ice — is the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law.
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region high frost country. Rarity: very rare in the wild; a known individual class of creature, more often a lifetime partner's final form. Method: snow walk, deep-winter season class; event-class meetings at old wintering grounds. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one where its tracks have been famous for years.
species.cry: Source character: a great wolf howl with ice-singing in it — the spine runes resonate like a struck glacier edge. Pitch contour: a long rise, a held ringing peak, a slow chiming fall. Duration: very long. Rhythm: single howls, spaced like weather. Variations — idle: breath-crackle and faint rune-song in wind; call: the full howl, answered by distance itself; hurt: a cracking roar-howl; faint: the song dimming as the ice dulls, never quite to silence; affection: a low private howl-note with the blade lowered; evolution moment: Frosfang's howl taking on the ice-song as the blade grows with a sound like a lake freezing at speed.
species.anatomyNotes: Great quadruped wolf — it does *not* stand up; the break is scale, runes, and the blade, not posture. The ice blade grows from one shoulder (asymmetric, per the Region 2 silhouette licence) and is swung by shoulder and neck motion, never held. Runes are raised ice script-forms along the spine — original glyph shapes, glowing faintly with cold when it acts. Jaw carries frosted fangs at great scale. Locomotion: immense loping strides, and stillness like a monument.
species.paletteSeed: glacier white, deep ice blue runes and blade, storm grey undercoat, pale gold eye.
species.footprint: Print shape class: great pad prints with claw scores. Gait: immense alternating lopes; at wintering grounds, prints arrange in a slow circuit walked the same way each year. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: frost-tracing — per canon's frost-trace precedent, its passing leaves a frost line in its track and across surfaces it brushes, carrying a faint cold shimmer; old circuits stay frost-marked longest.
species.silhouette: Outline class: monumental wolf with a shoulder blade. Proportions: body massive and long, head a noble wedge, one shoulder rising into the ice blade's vertical. Key masses: torso and the blade. Reads at sprite size as a wolf with a sword grown from its shoulder and writing on its back. Identifying negative space: the arc between blade and neck, and the gaps between the raised spine-runes read as a dashed light-line.
species.statProfile: strong, durable, and fast in bursts; a mythic all-rounder leaning physical. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A great wolf with ice runes grown along its spine and an ice greatsword grown from one shoulder — mythic escalation of a snow pup, still plainly a wolf. Must never change: the runes are a map of everywhere it has wintered — the line keeps a diary on its back (source evolution note), so rune count/placement is biography, not decoration; the blade is grown from the shoulder, never held in the mouth or a paw as a weapon prop; it stays quadruped — the break is mythic scale, not humanoid form.

species.name: Lonelily
species.dexText: Lonelily is a shy lily bud that grows facing the nearest other Lonelily, if there is one, and faces the wall if there is not. It blooms for no audience and opens a fraction wider on days when another bud is near. Gardeners who keep them learn to plant in twos, and to pretend they have not noticed why.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source mechanic flag (source §Bucket A, A9): this is the bucket's bond mechanic — evolution as a relationship event (Digimon's partner logic, Pokémon's gentleness). The only line whose evolution is a pair of creatures becoming a pair-shaped one. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5. ⚑ Open owner-class question carried, not invented: how the pair-to-one evolution is represented in roster/data terms (two entries becoming one entry) is game-design class and is not decided by this sheet.
species.lineConcept: A9 — a single shy lily bud. It cannot evolve alone: two Lonelily raised within sight of each other bloom into one Pairbloom, and two Pairbloom in accord become Twinvow.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a single bud on a stem, small enough to hide behind its own leaf, and it does.
species.temperament: Shy, gentle, and quietly hopeful; loneliness is its weather, not its character.
species.habitat: Region 2 shaded garden corners, quiet pond edges, and the dim Flora ground under old walls.
species.dietBehaviour: Feeds on water, shade-filtered light, and stillness. It turns slowly through the day — toward company, not sun. A lone Lonelily leans; a paired one stands straight.
species.evolution: It cannot evolve alone (source law for this line — the bucket's one bond mechanic). Two Lonelily raised within sight of each other bloom into one Pairbloom: evolution as a relationship event, the pair becoming a pair-shaped one. No level or solitary method exists for this stage.
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route shaded gardens and quiet pond edges. Rarity: uncommon (easy to overlook — it prefers that). Method: grass walk, daytime, still weather; gift/bond-class first meetings are also normal — gardeners give them in pairs. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first plausibly meets one by being quietly leaned toward by a bud they nearly missed.
species.cry: Source character: the softest bell-note — a single petal-clear chime made by the bud trembling, barely louder than a leaf falling. Pitch contour: one pure note, slight downward fade. Duration: very short. Rhythm: single notes, widely spaced; in company, two buds answer note-for-note. Variations — idle: a rare single chime; call: a chime offered, then a listening silence; hurt: a tiny cracked chime and closing; faint: the note flattening as the bud droops; affection: a warmer chime, bud opening a fraction; evolution moment: two chimes finding one pitch together — the sound of Pairbloom arriving.
species.anatomyNotes: A bud on a slender stem: one leaf, root-toes below, no arms, no jaw — the face is suggested by the bud's opening seam and a shy tilt. All expression is posture: lean, turn, close, open a fraction. Locomotion is near-none — it re-roots over days, a slow creep toward company.
species.paletteSeed: dusk-lily white, Umbral violet shading at the bud base, soft green stem, one deep purple throat-spot not yet visible.
species.footprint: Leaves no ordinary footprint. Trace spec: a tiny ring of root-toe pricks where it has stood, and a slow comma-drag of pricks charting its days-long creep — a track read in patience, usually pointing at another Lonelily. Distinctive marker: the prick-trail always curves toward company, never toward food or light alone.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a single bud on a line — minimal. Proportions: bud small, stem the whole height, leaf one accent. Key masses: the bud. Reads at sprite size as a shy closed flower. Identifying negative space: the crescent between bud and leaf, and the lean — its silhouette is never quite vertical.
species.statProfile: frail, slow, special-leaning in potentia; its strength is entirely relational. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: One shy lily bud, leaning toward company. Must never change: it is a *single* bud — the pairing is the evolution, not a design variant; the read is loneliness-with-hope, never spookiness despite the Umbral shading; this line's bond evolution is the bucket's one bond mechanic (source) and must not be diluted or copied onto other lines.

species.name: Pairbloom
species.dexText: Pairbloom is what two Lonelily become when they have been raised within sight of each other long enough to mean it: two blooms on stems that have grown together at the base, opening in turns so one is always awake. They finish each other's blooming the way old friends finish sentences — without hurry, and slightly wrong on purpose when it is funny.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source mechanic flag (source §Bucket A, A9): the bucket's bond mechanic — evolution as a relationship event; this stage is reached only by two Lonelily raised within sight of each other, and leaves only by two Pairbloom in accord. ⚑ Roster/data representation of pair-evolution remains owner/game-design class (see stage 1 flag). No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A9 — a single shy lily bud. It cannot evolve alone: two Lonelily raised within sight of each other bloom into one Pairbloom, and two Pairbloom in accord become Twinvow.
species.sizeClass: Small — two blooms on joined stems, together about the height of a garden lantern.
species.temperament: Warm, companionable, and gently teasing; contentment as a personality.
species.habitat: Region 2 kept gardens, pond edges, and window boxes — places where pairs are planted on purpose.
species.dietBehaviour: Shared roots, shared water: each bloom feeds a little better than a lone lily ever does. They turn to face callers in alternation, and close together at night, two lamps dimming in sequence.
species.evolution: Two Pairbloom in accord become Twinvow (source law for this line): the pair-evolution repeats at the next scale — accord, not proximity alone, is the trigger at this stage. No solitary method exists.
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region kept gardens and tended pond edges. Rarity: rare in the truly wild (it requires the pairing to have happened); uncommon where gardeners plant for it. Method: grass walk, daytime; gift/bond-class — a raised pair is the common way a Ranger has one. Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one in a garden where somebody loved two Lonelily properly.
species.cry: Source character: two bell-chimes in harmony, stems resonating together. Pitch contour: two notes that find and hold a chord. Duration: short-medium. Rhythm: alternating and answering phrases — a duet structure in every state. Variations — idle: soft alternating chimes; call: a chord offered together; hurt: one chime sharp, the other answering low in concern; faint: the chord loosening, both notes dimming in turn; affection: warm doubled chimes, blooms turned to the Ranger together; evolution moment: two Pairbloom's chords aligning into a four-note accord as Twinvow forms.
species.anatomyNotes: Two bloom-heads on stems joined at a shared base/root — animate as one body with two centres of attention: heads turn independently, stems sway against each other, roots are common. No limbs, no jaws; mouths are the blooms' throats, opening in flower, never in speech. Movement is sway and lean only.
species.paletteSeed: lily white and violet, Umbral purple deepening at the joined base, soft green double stems, gold throat accents.
species.footprint: Leaves no ordinary footprint. Trace spec: a double ring of root-pricks at the shared base and paired comma-creeps if the pair re-roots over a season — two trails, always converging. Distinctive marker: the joined ring — one root-print set, two stems; gardeners read it as a signature.
species.silhouette: Outline class: twin blooms on a forked stem. Proportions: two heads equal, stems the long vertical, shared base narrow. Key masses: the two blooms, balanced. Reads at sprite size as a two-headed flower, friendly. Identifying negative space: the heart-shaped gap between the two blooms and stems, and the fork notch above the joined base.
species.statProfile: still frail, special-leaning, with a defender's alternation — something is always awake. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Two blooms, one joined base — a pair-shaped creature, not two creatures standing close. Must never change: the shared root/base is structural and visible; the blooms are equals in size and presence; the mood is married contentment, never eerie twinness — Umbral here is dusk, not darkness.

species.name: Twinvow
species.dexText: Twinvow is two flowers on one root, facing opposite directions, so that one always watches the other's back. Nothing has ever surprised a Twinvow. Travellers leave messages under them — a Twinvow keeps what it is told in the bloom that heard it, and the other bloom, which did not, keeps the secret perfectly.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Source mechanic flag (source §Bucket A, A9): the bucket's bond mechanic and its only pair-evolution line. ⚑ Roster/data representation of pair-evolution remains owner/game-design class (see stage 1 flag). No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5. ---
species.lineConcept: A9 — a single shy lily bud. It cannot evolve alone: two Lonelily raised within sight of each other bloom into one Pairbloom, and two Pairbloom in accord become Twinvow — two flowers, one root, facing opposite directions so one always watches the other's back.
species.sizeClass: Medium — two great blooms on one root, standing about waist-high on a person, watching both ways.
species.temperament: Devoted, vigilant, and serene; a promise that photosynthesises.
species.habitat: Region 2 old garden walls, pass-ends, and threshold plantings — places where watching both ways is a kindness.
species.dietBehaviour: Deep shared root-work; the two blooms trade light through the stem across the day, the lit one feeding the shaded one, the debt reversing by evening. In danger, the threatened bloom closes and the watching bloom opens fully, flaring dusk-purple — the vow, kept in real time.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached only when two Pairbloom in accord become one Twinvow (source law for this line — the pair-evolution is the line's whole path; there is no solitary route at any stage).
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region old gardens and threshold places. Rarity: very rare in the wild; an achievement of gardening and time more than a find. Method: event / gift-bond class — a Ranger raises one through both pairings, or is given cuttings of a famous pair; wild meetings happen at legendary plantings. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one where a message was left for them, kept faithfully, facing the other way.
species.cry: Source character: two deep bell-chimes that never sound together by accident — a watcher and a keeper, alternating, in accord. Pitch contour: low paired notes, chorded only at the vow-moments. Duration: medium. Rhythm: strict alternation; a full chord means something important. Variations — idle: slow alternating chimes through the day; call: one bloom chimes, the other answers from the far side; hurt: a chord — both at once — then protective silence; faint: chimes dimming in alternation, the last from the watching bloom; affection: a rare warm chord, offered deliberately; evolution moment: the four-note accord of two Pairbloom resolving into Twinvow's first alternating pair.
species.anatomyNotes: Two large blooms on stems from one root mass, facing opposite directions — this facing is the anatomy note that matters most: the pair can never both face the same way. Shared root is broad and visible at the base. Light-trading shows as a slow glow-shift along the stems. No limbs or jaws; threat display is one bloom closing, the other flaring open.
species.paletteSeed: deep lily white, rich Umbral violet, dusk purple flare, shared-root moss green, gold throats.
species.footprint: Leaves no ordinary footprint. Trace spec: a single broad root-ring print — one root, read clearly — with decades of stillness around it: moss lines, message-stones, and a worn hollow on each side where travellers have stood to talk to each bloom. Distinctive marker: the double worn hollow, one root: the vow's own track is the place it keeps.
species.silhouette: Outline class: twin blooms back-to-back on one root. Proportions: two equal bloom masses opposed at the top, stems crossing to a single base. Key masses: the two blooms. Reads at sprite size as a flower facing both ways at once. Identifying negative space: the diamond gap between the opposed blooms, and the single-root notch at the base that proves it is one creature.
species.statProfile: special-leaning, durable for a flower, slow; a sentry-pair in one body — coverage over speed. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Two flowers, one root, facing opposite directions so one always watches the other's back (source, verbatim in spirit). Must never change: opposite facing is absolute; the root is one and visibly shared; the pair-evolution path (Lonelily in sight → Pairbloom, Pairbloom in accord → Twinvow) is this line's alone in the bucket — Digimon's partner logic at Pokémon gentleness (source drift marker), never a template for other lines.

species.name: Noodlet
species.dexText: Noodlet is an eel the width of a noodle and the optimism of a kite. It ties itself in practice knots in the shallows, unties most of them, and is found in the rest by its friends, who help. Currents carry it further than it means to go, and it treats every arrival as a decision it made.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag (lane standard, from source §1's element note): "Gale" is a brainstorm working label (see A7 stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Inspiration note (source §Bucket A, A10): the azure-dragon shape, re-coined (azure + *long*, the Chinese dragon word) — a shape homage, no source name carried. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A10 — a noodle-thin ribbon eel; a longer, ribboned angler of shallow seas; a majestic sky-serpent that leaves the water entirely and swims the wind over the coast.
species.sizeClass: Small — a noodle-thin eel about as long as a person's arm and almost as wide as a ribbon on a gift.
species.temperament: Cheerful, wriggly, and distractible; the sea's loose thread.
species.habitat: Region 2 shallow seas, eelgrass beds, and warm tidal channels.
species.dietBehaviour: Snaps tiny shrimp and plankton blooms from the water as it streams past. Swims in constant ribbons and loops — straight lines are for other fish.
species.evolution: Becomes Ribbongler as it grows longer and its ribbons develop (growth class — the awkward middle begins).
species.discovery: Region 2 — early-route shallows and tidal channels. Rarity: common. Method: water (shallows), daytime. Level band: early-route. A Ranger first meets one knotted, cheerfully, around something they were using.
species.cry: Source character: a wet bubbly squeak, like air escaping a toy in the bath. Pitch contour: wiggly up-down, matching its swimming. Duration: short. Rhythm: squeak-bursts in loops of three. Variations — idle: occasional single squeaks while knotting; call: a loop of squeaks down the channel; hurt: one tight squeak and a knot; faint: squeaks flattening as it drifts; affection: rapid happy squeaks while ribboning around a wrist (loosely); evolution moment: squeaks stretching longer and smoother as the body lengthens.
species.anatomyNotes: A true eel: no limbs, no fins beyond a continuous ribbon fin along the body, small mouth at the front that can gape comically. The whole body is the animator's instrument — knots, loops, ribbons. Locomotion: serpentine swimming only; on land it ribbons helplessly and good-naturedly.
species.paletteSeed: pale aqua, ribbon-pink fin edge, cream belly line, dark bead eyes.
species.footprint: Leaves no footprints. Trace spec: in shallow sand, sinuous ribbon-grooves far narrower than any snake's, with occasional neat knot-loops pressed into the bed — a signature no other shallow creature writes. Distinctive marker: the knot-loop in its own trail.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a living ribbon — one long low wave. Proportions: all length, no height; head barely wider than body. Key masses: none — evenness is the read. Reads at sprite size as a noodle with eyes. Identifying negative space: the loops' inner holes when it knots, which are the silhouette's whole event.
species.statProfile: quick in water, frail, elusive; tied in knots, statistically and literally. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A noodle-thin ribbon eel of pure cheerful wriggle — the humble start of the bucket's humble-to-majestic leap. Must never change: humble is the point (source drift marker — Digimon's small-cute → noble-final jump needs a genuinely small-cute start); no proto-wings or sky hints beyond optimism; body stays ribbon-thin.

species.name: Ribbongler
species.dexText: Ribbongler is the awkward century of its line: too long for the shallows' small talk, not yet the sky's majesty, trailing ribbons it has not grown into. It angles in shallow seas with endless patience, watching the clouds with an expression its elders recognise. They do not tease it. They remember.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Gale" is a brainstorm working label (see A10 stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Inspiration note (source §Bucket A, A10): azure-dragon shape homage, name re-coined, no source name carried. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5.
species.lineConcept: A10 — a noodle-thin ribbon eel; a longer, ribboned angler of shallow seas; a majestic sky-serpent that leaves the water entirely and swims the wind over the coast.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a long ribboned eel, longer than a person is tall and still nearly as thin.
species.temperament: Patient, wistful, and self-conscious about the ribbons; quietly certain its day is scheduled.
species.habitat: Region 2 shallow seas deepening toward the drop-off, harbour mouths, and the undersides of piers.
species.dietBehaviour: Angles for small fish from stillness, ribbons streaming as lures of light, then one neat strike. Spends long hours at the surface on calm days, tasting the wind — the only stage that does this, and it does not know why yet.
species.evolution: Becomes Azulong at full maturity, when it leaves the water entirely and takes to swimming the wind over the coast (growth class into the line's single final-stage break — the humble-to-majestic leap).
species.discovery: Region 2 — mid-region shallows and harbour mouths. Rarity: uncommon. Method: water, calm daytime (surface-watching weather). Level band: mid-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one at a pier, both of them looking at the sky, only one of them knowing why.
species.cry: Source character: a longer, smoother bubble-call with a wistful slide in pitch, like a note bent on a wet string. Pitch contour: rises, bends, settles. Duration: medium. Rhythm: slow single calls; surface calls come in thoughtful pairs. Variations — idle: soft single bubble-notes; call: a bending call across the shallows; hurt: a tight squeak, Noodlet-like, then dignity; faint: the note sliding down and away; affection: gentle looped calls, ribbons calming; evolution moment: the call leaving the water — rising out of bubble-register into open air as the first wind-swim begins.
species.anatomyNotes: Eel body much longer, with developed ribbon fins along its length that stream, flare, and catch light — proto-wings in read only; they are fins, and it still swims. Head slightly finer, mouth the same small angler's gape. Locomotion: slow serpentine cruising and long still angling poses; surface behaviour (head raised, tasting wind) is its unique beat.
species.paletteSeed: deeper aqua, pink-to-pale-gold ribbon fins, cream belly, wistful dark eyes.
species.footprint: Leaves no footprints. Trace spec: wide slow ribbon-grooves in shallow sand, much longer between turns than Noodlet's, ending at deep-water edges; on calm surfaces, a ribbon wake that sometimes, briefly, continues a body's length past where the eel turned — wind rehearsing. Distinctive marker: the over-long straight stretches in its trail, where it lay still, angling.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long ribbon at rest — low, elegant, unresolved. Proportions: extreme length, ribbons adding side mass in motion only. Key masses: the coiled mid-body at rest. Reads at sprite size as a beautiful eel that seems to be waiting for something. Identifying negative space: the wide loops of its resting coil, and the lifted head's gap above the waterline in its signature pose.
species.statProfile: balanced and patient, special-leaning as the wind starts to notice it; mid-line awkwardness in every stat's story. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A longer, ribboned angler of shallow seas — stage 2 is the awkward century, and the brief must keep it awkward: ribbons not yet mastered, majesty not yet arrived (source evolution note). Must never change: it does not fly, skim, or leave the water at this stage — the sky is the final stage's alone; wistfulness is a design feature, not a flaw to be designed out.

species.name: Azulong
species.dexText: Azulong leaves the water entirely and swims the wind over the coast, ribbons become weather, and harbours fly flags on the days it passes. It remembers being a noodle, and is kind to noodles. Fishermen read its route the way farmers read rivers: as a fact of the world that is also, unmistakably, a favour.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚑ Type-vocabulary flag: "Gale" is a brainstorm working label (see A10 stage 1 flag); recorded exactly as the source gives it, reconciliation owner/game-design class. Inspiration note (source §Bucket A, A10): the azure-dragon shape, re-coined (azure + *long*) — a shape homage, no source name carried. No ⚠ animal-sharing recorded for this line in source §5.4/§5.5. --- *End of Bucket A (Region 2) — 10 lines, 30 stage sheets. All ⚑ items are owner / game-design class and are flagged in place; nothing numeric has been assigned by this file.*
species.lineConcept: A10 — a noodle-thin ribbon eel; a longer, ribboned angler of shallow seas; a majestic sky-serpent that leaves the water entirely and swims the wind over the coast.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a majestic sky-serpent, river-long, that swims the wind over the coast; its shadow crosses whole beaches.
species.temperament: Majestic, benevolent, and amused; the patience of Ribbongler, paid in full.
species.habitat: Region 2 coastal skies, sea-wind currents, and the high air above estuaries; it returns to great waters only to visit, like royalty at a childhood home.
species.dietBehaviour: Takes great fish at the surface in ribboning dives and snaps storm-scattered birds' lost feathers out of the air for no reason it will explain. It flies the coast in a grand circuit, and its calm-weather loops are a coastal festival no one organises and everyone attends.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line. Reached from Ribbongler at full maturity (growth class); leaving the water for the wind is the line's single permitted body-plan break under the Region 2 law — and the bucket's humble-to-majestic leap (source drift marker).
species.discovery: Region 2 — late-region coasts and estuary skies. Rarity: very rare — a known, named-in-effect presence over the coast; event-class meetings are the norm. Method: coast walk / sky watching, calm clear daytime; it comes to weather, not to searching. Level band: late-region. A Ranger first plausibly meets one as a shadow crossing the beach, then the whole sky agreeing to be looked at.
species.cry: Source character: a vast smooth call — wind through a great ribbon, with the eel's old bubble-note transposed into open air as a pure sustained tone. Pitch contour: a long slow rise, a held crest, a ribboning fall. Duration: very long. Rhythm: single calls that harbours hear in sequence as it passes. Variations — idle: wind-rustle tones along its ribbons; call: the full coast-carrying note; hurt: a tearing wind-cry, weather answering; faint: the tone descending into the sea-wind and being carried off (it falls rarely, and slowly); affection: a warm looping call, ribbons loosening around an old friend's tower or mast; evolution moment: Ribbongler's surface call lifting clean out of the water into Azulong's first full sky-note.
species.anatomyNotes: Sky-serpent: immense ribbon body flown in serpentine swimming motions through air — the swimming *is* the flying, per the source ("swims the wind"). Ribbon fins run the body's length, now vast and weather-catching. No legs; whisker-like barbels and a noble drake head acknowledge the azure-dragon shape homage without copying any source design. Mouth is the angler's gape at majestic scale. Animation signature: the body never stops its slow swimming, even at rest in a coil of air.
species.paletteSeed: azure blue, pale gold ribbons, pearl belly, storm-white barbel and crest accents.
species.footprint: Leaves no footprints — it does not land. Trace spec: its trace is aerial and coastal: ribbon-press patterns left in flattened eelgrass where its wind-wake has combed a meadow in one direction, and calm spiral marks in harbour water under its resting air-coils. Distinctive marker: the combed-grass swathe, all one way, under a sky with nothing in it anymore.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a river in the sky — one immense ribboned serpentine. Proportions: all length and ribbon, head noble and small against the whole. Key masses: the coiled mid-body and ribbon fins. Reads at sprite size as a sky-dragon silhouette, unmistakable and unhurried. Identifying negative space: the great loops' inner sky-holes, and the fine gaps between streaming ribbons.
species.statProfile: majestic all-round presence — fast in the wind, special-leaning, durable; the leap, quantified in words only. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A majestic sky-serpent that leaves the water entirely and swims the wind — the noodle's whole story, answered. Must never change: it *swims* the air in eel motion (no bird-wing flight, no legged dragon stance); the azure-dragon read is a shape homage only — original design, re-coined name, no source design carried (source inspiration note); majesty must stay kind — this is the creature that is kind to noodles.

species.name: Plowpus
species.dexText: Plowpus tills the festival fields each spring, drilling seed rows with its bill and turning the soil with ploughshare claws. It is paid in river pebbles, which it does not need and keeps anyway in a tidy pile. A field it has finished is known by its ruler-straight rows.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Shares the platypus with Psyduck (Psyduck is widely documented as platypus-based, §5.3) — concept kept but flagged (B1): the seed is a digging farm animal, no duck, no headache-psychic read (see §5).
species.lineConcept: B1 Plowpus — a platypus whose bill is a seed-drill and whose claws are ploughshares; it tills the festival fields in spring and is paid in river pebbles it doesn't need.
species.sizeClass: Small — a low, long-bodied creature at sturdy farm-cat scale, built close to the ground with its weight carried forward into the bill and foreclaws.
species.temperament: methodical — it works a field in straight, patient passes, finishes a row before it starts the next, and treats a skipped patch as a personal debt.
species.habitat: Festival fields and the riverbanks beside them in Region 3 ranch country; it sleeps near the water it works beside and returns to the same fields each spring.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats riverside grubs, worms, and soft roots turned up by its own ploughing. It accepts river pebbles as payment, keeps them in a neat bankside pile, and has no use for them beyond the keeping. In spring it is all work; out of tilling season it is a slow, unhurried swimmer.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Common — met at work. Method: festival fields and adjoining riverbanks, tilling alongside ranch hands. Time/season: spring, when the festival fields are being prepared; quieter and mostly in the water the rest of the year. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by being handed a row to work next to it, pebble payment pile and all.
species.cry: Source character: low, earthy bill-clacks and soft churring grunts, with a splashy snort when the bill comes up wet. Pitch contour: low and flat, dipping lower at the end of a pass. Duration class: short bursts, repeated evenly. Syllable/rhythm pattern: an even, row-like *clack — churr — clack*, paced like work. Variations — idle: a slow contented churr while it re-sorts its pebbles; call: a louder bill-clack volley across the field; hurt: a sharp squawk and bill-snap; faint: a tired snort that trails into snoring; affection: a soft, rapid bill-nibbling chatter against a trusted hand; evolution moment: none — single-stage, the cry never marks a change.
species.anatomyNotes: Four short webbed feet; the foreclaws are broad ploughshare blades and the hind feet steer like rudders. The bill is a working seed-drill, not a duck bill: it opens only a little, and the drama is in the drilling push, not a bite. Locomotion is a low waddle on land and a smooth, whole-body swim in water. Manipulators: the foreclaws and bill only. Proportion-licence feature: the oversized drill-bill and ploughshare foreclaws. An animator must never give it a headache-psychic pose or a duck's quacking gape.
species.paletteSeed: river-mud brown, wet slate, seed-green, pebble grey, bill ochre
species.footprint: Print shape class: webbed. Each print is a broad, fan-shaped webbed impression with ploughshare claw grooves scored ahead of it; the hind prints are narrower steering fans. Toe/claw count and arrangement: webbing makes a single fan rather than separate toes, with the forefoot's blade-claws leaving a short row of deep parallel scores at the front edge. Gait pattern: alternating steps in a low waddle, in long straight passes. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: twin furrow-lines dragged between the rows of prints, and seed holes drilled at even intervals beside the track — no other ranch track comes with its own planting.
species.silhouette: Outline class: low horizontal torpedo. Proportions in words: a long flat body, most of its length in the torso and tail, almost none in leg height. Key visual masses sit at the front (drill-bill and blade foreclaws) and the back (flat paddle tail), with a smooth unbroken back between them. What reads at sprite size: the flat bill, the paddle tail, and the shine on the foreclaws. Identifying negative space: the low wedge of open air under the bill, between the drill tip and the foreclaws, and the notch where the tail meets the waterline when it swims.
species.statProfile: A steady workhorse profile — solid defence and stamina for long field work, modest attack delivered through the bill and claws, unremarkable speed on land and better in water — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a low, flat platypus body carried on short webbed feet, read instantly by the seed-drill bill and ploughshare foreclaws. Key features: drill-bill, blade foreclaws, paddle tail, a bankside pebble pile as its signature prop. Must-never-change list: the bill stays a farm implement, never a duck bill; no headache-psychic read; the body stays a digging farm animal's body; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Sentripea
species.dexText: Sentripea keeps watch over the ranch from its stalk, one large eye turning to follow every cart, creature, and cloud. When it spots trouble — or anything it finds interesting — it rattles the peas in its pod to raise the alarm. The peas are the rattle, and the rattle is rarely wrong about something having happened.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ The one-eye-stalk echoes Monster Rancher's Suezo signature — a donor-side proximity flagged in §5 / §5.4 for the owner's eye rather than hidden: the seed here is a plant with peas, not an eyeball monster.
species.lineConcept: B2 Sentripea — a pea-pod on a stalk with one large eye at the top; the ranch lookout, it rustles the pod to sound alarms (the peas are the rattle).
species.sizeClass: Small — mostly stalk and eye; the pod body itself is small, light, and held high, so the creature reads taller than it is heavy.
species.temperament: nosy — it watches everything, leans toward gossip at the fence line, and reports movements nobody asked it to track with exactly the same rattle as a real alarm.
species.habitat: Ranch fence lines, garden gates, and lookout posts across Region 3 ranch country, wherever a stalk can root in sight of a road, a pen, or the festival grounds.
species.dietBehaviour: A plant creature that feeds on sunlight, rain, and rich garden soil, with a taste for being where it can see. Its whole behaviour is watching: the eye tracks passers-by, and any excitement sets the pod rattling — the loose peas inside are the alarm.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Common — met at work. Method: ranch lookouts, garden gates, and fence lines, where it is already on duty. Time/season: year-round, most vocal in the busy festival season when there is the most to watch. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by being rattled at, thoroughly, for approaching a gate it has decided is its gate.
species.cry: Source character: no voice-box cry in the usual sense — a dry pod-rattle, leaf-rustle, and a small peeping squeak from the pod's seam. Pitch contour: the squeak sits high and rises when it is excited; the rattle has no pitch, only speed. Duration class: short rattles, very repeatable. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *shaka-shaka … peep* — rattle first, squeak as the verdict. Variations — idle: an occasional lazy half-rattle at passing clouds; call: a full fast rattle that can carry across a ranch yard; hurt: a single hard shake and a thin squeak; faint: the pod droops and the peas settle with one last soft tick; affection: a gentle, purring rustle and the eye leaning close; evolution moment: none — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: No limbs and no hands: the body is a rooted or tiptoeing stalk, a hanging pea-pod, and one large eye at the top. The mouth, if shown at all, is the pod's seam — expression lives in the eye and in how the pod swings and rattles. Locomotion is a stalk-lean, a hop of the root, or a carried sway; it never walks. Proportion-licence feature: mostly eye and stalk — the eye is the head, the face, and most of the acting. An animator must keep it a plant with peas, never an eyeball monster.
species.paletteSeed: pea green, stalk sage, pod-lime, eye white, iris amber
species.footprint: Print shape class: none — it has no feet. Toe/claw count and arrangement: none; in place of a pad print, the stalk's root-tip leaves a single small round dimple, ringed by fine rootlet scratches. Gait pattern: when it moves at all, the dimples appear in a slow single file with long gaps, each one leaned in the direction it was looking. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the dimple trail itself, plus shed peas and pod husks near lookout posts — and the fact that the dots keep stopping in clusters wherever there was something worth watching.
species.silhouette: Outline class: vertical exclamation mark. Proportions in words: a thin stalk carrying almost all the height, a small pod hanging to one side, and the eye crowning the top like a flag. Key visual masses: the eye at the summit and the pod at mid-height; everything else is line. What reads at sprite size: the single big eye and the pod's curved bulge. Identifying negative space: the tall open triangle between the stalk, the pod's hanging curve, and the ground — the emptiest silhouette in the bucket, by design.
species.statProfile: A lookout's profile — keen perception and just enough speed to rattle first, very little bulk or attack; it wins by being noticed early, not by fighting — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a stalk, a pod, and one huge eye — the proportion licence taken to its limit. Key features: single eye on top, pea-pod body with visible peas as the rattle, rooted stance at gates and fences. Must-never-change list: it stays a plant with peas, not an eyeball monster; the eye is one, large, and on top; the peas must be readable as the alarm rattle; no limbs; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Cinderewe
types: Flame (the crossing is recorded in the source as Flame × Aqua → Volt)
species.dexText: Cinderewe's wool smoulders softly all year, too gentle to burn and too warm to ignore. At shearing time the fleece is gathered as winter kindling, and one ewe can keep a ranch house's fires starting through the cold months. It is one of the two parents of the Stormewe cross.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Sheep are Pokémon-occupied (Wooloo) — these are elemental weather-sheep, not wool livestock (see §5 / §5.4, B3 sheep). ⚑ Additionally: no one-word temperament is given in the source for the B3 crossing — flagged open, owner-class, not invented here.
species.lineConcept: B3, the Stormewe crossing — Cinderewe, one of two ewe species designed as a Rancher crossing pair, whose wool smoulders softly and is sheared for winter kindling. Cross: Cinderewe × Rainewe → Stormewe.
species.sizeClass: Medium — an ordinary ewe's scale, made to look larger and rounder by a full fleece that never quite stops smoking at the edges.
species.temperament: ⚑ No one-word temperament is given in the source for this crossing — owner-class, unassigned in the source. Its colour, from the seed alone: a creature whose warmth is a service, shorn each year so other creatures' fires can start.
species.habitat: Ranch pastures and shearing sheds in Region 3, kept near barns and winter stores; it favours dry bedding well away from haystacks — including away from Shagdox.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes pasture grass and favours dry, resinous herbs at the field edges. Its wool smoulders softly and continuously, never flaming; at shearing time the fleece comes off as winter kindling, and the ewe spends a short while looking surprised and much smaller.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve. Crossing note: Cinderewe is a designed crossing parent — Cinderewe × Rainewe → Stormewe (see the Stormewe sheet, B3). Stormewe is the cross of the two species, not an evolution of Cinderewe alone.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: ranch pastures and shearing sheds, where it is kept for its fleece. Time/season: most sought and most shorn in the run-up to winter; its smoulder is easiest to spot at dusk in any season. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it at shearing time, carrying away a bundle of its warm wool.
species.cry: Source character: a soft ewe's bleat with a fireside crackle woven through it, and a faint hiss when rain surprises it. Pitch contour: mid and warm, falling gently. Duration class: short bleats, often doubled. Syllable/rhythm pattern: a plain *baa-baa* with a crackle tail. Variations — idle: a low crackling hum from the wool under an occasional bleat; call: a louder, sharper bleat that makes nearby kindling smoke; hurt: a startled bleat and a puff of sparks; faint: a small bleat that dies into embers-quiet; affection: a warm, sleepy bleat with the crackle turned soft as a hearth; evolution moment: none of its own — but at the crossing moment with Rainewe its crackle is the sound Stormewe's first thunder answers.
species.anatomyNotes: A four-legged ewe: cloven hooves, a wool-swollen body, a small head that peers out of the fleece. No manipulators; expression is in the ears, the head tilt, and how much the wool is smoking. The jaw is a grazer's jaw — side-to-side cud motion, no bite read. Locomotion is an unhurried ewe's amble and trot. Proportion-licence feature: the fleece itself — a body that is mostly wool, with head and legs as accessories. Shearing must visibly shrink the silhouette.
species.paletteSeed: ember orange, ash grey, cream wool, soot charcoal, hearth red
species.footprint: Print shape class: hoof. Each print is a clean cloven impression, two pointed halves side by side. Toe/claw count and arrangement: two hoof toes per foot, no claws, the halves slightly splayed under the fleece's weight. Gait pattern: alternating steps in a placid walking trail, four prints to a group. Print size class: medium-small. Distinctive marker: in dry grass the edges of its prints are faintly singed and smell of woodsmoke, and a little fallen ash drifts inside the trail — a hoofprint that has been warmed.
species.silhouette: Outline class: round cloud on legs. Proportions in words: fleece first, everything else second — a big soft oval of wool with a small head poking out at the front and four thin legs below. Key visual masses: the fleece dome, with smoke wisps rising off its top edge. What reads at sprite size: the round wool mass, the small dark face, and the smoke. Identifying negative space: the narrow gaps between the four legs under the fleece's low hem, and the notch between the head and the fleece where the neck disappears into wool.
species.statProfile: A cosy defensive profile — bulky through the fleece, slow, with a modest Flame presence that serves warmth before battle — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is an ewe-shaped bonfire that never quite lights: a dome of smouldering wool, small face, thin legs, permanent smoke wisps. Key features: gently smoking fleece, shearable kindling wool, ember glow at the fleece's deep places. Must-never-change list: the wool smoulders, it never erupts into open flame as its resting state; it is an elemental weather-sheep, not wool livestock; the cross with Rainewe must be noted wherever it is presented; no baked-in shadow.
species.job: winter kindling — its wool is sheared for winter kindling; the ewe is the ranch's stored warmth.

species.name: Rainewe
types: Aqua (the crossing is recorded in the source as Flame × Aqua → Volt)
species.dexText: Rainewe's wool is a permanent personal raincloud, and it rains on Rainewe without pause. Gardens it is led through flourish, and dry pastures are measured out so it can stand in them. It is one of the two parents of the Stormewe cross.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Sheep are Pokémon-occupied (Wooloo) — these are elemental weather-sheep, not wool livestock (see §5 / §5.4, B3 sheep). ⚑ Additionally: no one-word temperament is given in the source for the B3 crossing — flagged open, owner-class, not invented here.
species.lineConcept: B3, the Stormewe crossing — Rainewe, one of two ewe species designed as a Rancher crossing pair, whose wool is a permanent personal raincloud. Cross: Cinderewe × Rainewe → Stormewe.
species.sizeClass: Medium — an ordinary ewe's scale, its fleece a dark, heavy, rain-swollen cloud that drips as it walks.
species.temperament: ⚑ No one-word temperament is given in the source for this crossing — owner-class, unassigned in the source. Its colour, from the seed alone: a creature that carries its own weather with it and is rained on even at its own celebrations.
species.habitat: Ranch pastures, water meadows, and garden plots in Region 3 that benefit from a resident rain; it is kept away from Cinderewe's winter stores, for both their sakes.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes wet pasture and lush water-edge grass, and drinks a great deal, as if refilling itself. Rain falls from its wool continuously onto whatever is directly beneath it; it naps standing in its own puddle and seems to find the sound restful.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve. Crossing note: Rainewe is a designed crossing parent — Cinderewe × Rainewe → Stormewe (see the Stormewe sheet, B3). Stormewe is the cross of the two species, not an evolution of Rainewe alone.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: ranch pastures and garden plots, found by following the sound of rain on a clear day. Time/season: year-round; most valued in dry spells and at festival time, when its rain is borrowed for the grounds. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by getting rained on from a cloud no bigger than a sheep.
species.cry: Source character: a soft ewe's bleat under a constant patter of rain, with drips and small splashes keeping time. Pitch contour: mid and mild, with the patter flattening everything. Duration class: short bleats over a continuous rain bed. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *baa* … *baa*, spaced like drips from a gutter. Variations — idle: sparse bleats through steady patter; call: a louder bleat and a sudden heavier shower; hurt: a startled bleat and a scatter of drops; faint: the bleat fades and the rain thins to a drizzle; affection: a gentle bleat in warm rain, the patter turning rhythmic and calm; evolution moment: none of its own — but at the crossing moment with Cinderewe its rain hiss is the sound Stormewe's first thunder rolls over.
species.anatomyNotes: A four-legged ewe built exactly as Cinderewe is — cloven hooves, grazer's jaw, no manipulators — with the fleece as a living raincloud. Expression is in the ears, the head, and the rain's intensity, which is an acting dial: drizzle for calm, downpour for feeling. Locomotion is an ewe's amble that splashes as it goes, because it is always standing in its own puddle. Proportion-licence feature: the cloud-fleece, a body that is mostly weather.
species.paletteSeed: raincloud slate, wet wool grey-blue, puddle silver, fresh green, brand blue `#70b0d0`
species.footprint: Print shape class: hoof. Each print is a cloven impression, two pointed halves side by side, identical in shape to Cinderewe's. Toe/claw count and arrangement: two hoof toes per foot, no claws. Gait pattern: alternating steps in a walking trail. Print size class: medium-small. Distinctive marker: unmistakable — every print is a small full puddle, dark and wet even at the end of a dry day, and the trail between them is damp. A Rainewe trail can be followed by touch, eyes closed, in a drought.
species.silhouette: Outline class: round cloud on legs, darker and lower-slung than Cinderewe's. Proportions in words: a heavy horizontal oval of cloud-wool, head low at the front, legs short below, and a visible curtain of rain falling from the fleece's hem to the ground. Key visual masses: the rain-dark fleece and the puddle it stands in. What reads at sprite size: the dark wool mass, the falling rain lines, and the pale face. Identifying negative space: the bright gaps between the rain lines under the fleece, and the dry notch of air either side of its personal downpour — rain here, none there.
species.statProfile: A sustaining profile — bulky and slow like its cross-partner, with a steady Aqua presence built around endurance and field control rather than impact — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is an ewe wearing its own weather system: dark cloud-fleece, permanent falling rain, a puddle that travels with it. Key features: rain that never stops, a fleece that reads as cloud before it reads as wool, a calm wet face. Must-never-change list: the rain is personal — it falls on Rainewe, not on the whole scene; it is an elemental weather-sheep, not wool livestock; the cross with Cinderewe must be noted wherever it is presented; no baked-in shadow.
species.job: raincloud-bearer — its wool is a permanent personal raincloud; where Rainewe stands, it is raining, and the ranch plans around that.

species.name: Stormewe
types: Volt (the crossing is recorded in the source as Flame × Aqua → Volt)
species.dexText: Stormewe, the cross of Cinderewe and Rainewe, wears a thunderhead for wool. It rains on one chosen flowerbed at a time, crackles when it is pleased, and serves as the official weather of the Mochichao Festival. The festival programme does not list a forecast. It lists Stormewe.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Sheep are Pokémon-occupied (Wooloo) — these are elemental weather-sheep, not wool livestock (see §5 / §5.4, B3 sheep). ⚑ Additionally: no one-word temperament is given in the source for the B3 crossing — flagged open, owner-class, not invented here.
species.lineConcept: B3, the Stormewe crossing — Stormewe, the designed cross of Cinderewe × Rainewe, wears a thunderhead: wool that crackles, rains on one chosen flowerbed at a time, and is the festival's official weather.
species.sizeClass: Medium — an ordinary ewe's scale in the legs and body, made imposing by a towering thunderhead fleece that doubles its read height and crackles at the edges.
species.temperament: ⚑ No one-word temperament is given in the source for this crossing — owner-class, unassigned in the source. Its colour, from the seed alone: weather with a sense of occasion, choosing one flowerbed at a time to favour with its rain.
species.habitat: The festival grounds of Region 3 above all; between festivals, high pastures where its thunderhead can grumble without alarming the stock. Its year turns around the Volcano Oni's Mochichao Festival.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes festival-ground grass and flowerbed edges, carefully — its rain is aimed, never careless. The wool crackles with static, rains on one chosen flowerbed at a time, and builds to a dramatic rumble whenever a crowd gathers, which at festival time is always.
species.evolution: Does not evolve, and is not evolved into by either parent alone. Stormewe is the designed CROSS of Cinderewe × Rainewe (Flame × Aqua → Volt): the crossing is its origin, recorded here in full — Cinderewe contributes the smoulder, Rainewe contributes the rain, and Stormewe is what the two weathers make together. Combination is flavour and silhouette, per the R3 law; any breeding-system mechanics stay owner-side. Crossing note carried on both parents' sheets (Cinderewe, B3; Rainewe, B3).
species.discovery: Event — very rare outside its occasion. Method: festival, as the festival's official weather; it is met on duty, not caught at random. Time/season: the Mochichao Festival itself; between festivals it keeps to high pastures as an uncommon sight. Level band: mid. A Ranger first plausibly meets it when the festival programme calls for weather and the weather walks in on four legs.
species.cry: Source character: an ewe's bleat inside a thunderhead — deep rumble, electric crackle, and rain-patter braided together, the bleat arriving a breath after a small flash in the wool. Pitch contour: low rumble under a mid bleat, crackle spiking high at the edges. Duration class: longer than its parents' cries, built to roll. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *flash — baa — rumble*, in that order, every time. Variations — idle: a distant, contented grumble with occasional single raindrops; call: a full crack-and-bleat that makes the flowerbeds jump; hurt: a sharp thunderclap bleat, then sulking drizzle; faint: the rumble winds down like a storm leaving the valley; affection: warm rain and a low, pleased bleat with the crackle turned to fizz; evolution moment: its arrival moment is the crossing itself — first a hiss (Rainewe's rain meeting Cinderewe's smoulder), then the first small thunder, then the bleat.
species.anatomyNotes: A four-legged ewe on the same body plan as both parents — cloven hooves, grazer's jaw, no manipulators — carrying a thunderhead instead of a fleece. Acting lives in the head and ears and, above all, in the wool: flash, crackle, rain-aim, and rumble are its expression system. Its rain is targeted locomotion-adjacent acting — the body turns so the chosen flowerbed is under the cloud. Proportion-licence feature: the thunderhead fleece, taller than the ewe under it. An animator must keep the storm readable as wool, not as a special effect pasted over a sheep.
species.paletteSeed: thunderhead charcoal-violet, lightning white, rain silver, storm blue, flowerbed green (accent, where the rain lands)
species.footprint: Print shape class: hoof. Each print is a cloven impression, two pointed halves side by side, as both parents leave. Toe/claw count and arrangement: two hoof toes per foot, no claws. Gait pattern: alternating steps in a deliberate, processional walk — festival pace. Print size class: medium-small. Distinctive marker: each print is at once damp and faintly scorch-cracked, a wet hoofprint with a lightning-fern of tiny cracks in the mud around it, and only the prints — never the ground between gatherings — carry both marks together.
species.silhouette: Outline class: anvil cloud on legs. Proportions in words: a modest ewe body almost lost under a huge, flat-bottomed, billowing thunderhead mass that rises well above the back and overhangs the head. Key visual masses: the thunderhead first, the face lit from inside it second. What reads at sprite size: the dark anvil wool, an internal flash, and the thin legs. Identifying negative space: the straight-edged gap between the thunderhead's flat base and the ewe's back, and the single column of open air where its aimed rain falls beside it, not on it.
species.statProfile: The cross out-powers either parent — a dramatic special-attacking weather profile, crackling offence and festival presence, still on a slow ewe's legs — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a sheep under a personal thunderhead: anvil wool, internal lightning, aimed rain, thin legs in procession. Key features: thunderhead fleece that flashes, rain that chooses one flowerbed, the visible inheritance of both parents (smoulder at the wool's roots, rain at its hem). Must-never-change list: Stormewe is a cross, never presented as an evolution of a single parent; the wool stays wool, not a pasted-on storm effect; it is an elemental weather-sheep, not wool livestock; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Stackid
species.dexText: Stackid stands at trail turns as a living signpost, a goat in form and a cairn in fact. Travellers navigate by it, and it resents all decoration — except at festival, when it allows ribbons. A Stackid that has been moved is a contradiction the region does not contain.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Goats are Pokémon-occupied (Skiddo/Gogoat) — this body is a cairn, not a goat shape (see §5 / §5.4, B4 goat).
species.lineConcept: B4 Stackid — a goat made of stacked flat stones, cairn-bodied; it stands at trail turns as a living signpost and resents being decorated, except at festival, when it allows ribbons.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a goat's worth of stones stacked to signpost height; it reads less as an animal that stands and more as a landmark that happens to breathe.
species.temperament: stubborn (literally and otherwise) — it will not be moved, redirected, or redecorated, and the one exception it grants, festival ribbons, is granted the way a mountain grants weather.
species.habitat: Trail turns, passes, and crossroads across Region 3's ranch and festival country, on routes walkers actually need marked — the same stones, in the same places, year after year.
species.dietBehaviour: A stone body with an animal's habits: it licks mineral salts from roadside rock and browses the moss and lichen that grow between its own slabs. It stands at its post through all weather. Decoration is shaken off within the hour — except at festival, when ribbons are permitted, and worn with enormous dignity.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: trails, at the turns — it is discovered by being navigated by. Time/season: year-round at its post; ribboned, and therefore unmistakable, during the Mochichao Festival. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by rounding a bend, reading it as an ordinary cairn, and being looked at.
species.cry: Source character: a goat's bleat with stones in it — a dry, clattering call, each note edged with a small rock-on-rock tick. Pitch contour: mid, flat, and unyielding; it does not rise to meet anyone. Duration class: short, single, final. Syllable/rhythm pattern: one *baa-clack*, then silence that feels like a decision. Variations — idle: near-silence, the occasional stone settling with a soft tick; call: the full clattering bleat, which carries down a trail like a sign being pointed at you; hurt: a harsh bleat and a slab-shift that grinds; faint: it does not fall so much as settle, stones ticking into rest one by one; affection: a very small bleat and — from a creature that allows almost nothing — one top stone tipped a fraction in your direction; evolution moment: none — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: A goat's plan rebuilt as a cairn: four legs of stacked stone, a torso of flat slabs, a head-stone with a goat's face and horns of balanced rock. No manipulators; the slabs are the body, and expression is in the head-stone's tilt and the slow re-stacking of a shoulder. The jaw is stone — chewing is a grinding, side-to-side slab motion. Locomotion is rare, slow, and deliberate: it mostly does not move, and animation should treat stillness as its default performance. Proportion-licence feature: it is a stack — a species that is mostly pile.
species.paletteSeed: trail slate, lichen green, dust tan, horn grey, festival ribbon red (seasonal accent only)
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad — a flat slab print, neither hoof nor paw: each foot comes down as a single rounded-rectangle stone impression with no toe separation. Toe/claw count and arrangement: none — one solid slab-face per foot. Gait pattern: alternating steps, widely spaced and rarely repeated, because it so seldom walks. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: the prints are unnaturally even, as if set by hand, and are usually accompanied by a sift of stone dust and one or two shed pebbles — cairn leavings, in a line.
species.silhouette: Outline class: vertical stack. Proportions in words: a tall, tapering pile of flat stones on four short stone legs, the head-stone at the top barely wider than the slab below it. Key visual masses: the stacked torso is the whole read; horns and beard-stone are detail. What reads at sprite size: stacked horizontal slab lines and the goat face at the summit. Identifying negative space: the thin dark seams between slabs — the silhouette is identified by its internal gaps, a stack read by its joints.
species.statProfile: A wall — enormous defensive bulk and patience, minimal speed, an attack that is mostly gravity and refusal — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a cairn that is also a goat: flat stacked stones, slab seams as the drawing's rhythm, a goat's head and horns crowning the pile. Key features: visible slab construction, signpost stance, festival ribbons as the one permitted softness. Must-never-change list: the body is a cairn, not a goat shape wearing stones; it must never read as a lively, prancing goat; stillness is the performance; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Pipworm
species.dexText: Pipworm is a pip-small worm that lives in a fallen apple, having chosen the apple personally and to a high standard. It eats its home slowly and reviews it as it goes. When the apple is finished, it does not grieve. It moves up in the world.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
