notes: ⚠ Worms are Pokémon-adjacent — the source seed flag names Wurmple (a caterpillar): this is an earthworm-class orchard worm (see §5 / §5.4, B5 worm-class). The §5.3 trap record is also carried here honestly: earthworm is occupied in Pokémon by Orthworm, which is why no "unused animal" claim is made for this line — the seed is the orchard apple-to-cider-barrel life, not the worm alone.
species.lineConcept: B5, the orchard line — Pipworm, a pip-small worm that lives in a fallen apple; it evolves by moving house into a cider barrel, becoming Ciderpent.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — pip-small, as the source says: a worm that treats a single fallen apple as a house with room to spare.
species.temperament: gourmet — even at apple scale it is choosy, sampling a fallen apple before moving in and rejecting the merely adequate with a whole-body wrinkle of distaste.
species.habitat: The orchard floor in Region 3 ranch country — fallen apples under the trees, leaf litter, and the path between the orchard and the cellar door.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats fallen apple, and only good fallen apple: it inspects windfalls, takes up residence in the best of them, and eats its home slowly from the inside while reviewing it. A worm of standards, at the size of the standard's smallest unit.
species.evolution: Stage 1 of 2 — evolves into Ciderpent by moving house: when its apple is done, it relocates into a cider barrel, and the relocation is the evolution — a promotion and a change of address in one (pure Rancher drift, per the source). No other trigger is recorded; no level is recorded.
species.discovery: Common — met at work, at orchard scale. Method: orchard floor, by turning over fallen apples during harvest work. Time/season: harvest season above all, when windfalls are plentiful; present in the orchard litter year-round. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by picking up the best apple in the orchard and finding it occupied, and being judged for the choice.
species.cry: Source character: a minute, juicy squeak — part nibble, part pip-pip piping — small enough that a Ranger has to kneel to hear it properly. Pitch contour: high and bright, rising at a good taste. Duration class: very short, in nibbling clusters. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *pip … pip-pip*, timed to bites. Variations — idle: soft irregular pips while it eats; call: a surprisingly determined squeak, still tiny; hurt: one sharp pip and total stillness; faint: a slowing *pip … pip …* into sleep rather than collapse; affection: a rapid, happy pip-chatter from inside the apple; evolution moment: the pips get muffled, then echo — the first sound it makes from inside the barrel is this same cry with a room around it.
species.anatomyNotes: A limbless earthworm-class body: segmented, soft, no feet, no claws, no jaw in the biting sense — the mouth is a small nibbling mouth at the front segment. No manipulators; it pushes, braces, and tastes with its whole front end. Locomotion is peristaltic inching, in and out of the apple through a single neat doorway hole. Proportion-licence feature: smallness itself — the species is mostly appetite in a body the size of a seed. An animator must keep it an orchard earthworm, never a caterpillar: no legs, no leaf-munching larva read.
species.paletteSeed: apple red (its house), worm rose, pip brown, orchard green, cream flesh
species.footprint: Print shape class: none — a drag trail. Toe/claw count and arrangement: none; it has no feet to count. Gait pattern: a continuous, fine, sinuous drag line through dust, leaf litter, and apple juice, tightening into coils where it stopped to taste something. Print size class: tiny — the narrowest trail in this bucket. Distinctive marker: the trail leads, without exception, to or from a fallen apple with one neat round doorway eaten in its side, pip-sized crumbs arranged outside like a welcome mat it would deny arranging.
species.silhouette: Outline class: small curve in a round house. Proportions in words: the apple is the silhouette — a round fruit mass with a worm's arc rising out of it; the creature itself is a single bent line. Key visual masses: the apple first, the worm's raised tasting end second. What reads at sprite size: an apple with a worm, the oldest orchard joke in the world, played straight. Identifying negative space: the round doorway hole in the apple's side, and the crescent of air inside the worm's tasting arc.
species.statProfile: Tiny and specialised — very low bulk and power, surprisingly respectable resilience for something that lives in fruit, and a connoisseur's precision that will matter more after it moves house — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is an apple with its worm: a round windfall, one neat doorway, and a small segmented arc of worm raised in judgement. Key features: pip-small scale against the apple, gourmet tasting pose, the apple as home rather than food-prop. Must-never-change list: it is an earthworm-class orchard worm, never a caterpillar; the apple is its chosen house; evolution is moving house, never a growth shine; no baked-in shadow.
species.job: cellar-keeper — the line's job; in this stage it is the orchard-floor apprentice of that post, living where the cellar's work begins.

species.name: Ciderpent
species.dexText: Ciderpent is the orchard's quality inspector and chief taster, a long mellow serpent who keeps the cider cellar. No batch leaves until it has coiled around the barrel and approved it. Its judgements are slow, kind, and final.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Worms are Pokémon-adjacent — the source seed flag names Wurmple (a caterpillar): this is an earthworm-class orchard worm (see §5 / §5.4, B5 worm-class). The §5.3 trap record is also carried here honestly: earthworm is occupied in Pokémon by Orthworm, which is why no "unused animal" claim is made for this line — the seed is the orchard apple-to-cider-barrel life, not the worm alone.
species.lineConcept: B5, the orchard line — Ciderpent, what Pipworm becomes on moving house into a cider barrel: a long, mellow serpent who is the orchard's quality inspector and chief taster.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a long serpentine body that coils comfortably inside and around a cider barrel; the barrel is furniture, throne, and address at once.
species.temperament: gourmet — full-grown now into a mellow, unhurried connoisseurship: it has tasted everything the orchard makes and can be hurried about none of it.
species.habitat: The orchard cellar in Region 3 ranch country — among the cider barrels, below the orchard it used to live on top of; it rises to the orchard floor for inspections at harvest.
species.dietBehaviour: Tastes cider for a living and apple in every form for pleasure — juice, must, windfall, and the cellar's stores, sampled in drops and recorded in memory. It inspects each barrel, pronounces on it with a coil-tightening or a coil-loosening, and is the final word on whether a batch is ready.
species.evolution: Stage 2 of 2 — the evolved form of Pipworm, reached by moving house into a cider barrel: evolution as promotion and relocation, not growth alone. Single-line terminus — does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: orchard cellar, on duty among the barrels; also met, more simply, by raising a Pipworm until it moves house. Time/season: cellar work year-round, most visible at harvest and pressing time, when every batch passes it. Level band: mid. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by bringing a sample down to the cellar and waiting, properly, for the verdict.
species.cry: Source character: Pipworm's piping grown long and mellow — a low, bubbly hum with a barrel's resonance in it, punctuated by wet tasting smacks. Pitch contour: low and round, rising only for a truly excellent batch. Duration class: long, lazy phrases. Syllable/rhythm pattern: a slow *bloop … bloop … smack*, timed like drips into a vat. Variations — idle: a soft fermenting hum from inside the barrel; call: a resonant bloop that makes the barrel staves answer; hurt: a startled splash and a sharp hum; faint: the hum flattens as it drapes itself over the barrel rim like a dropped rope; affection: a warm, bubbling purr-hum and a coil offered as a seat; evolution moment: already recorded at its arrival — Pipworm's pips echoing for the first time in barrel acoustics, deepening as it settles.
species.anatomyNotes: A limbless serpent: long segmented body, no feet or manipulators, all work done with the tasting front end and the strength of the coil. The mouth is a small, precise taster's mouth — sips and smacks, never a serpent's strike or gape. Locomotion is a slow pour of a crawl on land and a coil-and-release slide among barrels. Proportion-licence feature: length — a body that is mostly coil, arranged around a barrel that anchors every pose. An animator must keep the menace at zero: this is a cellar-keeper, not a snake in the grass.
species.paletteSeed: cider amber, barrel oak, apple green, cellar shadow-brown, cream foam
species.footprint: Print shape class: none — a drag trail, at serpent scale. Toe/claw count and arrangement: none. Gait pattern: a broad, smooth S-curve belly drag across cellar dust and orchard soil, the curves wide and unhurried. Print size class: medium, and unmistakably wide beside its pre-evolution's thread of a trail. Distinctive marker: where it has inspected, the drag trail pauses in a perfect flat coil-disc beside a barrel — a round, swept-clean signature pressed into the cellar dust.
species.silhouette: Outline class: coil and barrel. Proportions in words: a barrel's round mass with a long serpent poured over and around it, head raised at tasting height, tail lost in the coils. Key visual masses: the barrel and the topmost coil; the rest is rhythm. What reads at sprite size: barrel, coil, raised tasting head. Identifying negative space: the round gaps between coil and barrel, and the cellar-dark crescent under its raised head.
species.statProfile: A mellow mid-weight profile — respectable bulk in the coil, unhurried speed, its real strength in endurance and in a taster's precision rather than raw force — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a serpent keeping a barrel: long coils, oak staves, a head raised to taste the air. Key features: barrel as home and throne, mellow coil posture, taster's small precise mouth. Must-never-change list: it stays an earthworm-class orchard creature grown long, never a menacing snake and never a caterpillar-line adult; the barrel is a moved-into home, not a prop it carries; no baked-in shadow.
species.job: cellar-keeper — the orchard's quality inspector and chief taster.

species.name: Nudigger
species.dexText: Nudigger is a naked-mole-rat worker of the burrow colonies, pink, wrinkled, and tireless. The whole colony is its job, and it has never once asked what its job is. The colony notices such workers. In time, it promotes them.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: B6, the colony line — Nudigger, a naked-mole-rat worker, pink, wrinkled, tireless; a colony's most loyal worker may be promoted into Molerarch.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a small, low worker built for tunnels its own body barely clears, dwarfed by the burrow-city it maintains.
species.temperament: devoted — it works past tiredness as a matter of course, not of praise, and would need the idea of stopping explained to it slowly.
species.habitat: The colony burrows under Region 3 ranch country — tunnel networks below pasture and garden, surfacing at spoil heaps and garden edges.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats roots, tubers, and bulbs found in the digging, and shares finds down the line without being asked. Its behaviour is the colony's behaviour in miniature: dig, haul, tend the young, repair the roof, sleep in a pile, begin again.
species.evolution: Stage 1 of 2 — a colony's most loyal worker is promoted into Molerarch: evolution as coronation, a social promotion inside the colony rather than a solitary growth milestone. The colony is the context of the trigger; no level is recorded.
species.discovery: Common — met at work. Method: colony burrows and their spoil heaps, encountered by following fresh digging at a garden's edge or by being allowed, briefly, at a tunnel mouth. Time/season: year-round, underground seasons barely applying; most visible after rain, when repairs bring the colony up. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it face-to-face in a tunnel it has stopped, politely, to let them pass in.
species.cry: Source character: small, busy squeaks and tooth-chatter — a worker's noises: contact chirps, digging grunts, and a soft chitter that means *coming through*. Pitch contour: high and quick, in short rising chirps. Duration class: very short, near-constant in company. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *chit-chit … squeak*, a work rhythm more than a call. Variations — idle: low contact chittering, so the tunnel never feels empty; call: a piping colony-alarm squeak that relays from worker to worker down the line; hurt: one sharp squeak and a scrabble of retreat; faint: a tired squeak that ends in immediate, trusting sleep against the nearest colony-mate; affection: a soft tooth-purr and pressing into the pile; evolution moment: not its own to sound alone — at a promotion, the colony's chitter rises around the one being raised (see Molerarch).
species.anatomyNotes: A naked-mole-rat body: pink, wrinkled, nearly hairless, with prominent digging teeth that close in front of the lips, small eyes that do little of the work, and short strong limbs with digging claws. The teeth and foreclaws are the manipulators and the tools. The jaw is a digger's jaw — teeth first, used like a shovel. Locomotion is a scuttling tunnel-run, forwards and backwards with equal ease. Proportion-licence feature: the teeth — a small body organised around a pair of living tools. Skin must stay kind, never grotesque: wrinkles read as softness, per the R3 no-body-horror guardrail.
species.paletteSeed: mole-rat pink, wrinkle rose, tooth cream, tunnel earth, spoil-heap tan
species.footprint: Print shape class: clawed pad. Each print is a small soft pad mark scored through by long digging-claw grooves, the front prints wider and deeper than the hind. Toe/claw count and arrangement: a row of claw tips ahead of each pad — the claws print first and deepest, the pad second. Gait pattern: alternating scramble steps, close together, in tunnels and across spoil heaps, often doubled back over themselves. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the prints travel with a fan of freshly thrown soil on one side — a Nudigger track is a track with its own digging beside it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: low wrinkled sausage. Proportions in words: a soft, low, elongated body with almost no neck, the head barely wider than the shoulders, all its emphasis at the front teeth. Key visual masses: the wrinkled torso and the pale tooth pair. What reads at sprite size: pink wrinkle lines and two big front teeth. Identifying negative space: almost none — a burrow body with no gaps to spare; the one notch is the small V between the two front teeth.
species.statProfile: A worker's profile — low individual power, high stamina, and a speed that is all scuttle; it is statted by the colony in spirit even where the sheet must speak of one — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a small pink wrinkle with teeth: low, soft, tunnel-built, fronted by living digging tools. Key features: wrinkled naked skin kept cute, prominent front teeth, busy foreclaws. Must-never-change list: naked and wrinkled never becomes body-horror; the teeth are tools, not fangs; it is a colony worker, never a solitary pet read; no baked-in shadow.
species.job: the whole colony is the job — in this stage, a worker of that colony: digging, hauling, tending, without remainder.

species.name: Molerarch
species.dexText: Molerarch is the great queen of a burrow-city, promoted from the colony's most loyal worker in an evolution that is a coronation. Her city, tunnelled beneath the ranch country, is counted a minor wonder of the region. She rarely leaves it. She rarely needs to. It comes to her.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: B6, the colony line — Molerarch, the great queen a colony's most loyal Nudigger worker is promoted into, whose burrow-city is a minor wonder of the region.
species.sizeClass: Large — a great queen, many times a worker's bulk, filling her chamber the way a heart fills a chest: the tunnels are built to her scale at the centre and to worker scale at the edges.
species.temperament: devoted — the worker's devotion promoted with her: where Nudigger is devoted to the colony, Molerarch is devoted as the colony, and the distinction is the whole reign.
species.habitat: The heart chamber of a burrow-city under Region 3 ranch country — a minor wonder of the region, per the source: vaulted, tended, and reached only through the colony that is her court.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats the colony's best — roots, tubers, and bulbs carried to her by workers — and gives back order: young are raised around her, disputes end at her chamber door, and the city's digging follows her slow shifts of position like a tide chart. She rarely surfaces. The city is her behaviour, extended.
species.evolution: Stage 2 of 2 — the promoted form of Nudigger, reached by coronation: the colony's most loyal worker is raised to queen, evolution as social promotion (the bucket's second evolution experiment, per the source). Single-line terminus — does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Rare — approaching event in character. Method: the burrow-city itself, by audience rather than encounter: a Ranger is brought to her, through tunnels, by her colony. Time/season: year-round below ground; audiences are a festival-season honour, when the colonies show their cities to the ranch country above. Level band: late. A Ranger first plausibly meets her at the end of a long polite tunnel, in a chamber that makes the word "burrow" feel inadequate.
species.cry: Source character: Nudigger's squeak grown low, slow, and resonant — a chamber voice: deep contact hums and soft tooth-purrs that the tunnels carry like plumbing carries water. Pitch contour: low and level, with a queenly fall at the end of each phrase. Duration class: long, unhurried phrases. Syllable/rhythm pattern: a slow *hmm … chit … hmm*, with the colony answering in miniature around her. Variations — idle: a low humming that workers orient to without noticing; call: a deep piping that stills the whole city to listen; hurt: a great startled squeak that brings the tunnels to her at a run; faint: she does not fall — she settles, and the colony arranges itself around her until she wakes; affection: the tooth-purr, slowed to a heartbeat, felt through the chamber floor; evolution moment: her coronation cry is the first time the worker's chitter comes back to her from every tunnel at once, amplified — the colony sounding like one creature, because it is.
species.anatomyNotes: The mole-rat plan at queen scale: a vast pink wrinkled body, the same digging teeth — now ceremonial as much as useful — short limbs that move her rarely and with assistance of posture rather than travel. No manipulators beyond teeth and foreclaws, now mostly employed in gesture. The jaw keeps the digger's tooth-first close. Locomotion is processional: slow, chamber-to-chamber, with the court in attendance. Proportion-licence feature: scale itself — a worker's body plan promoted until it becomes architecture. Wrinkles stay soft; size never becomes horror.
species.paletteSeed: queen rose, deep wrinkle mauve, tooth ivory, chamber earth-dark, festival gold (audience accent)
species.footprint: Print shape class: clawed pad, at queen scale. Each print is a broad soft pad with deep, widely spaced claw grooves ahead of it. Toe/claw count and arrangement: a row of claw tips before each pad, as a worker leaves, but the grooves are dug with ceremonial slowness — fewer, deeper, straighter. Gait pattern: alternating, widely spaced, processional; almost always overprinted by dozens of tiny worker trails attending it. Print size class: large for this line. Distinctive marker: the trail is a court in cross-section — one great track down the middle of the tunnel floor, worker tracks woven around it like a border.
species.silhouette: Outline class: great soft mound. Proportions in words: a huge low dome of wrinkled body with the head as a gentle continuation, teeth pale at the front, limbs almost absorbed into the mass. Key visual masses: the torso-dome is everything; attendants at its edges give it scale. What reads at sprite size: pink dome, front teeth, and a retinue of tiny workers at the hem. Identifying negative space: the arched gap of her chamber doorway framing her — negative space supplied by architecture, because the body supplies none.
species.statProfile: A sovereign's profile — very high bulk and presence, minimal travel speed, power expressed as the colony's weight behind her rather than a queen's own strike — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a queen as a landscape: a great pink wrinkled dome in a vaulted chamber, crowned with nothing but her own teeth and court. Key features: worker body plan at architectural scale, coronation-by-promotion read, burrow-city as her extended silhouette. Must-never-change list: she is a promoted worker, never a separate species dropped in; majesty never becomes menace or body-horror; the colony is part of her presentation; no baked-in shadow.
species.job: the whole colony is the job — in this stage, she is the colony: its queen, its centre, and the reason the burrow-city holds.

species.name: Spindevil
species.dexText: Spindevil expresses every emotion by spinning — joy, rage, greetings, grief — and ranch hands read the spin-rate like a gauge. Its dawn spin wakes the household. It has never overslept, and neither, consequently, has anyone else.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: B7 Spindevil — a Tasmanian devil that expresses every emotion by spinning: joy, rage, greetings, grief. Ranch hands read the spin-rate like a gauge.
species.sizeClass: Small — a compact, muscular devil at sturdy small-dog scale, low and dense, built like something wound up.
species.temperament: all of them, rotationally — the source's own wording, kept verbatim: every temperament it has arrives as a spin, and the rate is the readout.
species.habitat: Ranch yards and den edges across Region 3, wherever a household needs waking; wild kin keep to scrubby den country at the ranch lands' margins.
species.dietBehaviour: An eager omnivore of ranch scraps, eggs, fallen fruit, and whatever the yard provides. Its entire emotional life is rotational: it spins for joy, rage, greetings, and grief, and the household sets its morning by the dawn spin, which has never once been late.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve. The source is deliberate: some creatures are finished as they are.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: ranch yards at dawn, found by ear: the dawn spin is audible before the creature is visible. Time/season: year-round, at dawn daily; festival mornings it spins for the whole grounds. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by being woken by it, at full greeting velocity, on their first morning at the ranch.
species.cry: Source character: a devil's yowling chatter pitched up by rotation — as it spins, the cry dopplers into a rising whir-cackle, part voice, part top. Pitch contour: climbs with spin-rate, drops flat when it stops. Duration class: as long as the spin; it cannot cry still. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *ya-ya-ya-ya* accelerating into a blur, then a hard stop. Variations — idle: a slow contented turn with a low muttering chatter; call: the dawn spin — maximum rate, full yowl, a living alarm bell; hurt: a yelp, a wobble, a furious half-spin to object; faint: the spin winds down in a spiral and it keels over still turning faintly, like a top; affection: a delighted fast spin around the feet of the greeted, cackling; evolution moment: none — single-stage, deliberately.
species.anatomyNotes: A four-legged devil: stocky body, big head, strong jaws, short legs, a tail that serves as a counterweight and a spin-stabiliser. No manipulators; the mouth is expressive and loud but the body's spin is the real performance channel. The jaw can gape wide — a devil's yawn-gape — used for calls, not menace. Locomotion is a scurrying run that tips into rotation without warning; animators should treat spin-rate as an emotion dial with readable stops — greeting spin, rage spin, grief spin (slow, low, wobbling). Proportion-licence feature: none oversized in the body — the licence is spent on motion instead: the creature is mostly spin.
species.paletteSeed: devil black-brown, cream chest blaze, pink ear, scrub tan, dawn gold (accent)
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad. Each print is a compact paw impression, toes ahead of the pad in a tight fan. Toe/claw count and arrangement: a row of small toe marks with short claw ticks before the pad, front prints slightly larger than hind. Gait pattern: bounding pairs on the run — then, characteristically, no gait at all: the trail breaks into a churned circular rosette where it spun, prints smeared into a ring. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the rosette — a perfect circle of scuffed earth interrupting an ordinary bounding trail, its tightness and depth telling whoever reads it exactly what Spindevil was feeling, and how much.
species.silhouette: Outline class: compact wedge, usually blurred. Proportions in words: a low dense body, big head carried forward, short legs, tail out behind as ballast — most often seen as a spinning oval with a head-tail axis. Key visual masses: the head and shoulders; the rest is momentum. What reads at sprite size: dark compact body, cream blaze, and rotation blur on the outline. Identifying negative space: the crescent gaps at either end of the spin-blur where head and tail break the circle — the silhouette has a spin direction, readable even frozen.
species.statProfile: A wound-up profile — surprising speed in bursts, a strong jaw's worth of attack, indifferent defence; everything about it is rate — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a compact devil caught mid-expression: low, dense, big-headed, its outline always implying rotation. Key features: readable spin-rates as emotion, dawn-spin alarm behaviour, cream blaze on a dark body. Must-never-change list: single-stage, deliberately — no evolution tease in the design; the spin is expression, not an attack gimmick first; it stays a devil animal, never a cartoon tornado with a face; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Faintail
species.dexText: Faintail faints theatrically at surprises, arguments, loud praise, and its own reflection. Between faints, it serves as the ranch's softest napping pillow. All baby creatures are parked on it. It considers this a career, and faints, proudly, at the compliment.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: B8 Faintail — an opossum that faints theatrically at surprises, arguments, loud praise, and its own reflection; between faints it is the ranch's softest napping pillow, and all baby creatures are parked on it.
species.sizeClass: Small — an opossum's scale, all of it soft: a body that reads as a cushion with a face, sized exactly for a baby creature to be parked on.
species.temperament: dramatic — every feeling is performed at full volume on the way to the floor, and the floor is reached often, gracefully, and with witnesses preferred.
species.habitat: Ranch houses, barns, and shaded porches across Region 3 — wherever naps happen and babies are minded; wild kin keep to hollow logs and quiet thickets nearby.
species.dietBehaviour: An easy omnivore of fruit, eggs, insects, and offered snacks, taken slowly and preferably lying down. It faints theatrically at surprises, arguments, loud praise, and its own reflection; between faints it is the ranch's softest napping pillow, and all baby creatures are parked on it as a matter of ranch routine.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Common — met at work. Method: the ranch house and barn, encountered mid-nap or mid-faint; being parked with the babies is a common first meeting. Time/season: year-round; during the festival it is stationed, honoured, in the nursery tent. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by sitting down on it, apologising, and being fainted at for the surprise.
species.cry: Source character: a soft opossum repertoire split in two — small hisses and chitters awake, and one signature sound before a faint: a rising, swooning sigh that is half cry, half curtain line. Pitch contour: awake, low and mumbling; pre-faint, a theatrical climb and fall. Duration class: short cries, one long swoon. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *chit … chit … ohhh* — two beats of warning, then the descent. Variations — idle: a drowsy chitter that keeps slipping toward snoring; call: a surprisingly carrying hiss-sigh, used to summon someone to witness what happens next; hurt: a genuine small squeak, then — reflexively — a faint; faint: the full swoon-cry, timed to the fall, ending in a tiny snore; affection: a happy clicking chitter from underneath a pile of sleeping babies, going nowhere; evolution moment: none — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: A four-legged opossum: soft round body, pointed face, bare grasping tail, small paws with an opposable touch on the hind feet. The tail is the one true manipulator — it curls, points, and applauds. The mouth is small; expression is carried by the eyes, the ears, and the whole body's commitment to falling over. Locomotion is an unhurried waddle; the signature motion is the faint itself — a staged collapse with a tail-curl finish, which an animator must be able to vary: surprise faint, offended faint, praise faint, reflection faint. Proportion-licence feature: softness — a body that is mostly pillow.
species.paletteSeed: opossum grey, pillow cream, pink nose and tail, sleepy mauve, nursery pastel (accent)
species.footprint: Print shape class: pad. Each print is a small soft pad impression with splayed toe marks, the hind print showing its spread, thumb-like inner toe angled wide. Toe/claw count and arrangement: toes fanned around the pad rather than in a claw row, hind inner toe set apart like a thumbprint. Gait pattern: alternating amble steps with a long, wavy tail-drag line weaving between them. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the trail regularly ends in a full stop of a different kind — a soft body-length impression in the dust where it fainted, tail curled in a spiral at one end, prints resuming afterwards as if nothing had happened.
species.silhouette: Outline class: horizontal cushion. Proportions in words: a low, wide, soft body with a small pointed head at one end and a long bare tail curling out of the other; legs barely trouble the outline. Key visual masses: the pillowed torso, then the tail's curl. What reads at sprite size: grey mound, pink nose, spiral tail — and, half the time, a baby creature asleep on top. Identifying negative space: the open spiral inside the tail's curl, the single most recognisable gap in the bucket.
species.statProfile: A pillow's profile — negligible offence, comfort-class bulk that absorbs babies and arguments alike, and a defensive strategy (the faint) that is a personality trait wearing a stat's clothes — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a cushion with a face and a curl: soft grey mound, pointed snout, bare pink tail in a spiral. Key features: theatrical faint as the signature animation, pillow body that other creatures are visibly parked on, tail as the expressive limb. Must-never-change list: the faints are theatre, never genuine distress played for pity; it is an opossum, soft first, not a rat read; baby creatures on its back are part of its presented life; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Platemoll
species.dexText: Platemoll, a chiton of eight perfect plates, curls into a flawless wheel. It volunteers as the mill's rolling pin on weekdays and a cart wheel on market days. It uncurls only for lunch, and lunch has never been negotiated.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: B9 Platemoll — a chiton with eight perfect plates that curls into a flawless wheel; it volunteers as the mill's rolling pin on weekdays and a cart wheel on market days, and uncurls only for lunch.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a chiton grown to working scale: flat and oval uncurled, and exactly wheel-sized curled, which is the size its whole life is organised around.
species.temperament: obliging — it volunteers. Weekdays at the mill, market days under a cart, and the only boundary it has ever drawn is lunch, which it uncurls for, promptly.
species.habitat: Rocky shores and millpond edges in Region 3 where the wild kind live, and — for the ranch population — the mill and the market road, where it is infrastructure with a lunch break.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats algae, scraped from shore rocks and millstones alike with a grazer's patience. Its behaviour is a rota: rolling pin at the mill on weekdays, cart wheel on market days, uncurled only for lunch — a schedule it keeps without being asked and would presumably keep without being thanked.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: the mill on weekdays and the market road on market days; wild, on the rocky shore at the water's edge. Time/season: the working week is its season; at festival it is booked, heavily, by every stallholder with a cart. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by riding on a cart it is being the wheel of, and being set down, gently, at lunch.
species.cry: Source character: a low stony grinding hum with a wet edge — part millstone, part shore — and a small clicking from the plates as they settle. Pitch contour: low and level, rising a fraction under load. Duration class: long hums while rolling; it is quietest uncurled. Syllable/rhythm pattern: a continuous *grrr-click … grrr-click*, one click per plate-shift. Variations — idle: a slow grazing scrape-hum against rock; call: a resonant grinding ring, bell-like, that carries down the market road; hurt: a sharp plate-clack and instant tight curling; faint: the hum winds down and the wheel rolls, slower and slower, to a stop on its side; affection: a soft, contented click-sequence, plates settling like a cat's purr in stone; evolution moment: none — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: A chiton: a low oval body armoured in eight perfect overlapping plates (the source's count, kept), a broad muscular foot underneath, no head to speak of, no limbs, no manipulators. The mouth is a grazing scraper under the front edge. Locomotion is the whole act: a slow foot-crawl uncurled, and a flawless roll curled — an animator gets two movement systems, crawl and wheel, and the curl transition between them is the signature shot. Proportion-licence feature: the source says it plainly — it is basically a wheel that eats algae, and the design should spend everything on that.
species.paletteSeed: plate chrome, shore stone, algae green, sea silver, mill flour-white (dusted accent)
species.footprint: Print shape class: none — a wheel-rut. Toe/claw count and arrangement: none; in its place the curled body leaves one continuous rut. Gait pattern: a single unbroken rolling line, the rut patterned with eight repeating plate segments in a regular rhythm — plate, plate, plate — the count written into the road. Uncurled, it leaves only a wide, smooth foot-scrape with algae-green smears. Print size class: medium, and the widest single-line track in this bucket. Distinctive marker: the segmented rut itself — a track that is also a timetable: mill-ward on weekday ruts, market-ward on market days, and a flour-dusted pause where it uncurled for lunch.
species.silhouette: Outline class: wheel, or low oval — two silhouettes, both perfect. Proportions in words: curled, a flawless circle with eight plate arcs; uncurled, a flat armoured oval with no head, no tail, and no apology. Key visual masses: the plate shell is the entire mass, in both forms. What reads at sprite size: the segmented circle — nothing else in the bestiary is a true wheel. Identifying negative space: the small round hub-gap at the centre of the curled form, and the thin bright seam-lines between plates.
species.statProfile: An infrastructure profile — high defensive hardness in the plates, strong and steady under load, very slow to start and nearly unstoppable politely once rolling — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a perfect segmented wheel that is also, uncurled, a perfect chiton oval. Key features: eight plates, flawless curl, the mill/market rota as its presented life. Must-never-change list: eight plates, no more, no fewer — the source's count; the wheel is a curl of its own body, never a carried or built wheel; obliging never becomes servile — it volunteers, and it uncurls for lunch; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Shagdox
species.dexText: Shagdox is a musk ox so shaggy that only its nose and the tips of its horns exit the wool. Birds nest in it without asking. At shearing time it donates a haystack, and is thanked, and unbotheredly grows another.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Buffalo are Pokémon-occupied (Bouffalant) — the musk ox is a distinct animal and the seed is the shag, not the charge (see §5 / §5.4, B10 musk ox vs. buffalo).
species.lineConcept: B10 Shagdox — a musk ox so shaggy that only its nose and the tips of its horns exit the wool; birds nest in it without asking; at shearing time it donates a haystack.
species.sizeClass: Large — a musk ox's full scale, then the shag on top of it: the creature is a landmark of wool with an animal implied inside.
species.temperament: unbothered — birds nest in it without asking, seasons arrive and leave, shearing happens; the nose registers all of this and declines to make a fuss about any of it.
species.habitat: Cold upland pasture at Region 3's chilly edges, and the ranch's winter fields; it comes down for the festival season as walking shelter and is used, respectfully, as a landmark.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes coarse upland grass and winter forage, excavated from under snow with slow sweeps of the head. The shag is the behaviour: birds nest in it without asking, small creatures shelter on its lee side, and at shearing time it donates a haystack's worth of wool and stands, briefly visible, looking like a rumour of an ox, before growing the landmark back.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work, in the sense that standing there being a haystack is the work. Method: cold upland pasture and winter fields, found by heading for the haystack that is breathing. Time/season: winter above all; at shearing time it is the centre of a small festival of its own inside the festival season. Level band: mid. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by sheltering from wind beside it for some minutes before noticing the nose.
species.cry: Source character: a deep, muffled bellow heard through a haystack — all bass, no edges, arriving with a snort of frost. Pitch contour: low, slow, and falling; the wool eats the high end. Duration class: long, rare, and worth waiting for. Syllable/rhythm pattern: a single *mmrrrooo* with a snort in the middle, like punctuation. Variations — idle: mostly silence and breathing; an occasional contented snort that sets the nesting birds up and settles them again; call: the full muffled bellow, felt in the ground through the wool; hurt: a sharper snort and one stamp — the most alarm it has ever shown; faint: it does not so much fall as subside, the shag settling over it like snow over a hill, snoring faintly; affection: a long warm snort and the whole haystack leaning, very slightly, toward you; evolution moment: none — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: A musk ox almost entirely withdrawn into its own coat: four sturdy legs under the curtain, a head that never fully emerges — nose and horn-tips only, per the source — and no manipulators. The mouth is behind the wool and is heard rather than seen; chewing is a slow movement in the shag. Locomotion is a deliberate, heavy walk, the coat swinging like a bell. Proportion-licence feature: the shag itself — a species that is mostly coat, with the animal as a rumour inside it. An animator's entire performance vocabulary is nose-wrinkle, horn-tip angle, coat sway, and lean.
species.paletteSeed: shag umber, winter straw, horn bone, nose black, frost white (rim accent)
species.footprint: Print shape class: hoof. Each print is a broad cloven impression, two blunt halves, pressed deep. Toe/claw count and arrangement: two hoof toes per foot, no claws. Gait pattern: alternating heavy steps, close and even, the trail of a creature going somewhere slowly and arriving. Print size class: large — the deepest prints in this bucket. Distinctive marker: the hoofprints arrive inside a wide corridor of dragged fringe-lines where the coat swept the ground, scattered with shed wool and, in nesting season, the occasional feather — a haystack's trail, signed in its own material.
species.silhouette: Outline class: haystack dome. Proportions in words: a huge rounded mound of hanging shag from back to ground, legs as short pillars below, the head not a separate shape at all — just a nose and two horn-tips exiting the front of the wool. Key visual masses: the coat is the creature, visually; everything else is exit points. What reads at sprite size: dome, nose, horn-tips, and birds. Identifying negative space: almost none inside the mound — the identifying gaps are the two small notches where the horn-tips part the wool, and the dark triangle under the chest where the legs disappear into shadow and shag.
species.statProfile: A fortress profile — exceptional bulk and cold-weather endurance, very slow, an attack that is mostly mass arriving — offered without urgency — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a walking haystack: a dome of shag to the ground, a nose, two horn-tips, and tenants. Key features: wool as architecture and ecosystem, shearing that donates a haystack, the animal implied rather than displayed. Must-never-change list: only nose and horn-tips exit the wool in the resting design — never draw the full ox face as the default read; the seed is the shag, not the charge; birds nesting uninvited are part of the presentation; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Dustbunny
species.dexText: Dustbunny is not a rabbit. It is a colony of dust that has taken a rabbit's shape, the way dust takes a corner's shape. It cleans the ranch house by absorbing dust into itself, is always slightly hungry, and hides under furniture when thanked.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Rabbits are heavily Pokémon-occupied — this is not a rabbit animal at all, only a rabbit-shaped absence of one (see §5 / §5.4, B11 rabbit shape only, not a rabbit animal). --- *End of Bucket B — Region 3: 11 concepts, 15 stage sheets (B1 Plowpus; B2 Sentripea; B3 Cinderewe, Rainewe, Stormewe; B4 Stackid; B5 Pipworm, Ciderpent; B6 Nudigger, Molerarch; B7 Spindevil; B8 Faintail; B9 Platemoll; B10 Shagdox; B11 Dustbunny).*
species.lineConcept: B11 Dustbunny — not a rabbit: a colony of dust that has taken a rabbit's shape the way dust takes a corner's shape. It cleans the ranch house by absorbing dust into itself (it is always slightly hungry), hides under furniture when thanked, and sneezes in tiny grey puffs.
species.sizeClass: Small — rabbit-shaped and rabbit-sized, and no denser than the comparison allows: a shape dust is keeping, at the scale dust keeps it.
species.temperament: shy — it works when the house is quiet, absorbs thanks even worse than it absorbs praise, and hides under furniture when thanked, which is often, because it is good at its job.
species.habitat: The ranch house, indoors above all — corners, under furniture, along the skirting of quiet rooms across Region 3; a Dustbunny address is any room that has been left peacefully alone.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats dust — absorbs it into itself, cleans the ranch house by doing so, and is always slightly hungry, because a house makes dust faster than one bunny-shaped colony can want it. It sneezes in tiny grey puffs, works the corners first, and treats gratitude as a loud weather event to be waited out under the sofa.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve.
species.discovery: Uncommon — met at work. Method: the ranch house, indoors: follow the clean corners in a dusty house, or thank a room and watch under the furniture. Time/season: year-round, busiest in the festival season when the ranch house is cleaned for guests — and hardest to find then, for the same reason. Level band: early. A Ranger first plausibly meets it by sneezing, and being answered, from under a chair, in kind.
species.cry: Source character: barely a cry at all — a dry, whispery husk of sound: tiny sneezes, a soft *fff* of moving dust, and a small squeak that seems to come from the shape rather than a throat. Pitch contour: high, thin, and falling away, as if apologising for the note. Duration class: the shortest in this bucket; its sounds end before they are noticed. Syllable/rhythm pattern: *fff … tss* — a drift and a sneeze. Variations — idle: a near-silent dust-hush as it works, with an occasional tiny sneeze; call: it does not call — the closest thing is a slightly louder sneeze that other Dustbunny shapes, in other corners, answer before hiding; hurt: one sharp grey puff-sneeze and a partial loss of outline; faint: it does not fall — it settles, the rabbit shape relaxing into an ordinary dust pile that is, later, a rabbit again; affection: a soft rapid series of tiny sneezes and the shape pressing, weightlessly, against a skirting board near you; evolution moment: none — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: No true anatomy, and the sheet must say so plainly: a colony of dust holding a rabbit's shape — long ears, round body, hind-leg spring in the outline — with no skeleton, no true mouth, and no manipulators beyond the whole shape pressing and absorbing. Where a mouth would be, dust simply parts and takes things in. Locomotion is a rabbit's hop performed by dust: the shape leaves the floor as a shape and lands as one, shedding a little of itself at each landing. Proportion-licence feature: the ears — rabbit ears made of the least substantial material in the region. Mixture here is the Rancher object-hybrid spirit, never body-horror: the effect is a soot-soft toy, not a swarm.
species.paletteSeed: dust grey, corner shadow, skirting cream, sneeze silver, Umbral violet (deep accent)
species.footprint: Print shape class: none — a true print is exactly what it does not leave. Toe/claw count and arrangement: none to count. Gait pattern: in place of prints, a hopping trail of faint grey pad-shaped smudges in clean-floor dust — front smudges paired, hind smudges long — each one fading as it is watched, because the trail is made of the creature and the creature keeps moving. Print size class: small, when it can be said to have a size at all. Distinctive marker: the track runs backwards to logic — the floor inside the trail is cleaner than the floor outside it, and the trail ends, without exception, under furniture, in a small arrangement of tiny grey sneeze-puffs.
species.silhouette: Outline class: rabbit, remembered by dust. Proportions in words: a round soft body, long upright ears, a hindquarter curve built for a hop — all of it with edges that will not hold still, fraying gently into the room's air. Key visual masses: the ears and the round hindquarters; the middle is negotiable. What reads at sprite size: rabbit ears and a grey softness that no other species in the bucket shares. Identifying negative space: the gap between the ears is the clearest space in the design — and the faint bite of missing outline at the body's lower edge, where it is always slightly coming undone into the floor it cleaned.
species.statProfile: A cleaner's profile — very low bulk and direct power, high elusiveness, its strength in persistence and in being, functionally, already everywhere in the room — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a rabbit shape kept by dust: long ears, round body, edges fraying into grey softness. Key features: absorption cleaning as its presented life, sneeze-puffs, the under-furniture refuge, a body with no true anatomy to draw. Must-never-change list: it is NOT a rabbit animal — only a rabbit-shaped absence of one, and never drawn as a flesh rabbit in grey; the dust colony is a gentle object-hybrid, never a horror swarm; it hides when thanked — gratitude is its weather; no baked-in shadow.

species.name: Marblit
species.dexText: Marblit is most often found as a smooth, feather-carved ball sitting perfectly still among Rift stones. If a trusted voice calls or a sudden noise startles it, the ball pops open with a clear, ringing pop — wings first — and a small griffin chick tumbles out, blinking. It folds itself away again just as neatly to sleep, roll downhill, or hide from anything larger than itself.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Name proximity noted in §5.5 of the source: Marblit was a closest surviving call (vs. Litwick — different word, different creature, kept).
species.lineConcept: C1-1 Marblit → Popriffin — a chick that sleeps, travels, and hides as a perfect carved ball, springing open into a griffin when startled or called; donor mechanic: the pop-open battle toy, translated into a ball resting form and a spring-open anatomy event.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — about the size of a curled-up hedgehog or a large grapefruit held in two hands, easily cupped and carried.
species.temperament: Shy, startle-prone, and deeply comforted by routine; bold for a heartbeat after popping open, then quick to fold away again.
species.habitat: Rift scrub, stony crossings, and the quieter edges of the institute grounds in Region 4, where round stones give its ball form good company.
species.dietBehaviour: Pecks seeds, soft berries, and small insects in its open form; spends much of the day balled, rolling short distances rather than walking them, and naps in shallow stone hollows it has worn smooth.
species.evolution: The pop-open is a form change, not an evolution — seams along the feather-shell part, the wings unfold first, then head, talons, and tail spring free, and the whole body can refold along the same seams. It evolves into Popriffin after a life of startles survived and flights attempted, when its wings are strong enough to carry the ball form rather than merely burst out of it; the ball form itself is never outgrown.
species.discovery: Region 4 Rift crossings and stony institute outskirts; rarity class uncommon, because most are passed over as stones. Method: wild encounter — listen for a soft pop at dawn, or call gently near suspiciously perfect round stones. Conditions: calmest and most likely to open in morning light; stays balled through storms. Level band in words: low band. First-meeting note: first meetings almost always begin with the pop — Rangers are advised not to flinch, as flinching sends it straight back into the ball.
species.cry: Source character — a small hollow pop followed by a bright chick chirp, the pop made by the feather-shell seams, the chirp from a small hooked beak. Pitch contour in words: a flat percussive pop, then a chirp that rises quickly and settles. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: single pop-chirp, sometimes doubled when excited. Variations per state — idle: soft muffled chirps from inside the closed ball; call: pop first, then a loud repeated chirp to answer a trusted voice; hurt: a sharp squeak and an instant refold click; faint: a dwindling chirp as the ball settles loosely; affection: quiet peeping with the head tucked out of a half-open ball; evolution / form-change moment: the pop itself is the signature sound, louder and rounder at evolution into a full ringing crack of feathers.
species.anatomyNotes: Four limbs in open form — two winged fore-limbs with feathered wings that emerge first, and two hind talon legs for hopping and perching; no hands, manipulation is by beak and talon grip. Mouth is a small hooked griffin beak that opens wide for chirps. Locomotion is triple-mode: rolling in ball form, hopping and scrambling open, and short fluttering bursts — it cannot yet sustain flight. Mode-change anatomy is the whole brief: the feather-shell is continuous body surface with visible seam lines, the wings fold outermost, and the pop must read as a flower opening, fast and organic, never as panels on a hinge.
species.paletteSeed: warm cream, dusty gold, soft sky blue, stone grey
species.footprint: Two traces, form-dependent. Ball-form travel leaves a rolling track: a single continuous smooth groove, narrow and shallow, with faint feather-seam ridges pressed at regular turns and no footfalls at all. Open form leaves tiny griffin prints — three narrow forward talon toes and one short back toe, in a hopping pattern of paired prints with frequent gaps where it fluttered. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: a rolling groove that abruptly becomes hopping talon prints where it popped open.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — resting/ball: a perfect circle, unbroken except for a faint seam arc; open: a round chick body dominated by two oversized unfolding wings, small hooked head at the top, short tail fan at the back. Proportions in words: head large for the body, wings larger still when spread, legs short. Key visual masses: the ball itself, then the wings. What reads at sprite size: circle, seam line, wing burst. Identifying negative space: the clean crescent gaps between each spread wing and the round body.
species.statProfile: Modest all-round with surprising burst speed on the pop and in short flights; fragile when caught open, hard to hurt when balled; low staying power. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a perfect ball that becomes a griffin chick, wings first. Key features are the carved-feather seam lines on the ball, the hooked beak, and wings visibly too grand for the chick. Must-never-change list: the ball is the creature's own feathered body, never a shell it carries or a toy it lives in; the pop is anatomy, never mechanism; the griffin read — beak, wings, talons — stays at both stages.

species.name: Popriffin
species.dexText: Popriffin keeps Marblit's trick for life: however grand its wings and talons become, it still folds into a seamless ball to sleep, and the oldest individuals are so perfectly round that Rift travellers mistake them for carved monuments. Its pop is famous across the region — a deep, resonant crack of feathers that locals use as a doorbell, a greeting, and a warning. In flight it is a true griffin, eagle-fronted and lion-bodied, proud of every feather.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-1 Marblit → Popriffin — the adult griffin that still folds back to a perfect ball to sleep, old ones becoming perfectly round; donor mechanic: the pop-open battle toy, translated into a lifelong ball resting form retained at full size.
species.sizeClass: Medium — about the size of a large dog or a small pony when open, and a strikingly large, smooth ball when folded.
species.temperament: Proud, territorial over favourite perches and sleeping hollows, and theatrical — it enjoys the pop, and times it for an audience when it can.
species.habitat: High Rift crags, crossing towers, and old institute rooftops and gateposts in Region 4, anywhere a ball can sit in plain sight and a griffin can launch.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts small Rift gamebirds and mountain rodents, scavenges generously, and carries food back to its perch in its talons; sleeps balled through the hottest and coldest hours, and answers other Popriffin's pops across valleys in rolling conversation.
species.evolution: Final stage; no further evolution. The form change is unchanged in kind from Marblit and grander in scale — the ball's seams part, wings burst out first with the full pop, then the eagle head, fore-talons, lion hindquarters, and tail unfold in sequence. Elders fold more slowly and open more deliberately, and their roundness in ball form is a mark of age and honour in the species.
species.discovery: Region 4 high Rift crossings, crag paths, and institute rooftops; rarity class rare — more often heard (the pop, carrying far) than seen open. Method: wild encounter at perch sites; approach a resting ball openly and call, never sneak, as a startled pop at this size is a physical event. Conditions: opens most readily at dawn and at familiar voices. Level band in words: mid-to-upper band for wild Rift adults. First-meeting note: the first pop is routinely described as a door slamming and a banner unfurling at once — stand clear of the wing arc.
species.cry: Source character — a deep seam-pop from the feather-shell under a powerful eagle-griffin screech. Pitch contour in words: percussive pop low, then a screech that climbs, holds, and cuts off clean. Duration class: short but carrying. Rhythm pattern: pop-screech as a single unit; greeting exchanges are answering pairs across distance. Variations per state — idle: low feathered huffs and occasional soft pops from shifting in its sleep; call: full pop and screech together, unmistakable; hurt: a harsh bark-screech and a defensive half-open wing flare; faint: a weakening screech as it folds, ending in a dull final pop; affection: a surprisingly gentle churring screech with the ball rocking slightly; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution remains, but every pop-open carries the same signature crack, deepest in old, round individuals.
species.anatomyNotes: Four limbs — eagle forelegs ending in true talons that are its main manipulators, lion hindlegs for launching and landing, and very large feathered wings rooted at the shoulders that always deploy first in the pop. Mouth is a strong hooked beak; jaw opens on a clear hinge for screech and prey-carrying, never for speech. Locomotion: rolling in ball form (slow, deliberate, downhill-assisted), powerful sustained flight open, and a bounding quadruped run. Mode-change anatomy: seam lines run visibly through the adult feathering and flank fur; the fold order — tail, hindquarters, head, talons, wings last — and the reverse on opening must stay consistent for animators.
species.paletteSeed: rich gold, warm cream, deep bronze, sky blue, stone grey
species.footprint: Two traces, form-dependent. Ball-form travel leaves a rolling track: one broad, deep, continuous groove, wide as the folded body, pressed smooth with faint seam ridges, often running in long straight downhill lines. Open form leaves a mixed griffin print — large three-toed talon marks in front and broad padded lion-paw prints behind, in a bounding gait that breaks into long printless stretches where it took wing. Print size class: large for its size class. Distinctive marker: a monument-smooth groove that ends in an explosion of talon and paw prints at the pop-open point.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — resting/ball: a perfect, monumental circle; open: a classic griffin — eagle head and wings over a lion body, tail curving out behind. Proportions in words: wings the dominant mass, head held high, hindquarters heavy and grounded. Key visual masses: wing pair, feathered chest, ball form's pure roundness. What reads at sprite size: circle versus winged griffin, nothing between. Identifying negative space: the tall arch between the raised wings and the back when it flares.
species.statProfile: Strong and fast in the air with a powerful opening burst; well-defended balled, exposed in the half-second of opening; proud stamina over long flights. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A true griffin that happens to fold into a perfect ball, at both ends of its life. Key features are the resonant pop, the seam-lined feathering and fur that allow the fold, and the elder's perfect roundness. Must-never-change list: the ball never goes away and is never a separate object; wings always emerge first; no harness, saddle, or artefact read — this is folklore griffin anatomy, start to finish.

species.name: Whirligig
species.dexText: Whirligig's body is a dense, polished top of a beetle, and its way of settling anything is to spin. At rest it waddles on short legs, mild and a little dizzy-looking; wound up by its own effort, it spins faster and faster until the shell blurs — and through the blur, small and bright, the creature's true face shows, calm at the centre of the storm. Duels between Whirligig are contests of endurance, balance, and nerve, and can outlast their audience.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-2 Whirligig → Cyclossus — a top-bodied beetle that battles by spinning, its small bright creature-core showing its face at full spin; donor mechanic: the spirit-core housed in a spinning toy body, translated into a dense spinning beetle body with a living core-face.
species.sizeClass: Small — about the size of a household spinning top crossed with a plump beetle, easily held in one hand when still.
species.temperament: Patient, stubborn, and serenely competitive; rarely starts a quarrel, almost never concedes one.
species.habitat: Hard flat ground across the Region 4 Rift — crossing plazas, dried lakebeds, institute courtyards — anywhere smooth enough for a long spin.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes algae, lichen, and fallen fruit, storing energy in its dense body for long spins; spends still hours sunning its shell to a polish, and settles disputes with neighbours by formal spin-duel rather than by biting or fleeing.
species.evolution: No second form; the spin is a state, not a form — legs tuck, the body drops onto its spinning point, and the shell blurs as speed builds until the core-face shows. It evolves into Cyclossus when a lifetime of duels has grown the body massively around the core, the face at the centre remaining exactly itself.
species.discovery: Region 4 institute courtyards, Rift crossing plazas, and dried flats; rarity class common in the right places, where the ground is scored with old duel circles. Method: wild encounter — follow the humming of a duel in progress, or set down a smooth stone and wait. Conditions: most active and most willing to spin in dry, still weather. Level band in words: low band. First-meeting note: a first meeting is usually mid-spin; wait for it to wobble to a stop rather than reaching in, as a grabbed Whirligig spins harder on principle.
species.cry: Source character — a small bright chirring voice from the core-face, layered under the rising hum of the spinning shell. Pitch contour in words: at rest, low soft chirrs; spinning up, the hum climbs steadily while the voice stays level at the centre. Duration class: short calls, but the spin hum itself can run long. Rhythm pattern: even chirrs in a steady beat, quickening slightly as balance is challenged. Variations per state — idle: drowsy chirrs between long silences; call: a clear level chirr held through a full spin; hurt: a wobbling, pitch-dipping chirr as the spin falters; faint: the hum runs down in a long descending slide, voice last; affection: gentle chirrs at a slow, rocking spin; evolution / form-change moment: entering full spin is marked by the shell's hum swallowing the voice, then the voice re-emerging, unchanged, at the centre.
species.anatomyNotes: Six short beetle legs that tuck completely away at spin; no hands — manipulation is by two small foreleg claws and by nudging with the shell. Mouth is the core-face's small mouth, set in the bright inner creature that only becomes visible at full spin — the face is the creature, and animators must keep it identical at every speed. Locomotion: a waddling six-leg walk at rest, and true gyroscopic spinning on a single body point in duel, travelling in slow drifting arcs while spinning. The shell is grown and polished, with ridge rings that catch light at speed; the blur of the shell and the clarity of the core-face must read simultaneously.
species.paletteSeed: polished bronze, bright teal, warm cream, beetle black
species.footprint: Two traces, state-dependent. Walking leaves a double row of tiny six-leg beetle ticks, small and neat. Spinning leaves its signature trace instead of footprints: a spiral scuff — concentric scored circles with an inward spiral tail where it drifted, polished bright at the centre point. Print size class: tiny for the steps, small-to-medium for a finished duel scuff. Distinctive marker: duel grounds keep overlapping spiral scuffs like signatures, newest brightest.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — resting: a squat beetle-top, domed shell over a pointed base, legs splayed; spinning: a clean spinning-top cone-and-dome with blurred edges and a small bright face at the centre. Proportions in words: body almost entirely shell, legs minimal, core-face small. Key visual masses: the polished dome and the bright core. What reads at sprite size: top shape and central face. Identifying negative space: the thin clear ring between the blurred shell edge and the still centre where the face sits.
species.statProfile: Defence and endurance carry the species — it wins by still spinning when the other stops; modest offence that is mostly momentum, low walking speed, remarkable balance. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A beetle that is also a top, with a small bright face at its heart. Key features are the dense polished shell with its ridge rings, the tuck-away legs, and the core-face that appears at full spin. Must-never-change list: the core face is the same individual at both stages and is the creature itself — the body is never a toy it operates; duels are endurance and balance, never blades or blows; the shell is grown beetle chitin with a chrome sheen, never metal plating.

species.name: Cyclossus
species.dexText: Cyclossus walks the Rift like weather coming, a mountain of a beetle-bodied giant — until a dispute is put to it, when it lowers itself, tucks its great legs, and spins. Nothing that big should spin that long, and nothing that spins that long should have so small and calm a face at its centre, yet there it is: the same bright core-face Whirligig had, unchanged. No one has ever seen a Cyclossus stop spinning of its own accord; duels end when the other party, the audience, or the day gives out.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-2 Whirligig → Cyclossus — a walking colossus that still settles disputes by spin-duel and has never once been seen to stop on its own; donor mechanic: the spirit-core in a spinning toy body, translated at colossal scale — the body grew, the core-face did not change.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a walking colossus, taller than the institute's gatehouses, whose shadow settles arguments before it arrives.
species.temperament: Imperturbable, formal, and almost ceremonially fair; treats every duel as a court session and every result as final.
species.habitat: The open Region 4 Rift flats and the great crossing grounds, where there is room to spin; it walks established duel-circuits between them like a judge on rounds.
species.dietBehaviour: A slow, vast grazer of Rift scrub, lichen beds, and windfall fruit, eating in the long still hours between walks; its social life is its circuit — arriving, hearing disputes simply by being present, spinning, and walking on.
species.evolution: Final stage; no further evolution. The form change is the duel stance: walking body settles onto its spinning point, legs tuck in tiers, the colossal shell builds speed until it blurs to a shining wall, and the small core-face shows, calm and identical, at the centre. Returning to walking is equally deliberate — a long, controlled run-down that it permits rather than suffers.
species.discovery: Region 4 great Rift flats and named-by-use duel grounds near crossings; rarity class very rare, and effectively announced — humming and dust announce one long before it is seen. Method: wild encounter by following a duel-circuit; wait at a marked duel ground. Conditions: walks in clear weather, spins in any weather a dispute demands. Level band in words: upper band. First-meeting note: first meetings are formal — stand at the edge of the duel ground, state nothing, want nothing loudly, and let it regard you with the small calm face.
species.cry: Source character — the same small bright voice as Whirligig, improbably unchanged, carried at the centre of a shell-hum like distant thunder rolling in a circle. Pitch contour in words: voice level and clear; the hum rises in vast slow steps as speed builds and falls just as slowly. Duration class: long — calls and hums outlast ordinary encounters. Rhythm pattern: slow even chirrs, widely spaced, metronome-steady through a duel. Variations per state — idle: rare, soft chirrs from a body at monumental rest; call: one level call that carries absurdly far on the spinning air; hurt: the voice dips once, steadying as balance is recovered; faint: a run-down lasting a long while, hum descending storey by storey, voice calm to the end; affection: a low rocking spin and warm slow chirrs, usually for a lifelong keeper; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution remains; entering the duel spin, the thunder arrives first and the familiar small voice emerges inside it.
species.anatomyNotes: Six colossal legs in tucking tiers for walking and stance changes; no hands — it acts on the world by presence, spin, and delicate nudges of the shell rim. The mouth belongs to the core-face only; the great body has no other face, and animators must resist adding one. Locomotion: slow mountainous walking, and gyroscopic spinning on the body point with a drifting, arena-filling travel arc. Anatomy emphasis for move animation: attacks are momentum, balance, and endurance made visible — rams are glancing, duels are won by outlasting; the core-face's expression carries the emotion of every scene while the body carries the scale.
species.paletteSeed: weathered bronze, bright teal, warm cream, deep slate
species.footprint: Two traces, mode-dependent. Walking leaves huge round beetle-foot prints in two heavy rows, each print a broad polished oval, with a furrowed drag line where the spinning point trails between strides. Spinning leaves its true signature: a vast spiral scuff, arena-sized — concentric scored rings running inward to a bright polished centre, cut deeper with every hour of the duel. Print size class: huge in both modes. Distinctive marker: a finished Cyclossus duel ground can be read like a record — rings for the duel's length, centre for its calm.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — walking: a domed mountain on six legs, core-face a small bright point at the front centre; spinning: a colossal top, a shining blurred dome-and-cone with a still, tiny, bright face at its exact centre. Proportions in words: body overwhelmingly shell, legs long but visually minor, face deliberately, startlingly small. Key visual masses: the dome, the blur wall at spin, the core point of light. What reads at sprite size: giant top, tiny face — the contrast is the species. Identifying negative space: the calm circular eye of stillness at the centre of the spinning blur.
species.statProfile: Enormous defence and endurance, respectable force delivered as momentum rather than strikes; slow to start, slower to stop, and nearly impossible to unbalance. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A colossus built around an unchanged small face. Key features are the tiered tucking legs, the polished monumental shell, and the core-face that is Whirligig's own, exactly. Must-never-change list: the face never scales up, ages into menace, or moves off-centre; it has never been seen to stop on its own — frame its stopping as permission, never defeat-by-exhaustion played cheaply; duels stay contests of endurance and nerve, never brawls.

species.name: Packpup
species.dexText: Packpup cannot be persuaded to walk anywhere empty-backed. It collects — sticks, stones, lost tools, smaller friends — and arranges its load with a pup's total seriousness, trotting the Rift paths with its spine already dipping into the shallow saddle shape it was born with. Dropped objects along the crossings are understood locally to be Packpup deliveries in progress, and are left exactly where they lie.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-3 Packpup → Rigrex — a pup that carries things on its back by instinct; donor mechanic: the alt-mode idea in seed form — a back already shaped by the carrying it will one day do at full scale, translated wholly into biology.
species.sizeClass: Small — a sturdy pup about the size of a young farm dog, broad-backed well beyond its height.
species.temperament: Helpful to a fault, earnest, and mildly offended by uncarried things; happiest mid-errand.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift paths, crossing camps, and institute service yards — anywhere with traffic, loads, and an audience for carrying.
species.dietBehaviour: An omnivore of camp scraps, tubers, and tough Rift grasses; behaviour is defined by the carrying instinct — gathering, balancing, delivering, and returning for more, with play-fights conducted entirely under load and points awarded by onlookers for nothing dropped.
species.evolution: No alt-mode yet at this stage — the saddle-dip back is a promise, not a second form. It evolves into Rigrex as the carrying life grows it into a great saurus, when the load it can take, and the riders it can welcome, outgrow a pup's back entirely.
species.discovery: Region 4 Rift paths and institute service yards; rarity class common, and usually discovered already at work. Method: wild encounter along travelled routes — the reliable way is to set down something carryable and step back. Conditions: active all day, busiest at crossing rush hours. Level band in words: low band. First-meeting note: first meetings typically involve being relieved of a bag, a hat, or a smaller companion, carried a short and honourable distance, and returned with ceremony.
species.cry: Source character — a bright pup bark and whine set, all dog, no words. Pitch contour in words: barks short and level, whines rising at the end like a question. Duration class: very short barks; longer pleading whines when a load is refused. Rhythm pattern: bark pairs when setting off, single checking yips at each rest stop. Variations per state — idle: contented huffs and the odd experimental bark at its own load; call: an eager triple bark, tail going; hurt: a sharp yelp, load protected before itself; faint: a trailing whine as it sits down carefully so nothing spills; affection: squeaky whines with the whole rear end wagging; evolution / form-change moment: no form change at this stage — the carrying settle, a little grunt as the load seats on the saddle-dip, is its signature sound.
species.anatomyNotes: Four sturdy legs, a broad flat back with a visible shallow saddle dip grown into the spine, and a short balancing tail. No hands — manipulation is mouth-carry and back-carry only, and loads rest on the saddle-dip, held by body posture rather than straps. Mouth is a pup's jaw, good for sticks and handles, gentle by instinct with living cargo. Locomotion: an earnest trot with a built-in load-compensating sway; animators should bounce the cargo, never the spine. Its signature move animation is the proud set-off — dip, settle, tail up, trot.
species.paletteSeed: sandy tan, warm brown, cream belly, dusty red
species.footprint: A single trace at this stage: four-toed pup paw prints with clear pad marks and short claw ticks, in a steady trotting gait of evenly spaced alternating prints, often running in purposeful straight lines between crossing points. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: prints frequently pause in neat clusters beside a shallow resting-scuff where a load was set down and taken up again — a delivery, recorded in dust.
species.silhouette: Outline class — one form only: a low, broad-backed pup, saddle dip readable even in outline, ears up, tail a short flag. Proportions in words: back long and wide for its height, head mid-sized, legs sturdy and short. Key visual masses: the back and whatever it is carrying. What reads at sprite size: dip-backed pup plus load. Identifying negative space: the shallow concave arc of the saddle dip against the sky — no other Rift pup has a hollow in its outline.
species.statProfile: Balanced and hardy for a first stage, leaning to defence and stamina; speed is a working trot, and its best stat in practice is not dropping things. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A pup whose back is already a saddle and whose character is already a porter. Key features are the grown saddle dip, the earnest expression, and the ever-present load. Must-never-change list: the saddle is grown anatomy, never tack or equipment; the carrying is instinct and joy, never labour imposed on it; nothing about the pup reads as a vehicle — it is a dog doing a dog's chosen job at larger meaning.

species.name: Rigrex
species.stageNote: final stage, beast mode and carrier mode
species.dexText: Rigrex is the Rift's living road. In beast mode it is a great saurus entire — browsing, bellowing, shaking the ground at a run. In carrier mode the same body settles, levels, and opens along grown rails of rib and saddle into a walking cargo frame, and smaller species climb aboard and ride like passengers on a bus with strong opinions about the route. Both modes are wholly the creature; it chooses between them the way other beasts choose between walking and swimming.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-3 Packpup → Rigrex — a great saurus with two complete ways of being: beast mode, and carrier mode, a walking cargo frame smaller species ride like a bus with opinions; donor mechanic: alt-modes, one being in two complete forms, translated as grown anatomy — nobody built the frame, it grew saddle-shaped.
species.sizeClass: Large — a great saurus, long as a wagon train and tall enough at the shoulder for a standing Ranger to look it levelly in the eye in beast mode, lower and broader in carrier mode.
