species.temperament: Patient, route-proud, and stubborn about schedules it has invented entirely by itself; gentle with riders, immovable with anyone who treats it as furniture.
species.habitat: The long Region 4 Rift routes between crossings, institute depots, and Rift settlements — a wide-ranging species that treats the region's paths as its own territory.
species.dietBehaviour: A bulk browser of Rift canopy, tough shrubs, and depot-provided fodder, eating hugely in beast mode; its behaviour runs in services — regular routes at regular hours of its own choosing, rest stops where riders expect them, and a famous refusal to depart until a familiar passenger arrives.
species.evolution: Final stage; evolution from Packpup arrives with the second way of being. The alt-mode change is described purely as anatomy: in settling to carrier mode, the spine levels and locks into its grown saddle line, rib-rails lower into boarding steps and side frames, flank plates flatten into standing platforms, and the tail extends as a balancing counterweight — all muscle, bone, and posture, reversed just as organically into the arched, mobile saurus of beast mode. It can rest, eat, and be itself fully in either mode, and may refuse a mode change the way any creature may refuse anything.
species.discovery: Region 4 long Rift routes, crossing depots, and institute freight yards; rarity class uncommon but unmissable — discovery is usually by timetable, as locals can say when one will pass. Method: wild encounter at a known rest stop; wait with the other passengers. Conditions: carrier services run in fair weather; beast mode ranges in all weather. Level band in words: mid-to-upper band. First-meeting note: first meetings go best as a passenger — board when invited by its settled posture, sit where the smaller species sit, and hold opinions about the route until the second trip.
species.cry: Source character — a deep saurus bellow and rumble set, voiced through a great throat, warm rather than savage. Pitch contour in words: bellows rise from a chest rumble to a carrying horn-like peak; contentment sounds stay low and level. Duration class: long bellows, short working grunts. Rhythm pattern: a setting-off double-bellow in carrier mode; single spaced rumbles at rest stops. Variations per state — idle: slow rumbling breaths and leaf-tearing sounds; call: the full route bellow, answered by waiting passengers' species in chorus; hurt: a cut-off bellow dropping into pained grunts, riders steadied before itself; faint: a descending rumble as it kneels, carefully, in whichever mode it holds; affection: a deep happy chuffing, usually with the head lowered to rider height; evolution / form-change moment: the mode change has its own sound — a rising series of settling creaks, clicks of rib-rail and plate finding their places, and a final satisfied grunt when the frame is true.
species.anatomyNotes: Four massive column legs; in beast mode the gait is an arched, bounding saurus run, in carrier mode a slow, level, shock-absorbed walk with minimal load sway — the two walks must animate as different creatures sharing a body. No hands; manipulation is by mouth, tail, and the deliberate placement of boarding steps and platforms for riders. Mouth is a great browsing saurus jaw with a clear bellow posture. Mode-change anatomy is the brief: spine line (arched versus level-locked), rib-rails, flank platforms, and tail counterweight are all visible grown structures whose movement is muscular and sequential, never mechanical unfolding; riders are cargo-with-feelings held by posture and rails, never strapped machinery.
species.paletteSeed: moss green, warm brown, sandy tan, cream, dusty red
species.footprint: Two traces, mode-dependent, and telling them apart is a basic Rift skill. Beast mode leaves deep, three-toed saurus prints with heavy claw gouges, long bounding strides, and a swinging tail-drag line that comes and goes. Carrier mode leaves different prints entirely: broad, flat, evenly weighted oval prints with softened claw marks, in a short, metronome-regular gait with no tail-drag — the tail rides raised — plus a churned boarding patch at rest stops where many small prints of passenger species cluster at its flank. Print size class: large in both modes. Distinctive marker: the same individual's prints change character mid-trail at a mode change, claws and stride smoothing out like a signature changing hands.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — beast mode: a classic great saurus, arched back, high head, tail a long countercurve; carrier mode: a level-topped walking frame, spine flattened into a long horizontal line, rib-rails and flank platforms stepping down the sides, head lowered to route height. Proportions in words: length dominates in both modes; carrier mode is broader and lower, beast mode taller and more arched. Key visual masses: the saddle-line back, the rib-rail flanks, the tail. What reads at sprite size: arched saurus versus flat-topped carrier — the back line alone tells the mode. Identifying negative space: in carrier mode, the regular rectangular gaps between the lowered rib-rails along the flank; in beast mode, the tall open arch under the raised tail.
species.statProfile: Very high stamina and carrying strength, high defence in both modes; speed belongs to beast mode, stability to carrier mode; offence is a saurus's — real, and rarely its first idea. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: One great saurus, two complete silhouettes, both entirely animal. Key features are the grown saddle spine, the rib-rail flanks that serve as steps and frame, and a face with opinions in both modes. Must-never-change list: both modes are the creature — the carrier frame grew, nobody built it, fitted it, or drives it; Rigrex chooses its modes, routes, and passengers; no wheels, panels, harnesses, or vehicle vocabulary in any depiction.

species.name: Pilotto
species.dexText: Pilotto is half of something. Alone it is a bright, quick, otter-like swimmer and climber of the Rift canopy; bonded — and Pilotto bond young and for life — it is the rider of a Framoth, the small warm mind at the heart of a giant's flight. The Mochiioteca lists Pilotto and Framoth as one entry in two bodies, because neither the record-keepers nor the creatures themselves recognise a version of either that is complete alone.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-4 Pilotto & Framoth, a pair-entry — Pilotto is the palm-sized otter-like rider who bonds for life with the giant Framoth; donor mechanic: the small pilot of a large frame, translated into a lifelong creature-bond between two species — symbiosis, not machinery, and the pair is the species-entry.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — palm-sized in truth, a small otter that rides cupped in two hands or curled in the hollow of its partner's wing-cape.
species.temperament: Bright, devoted, and brave out of all proportion to its size; anxious when separated from its Framoth, and fearless in the air it trusts.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift canopy, river crossings, and high institute gardens — always, after bonding, wherever its Framoth roosts, which is to say the pair's habitat is the pair.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats fish fry, river greens, berries, and whatever the scale-mite swarm brings home; behaviour is pair behaviour — scouting ahead on short flights of its own small wings is beyond it, so it scouts by climbing, swimming, and directing from the nest-hollow, grooming Framoth's wing-scales and tending the mites like younger siblings.
species.evolution: No evolution; Pilotto is a complete species whose life change is the bond itself. It bonds for life with one Framoth, the pairing made in youth by mutual choice over days of shared flight and feeding, and unmade only by death. Its half of the pair-bond: it rides in the nest-hollow where Framoth's wing-cape folds, steers the partnership by voice, weight, and trust, and is the social heart of the scale-mite swarm — Framoth's shed wing-scales, living mites that fly in formation as a swarm shield around the pair, who answer Pilotto's calls like a scattered family being called home.
species.discovery: Discovery is of the PAIR — Pilotto is never encountered wild and alone for long, and an unbonded juvenile is found only in the company of Framoth roosts. Region 4 canopy crossings and high institute gardens; rarity class rare as an encounter, because the pair is usually first seen in flight overhead. Method: wild encounter at Framoth roosts at dawn, when the pair is waking and the mites are settling back into the wing-scales. Conditions: calm mornings; the pair ranges widely in fair weather. Level band in words: mid band for bonded pairs. First-meeting note: greet the Framoth first and the Pilotto second — the rider judges every stranger by how they address its giant.
species.cry: Source character — a quick, bright otter chitter and whistle set, small and carrying, made to be heard across a giant's wingspan. Pitch contour in words: whistles rise sharply and fall in quick arcs; chitters stay level and rapid. Duration class: very short notes in long conversational strings. Rhythm pattern: call-and-answer with Framoth's wing-sounds and the mites' faint ticking flight. Variations per state — idle: musical chittering while grooming scales; call: a piercing two-note whistle that brings the swarm home; hurt: a thin squeal that brings Framoth's wing down around it like a wall; faint: whistles weakening into chitter, then quiet in the nest-hollow; affection: soft bubbling chitters against Framoth's neck; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution — the bond moment is the signature sound, juvenile Pilotto and Framoth exchanging one whistle and one deep wing-note, back and forth, until the mites settle for the first time.
species.anatomyNotes: Four otter limbs with nimble webbed paws — true manipulators, the best hands in this bucket — plus a long rudder tail for swimming. Mouth is a small otter muzzle; it vocalises constantly while working, never in words. Locomotion: swimming, climbing, and scrambling on the ground; in the air it does not fly — it rides, and its airborne animation is posture, signalling, and trust in the nest-hollow, leaning into turns its partner makes. Animation emphasis: Pilotto is the pair's face and hands — it points, grooms, signals, and holds on; every pair animation should be readable from its small reactions alone.
species.paletteSeed: river brown, cream, bright teal, leaf green
species.footprint: A tiny trace, almost always found as half of a pair record: small webbed otter prints, five-toed with hand-like foreprints, in a bounding-then-scampering gait along banks and roost branches. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: Pilotto prints orbit — they circle, double back, and cluster inside the wide dusted margin of Framoth's traces and scale-mite dust, never striking out alone for long.
species.silhouette: Outline class — one form: a sleek small otter, round-eared, long-tailed, usually seen upright in a signalling posture or curled in the nest-hollow. Proportions in words: head large and expressive, body otter-long, tail half its length again. Key visual masses: head and tail; in pair silhouette, Pilotto is a small warm comma at the centre of Framoth's great wing-cape. What reads at sprite size: otter shape and raised signalling paws. Identifying negative space: the curved gap between its raised tail and back when it sits up to call the swarm.
species.statProfile: Low direct power and fragile alone, as the record expects; within the pair it contributes speed of decision, perception, and the swarm's coordination — the pair's shared profile is listed with Framoth. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A palm-sized otter rider whose whole design is devotion at small scale. Key features are the expressive paws, the signalling whistles, and the curled sleeping shape that exactly fits its partner's nest-hollow. Must-never-change list: Pilotto is a creature, never a pilot operating equipment — it rides a friend, not a vehicle; the bond is mutual choice for life; Pilotto alone is an incomplete picture and should not be presented as the whole entry.

species.name: Framoth
species.dexText: Framoth is a moth the size of weather, and the gentlest entry in the Rift records. Its great wing-cape folds, at rest and in flight, into a warm nest-hollow at the shoulders, and there — by lifelong mutual choice — its Pilotto rides. Its wing-scales shed continually as living scale-mites, tiny bright children of the wing that fly in formation as a shield around the pair, and return to roost in the cape; a bonded Framoth is therefore never one creature but a small, devoted constellation.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Flag carried from the source (§5): moths are Pokémon-crowded (Volcarona, Frosmoth…) — the design is the pair-bond and the frame, not the moth.
species.lineConcept: C1-4 Pilotto & Framoth, a pair-entry — Framoth is the gentle giant moth whose wing-cape folds into a nest-hollow cockpit, and whose shed wing-scales live as a scale-mite swarm shield, the pair's remote children; donor mechanic: the large piloted frame with remote child units, translated into a bonded frame species and its living mite swarm — symbiosis, not machinery.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a gentle giant of a moth, its wing-cape spanning wider than a crossing bridge, large enough to carry its rider, its nest, and its swarm in one slow flight.
species.temperament: Gentle, slow to alarm, and utterly steady; its whole emotional life is organised around its rider's safety and its swarm's return.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift canopy, high crossings, and the tallest institute gardens and towers, where it roosts wing-spread in the sun; the pair's range is the whole sky over the Rift.
species.dietBehaviour: A vast, mild grazer of canopy leaves, Rift blossom nectar, and flowering vines, feeding on the wing at dawn; behaviour is pair and swarm behaviour — ferrying its Pilotto, shepherding its mites, and hanging in slow patrols over crossings where smaller species travel under its shadow like an escort.
species.evolution: No evolution; Framoth is a complete species whose life change is the bond itself. It bonds for life with one Pilotto, chosen in youth and kept without exception, the nest-hollow in its wing-cape deepening with age to the exact shape of its rider. Its half of the pair-bond: it carries, shelters, and answers — flying as its rider directs by voice and weight — and it parents the scale-mite swarm, the living shed scales of its own wings that detach, fly in shield formation as the pair's remote children, and re-roost in the cape to rest and be replaced as new scales grow.
species.discovery: Discovery is of the PAIR — Framoth is met as a bonded pair with Pilotto, at Region 4 canopy crossings, high institute gardens, and dawn roosts; rarity class rare, though a passing pair is visible for a long way. Method: wild encounter at roosts before first flight, or by watching crossing patrols. Conditions: dawn and fair weather; pairs shelter deep in canopy through Rift storms, mites and all. Level band in words: mid-to-upper band for bonded adults. First-meeting note: approach under the wing, in the open, and let the Pilotto inspect you first — a Framoth's calm is its rider's verdict made visible.
species.cry: Source character — Framoth barely voices at all: a deep, soft wing-note, air through a great cape, under a low moth hum from the thorax, with Pilotto's whistle carrying the pair's conversation. Pitch contour in words: very low, level, and slow, felt in the chest more than heard. Duration class: long, breath-paced notes. Rhythm pattern: single wing-notes spaced by full wingbeats; quicker, shallower notes when the swarm is called home. Variations per state — idle: slow hums and the ticking patter of mites resettling; call: one vast wing-note that Pilotto answers, the pair's shared signature; hurt: a deep shuddering hum, wings closing protectively over the nest-hollow; faint: the hum sinking and slowing as it glides down to a belly landing, rider sheltered throughout; affection: warm low hums with the cape curled fully around its Pilotto; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution — the bond moment is its signature, the first deep wing-note answered by a juvenile Pilotto's whistle, repeated until the swarm settles.
species.anatomyNotes: Six slender moth legs for roosting and gentle ground handling, useless for carrying; the manipulators of the pair are Pilotto's paws and the swarm. Mouth is a soft moth proboscis for nectar, no jaw for battle. Locomotion: slow, enormous flight on the wing-cape, and a careful, rarely seen ground shuffle. The defining anatomy is the wing-cape itself — its fold geometry creates the nest-hollow at the shoulders, its scales visibly shed and return as mites, and its rim curls as a shield wall; animators must treat the cape as one living organ performing carrying, sheltering, and parenting at once, and the swarm's formations should read as children flying, never as devices deploying.
species.paletteSeed: soft sage, cream, dusty rose, leaf green, bright scale-teal
species.footprint: It leaves almost no true footprint — Framoth's trace is a dusting: a broad, soft-edged fall of shed scale-powder and resting mites' pinprick dots beneath roosts and along low flight paths, with, only where it has shuffled on the ground, six faint slender leg-ticks in two loose rows. Print size class: negligible prints, huge trace. Distinctive marker: the scale-dust margin is the pair's map — Pilotto's tiny prints are found inside it, and a dusted patch shaped like a great wing's shadow marks a roost.
species.silhouette: Outline class — roosting: a vast folded cape like a hanging tent of wings, nest-hollow a warm notch at its top centre; in flight: a full wing-cape crescent, Pilotto a small bright shape at the leading centre, the swarm a faint halo of points around the rim. Proportions in words: wings overwhelmingly the body, thorax deep and soft, head small and downy between the cape's shoulders. Key visual masses: the cape, the cape, and the cape — then the rider at its heart. What reads at sprite size: giant moth-cape with a dot of rider at its centre. Identifying negative space: the nest-hollow notch at the cape's top edge, occupied or unmistakably shaped by its occupant.
species.statProfile: The pair's shared profile: high defence built on scale, cape, and swarm shield, high stamina for long flights, modest offence that is mostly weather and weight; Framoth alone is gentle force, Pilotto alone is fragile — together they are the entry. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A giant moth designed as a home in flight. Key features are the wing-cape and its nest-hollow, the living scale-mite swarm orbiting as shield and family, and a small rider at the centre of every composition. Must-never-change list: the design is the pair-bond and the frame, not the moth alone — Framoth is never depicted as a solo monster; the nest-hollow is a fold of living wing, never a cockpit or machine space; the mites are its shed living scales and children, never drones or equipment.

species.name: Shacklet
species.stageNote: first stage, born in restraint armour
species.dexText: Shacklet is born already armoured — not fitted, not made: its shell of bands and overlapping plates is its own grown body, present from its first hour, and fitted exactly to the enormous strength underneath. The armour is a kindness the species does itself; it lets a very strong, very gentle beast live among smaller things without thinking about its strength every moment. A Shacklet at ease hums, leans into familiar voices, and unclenches — visibly, plate by plate — as it relaxes.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-5 Shacklet → Restreint — a large, gentle beast born inside a shell of grown restraint-armour, bands and plates it grew itself, which keep its enormous strength company; donor mechanic: the living organism in restraints, translated into grown calming armour — drama is trust and panic, never horror.
species.sizeClass: Large — even young, a big beast, taller at the shoulder than a standing Ranger and built like a bank vault with a kind face.
species.temperament: Gentle, trusting, and anxious in unfamiliar places; calm is its natural state and other people's calm is contagious to it.
species.habitat: Quiet Region 4 Rift valleys, institute sanctuary grounds, and sheltered crossing pastures — calm places, kept calm partly by its presence.
species.dietBehaviour: A heavy grazer of Rift grasses, roots, and mineral-rich clay, eating slowly and often; behaviour centres on its keeper-bond — it follows familiar voices, stations itself near trusted Rangers, and when frightened looks for its people first, calling and searching rather than striking out.
species.evolution: No form change; the armour is never removed in either stage, and is not removable — it is body. It evolves into Restreint as body and armour grow together into their full scale, and its real growth, in the record's own framing, is character: learning to unclench one plate at a time, in trust, is its arc at every age.
species.discovery: Region 4 institute sanctuary grounds, quiet Rift valleys, and crossing pastures; rarity class uncommon — keepers move with most known individuals, so a truly alone Shacklet usually means a separated one, and helping it search is the correct first response. Method: wild encounter by voice — call steadily and let it come to the sound. Conditions: most at ease in calm, overcast, quiet weather; unsettled by Rift storm noise. Level band in words: mid band. First-meeting note: introduce your voice before your face — speak from where it can hear you, keep speaking, and let the plates unclenching tell you how the meeting is going.
species.cry: Source character — a deep, soft beast voice, muffled slightly by the armour's bands, with the faint grown-shell creaks and plate settlings that accompany its feelings. Pitch contour in words: low and level at ease, rising in a searching arc when calling for its keeper. Duration class: long, slow calls; short huffing breaths at rest. Rhythm pattern: spaced single calls when searching, with listening silences between — the silence is part of the pattern. Variations per state — idle: low humming breaths and occasional contented plate-creaks; call: a carrying, rising call aimed at a familiar voice, repeated until answered; hurt: a startled bellow cut short, then anxious huffing; faint: calls weakening into breath, armour settling with soft final clicks; affection: a warm, low, almost purring rumble with plates loosening audibly one by one; evolution / form-change moment: no form change — at evolution the signature sound is the great settling, plates of the new scale finding their places over days, punctuated by its unchanged young voice.
species.anatomyNotes: Four massive limbs ending in broad, blunt-clawed feet; strength is everywhere and must animate as weight, not menace. No hands — manipulation is by mouth, forehead, and the careful placement of its bulk to shelter, lean, and carry. Mouth is a gentle grazer's jaw inside the armour's face bands; the face stays kind and readable at all times. Locomotion: a slow, deliberate, ground-shaking walk. The armour is the animation brief: grown bands and plates with living give, able to clench tight in panic and unclench plate by plate in trust — an emotional instrument worn on the outside of the body, articulated by muscle, never by mechanism, and never opening to reveal anything but the same gentle beast.
species.paletteSeed: deep indigo, slate chrome, muted violet, warm cream
species.footprint: A heavy trace: broad four-toed beast prints, blunt claw marks short and shallow for its size, each print ringed on its outer side by a faint secondary impression — the lower edge of an armour band settling beside the foot. Gait pattern: slow, even, four-square walking with short strides for its bulk. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the band-edge halo beside every print, and, at resting places, a wide polished patch where its plated belly has settled and shifted as it relaxed.
species.silhouette: Outline class — one form: a great rounded beast almost entirely wrapped in overlapping bands, head low and kind between face plates, the body's true outline soft under the shell's hard arcs. Proportions in words: mass first, legs sturdy and partly banded, head small-seeming for the body though it is not. Key visual masses: the banded barrel of the body, the plated shoulders. What reads at sprite size: wrapped giant with a gentle face. Identifying negative space: the narrow bright gaps between bands at the neck and joints, which widen visibly as it unclenches.
species.statProfile: Exceptional strength and defence, held in check by temperament rather than by any lack; low speed, low inclination to offence at all — its danger, on the record, is only ever its size in a panic. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A gentle giant wearing its own calm. Key features are the grown band-and-plate armour, the kind face inside it, and the visible clench-and-unclench that tells every scene's emotion. Must-never-change list: the armour is grown body and is never removed, opened like a container, or treated as equipment; the tone is trust and panic, never horror, never gore, never menace from the creature itself; its strength is a responsibility it carries sweetly, not a threat the design sells.

species.name: Restreint
species.dexText: Restreint is Shacklet grown to the full meaning of its armour: a mountain of a beast inside bands and plates it grew itself, strong past measuring and gentle past argument. At its keeper's voice it calms instantly — the great plates loosen, the breathing slows, the day is saved by a sound. Separated and frightened, it does not rage; it searches, calling and walking and pushing carefully through a world built smaller than its worry, and that search, at its size, is the problem the whole Rift turns out to help with.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-5 Shacklet → Restreint — the fully grown beast in its self-grown restraint-armour, which calms instantly at its keeper's voice and, separated and frightened, does not rage but searches, which at its size is enough of a problem; donor mechanic: the living organism in restraints with a partner sync-bond, translated into grown armour and a voice-bond — trust and panic, never horror.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a colossal gentle beast, its plated shoulder taller than an institute doorway, its searching walk a local emergency of kindness.
species.temperament: Profoundly gentle, deeply bonded, and anxious only about the whereabouts of its people; in company, the calmest large creature in the region.
species.habitat: Region 4 institute sanctuary grounds and the wide quiet valleys of the Rift, ranging further only on its searching days, which the region's storytellers map like weather.
species.dietBehaviour: A colossal grazer of valley grasses, roots, and clay banks, feeding in long peaceful hours near its keepers; behaviour is bond behaviour at scale — voice-checks through the day, station-keeping near home ground, and the famous searching pattern: call, listen, walk, call again, plates clenched, gentleness intact, fences and crossings rearranged by worry rather than anger.
species.evolution: Final stage; no further evolution and no form change. The armour is never removed at this stage either — growth, trust, and the slow art of unclenching one plate at a time remain the species' whole arc, and an old Restreint at complete ease, every plate loose in the sun beside its keeper, is the record's picture of a finished life.
species.discovery: Region 4 sanctuary grounds and quiet Rift valleys; rarity class rare — most are known individuals with known keepers and known voices. Method: wild encounter is rarely the frame; meeting one is arranged by its people, or happens on a searching day, when the correct discovery method is to be found, calmly, in the open, calling back. Conditions: at home in calm weather; searching behaviour follows separations and Rift storms. Level band in words: upper band. First-meeting note: a first meeting is a voice meeting — be introduced by a keeper it trusts, keep talking, and watch the plates: they will introduce its feelings before its face does.
species.cry: Source character — a vast, soft voice with a hall's worth of resonance, wrapped in the slow creaks and settlings of great grown plates. Pitch contour in words: very low, rising only in the searching call, which climbs in a long anxious arc and falls into listening silence. Duration class: very long calls at this scale. Rhythm pattern: the search rhythm — call, long listening pause, a few enormous steps, call again — is recognisable across valleys. Variations per state — idle: slow tidal breathing and deep contented plate-creaks; call: the searching call, or, answered, a settling rumble of recognition; hurt: a pained bellow immediately damped by its own effort at gentleness; faint: voice sinking into breath as it kneels with care for everything beneath it; affection: the keeper's-voice response — a warm loosening rumble with plates unclenching in audible sequence; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution remains — the unclenching itself, plate by plate at a trusted voice, is the species' signature transformation and its sound.
species.anatomyNotes: Four column limbs of enormous strength, broad blunt-clawed feet placed with a grazer's care; no hands — it shelters with its body, leans, and lifts with forehead and shoulder under direction it trusts. Mouth is a grazer's jaw behind the face bands, built for cropping and calling, and its expressions — worry, recognition, ease — must carry scenes. Locomotion: slow tectonic walking, a careful searching stride, and a kneel-and-settle rest posture. Animation emphasis: the armour's clench state is a full-body performance channel — tight and high in panic, loose and low in trust — moved by visible living effort; panic must always animate as searching and calling, never as attack, and its scale effects on the world are accidents of worry, played for pathos and comedy of scale, never destruction as spectacle.
species.paletteSeed: deep indigo, slate chrome, muted violet, warm cream, dusk purple
species.footprint: An unmistakable trace: very broad four-toed prints with short blunt claw scores, each haloed by the deep secondary crescent of a settling armour band, in a slow four-square gait — and, on searching days, the same prints in long purposeful lines between settlements, with resting patches where the whole plated mass settled, listened, and rose again. Print size class: huge. Distinctive marker: the band-halo at full depth reads like a second, larger foot stepped around the first, and a search trail can be followed valley to valley by it alone.
species.silhouette: Outline class — one form: a plated mountain in profile, back a long arc of overlapping bands, head low and gentle at the front, legs as banded columns. Proportions in words: body mass dominates everything; head modest, neck short, plates at the shoulder the highest point. Key visual masses: the banded back, the shoulder plates, the kind low head. What reads at sprite size: wrapped colossus, visible band lines, soft face. Identifying negative space: the bright joint-gaps between bands, widest at the neck in trust, pinched shut in panic — silhouette alone tells its state.
species.statProfile: Strength and defence at the top of this bucket's register, speed at the bottom; offence is a category the species declines — the relevant contest is always emotional, and its keeper's voice is the strongest force in any encounter with it. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Scale plus gentleness, armoured by its own body. Key features are the full-grown band-and-plate shell, the voice-bond made visible in the unclenching, and a searching — never raging — panic. Must-never-change list: armour grown and never removed; tone is trust and panic, never horror, gore, or cruelty, and the creature is never a monster in any scene's grammar; no operator, no controls, no machinery reading — there is only a beast, its body, and the people it loves.

species.name: Masklet
species.dexText: Masklet grows its face the way other species grow antlers. When it takes a role in its tribe — tide-watcher, ember-tender, road-walker — its body slowly grows a carved shell-mask of that role, chitin laid down in original patterns over a season of assuming the work. When the role changes, the old mask is shed, whole and beautiful, and hung with ceremony on the tribe's mask-tree, where the tribe's whole history can be read by anyone who knows the carvings.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-6 Masklet → Sigilord — a tribal creature that grows a carved shell-mask for each role it takes in life and sheds the old one onto the tribe's mask-tree; donor mechanic: masks as power and role, translated into grown chitin masks whose power is social and ritual, never technological.
species.sizeClass: Small — a sturdy little creature about the size of a young badger, most of its presence carried in the mask it wears.
species.temperament: Earnest, role-proud, and community-minded; a Masklet between roles is thoughtful and a little shy, and one newly masked is quietly radiant.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift tribal grounds — mask-tree groves near crossings, institute-adjacent settlements, and the tide, ember, and road stations its roles serve.
species.dietBehaviour: An omnivore of grove fruit, insects, shellfish at tide stations, and shared tribe meals; behaviour is organised by role — the day is the mask's work, the evening is carving-polish, story, and the mask-tree, and mask-shedding ceremonies are the tribe's calendar made visible.
species.evolution: The mask changes are the form changes of this line, and they are life events, not battle forms: growth is slow, the new role's mask grows over the old over a season, and the shed is ceremonial. It evolves into Sigilord only in age and honour, when one individual has held so many roles that its masks no longer shed cleanly but layer — the mask of masks beginning to form.
species.discovery: Region 4 mask-tree groves and tribal crossing grounds; rarity class uncommon, and usually announced by the mask-tree itself, which no ranger forgets. Method: wild encounter at groves and role stations; be introduced at a shedding ceremony if fortune allows. Conditions: most visible at role-work hours and at ceremonies in fair weather. Level band in words: low-to-mid band. First-meeting note: first meetings are read off the mask — greet the role it is wearing, not just the creature, and it will consider you unusually polite and entirely correct.
species.cry: Source character — a warm, woody little voice, slightly hollowed by the mask it speaks through, so each role's mask tunes the same creature's cry a little differently. Pitch contour in words: level and unhurried, with ceremonial rising notes at beginnings. Duration class: short phrases, often repeated for the group. Rhythm pattern: work-chants in steady beats at role stations; single clear calls at ceremonies. Variations per state — idle: soft humming through the mask while polishing carving; call: a clear role-call note, answered by tribe-mates in their own mask-tunes; hurt: a muffled yip and a protective paw to the mask; faint: voice thinning as it sits, mask tipped forward; affection: gentle clicking churrs against a tribe-mate's mask, carving to carving; evolution / form-change moment: the shedding has its own sound — days of soft creaking growth, then one clean, soft crack as the old mask lifts free, met by the tribe's chant.
species.anatomyNotes: A compact biped with short, dexterous arms and true little hands — it adjusts, polishes, and offers its masks with them — and broad, steady feet for station work. The mouth is its own, small and expressive, set under the mask's lower rim; the mask is grown chitin continuous with the brow and skull, moving subtly with expression rather than sitting as a separate object, and animators must never treat it as a removable prop mid-scene. Locomotion: a purposeful waddling walk and short trots between stations. Signature animation: the role-postures — tide-mask leans listening, ember-mask crouches tending, road-mask strides — one body language per mask, learned by the animator per role.
species.paletteSeed: warm bark brown, shell cream, ember orange, tide teal
species.footprint: A neat tribal trace: broad three-toed footprints with a clear heel pad, in an alternating biped gait of short, purposeful strides, frequently overprinted by the tribe's communal paths between grove, stations, and mask-tree. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: at a mask-tree the ground is ringed with one individual's neat prints at the shedding spot and a scatter of older, larger shed masks above — the footprint of a life, in both senses, is read upward.
species.silhouette: Outline class — one body, many mask outlines: the body silhouette stays a compact round biped, while the mask's silhouette carries the role — wide and listening for tide, low and hooded for ember, long and forward for road. Proportions in words: mask large for the head, body sturdy, hands visible at the sides. Key visual masses: the mask first, then the round body. What reads at sprite size: creature plus mask shape, role legible at a glance. Identifying negative space: the gap between mask lower rim and chin where its own small face breathes and speaks.
species.statProfile: Modest and balanced, tilting with its current role — road-masks enduring, ember-masks spirited, tide-masks patient; its real strength is social, and the record declines to separate the creature from its tribe. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A small tribal creature wearing its biography. Key features are the grown carved chitin mask, original in every pattern, the role-postures, and the mask-tree behind every scene it is in. Must-never-change list: masks are grown body, original carvings — no donor mask shapes, names, or motifs carried; mask power is social and ritual standing, never technology or magic machinery; a shed mask is a treasured record, never litter or loot.

species.name: Sigilord
species.stageNote: final stage, elder of the mask of masks
species.dexText: A Sigilord is what a Masklet becomes when a whole life of roles stops shedding and starts layering. Tide, ember, road, and every other service it has given the tribe grow over one another into a single towering mask of masks, strata of carved chitin that elders of other tribes travel to read. It speaks rarely, works still, and is consulted on everything — not because the mask grants it power, but because the mask is proof, worn in public, of everything it has already done for everyone.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-6 Masklet → Sigilord — an elder wearing the mask of masks, a layered shell of every role it has ever held; donor mechanic: masks as power and role, translated into a lifetime of grown chitin layers — authority as biography, ritual, and memory, never technology.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a tall, grave elder about the size of a standing bear in presence though slighter in build, its layered mask giving it the height of a monument.
species.temperament: Grave, generous, and dryly funny in the way of very old community servants; its patience is famous and its judgements are short.
species.habitat: Region 4 mask-tree groves and tribal council grounds of the Rift, almost always at the grove of its own tribe, beneath the tree that holds its shed youth.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats lightly for its size — grove fruit, shared ceremonial meals, tide and ember station offerings — and spends its days in the elder's roles: reading shed masks for the young, settling role disputes, presiding at sheddings, and still taking a small daily station shift, because the mask of masks includes, always, today's work.
species.evolution: Final stage; no further evolution. Its form change is complete and biographical — the layered mask continues to grow by thin strata with each late honour, but nothing sheds now; what a Sigilord was, it wears. Ceremonially it may tilt and present particular layers to be read, the nearest thing the line has to a display form.
species.discovery: Region 4 mask-tree groves and council grounds; rarity class very rare — a tribe has one at a time, and some have none. Method: wild encounter is the wrong frame; one is met, by introduction, at its grove, ideally at a ceremony. Conditions: presides in fair weather and foul alike; most approachable at evening mask-readings. Level band in words: upper band. First-meeting note: bring a role, a question, or useful work — a Sigilord reads visitors the way it reads masks, and idleness is the only introduction it finds uninteresting.
species.cry: Source character — a deep, resonant voice through layered chitin, the strata giving it a soft chord-like fullness, one creature heard as a small chorus of its own past roles. Pitch contour in words: low, slow, and level, with ceremonial rises reserved for beginnings and verdicts. Duration class: long, unhurried phrases with silence kept between them. Rhythm pattern: single statements, widely spaced; at ceremonies, a call that the tribe answers role by role. Variations per state — idle: rare soft humming, layers ticking faintly as they grow; call: a chord-deep summons that carries across the grove; hurt: a low note of pain and both hands raised to steady the great mask; faint: the voice settling downward layer by layer into quiet as it is helped to sit; affection: warm low churrs for the young, with the mask tilted down to their height; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution remains — the layering moments are its transformations, marked by a soft creak, a ceremony, and one new stratum catching the light.
species.anatomyNotes: A tall biped with long, careful arms and dexterous elder hands that read carvings by touch; posture is upright but weighted, every movement planned around the mask's layered mass. The mouth is its own beneath the lowest stratum; the mask layers are continuous grown chitin from brow and skull, flexing minutely as one living structure, with older role-carvings still legible in the strata. Locomotion: a slow processional walk, station shifts taken at a deliberate pace, and long stillnesses that should animate as presence, not idleness. Signature animation: the reading tilt — head and mask inclining so a chosen layer catches light and attention — and the shedding-preside gesture, hands open under a young one's lifting mask.
species.paletteSeed: deep bark brown, shell cream, ember orange, tide teal, aged gold
species.footprint: A grave trace: broad three-toed elder prints with a heavy heel pad and, flanking them, the shallow round dents of the staff-like walking stick it does not carry — they are, on inspection, the prints of its own knuckles, touched down at each step in elder fashion while reading ground and carving. Gait pattern: slow, even, processional, often in the grove's oldest paths where generations of the tribe's prints are layered like its mask. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: its trails run mask-tree to station to council stone and back, a whole office written in footprints.
species.silhouette: Outline class — one form: a tall figure crowned by a towering layered mask, strata edges stepped like a carved cliff, body beneath it comparatively plain and sturdy. Proportions in words: mask is the upper half of the presence, shoulders broad under it, hands low and open. Key visual masses: the stratified mask, then the upright elder body. What reads at sprite size: stepped mask-tower over a small solemn figure. Identifying negative space: the deep shadowed undercut beneath the mask's lowest layer, where its own face sits in shade — the private creature inside the public biography.
species.statProfile: High defence and wisdom-weighted presence, low speed, and offence replaced almost entirely by authority; in battle terms the record notes respectable resilience and support weight, and leaves the tribe's safety, as ever, a communal project. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: An elder whose face is its whole service record. Key features are the stratified mask of masks with every carving original and legible, the processional posture, and the shaded real face beneath. Must-never-change list: the layers are grown chitin biography, never assembled armour or artefacts; its authority is earned social standing, depicted with warmth and humour, never mystic machinery; no borrowed mask designs, names, or tribal motifs from any donor fiction.

species.name: Ratchetta
species.dexText: Ratchetta's fur grows in fine, regular ridges that click softly against each other as she moves, so a thoughtful Ratchetta sounds like something being carefully decided. She is one of the Gestalt three, and alone she is entirely herself — hunter, climber, critic. Combined, her body takes the head, forequarters, and directing role of Gestaltitan, a responsibility she accepts each time as though it had never been discussed, and disputes each time, afterwards, in detail.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-7 The Gestalt three — Ratchetta is the ratchet-furred cat of the combining trio, a small species who can, by agreement with Coilcoon and Dingbat, combine into Gestaltitan for exactly one job; donor mechanic: combining (gestalt) species, translated into a consensual merge of living creatures — separation and the argument afterwards are part of the species.
species.sizeClass: Small — a compact cat about the size of a sturdy housecat, dense with ridged fur and muscle.
species.temperament: Precise, proud, and argumentative in good faith; keeps the trio's standards and most of its grudges, all of them affectionate.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift rooftops, institute rafter spaces, and crossing scaffolds in the trio's shared home range, where all three component species live within calling distance.
species.dietBehaviour: A hunter of Rift rodents, large insects, and dropped rations, eating quickly and neatly; behaviour runs in trio rhythm — solo patrols, shared sunning scaffolds, and the combining agreement itself, a formal negotiation of job, duration, and whose posture leads, conducted at speed in cries and gestures before any merge is agreed.
species.evolution: No evolution; the form change is the combining, and it is never hers alone. By the trio's agreement — all three consenting, one job named — she merges with Coilcoon and Dingbat into Gestaltitan, her body forming its head, forequarters, and forelimbs, her ridged fur locking along the merge lines like a living seam. Separation is guaranteed by the agreement's shape: when the one job is done, the trio comes apart, and Ratchetta's first act as herself is reliably to open the argument about whose fault the posture was.
species.discovery: Region 4 trio home ranges around Rift crossings and institute roofs; rarity class uncommon solo, since observers usually meet the three together. Method: wild encounter by scaffold and rooftop at dusk, or by following the soft clicking of her moving fur. Conditions: most active at dusk and in dry weather; combines only for a named job, never for display. Level band in words: mid band. First-meeting note: first meetings are inspections — she will circle, click, and judge; being judged acceptable by Ratchetta is understood to be the trio's door opening.
species.cry: Source character — a clear cat cry set threaded with the soft clicking of her ridged fur, the clicks speeding and slowing with her certainty. Pitch contour in words: level, precise calls with neat rises at the ends of phrases. Duration class: short cries; long, detailed complaining strings after a separation. Rhythm pattern: measured, almost counted chirps and mews in negotiation; rapid click-chatter when a combine is proposed. Variations per state — idle: quiet mews under constant thoughtful clicking; call: a crisp summons the other two answer from their scaffolds; hurt: a sharp yowl and a full-body fur-lock, clicks stopping dead; faint: cries spacing out into silence as the ridges settle flat; affection: a purring churr with slow, contented clicking; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution — at the combine, her call is the count-in, fur-clicks rising to a final locking rattle as the merge lines close.
species.anatomyNotes: Four cat limbs with retractable claws and the trio's best climbing gear; forepaws are capable manipulators for grooming, pointing, and merge-alignment. Mouth is a cat's jaw, expressive in yowl and complaint. Locomotion: classic cat — stalk, sprint, vertical climb. The combine anatomy an animator must know: her spine extends the merge's axis, forequarters broaden as Gestaltitan's chest and arms, and her ridged fur is the visible seam tissue where bodies join — ridges grown, flexible, and alive, clicking with strain and alignment in the combined form.
species.paletteSeed: gunmetal grey, bright copper, cream, volt yellow
species.footprint: A precise solo trace: small four-toed cat pad prints, claws usually sheathed and invisible, in a neat alternating walk that breaks into bounding hunting patterns. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker, and the trio's signature in dust: her prints, Coilcoon's, and Dingbat's traces converge before a job site and are replaced beyond it by Gestaltitan's single great trail — three tidy lines becoming one.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — solo: a compact ridged cat, fur edges visibly toothed in outline, tail carried in precise curves; combined contribution: Gestaltitan's head, chest, and forelimbs, her cat profile still readable at the top of the tower. Proportions in words: solo, head and shoulders dominate; her ridge fur adds a fine serration to every edge. Key visual masses: ridged back, bright face, upright ears. What reads at sprite size: serrated-edged cat. Identifying negative space: the clean triangular gaps between her raised ridged fur and her tail curve when she is mid-argument.
species.statProfile: Quick, precise, and sharp-clawed solo, with modest defence; in the trio's shared profile she contributes Gestaltitan's aim, nerve, and forelimb work — see Gestaltitan's sheet for the combined picture. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A cat whose fur is a living ratchet of ridges, built to be one third of a tower. Key features are the clicking ridge fur, the proud directing posture, and merge seams that read as her fur locking home. Must-never-change list: the ridges are grown fur and body, never a mechanism she wears; combining is by her agreement, for one job, every time; alone she is a complete cat and a complete character, never a spare part waiting for assembly.

species.name: Coilcoon
species.dexText: Coilcoon's tail is one continuous, powerful coil of muscle, banded and bright, on which he bounces, hangs, climbs, and occasionally sleeps. He is the Gestalt three's foundation in every sense: combined, his body forms Gestaltitan's lower half and his tail its great counterbalancing spring. Alone, he is the trio's optimist and provisioner, first to find food, first to forgive the posture argument, and — the record notes — usually the one whose fault, by acclamation, the posture was.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-7 The Gestalt three — Coilcoon is the spring-tailed raccoon of the combining trio, who can, by agreement with Ratchetta and Dingbat, combine into Gestaltitan for exactly one job; donor mechanic: combining (gestalt) species, translated into a consensual living merge built, in his case, on a coiled muscular tail that becomes the combined form's engine of balance and lift.
species.sizeClass: Small — a round-bellied raccoon about the size of a well-fed housecat, with a tail that adds a second creature's worth of coil behind him.
species.temperament: Cheerful, unembarrassable, and resourceful; treats every setback as a bounce that hasn't happened yet.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift crossing markets, institute store-rooms and rafters, and riverbank scaffolds throughout the trio's shared home range.
species.dietBehaviour: A classic raccoon omnivore — fruit, eggs, shellfish, market leavings, all washed when water allows; behaviour is provisioning and play, punctuated by the combining agreement, in which his role is enthusiastic consent, practical questions about the one job, and immediate forgiveness scheduled in advance.
species.evolution: No evolution; the form change is the combining, held in common with the trio. By agreement — all three consenting, one job named — he merges with Ratchetta and Dingbat into Gestaltitan, his body forming its hips, legs, and spring-tail base, his coil becoming the combined form's balance and leap. When the job is done the trio separates without ceremony or residue, and Coilcoon characteristically bounces once, checks everyone is whole, and starts the argument fresh as a game.
species.discovery: Region 4 trio home ranges — crossing markets, institute stores, riverbank scaffolds; rarity class uncommon solo, common in trio company. Method: wild encounter at food-rich edges at dawn and dusk; a washing raccoon with a coiled tail is unmistakable. Conditions: active in most weather, happiest after rain when everything can be washed. Level band in words: mid band. First-meeting note: first meetings involve an offered, washed food item of mysterious origin; accepting it gracefully is the trio's second door.
species.cry: Source character — a bright raccoon chitter and chirr set over the soft boinging punctuation of his tail compressing and releasing. Pitch contour in words: bubbling, rising chitters; contentment sounds that descend in a happy slide with the tail's settle. Duration class: short notes in long sociable strings. Rhythm pattern: chitter bursts matched to bounces; a rolling chatter during combine negotiations. Variations per state — idle: washing churrs and occasional experimental bounces with their soft spring note; call: a ringing chitter answered by cat and bat from across the scaffolds; hurt: a sharp chirp and a full protective tail-wrap around himself; faint: chitters slowing into the tail's long final uncoiling sigh of sound; affection: purring chitters with the tail curled around a friend; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution — at the combine, his spring-note deepens through a rising compression creak into the locking boom that seats Gestaltitan's stance.
species.anatomyNotes: Four raccoon limbs with famously dexterous five-fingered forepaws — the trio's best hands — for washing, carrying, and merge-alignment gestures. Mouth is a masked raccoon's quick jaw, built for chittering and tasting. Locomotion: quadruped scurry, biped stands for work, and true bouncing travel on the coiled tail, which is a single muscular organ — grown spring in shape and function, with no metal in it — that compresses, stores, and releases his whole weight. Combine anatomy: hips and hindquarters broaden into Gestaltitan's base, tail anchors at the combined spine's foot as counterweight and spring; animators should keep his banded mask-face's cheer readable in negotiation close-ups even though his face is not the combined form's head.
species.paletteSeed: warm grey, banded cream, copper, volt yellow
species.footprint: A busy solo trace: small hand-like five-toed raccoon prints, fore and hind distinct, in a waddling alternating gait constantly interrupted by round coil-dents where the tail pressed, pushed, or bounced him onward — some stretches are tail-dents alone, prints airborne between them. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: his trail converges with Ratchetta's prints and Dingbat's traces before job sites, and Gestaltitan's great trail replaces all three beyond them.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — solo: a round raccoon dominated behind by the great circular coil of the tail, banded rings readable in outline; combined contribution: Gestaltitan's lower body and spring base, the coil still legible at the tower's foot. Proportions in words: belly and tail are the masses; head small and masked between clever paws. Key visual masses: tail coil first, belly second. What reads at sprite size: raccoon plus spring-ring tail. Identifying negative space: the perfect round hole at the centre of the tail coil — the trio's most recognisable gap.
species.statProfile: Hardy, dexterous, and surprisingly strong in the legs and tail, with modest speed afoot and excellent bounce mobility; in the trio's shared profile he contributes Gestaltitan's stance, lift, and endurance — see Gestaltitan's sheet for the combined picture. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A raccoon whose tail is a living spring and whose role is the foundation. Key features are the coiled muscular tail with its central round gap, the banded mask face, and washer's hands. Must-never-change list: the spring is muscle grown in a coil, never a metal part; he is a complete, cheerful animal alone, never a component awaiting use; combining is by his agreement, for one job, and separation always restores him exactly himself.

species.name: Dingbat
species.dexText: Dingbat's body is shaped like a bell and sounds like one — a clear, carrying tone rings softly from her chest whenever she lands, launches, or is startled, which in the Rift is treated as a small public service. She is the Gestalt three's wings and voice: combined, her body sets into Gestaltitan's chest as its resonant bell-core and her wings spread from its back. Alone she is a dreamy, echo-guided night hunter who navigates the crossings by a world made entirely of returning sound.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-7 The Gestalt three — Dingbat is the bell-bodied bat of the combining trio, who can, by agreement with Ratchetta and Coilcoon, combine into Gestaltitan for exactly one job; donor mechanic: combining (gestalt) species, translated into a consensual living merge in which her hollow, resonant body becomes the combined form's chest bell and her wings its flight and balance planes.
species.sizeClass: Small — a plump bat about the size of a small kettle when roosting, most of her roundness being the hollow bell of her body.
species.temperament: Dreamy, musical, and unbothered; the trio's calm centre, whose response to the posture argument is usually a single bell note and sleep.
species.habitat: Region 4 Rift bell-towers, institute belfries and rafter vaults, and scaffold roosts across the trio's shared home range, active over all of it by night.
species.dietBehaviour: A hunter of Rift night insects and moths (the unbonded, ordinary kind), taken on the wing by echolocation; behaviour is nocturnal patrol, communal roosting near the other two, and combine negotiations in which her consent is given — characteristically — as one clear bell tone for yes, and silence, pointedly sustained, for no.
species.evolution: No evolution; the form change is the combining, shared by the trio. By agreement — all three consenting, her bell-note of yes included — she merges with Ratchetta and Coilcoon into Gestaltitan, her body seating as its chest bell-core and her wings becoming its back-spread balance and gliding planes. When the one job is done, the trio separates, and Dingbat's first act as herself is to ring once, softly, like a meeting adjourned.
species.discovery: Region 4 trio home ranges — towers, belfries, and scaffold roosts; rarity class uncommon, and an encounter is usually heard before it is seen. Method: wild encounter at roosts at dusk emergence; listen for landing bells around crossings. Conditions: nocturnal; shelters through Rift storms in deep rafters with the trio. Level band in words: mid band. First-meeting note: first meetings happen upside down — address the roosting bell politely, wait for an answering tone, and understand that the trio's third door has opened.
species.cry: Source character — a true bell tone from the hollow chest, pure and carrying, layered with a small bat's squeaks and echolocation clicks pitched for the trio's ears. Pitch contour in words: the bell note is level and sustained with a slow natural decay; squeaks rise in quick arcs between notes. Duration class: bell notes are the longest single sounds of any component; squeaks very short. Rhythm pattern: navigation click-trains in flight; single ceremonial bell notes for decisions. Variations per state — idle: soft half-asleep bell sighs when the roost shifts; call: one full bell tone that Ratchetta and Coilcoon answer at once; hurt: a cracked, flat bell note and frantic squeaks, wings folding tight; faint: the bell note decaying far beyond its usual length as she settles; affection: a warm, muted bell hum against a roost-mate; evolution / form-change moment: no evolution — at the combine, her bell provides the merge's keynote, a rising resonant tone under Ratchetta's count-in and Coilcoon's seating boom, resolving into Gestaltitan's first deep chord.
species.anatomyNotes: Two true wings with finger-strutted membranes and thumb-claws that serve as her manipulators for roosting and merge-alignment; two small hind feet built for hanging. Mouth is a small bat muzzle; the sound organ is the hollow chest — a resonant body cavity with a visible throat-and-belly vibration, grown, sonorous, and entirely flesh and bone. Locomotion: true flight, and an awkward, charming waddle on wing-thumbs when grounded. Combine anatomy: torso anchors at Gestaltitan's chest with the bell cavity forward, wings re-root at the combined back without tearing or folding unnaturally — animators should trace wing position continuously through merge and separation so her contribution reads as her body arriving, not equipment attaching.
species.paletteSeed: dusk purple, warm bronze, cream, volt yellow
species.footprint: She leaves almost no footprint and a rich trace instead: on the ground, only the paired pinprick dents of wing-thumb claws and tiny hind-foot ticks where she has waddled, widely spaced and soon abandoned for flight; her true trace is acoustic and aerial — bell-tone landing marks recorded by locals, plus a soft scatter of insect wings beneath feeding roosts. Print size class: negligible. Distinctive marker: her trace joins the others' trails at roost bases — cat prints and coil-dents circle a tower whose ground shows almost nothing of her, and beyond the job site, Gestaltitan's trail replaces all three.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — roosting: a hanging bell with folded wings, round and still; in flight: a plump round body carried between wide scalloped wings; combined contribution: Gestaltitan's chest bell and back wings, her roundness visible at the tower's heart. Proportions in words: body one round mass, wings twice its width spread, ears small above a dreamy face. Key visual masses: bell body, wing pair. What reads at sprite size: bell with wings. Identifying negative space: the scalloped gaps along the wing trailing edges, and, roosting, the clean crescent between her bell rim and the beam.
species.statProfile: Fragile solo and not built for ground contests, with excellent flight, perception by sound, and a bell that coordinates the trio; in the shared profile she contributes Gestaltitan's balance, glide, and voice — see Gestaltitan's sheet for the combined picture. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A bat shaped and sounded like a bell. Key features are the hollow resonant bell body, scalloped wings, and a dreamy upside-down resting life. Must-never-change list: the bell is her living body — grown cavity, bone, and flesh — never a metal object she wears; her consent, given or withheld in bell tones, is the trio's law like the others'; alone she is a complete hunter and character, never a part in storage.

species.name: Gestaltitan
species.stageNote: combined form of Ratchetta, Coilcoon, and Dingbat
species.dexText: Gestaltitan exists the way a decision exists — briefly, on purpose, and because three friends agreed. When a job in the Rift is too big for any of them — a beam to lift, a crossing to hold, a lost traveller to reach — Ratchetta, Coilcoon, and Dingbat negotiate, consent, and combine into one towering titan: cat-headed and clever-armed, raccoon-based and spring-planted, bell-chested and wing-balanced. The job is done with a coordination witnesses describe as three arguments conducted at the speed of one thought. Then, always, they separate — and argue about whose fault the posture was.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C1-7 The Gestalt three — Gestaltitan is the towering combined form of Ratchetta, Coilcoon, and Dingbat, merged by agreement for exactly one job and separated afterwards, argument included; donor mechanic: combining (gestalt) species, the R4 signature move, translated into a consensual merge of three complete living creatures into one temporary, towering person.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a towering figure when combined, head in the institute's rafters, built from three small species who remain, inside the scale, entirely themselves.
species.temperament: A negotiated temperament — Ratchetta's precision, Coilcoon's cheer, and Dingbat's calm in continuous, audible committee; heroic in effect, domestic in process, and funnier than any titan has a right to be.
species.habitat: Wherever the trio's Region 4 home range presents a job of its size — Rift crossings, institute construction and rescue sites, riverbanks in flood season; Gestaltitan has no separate habitat, because Gestaltitan is a visit the trio pays to a problem.
species.dietBehaviour: Gestaltitan does not eat — a combine lasts for exactly one job, and meals belong to the separated lives before negotiation and after separation, where the trio characteristically eats the job's thank-you feast together and re-opens the posture argument over it. Behaviour in form is single-minded: arrive, align, do the one job with enormous care for bystanders, finish, and come apart.
species.evolution: No evolution; the form change is the merge, and this sheet carries its full description. The merge: on unanimous agreement to one named job, the three align — Coilcoon plants and compresses as the base, hips, legs, and spring-tail; Dingbat rises and seats as the chest, bell-core forward, wings spreading to the back; Ratchetta crowns the merge as head, forequarters, and forelimbs — their bodies joining along grown merge seams, Ratchetta's ridge fur locking the lines, every seam living tissue in continuity. Within the form they remain three minds in fast, constant negotiation. The separation is equally the design: the job done, consent lapses by its own terms, the seams unridged in reverse order — wings folding home, base uncoiling, cat dropping clear — and three small species stand in the dust, whole, themselves, and already arguing about the posture.
species.discovery: Region 4 job sites within the trio's range — crossings under repair, institute works, flood banks; rarity class very rare as an encounter, because it exists only mid-job. Method: wild encounter is really witness — meet the trio first, in their home range, and be present, usefully, when a job of the right size appears. Conditions: fair working weather preferred by Ratchetta, any weather accepted by Coilcoon, night jobs lit by Dingbat's echo and the site's lamps. Level band in words: high band while combined — the form's effective presence far exceeds any component's. First-meeting note: do not address Gestaltitan as a stranger; greet the three by name, in order, and state the job or hold your peace — a first meeting with the titan is a job interview conducted by a committee.
species.cry: Source character — a three-part chord: Ratchetta's clear cat call, Coilcoon's chittering undertow, and Dingbat's bell as the resonant core, voiced in near-unison with split-second disagreements audible as shimmer in the chord. Pitch contour in words: bell low and level at the centre, cat voice riding above in precise phrases, raccoon chatter filling the middle. Duration class: long, sustained calls; working sounds are continuous committee murmur. Rhythm pattern: count-ins, confirmations, and corrections in rapid rotation while working — a rhythm witnesses learn to follow like music. Variations per state — idle: no true idle exists in form; waiting is low murmured negotiation; call: the full chord, unmistakable across a crossing; hurt: the chord fractures into the three voices checking each other, bell first, before any response to the harm itself; faint: not a faint in the usual sense — distress forces an early separation, the chord resolving downward into three small exhausted voices; affection: rare and famous, the chord softening into harmony entirely by accident, denied by all three afterwards; evolution / form-change moment: the combine call itself — count-in, compression boom, bell keynote, locking rattle — resolving into the titan's first chord, and the separation's reverse sequence ending in three separate cries and the opening of the argument.
species.anatomyNotes: A towering bipedal composite: Ratchetta provides the head, neck, chest-frame, and forelimbs (cat paws scaled as the form's hands, claws for grip and climb); Dingbat provides the chest bell-core set into that frame and both wings, re-rooted at the back as balance and gliding planes; Coilcoon provides hips, legs, feet, and the great coiled tail-spring anchoring balance and absorbing landings. Mouths: the speaking and crying face is Ratchetta's, with Dingbat's bell resonating through the chest and Coilcoon's chitter audible in effort; animators must keep all three presences continuously readable — eye-lines, bell vibration, tail tension — so the titan always performs as a committee, not a single giant. Locomotion: planted spring-assisted strides, short glides on Dingbat's wings between Coilcoon's leaps, and absolutely no solo-hero posing that forgets the base is a raccoon concentrating. Merge and separation sequences must preserve body continuity for all three — paths traced, seams locking and unlocking in the stated order, no part appearing or vanishing.
species.paletteSeed: gunmetal grey, warm grey, dusk purple, copper and bronze, volt yellow
species.footprint: A combined trace utterly unlike any component's: very large oval sole prints in a deliberate bipedal gait, each print showing a broad raccoon-foot base pattern at scale with a deep circular coil-dent behind the heel where the spring-tail planted, and, at pauses, a soft radiating scuff where Dingbat's wings steadied the mass. Print size class: huge. Distinctive marker: the trail begins and ends in the dust of a job site where three small trails — cat prints, coil-dents, and almost nothing at all — converge, become this single great trail for exactly one job's distance, and diverge again into three, with a churned patch of small prints at the separation point that locals read as the argument's duration.
species.silhouette: Outline class per form — combined only: a towering stepped figure — spring coil at the base, bell curve at the chest, cat head and ears at the crown, wings as a scalloped mantle behind. Proportions in words: legs and coil give the lower third its planted width, chest bell the middle's roundness, head small and precise at the top — three small species' proportions honestly stacked, never smoothed into a generic giant. Key visual masses: tail coil, bell chest, wing mantle, cat head. What reads at sprite size: tower with coil base, bell middle, ears on top. Identifying negative space: the round hole of Coilcoon's coil at the base and the scalloped gaps along Dingbat's wing edges, both surviving at full scale — the components' signatures visible inside the titan.
species.statProfile: Combined profile: very high strength and reach from the merge, high resilience while alignment holds, and speed that is spring-and-glide bursts rather than running; its limiting stat is coordination — a trio in disagreement is a titan standing still, which the record counts, correctly, as a safety feature. — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Three friends, visibly and honestly stacked into a titan for one job. Key features are the stacked silhouettes with every component readable, the grown merge seams locked by ridge fur, and a posture that is always slightly negotiated. Must-never-change list: combining is always by unanimous agreement, for exactly one job, and separation — with the argument about the posture — always follows and is part of the species, not a footnote; Gestaltitan is three creatures in cooperation, never a machine assembled from parts and never a new fourth creature who replaces them; no component is diminished, dormant, or used — all three are present, deciding, and themselves throughout.

species.name: Capup
species.dexText: Born already calm, Capup dozes half-submerged at the water's edge while the bank bustles around it. Other small creatures instinctively settle against its warm side, and a sleeping Capup is rarely sleeping alone.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-1 — a capybara pup that is born unbothered; the real animal is the capybara (✓ verified open, no official Pokémon based on it).
species.sizeClass: Small — roughly a plump loaf a child could carry in both arms, low to the ground
species.temperament: Serene, unbothered, socially magnetic in the quietest possible way.
species.habitat: Warm riverbanks, reed beds, and slow shallows in Region 4's low wetlands.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes bank grasses and soft water plants in long, unhurried bouts; spends much of the day soaking, only its head and back above the surface. Never hurries away from company.
species.evolution: Evolves as its calm deepens — measured, in local saying, by how many other species are asleep on it.
species.discovery: Region 4 low wetlands and riverbank clearings; rarity class: common; method: walk along banks / shallows edge, daytime; conditions: warm, still water nearby; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: usually found already asleep with something smaller asleep on top of it.
species.cry: Source character: soft, breathy pup squeaks and contented huffs, never startled-sounding. Pitch contour: low and flat, a gentle rise only on the call. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: single notes spaced wide, or a drowsy double-huff. Variations — idle: slow huff-snore; call: soft rising squeak; hurt: brief surprised chirp, immediately settling; faint: sighing exhale trailing off; affection: low purring chatter through the teeth; evolution moment: a long, placid yawn-cry that makes nearby listeners yawn too.
species.anatomyNotes: Four short, sturdy legs; broad blunt muzzle, no visible fangs; no tail to speak of; locomotion is a steady waddle on land and a slow paddle in water; head sits low and heavy — animators should sell weight and stillness, not bounce.
species.paletteSeed: warm tan, river-mud brown, reed green, cream belly
species.footprint: Print shape class: blunt four-toed forefeet and three-toed hindfeet, toes slightly splayed for soft ground. Toe/claw count and arrangement: short, hoof-like nails in a neat front arc, no deep claw gouges. Gait pattern: alternating walk, prints in two close parallel lines. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: prints often end abruptly at the waterline where it slipped in to soak, and bank prints are frequently overwritten by the tiny prints of whatever was following it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: low, rounded rectangle — a loaf with a blunt head. Proportions in words: long body, short legs barely lifting the belly, head almost as wide as it is long. Key visual masses: one continuous back line from nose to rump with no neck break. What reads at sprite size: the flat top line and half-lidded head. Identifying negative space: almost none — the silhouette is deliberately solid; only the small gaps under the belly between the short legs break it.
species.statProfile: Slow, bulky for its stage, and exceptionally steady — a small wall whose defence is that nothing wants to disturb it — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A compact, loaf-bodied capybara pup with a broad blunt muzzle, half-lidded eyes, and short legs, reading instantly as calm. Must-never-change: the unbroken flat back that other creatures nap against, the blunt rectangular head, and the total absence of hurry or menace in the pose.

species.name: Chillbara
species.dexText: Chillbara's calm is contagious: things near it slow down and mean it. It takes up its place at the bank like a grandfather taking his chair, and by dusk its back is a dormitory of smaller species, all sleeping in a row.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-1 — the waterbank's self-appointed grandfather, a warm island every small creature naps against; the real animal is the capybara (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Medium — a broad, low island of an animal, large enough for several small creatures to sleep across its back at once
species.temperament: Grandfatherly, permissive, immovable in the kindest sense; its signature calm settles everything around it.
species.habitat: Established riverbanks, warm pools, and reed clearings where many species come to rest.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes coarse bank grasses for long stretches, soaks for hours with only eyes and ears above water, and tolerates — appears to welcome — being climbed on, nested on, and slept against.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 riverbank rest-clearings and warm pool margins; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, daytime, often located by finding the cluster of sleeping species first; conditions: calm weather, established bank; level band in words: mid wild band; first-meeting note: approach slowly — not for its sake, but because everything asleep on it will wake if you rush.
species.cry: Source character: deep, slow huffs, soft tooth-chatter purrs, and a low contented grunt. Pitch contour: low, mostly level, sinking at the end of phrases. Duration class: short-to-medium, unhurried. Rhythm pattern: widely spaced single notes; a slow chatter when pleased.
