Variations — idle: deep breathing huffs bordering on snores; call: low grunt repeated patiently; hurt: one startled bark, then calm reasserting; faint: a long settling sigh as it lies down; affection: sustained soft tooth-purr; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage — its arrival cry on first meeting a Ranger is the same low, welcoming grunt.
species.anatomyNotes: Four column-short legs, massive blunt head, barrel torso with a long flat dorsal plane — the back must animate as a stable platform; locomotion is a deliberate plod and a smooth, barely rippling swim; jaw works side-to-side when grazing.
species.paletteSeed: deep warm brown, tan, moss green on the wet lower body, grey-brown muzzle
species.footprint: Print shape class: blunt four-toed foreprints and three-toed hindprints, deeper and wider than Capup's. Toe/claw count and arrangement: short hoof-like nails, splayed on mud. Gait pattern: slow alternating walk, short stride, prints often surrounded by a scatter of much smaller species' prints converging on the same spot. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: the resting hollow — a broad, smooth, body-shaped depression in bank grass beside the prints where it lay and others piled on.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long, low, flat-topped island shape. Proportions in words: very long torso, short legs, huge blunt head carried level with the back. Key visual masses: the unbroken dorsal plateau is the whole read. What reads at sprite size: flat top, blunt front, sheer stillness. Identifying negative space: minimal — small notches under the belly only; the solid mass IS the identity.
species.statProfile: Slow and very bulky, a true wall with calming presence; offence is an afterthought — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A big, flat-backed capybara rendered as a living piece of bank furniture — warm, broad, and sleepy-eyed, with room on its back for the region to nap. Must-never-change: the flat dormitory back, the grandfatherly blunt head, and calm as a physical, contagious quality rather than an expression.

species.name: Punchrimp
species.dexText: Punchrimp lives in a burrow in the rock and settles every argument with one punch so fast the water in front of its fist briefly boils. It is very small, entirely aware of this, and completely untroubled by it.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Pokémon's Clauncher / Clawitzer is a *pistol* shrimp — a different animal with a different mechanism (§5.3). Punchrimp is a *mantis* shrimp: raptorial striking limbs, not a snapping claw. The distinction must survive every design and animation pass.
species.lineConcept: C2-2 — a thumb-sized shrimp whose punch boils the water in front of it; the real animal is the mantis shrimp (✓ verified open — distinct from the pistol shrimp, see Flags).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — thumb-sized in the source's own words, a curled spark of a shrimp
species.temperament: Bold, quick-tempered, territorial about its burrow mouth.
species.habitat: Rocky shallows, reef rubble, and Rift-touched tidal pools in Region 4.
species.dietBehaviour: An ambush hunter of small shelled prey, smashing shells from its burrow entrance; spends the rest of its time tidying the burrow and challenging passers-by many times its size.
species.evolution: Evolves as its punch and its colours develop together — the brawler grows into its rainbow.
species.discovery: Region 4 tidal pools and rocky shallows; rarity class: uncommon; method: water-edge / shallow wading, daytime; conditions: clear, sunlit shallows where burrow mouths are visible; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: often detected by a tiny, sharp *snap-boil* and a puff of disturbed sand before it is seen.
species.cry: Source character: not a voice so much as a punctuation — sharp clicks and snaps made with its striking limbs, plus a faint bubbling hiss when the punch boils water. Pitch contour: high, flat, percussive. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: single warning clicks, then a rapid-fire burst when committed. Variations — idle: occasional single click; call: paired clicks, challenge rhythm; hurt: frantic clicking rattle; faint: clicks slowing and stopping; affection: soft, slow clicking against a trusted shell or stone; evolution moment: one outsized boom-click with a visible boil-burst.
species.anatomyNotes: Segmented curled body; the signature organ is the pair of folded raptorial striking limbs under the head — they must read as cocked hammers that unfold faster than the eye; stalked eyes that move independently; swimmerets under the tail fan; locomotion is burrow-crawling and short backward flick-swims.
species.paletteSeed: jewel green, orange, electric blue accents, sand-pale underside
species.footprint: Water-trace instead of a land print: a burrow signature — a neat round hole in sand or rubble ringed with tiny excavated pellets, plus, after a strike, a scorched-clean semicircle of disturbed sand and a brief trail of micro-bubbles. Gait equivalent: no trackway; it holds position at the burrow mouth. Distinctive marker: the perfectly kept burrow entrance with shell fragments of opened prey stacked beside it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a curled comma with a cocked fist. Proportions in words: large head section, body curling tightly under, tail fan tucked. Key visual masses: the folded strikers under the front and the stalked eyes above it. What reads at sprite size: the curl, the eyes on stalks, the raised striker pair. Identifying negative space: the clear gap inside the body curl and the notch between the two folded strikers.
species.statProfile: Tiny, fast, and disproportionately hard-hitting for its size, but frail if actually caught — a glass striker — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A thumb-sized mantis shrimp, curled and cocky, with stalked swivelling eyes and visibly folded hammer-limbs. Must-never-change: the punch mechanism reads as a mantis shrimp's raptorial strike (never a claw that shoots or a pistol snap — see Flags), the independent stalked eyes, and the jewel-bright hint of the rainbow to come.

species.name: Rainbrawler
species.dexText: Rainbrawler sees colours nobody else in the region can, and describes them, patiently, to anyone who sits still. Between descriptions it remains a brawler: its punch still boils the water, and its burrow is still its castle.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Same distinction as Punchrimp: Clauncher / Clawitzer is a *pistol* shrimp (§5.3). Rainbrawler is a *mantis* shrimp — verified distinct and open (C2-2). Never give it a shooting claw.
species.lineConcept: C2-2 — wearing the full rainbow carapace, seeing colours nobody else in the region can; the real animal is the mantis shrimp (✓ verified open — distinct from the pistol shrimp, see Flags).
species.sizeClass: Small — still a shrimp, but a substantial one; a two-handed lift, all muscle and armour
species.temperament: Patient explainer and proud fighter in equal measure; gentle with listeners, absolute with challengers.
species.habitat: Reef edges, rock burrows, and clear Rift pools where the light is good.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts shelled prey with shell-shattering strikes; otherwise holds court at its burrow, turning its stalked eyes on visitors and — in cries and gestures — holding forth about colours only it can see.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 reef burrows and clear Rift pools; rarity class: rare; method: water-edge / shallow wading, bright daytime; conditions: strong clear light — it comes out to look at the light; level band in words: mid-to-high wild band; first-meeting note: it will study a new Ranger for a long moment with both eye-stalks before deciding between a display and a punch.
species.cry: Source character: resonant clicks and snaps, deeper than Punchrimp's, with rolling bubbling flourishes during displays. Pitch contour: percussive base with a surprisingly melodic rise-and-fall in display sequences. Duration class: short notes in longer conversations. Rhythm pattern: deliberate, almost speech-like phrasing — bursts, pauses, bursts — cries only, never words. Variations — idle: slow contemplative clicks; call: full rolling display sequence; hurt: hard rapid snaps; faint: a final dignified single click; affection: soft paired clicks offered like a gift; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Full segmented carapace as rainbow armour plates; raptorial strikers larger and more ornate, unfolding in a blur; stalked eyes are the most expressive feature — independent swivels, tilts, and slow blinks must carry its personality; tail fan strong for retreat flicks.
species.paletteSeed: full rainbow carapace — saturated red, orange, green, blue, and violet bands over a jewel base
species.footprint: Water-trace instead of a land print: a grander burrow signature — a wide, swept-clean arena in front of the burrow mouth, shell trophies arranged around it, and boil-scoured sand where strikes have landed. Distinctive marker: the arena is kept immaculate and rainbow shell fragments are sorted, not scattered.
species.silhouette: Outline class: an armoured curl, taller and prouder than Punchrimp, strikers raised like a boxer's guard. Proportions in words: big front section, arched segmented back, eye-stalks held high. Key visual masses: the rainbow back plates and the raised guard. What reads at sprite size: rainbow banding, stalked eyes, boxing-guard front. Identifying negative space: the gap between the raised strikers and the arch of the back, and the inside of the tail curl.
species.statProfile: Fast and very hard-hitting with strong senses; defence middling, endurance modest — it ends fights early — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A mantis shrimp as a rainbow-armoured prizefighter-philosopher: full spectrum carapace, high stalked eyes, strikers held in a guard. Must-never-change: the mantis (not pistol) strike anatomy, the full rainbow shell, and the patient, seeing-more-than-you expression in the eyes.

species.name: Tunlet
species.dexText: Tunlet is a water bear the size of a cub, with a barrel body and a permanently unbothered smile. Drought, frost, or the Rift's weird weather — its answer to all of it is the same: curl into its tun, and wait for a better century.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-3 — a microscopic-class water bear rendered at Mochi scale whose answer to every extreme is to curl into its tun form and wait; the real animal is the tardigrade (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a plump barrel-bodied bear-cub of a thing, low and round
species.temperament: Cheerful, patient to an inhuman degree, impossible to panic.
species.habitat: Moss beds, damp bark, puddle edges — and, in tun form, absolutely anywhere in Region 4, for as long as it takes.
species.dietBehaviour: Sups at mosses and the juices of tiny plants with a slow, contented graze; at the first sign of true extremes it withdraws its legs, rounds itself into the tun, and sleeps through whatever comes.
species.evolution: The line's evolution is a rumour other species tell — Tunlet is said to become Tardigreat simply by still being there when the waiting ends.
species.discovery: Region 4 moss beds, damp forest floor, and puddle margins; rarity class: uncommon (common in tun form, if you know what you're looking at); method: walk, any weather — in extreme weather search for tuns, not bears; conditions: none, which is rather the point; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: a first meeting may be with a tun — a dry little barrel that wakes, blinking, when the weather improves or a Ranger waits with it.
species.cry: Source character: tiny, round, contented squeaks — a bear-cub voice in miniature. Pitch contour: mid and gently domed, rising with pleasure, never spiking in fear. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: slow singles; a sleepy repeated peep as it settles into the tun. Variations — idle: soft wandering squeaks while grazing; call: a slightly louder, friendly peep; hurt: one squeezed squeak, then the tun response begins; faint: it does not so much faint as tun — a descending, satisfied sigh-peep as it curls; affection: warm, rapid little chuckle-peeps; evolution moment: the same cry, unchanged in character, emerging from a much larger barrel.
species.anatomyNotes: Plump barrel torso; four pairs of short stubby legs ending in tiny claws, all of which retract in the tun transformation; small round head with a blunt snout and no visible neck; locomotion is a slow, ambling, bear-like waddle; the tun form is a smooth, leg-less barrel — animators must make the curl-in read as cosy, not distressed.
species.paletteSeed: dusty rose, soft tan, moss green accents, cream face
species.footprint: Print shape class: tiny round pads in four paired rows — eight little prints per step cycle, each with minute claw ticks at the front. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four stubby toes' worth of claw marks clustered tight. Gait pattern: slow amble, prints in paired left-right bundles, trail often wandering in graze-curves through moss. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the trail simply stops where the tun formed, replaced by a single smooth barrel-roll impression in the moss.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a plump barrel on stubs, smiling. Proportions in words: body far wider than the legs are long; head a small rounding of the front, not a separate mass. Key visual masses: the barrel itself. What reads at sprite size: roundness, stub legs, contented face. Identifying negative space: tiny gaps between the paired stub legs under the belly; in tun form, none at all — a perfect sealed barrel.
species.statProfile: Extremely hardy and enduring beyond all proportion to its size; slow, weak-hitting, and in no hurry to be anything else — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A plump, barrel-bodied water-bear cub with four pairs of stubby clawed legs and a serene smile, built to curl into a smooth tun. Must-never-change: the barrel proportions, the eight stub legs, the tun as a smiling act of patience — and never make it look like an insect.

species.name: Tardigreat
species.dexText: Tardigreat is not stronger than Tunlet was. It is simply still there — after the drought, after the frost, after the Rift's worst weather, the same smile uncurls from the same tun, in a considerably larger barrel.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-3 — not stronger than the pup; simply still there; the real animal is the tardigrade (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Medium — the same barrel bear, grown great: a broad, low mass a Ranger could lean against
species.temperament: Monumentally patient, gently amused by everything, including history.
species.habitat: The oldest moss banks and stone hollows of Region 4; in tun form, wherever it happened to be when the century turned bad.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes moss and damp greenery at a geological pace; weathers every extreme in tun form; other species shelter against it in storms the way they shelter against a hill.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further. Its evolution remains, officially, a rumour other species tell.
species.discovery: Region 4 old-growth moss banks and weather-beaten hollows; rarity class: rare; method: walk — or find a tun and wait; conditions: post-extreme-weather moments are when it uncurls and can be met awake; level band in words: high wild band; first-meeting note: locals may insist the one you found has always been there, and decline to say since when.
species.cry: Source character: Tunlet's round squeak grown into a deep, slow, barrel-resonant hum-cry, still cheerful. Pitch contour: low and domed, unhurried. Duration class: medium — it takes its time. Rhythm pattern: single long notes, widely spaced; a slow settling sequence as the tun forms. Variations — idle: low grazing hums; call: a deep, carrying peep that sounds oddly small for its size, then doesn't; hurt: a grunt, followed by unhurried curling; faint: the tun sigh, enormous and content; affection: warm resonant chuckling through the whole barrel; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Same body plan at great scale: barrel torso, four pairs of thick stub legs with claws, blunt smiling head, full retraction into a vast smooth tun; locomotion is a slow, weighty amble — every step should land; in storms, animate it as landscape, not as a creature bracing.
species.paletteSeed: weathered rose-brown, stone tan, deep moss green, cream face
species.footprint: Print shape class: broad round pads in four paired rows, pressed deep. Toe/claw count and arrangement: stub claw ticks, widely set, at each pad's front. Gait pattern: slow amble, paired bundles, long wandering graze-trails that may be interrupted by a tun impression and resume — in some trails, on the far side of a visibly older patch of ground. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: trails that stop for a season and start again from the same barrel-roll hollow.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a great barrel — a hill with a smile. Proportions in words: immense width, legs almost lost under the mass, head a gentle front rounding. Key visual masses: one. What reads at sprite size: the barrel, the smile, the stubs. Identifying negative space: almost none; in tun form, a perfectly sealed, featureless barrel silhouette.
species.statProfile: Among the hardiest profiles in the bucket in words — endurance and bulk first, speed last, offence modest; it wins by remaining — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Tunlet's exact body plan, scaled to greatness: a vast, smiling barrel-bear whose power is persistence. Must-never-change: no added armour, weapons, or menace — its greatness is only size and survival; the tun must remain a smooth, cosy barrel at this scale too.

species.name: Tapaye
species.dexText: Tapaye spends the night tapping dead wood with its thin, ball-jointed finger, listening through ears like two open doors for what moves inside. By day it sleeps curled in the dark, one ear still half-open.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-4 — a night forager that taps dead wood with its thin ball-jointed finger and listens with ears like two open doors; the real animal is the aye-aye (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a crouched, big-eared night pup, mostly ears and eyes
species.temperament: Gentle, curious, utterly nocturnal; startles at daylight bustle, fearless in the dark.
species.habitat: Dead trees, hollow logs, and the deep shade of Region 4's night woods — the Dark Forest's counterpart country one region over.
species.dietBehaviour: Finds grubs and insects by tap-listening: tap, listen, hook them out with the same thin finger. Forages alone, in silence broken only by its own tapping.
species.evolution: The finger lengthens; the listening deepens.
species.discovery: Region 4 night woods and dead-tree groves; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, night only; conditions: darkness and quiet — it avoids lantern-lit paths; level band in words: early-to-mid wild band; first-meeting note: you will hear it before you see it — a soft, patient *tap… tap…* from inside a dead tree.
species.cry: Source character: small, dry clicks of the tapping finger form the percussion; the voice itself is a soft, breathy squeak, rarely used. Pitch contour: mid-high and tentative, falling at the end. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: voice comes in singles; the tapping carries the rhythm — slow, probing, irregular. Variations — idle: near-silence with occasional tap sequences; call: a hushed squeak repeated twice; hurt: sharp squeak and immediate stillness; faint: a tiny sigh as it curls tight; affection: soft squeak plus gentle tapping against the trusted person's hand or boot; evolution moment: the tapping slows, deepens, and the cry drops in pitch mid-sequence.
species.anatomyNotes: The signature organ is the thin middle finger with a ball joint — it must articulate independently, tapping and hooking; enormous thin ears that swivel and tilt separately; large forward eyes for night vision; crouched quadruped posture with grasping feet; locomotion is a careful climb and a low scurry, never a daytime bound.
species.paletteSeed: charcoal brown, ash grey, pale amber eyes, pink-grey ear membranes
species.footprint: Print shape class: grasping hand-like prints — long finger marks radiating from a small palm pad, hind prints showing an opposable toe angled inward. Toe/claw count and arrangement: five long digits, the middle one conspicuously thinner and longer in the foreprint. Gait pattern: crouched walk, prints close and overlapping around tree bases rather than in travel lines. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: foreprints circling dead trunks, paired with tiny tap-pits in the bark directly above them.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a crouch crowned by two huge ear-sails. Proportions in words: ears nearly as tall as the body is long, body low and hunched, tail a modest brush behind. Key visual masses: the ears dominate; the thin finger reads only in close view. What reads at sprite size: ear pair, big eyes, hunched back. Identifying negative space: the clear V between the two upright ears and the gap under the crouched belly.
species.statProfile: Frail and quiet, with senses far beyond its size — finds what hides, avoids what fights — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A gentle night pup defined by two enormous ears and one impossibly thin, ball-jointed tapping finger. Must-never-change: the ears-like-open-doors read, the specialised thin finger (never a claw, never a wand), and a kind — never sinister — expression despite the Umbral typing.

species.name: Ayeerie
species.dexText: Ayeerie is universally believed to be a ghost by species who haven't met one. Those who have describe a huge-eyed, gentle listener who taps the dead trees all night, keeping count of everything that stirs inside the wood.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-4 — the Dark Forest's counterpart one region over: huge-eyed, gentle, and universally believed to be a ghost; the real animal is the aye-aye (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Medium — a long, low night shape, taller at the ears than anything else in its woods
species.temperament: Serene, solitary, and kind; completely indifferent to its ghostly reputation.
species.habitat: The deepest dead-tree stands and hollow groves of Region 4's night country.
species.dietBehaviour: A master tap-forager: the lengthened finger and deepened listening let it map a whole trunk's hidden life before it ever breaks the bark. Moves through the canopy and the dark floor with equal, silent care.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 deep night woods, dead-tree stands; rarity class: rare; method: walk, deep night only; conditions: moonless or dim nights favour it; lantern light drives it back; level band in words: mid-to-high wild band; first-meeting note: most first meetings begin as a ghost story — two huge eyes and two ear-sails in the dark, resolving, on patience, into a gentle animal tapping a tree.
species.cry: Source character: a soft, low, breathy cry — almost a sigh with pitch — over the constant dry percussion of tapping. Pitch contour: low, slow rise and fall, eerie only in its quietness. Duration class: short-to-medium. Rhythm pattern: long silences between single cries; tapping sequences long, patient, and irregular. Variations — idle: tapping with no voice at all for long stretches; call: one low sigh-cry answered, sometimes, from another part of the wood; hurt: a thin wail, genuinely unsettling, then silence and retreat; faint: a descending sigh as it folds into a hollow; affection: soft breathy notes while tapping gently near the trusted person; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Elongated ball-jointed middle finger — the line's signature, now long and precise; ears even larger, thin and mobile, catching light at their membranes; huge reflective eyes; long low body with grasping hands and feet; locomotion is silent climbing and deliberate, finger-testing steps on the ground.
species.paletteSeed: deep charcoal, silver-grey, moon-pale ear membranes, luminous amber eyes
species.footprint: Print shape class: long-fingered grasping prints, larger and more splayed than Tapaye's. Toe/claw count and arrangement: five digits, the foreprint's middle digit dramatically longer and thinner, often pressed deeper — it leans on the listening finger. Gait pattern: slow, deliberate, prints spaced like a stalk, circling trunks and hollows. Print size class: small-to-medium. Distinctive marker: a single deep, thin finger-pit in soft ground or bark dust at the centre of each foreprint cluster — the listener's full stop.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low, long shadow under two vast ear-sails, eyes as the only bright points. Proportions in words: ears taller than the body is deep; finger invisible in silhouette except when raised to tap. Key visual masses: ears first, hunched body second. What reads at sprite size: ears, glowing eyes, hunch. Identifying negative space: the wide notch between the ears and the arch between forelegs and chest when it rears to listen.
species.statProfile: Still frail, still quiet — perception and evasiveness carry the profile; it is found on its own terms or not at all — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A gentle supposed-ghost: enormous ears, huge amber eyes, and the long listening finger, rendered kind rather than creepy. Must-never-change: the finger and ears as the twin signature organs, the ghost-reading coming from other species' superstition (never from menace in the design), and the aye-aye's real tap-foraging posture.

species.name: Fossle
species.dexText: Fossle is a low, long pup that treats the canopy as its floor, running branches head-up, tail-out, without a downward glance. It looks a little like a cat. It is not a cat, and the difference is in how it moves: like something the trees invented themselves.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ The fossa's cat-like read shares surface territory with canon's Kittember line (a domestic fire cat). §5.4 flags this for the owner to judge: different family (fossa, Madagascar), different region, different element — Beast, not Flame. The distance must be designed in, not assumed.
species.lineConcept: C2-5 — Madagascar's cat-that-isn't: a low, long, tree-running predator pup; the real animal is the fossa (✓ verified open; see Flags for the Kittember distance note).
species.sizeClass: Small — a long, low pup, all spine and tail, built along branches rather than across ground
species.temperament: Alert, playful-predatory, endlessly in motion among the branches.
species.habitat: Dense canopy and tangled mid-forest of Region 4's Madagascar-flavoured groves.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts small canopy prey and raids nests with quick, clean dashes; practices its adult silence as a game, ambushing leaves, siblings, and its own shadow.
species.evolution: Evolves as the tree-running perfects itself — longer, lower, quieter.
species.discovery: Region 4 canopy groves and tangled mid-forest; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, looking up — canopy paths and low branch crossings; conditions: dry weather, active hours at dawn and dusk; level band in words: early-to-mid wild band; first-meeting note: usually a shape crossing between two crowns, gone before the eye settles — the pup stage is curious enough to come back and look at you.
species.cry: Source character: a pup's short, sharp mew-chirp — cat-adjacent in pitch but rougher and more nasal, which is the point. Pitch contour: mid-high, quick rise, clipped fall. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: singles when watching; rapid doubles when chasing. Variations — idle: soft inquisitive chirps; call: repeated mew-chirps from the branches; hurt: sharp yelp; faint: a small, spent huff; affection: a rough purr-chirp while weaving around a trusted ankle or branch; evolution moment: the chirp deepens and stretches into the adult's low call mid-cry.
species.anatomyNotes: Long flexible spine, long balancing tail nearly the body's length, short powerful legs with semi-retractable claws and reversible-looking ankle flexibility for headfirst descents; jaw is a clean predator muzzle, smaller and narrower than any cat's in canon; locomotion is branch-running — flowing, level-backed, tail streaming.
species.paletteSeed: warm tawny, russet, cream throat, dark tail tip
species.footprint: Print shape class: compact oval pads with four toe pads in an arc — superficially cat-like, but narrower and longer in the heel. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four toes, claw ticks usually present (semi-retractable, so they show more often than a true cat's). Gait pattern: direct-register walk on ground, but the diagnostic trail is on bark — claw scoring along branches and headfirst descent scratches down trunks. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: trunk descent scoring — parallel claw lines running straight down bark, a fossa signature no ground trail matches.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long, low S-curve — spine and tail as one line. Proportions in words: body long, legs short, tail as long as the body, head small and low. Key visual masses: the continuous back-tail line. What reads at sprite size: length, lowness, streaming tail. Identifying negative space: the long shallow gap under the belly between short legs, and the curl-space when the tail lashes up.
species.statProfile: Fast, agile, and precise, with moderate bite for its size; endurance and bulk are low — a sprinter of the branches — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A long, low, tawny tree-runner pup that reads as its own animal, not a cat variant. Must-never-change: the elongated spine-and-tail line, the headfirst-descent climbing anatomy, and clear distance from the canon Kittember line (see Flags) — different family, different silhouette, different read.

species.name: Slashfoss
species.dexText: Slashfoss moves through the canopy like weather and lands without a sound anyone can point to. Prey species do not fear a shape; they fear a change in the air above the branches, and plan their mornings around it.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Same §5.4 flag as Fossle: fossa's cat-like read vs. canon's Kittember line — different family, different region, different element (Beast vs. Flame). Owner judges the distance; the design must make that judgement easy by maximising the differences.
species.lineConcept: C2-5 — moves through canopy like weather and lands without a sound anyone can point to; the real animal is the fossa (✓ verified open; see Flags).
species.sizeClass: Medium — a long, powerful canopy predator, its length mostly spine and tail
species.temperament: Composed, solitary, and absolute in its territory; not cruel — simply weather-like in its certainty.
species.habitat: High canopy and connected crown-country across Region 4's great groves.
species.dietBehaviour: The canopy's apex hunter, taking prey on the branch with silent, perfectly judged descents and leaps; spends its rest hours stretched along high limbs, watching its weather-system of a territory.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 high canopy and crown crossings; rarity class: rare; method: walk, dawn and dusk canopy-watch points; conditions: still air — on windy days it is indistinguishable from the weather it imitates; level band in words: high wild band; first-meeting note: most Rangers meet the silence first — birds stopping, a shadow crossing — and only then, if it permits, the animal itself along a high branch.
species.cry: Source character: a low, rough, carrying call — part mew, part growl, entirely un-catlike up close. Pitch contour: low, slow swell and fall. Duration class: medium. Rhythm pattern: solitary calls at long intervals; silence is its default instrument. Variations — idle: silence, or a single low huff; call: the full rough swell, answered only by quieter woods; hurt: a hard, spitting snarl; faint: a final low growl subsiding into stillness; affection: rare, and therefore notable — a deep purr-growl kept very low; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Extreme spinal flexibility, tail as a counterweight rudder in leaps, powerful hindquarters for branch launches, forepaws able to absorb a silent landing — impact frames must sell softness, not force; headfirst vertical descents are a signature move and should be animated as routine, not stunt.
species.paletteSeed: deep russet, tawny gold, dark umber tail, cream jaw
species.footprint: Print shape class: long-heeled oval pads, four toe pads, claw ticks common. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four toes in a tight arc, claws registering on soft landings. Gait pattern: on the ground, a purposeful long-strided walk; the true signature is arboreal — scored branches, and landing prints: a single set of four deep, soft prints in leaf litter beneath a crown gap, with no approach trail at all. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: the trailless landing — prints that begin from above.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a drawn-out horizontal streak, low head, tail extending the line to a point. Proportions in words: the longest silhouette in this bucket relative to its leg height. Key visual masses: spine-tail continuum; hindquarter power at the rear third. What reads at sprite size: sheer length and lowness, tail streaming. Identifying negative space: the long belly gap and the clean air between its body and the branch when it stretches at rest.
species.statProfile: Very fast and strong for the canopy, with stealth as a defining trait; bulk moderate, defence unremarkable — it is rarely where the blow lands — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: Fossle perfected: a long, low, silent canopy predator whose movement is weather, rendered tawny and unadorned. Must-never-change: the spine-tail single line, the silent-landing anatomy, and maintained distance from Kittember's domestic fire-cat read (see Flags) — no flame, no pet-cat proportions, no mane.

species.name: Okapup
species.dexText: Okapup is a shy pup whose legs carry the first pale stripes of rain. It startles at its own shadow, then stands very still and lets the forest decide it was never there.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-6 — the forest giraffe: a shy pup with rain-striped legs; the real animal is the okapi (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a sturdy, donkey-eared pup, all legs and shyness
species.temperament: Timid, gentle, watchful; brave only in the specific way of standing perfectly still.
species.habitat: Deep, dense forest floor in Region 4's wettest woods, where the light arrives in pieces.
species.dietBehaviour: Browses low leaves, shoots, and fallen fruit in quiet circuits between hiding places; freezes at sounds, ears rotating to collect them one by one.
species.evolution: The stripes arrive in full with the first storm it survives — evolution is weathered into it, not grown on a schedule.
species.discovery: Region 4 deep forest floor, dense undergrowth paths; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, quiet approach, early morning; conditions: damp weather favours it; it avoids open clearings at midday; level band in words: early-to-mid wild band; first-meeting note: likely a freeze-frame meeting — it will be standing motionless among the trees, hoping the meeting is already over.
species.cry: Source character: a very soft, breathy chuff and a faint, high bleat used only in alarm or to find its mother-shaped safety. Pitch contour: low for the chuff, brief high spike for the bleat. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: single, reluctant notes — this is a quiet animal by strategy. Variations — idle: near-silence, occasional chuff; call: soft repeated chuffs; hurt: sharp bleat; faint: a small exhaled bleat trailing down; affection: warm, close, barely audible chuffing; evolution moment: the chuff deepens and steadies as the storm that triggers it passes over.
species.anatomyNotes: Long upright ears that rotate independently; a giraffe-relative's sloping back — hindquarters lower than the shoulders' line in the pup, building toward the adult slope; striped legs are the animation flag: stripes sit on the legs only; long dark tongue for browsing, shown in feeding loops; locomotion is a careful, high-stepping walk.
species.paletteSeed: deep velvet brown, cream facial markings, white leg striping, leaf-shadow green accents
species.footprint: Print shape class: a cloven print — two pointed toe halves side by side, clean and narrow, unmistakably a forest giraffe-relative's track. Toe/claw count and arrangement: two toes only, no dewclaw marks in ordinary going. Gait pattern: careful walk, prints in a neat single wandering line through undergrowth, often doubling back on itself between hiding places. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the prints are frequently found standing in a tight, still cluster — four prints together where it froze and listened — before the line tiptoes on.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a compact body on stilt legs, crowned by two tall ears. Proportions in words: legs long for the body, neck short in the pup, back beginning its slope. Key visual masses: ears and striped legs carry the read. What reads at sprite size: tall ears, white-striped legs against a dark body. Identifying negative space: tall clean gaps between the thin legs, and the notch between the upright ears.
species.statProfile: Modest all round, tilted toward evasion and senses; a survivor by stillness rather than by fight — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A shy, dark, velvet pup with oversized rotating ears and the first white rain-stripes on its legs. Must-never-change: stripes confined to the legs, the giraffe-relative sloping build (never a horse or deer read), and shyness built into the posture — ears up, body ready to freeze.

species.name: Rainokapi
species.dexText: Rainokapi is said to appear only in the hour after rain, when its stripes are still wet and visible. In dry weather it is a rumour with hooves — heard, perhaps, in the deep forest, and gone before the dripping stops.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-6 — said to appear only in the hour after rain, when its stripes are still wet and visible; the real animal is the okapi (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Medium — a full forest-giraffe stature, deep-bodied and tall-eared, built for pushing quietly through wet undergrowth
species.temperament: Elusive, self-possessed, unbothered by being doubted; appears on rain's schedule, not anyone else's.
species.habitat: The deepest wet forest of Region 4, in the green gloom where rain takes longest to finish falling from the leaves.
species.dietBehaviour: Browses the deep-forest understory with its long tongue, moving in slow circuits timed — as far as anyone can tell — to the weather; the wet-stripe hour is when it walks openly.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 deepest wet forest; rarity class: very rare; method: walk, in the hour after rain only — the source's own condition; conditions: rain must have just passed; dry-weather searches find tracks, never the animal; level band in words: high wild band; first-meeting note: a first meeting is a privilege of timing: stripes bright and wet in the post-rain light, one long look, and then the forest closes.
species.cry: Source character: deep, soft chuffs and low, resonant cough-barks that carry oddly far through wet forest. Pitch contour: low, level, with a hollow resonance. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: singles at long intervals — a location note, not a conversation. Variations — idle: near-total silence; call: one deep chuff, repeated after a long pause; hurt: a startlingly loud bark-cough; faint: a low, resigned exhale; affection: close, warm chuffing, almost felt rather than heard; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Full sloping giraffe-relative back, shoulders high, hindquarters dropping away; striped legs in full — stripes must read as wet-bright in its signature hour; very long dark tongue, prehensile, central to feeding animation; ears tall and independently mobile; locomotion is a stately, deliberate, near-silent walk.
species.paletteSeed: near-black velvet brown, bright white leg striping, cream face mask, rain-dark green
species.footprint: Print shape class: cloven two-toe prints, deep and clean in rain-softened ground — this is how most people "meet" it. Toe/claw count and arrangement: two pointed toes, splaying slightly on wet slopes. Gait pattern: slow stately walk in long, confident lines that emerge from deep forest after rain and return to it before the ground dries. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: timing is the marker — fresh Rainokapi tracks exist almost exclusively in the post-rain window, gleaming wet-edged in the mud, and dry out into rumour.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a high-shouldered, sloping-backed forest shape on striped stilts. Proportions in words: long legs, deep chest, back sloping down to the rear, neck carrying the head level and calm. Key visual masses: the dark body mass against the bright leg striping below. What reads at sprite size: slope, stripes, tall ears. Identifying negative space: the long leg gaps, and the wedge of air under the sloping belly line.
species.statProfile: Sturdy and evasive with excellent senses; a defensive, endurance-leaning profile that prefers disappearance to confrontation — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A stately, dark forest giraffe whose white leg-stripes gleam in the hour after rain, built on a true sloping okapi frame. Must-never-change: leg-only striping, the sloped back and long tongue, and the rain-hour elusiveness written into its posture — it should always look like it is about to be a rumour again.

species.name: Casslet
species.dexText: Casslet is a striped chick with a nub of a casque and the bearing of a much larger bird. It practices its dignity daily, falling over only when it is fairly sure nobody important saw.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-7 — a cassowary chick with a nub of a casque; the real animal is the cassowary (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a round-bodied, long-legged chick, mostly appetite and indignation
species.temperament: Proud, bold for its size, already unbothered in the family style.
species.habitat: Rainforest floor and fruit-fall clearings in Region 4's dense green country.
species.dietBehaviour: Devours fallen fruit whole, stalks insects with exaggerated seriousness, and follows the adults' etiquette early: it does not approach others front-on, and expects the same courtesy.
species.evolution: Evolves as the casque grows from nub to full helmet and the chick's practiced dignity becomes real.
species.discovery: Region 4 rainforest floor, fruit-fall clearings; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, daytime, near fruiting trees; conditions: fruit-fall season brings families into the open; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: it will inspect a new Ranger from a careful angle — never front-on — and deliver its verdict by turning its back.
species.cry: Source character: bright chick peeps with a surprisingly throaty undertone already forming — the boom is in rehearsal. Pitch contour: high peeps with low, grumbling falls. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: insistent peep series when hungry; single dignified notes when practicing. Variations — idle: wandering peeps while foraging; call: loud, repeated peeping; hurt: a squawk with a throaty crack; faint: peeps subsiding into a grumble; affection: soft, low churring under the peeps; evolution moment: the voice breaks — peep, crack, and the first true low boom-note.
species.anatomyNotes: Long, powerful legs far ahead of the body's size; three-toed feet with the inner claw already notable; the casque is a small nub — animate its growth importance, not its size; tiny vestigial wings hidden in coarse hair-like plumage; locomotion is a striding, head-lowered walk and sudden Chick-fast dashes.
species.paletteSeed: warm brown chick striping, tan, dark leg grey, pale casque nub
species.footprint: Print shape class: a bold three-toed print — the cassowary track is distinctive in life: three thick forward toes in a wide fan, no hind toe. Toe/claw count and arrangement: three toes, the inner toe's claw mark longer and deeper than the others, registering as a distinct dagger tick. Gait pattern: long-strided walk, prints widely spaced for a chick, in confident straight lines between fruit falls. Print size class: small-to-medium — large for a chick, which is diagnostic. Distinctive marker: that inner-claw dagger tick, present from this stage onward.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a round body carried high on stilts, head forward and low. Proportions in words: legs half the total height, body a plump teardrop, neck short in the chick. Key visual masses: legs and appetite-round body. What reads at sprite size: stilt legs, striped round body, tiny casque nub. Identifying negative space: the tall open triangle between the legs and under the body.
species.statProfile: Quick-legged and sturdier than a chick should be, with kicking power already flagged in its profile; flight is not and never will be part of it — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A striped, stilt-legged cassowary chick with a proud bearing and a mere nub of casque. Must-never-change: the three-toed, dagger-clawed feet, the hair-like coarse plumage (not fluffy chick down), and pride as the chick's defining expression.

species.name: Helmbeak
species.dexText: Helmbeak wears the full helmet crest and one raptor claw, and the whole region agrees on the etiquette: you don't approach it front-on, you don't need to, it is busy. Its calm is not Chillbara's social calm — Helmbeak's is armed, and everyone respects the difference.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-7 — wearing the full helmet crest and one raptor claw; the whole region agrees you don't approach it front-on; the real animal is the cassowary (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Large — a towering, long-legged forest bird, eye-level with a tall Ranger and heavier than it looks
species.temperament: Respected, unbothered, absolute.
species.habitat: Deep rainforest floor, fruiting groves, and the old forest roads of Region 4 that it treats as its own.
species.dietBehaviour: A fruit-eater of consequence, swallowing fallen fruit whole and carrying the forest's seeds across the region in its wanderings; walks its circuits alone, at its own pace, and the forest arranges itself around the schedule.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 deep rainforest, old forest roads and fruiting groves; rarity class: rare; method: walk — encountered on paths, approached (if at all) from the side, per the region's etiquette; conditions: fruiting season; solitary year-round; level band in words: high wild band; first-meeting note: the correct first meeting is a mutual assessment at a respectful distance, concluded by Helmbeak deciding you are not its business and continuing on its way.
species.cry: Source character: a deep, booming, almost subsonic call felt in the ground and the ribs, plus hisses and grunts at close quarters. Pitch contour: very low, swelling, with a percussive start. Duration class: long for a bird — the boom hangs in the forest. Rhythm pattern: slow singles or pairs, widely spaced; close-range communication is hiss and grunt punctuation. Variations — idle: silence or a single distant boom; call: full ground-felt boom sequence; hurt: explosive hiss and a warning stamp; faint: a final low boom subsiding into the forest floor; affection: deep, soft booming kept almost private, with lowered crest; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: The casque is now a full helmet crest — a single tall keratin mass, the silhouette's crown; beak strong and deep; neck long, with vivid skin folds/wattles typical of the read in the source's register (kept abstract, colour carries it); legs are the weapons and the transport: three-toed feet, inner raptor claw prominent; wings vestigial, hidden in coarse black plumage; locomotion is a stately, ground-covering stride — Gale typing reads in its speed and storm-front presence, never in flight.
species.paletteSeed: jet-black coarse plumage, vivid blue neck skin, red wattle accents, grey-brown casque
species.footprint: Print shape class: the full cassowary track — three massive forward toes in a wide fan, deeply pressed, no hind toe. Toe/claw count and arrangement: three toes; the inner toe bears the raptor claw, whose mark is a long, deep dagger slot beside the toe print — the single most recognisable print in this bucket. Gait pattern: long, measured strides in straight, unbothered lines that cross other species' trails without deviating. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the dagger slot; rangers teach children to recognise, respect, and not follow it front-on — the track etiquette mirrors the animal etiquette.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a helmeted tower — tall casque, long neck, heavy teardrop body on column legs. Proportions in words: legs and neck make most of the height; body dense and sloped. Key visual masses: casque crown and the leg columns. What reads at sprite size: helmet crest, black body, stilt legs, vivid neck colour. Identifying negative space: the high arch under the body between the legs and the notch between casque and beak line.
species.statProfile: Powerful, fast over ground, and genuinely dangerous when pressed — high offence and speed for a flightless bird, with presence as a defensive stat in its own right — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A full cassowary rendered with complete respect: towering casque helmet, black hair-like plumage, vivid neck, and the one raptor claw carried like a duellist's sword. Must-never-change: the casque, the inner dagger claw, and etiquette-as-design — it is never goofy, never chased, never front-on; a deliberate armed mirror to Chillbara's social calm.

species.name: Kakapoof
species.dexText: Kakapoof is a round, flightless night parrot that smells of honey and old books. It climbs everything it cannot fly to, which is everything, and arrives at the top pleased with itself and smelling wonderful.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-8 — a round, flightless night parrot that smells of honey and old books; the real animal is the kakapo (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a round, soft ball of a parrot chick, built for the ground
species.temperament: Friendly, curious, nocturnal, and entirely at peace with the ground.
species.habitat: Night forest floor, low shrubs, and climbable trunks in Region 4's old green country.
species.dietBehaviour: Browses leaves, shoots, fruit, and seeds on night rounds, climbing bushes and small trees beak-and-foot to reach the good browsing; by day it rests in ground cover, camouflaged and content.
species.evolution: It never flies. It has never once minded. Evolution rounds it out into the valley's drum.
species.discovery: Region 4 night forest floor and low-shrub country; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, night; conditions: still, dark nights — it freezes comically when startled, trusting its camouflage completely; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: often found frozen mid-step in the leaf litter, visible mainly because it has stopped pretending to be a shrub at slightly the wrong moment.
species.cry: Source character: soft parrot chatters, clicks, and squeaks, with a tiny practice *boom* — a puff of low sound it is visibly proud of. Pitch contour: mid and round, the practice boom dropping suddenly low. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: chatty bursts while climbing; long contented silences while browsing. Variations — idle: soft chatter and beak-clicks; call: repeated squeak-chatters; hurt: a loud, startled squawk; faint: a deflating squeak; affection: rapid happy chattering and gentle beak-nibbling sounds; evolution moment: the practice boom finally lands at full depth mid-chatter, surprising the bird itself.
species.anatomyNotes: Flightless wings — small, soft, used for balance and parachute-hops down from climbs, never flight; strong beak for climbing and browsing; zygodactyl-type grasping feet for trunk work (kept simple: feet visibly grip); facial whisker-like feathers around the beak; locomotion is a waddling walk and determined three-point climbs.
species.paletteSeed: moss green, soft yellow-green face, cream belly, bark brown accents
species.footprint: Print shape class: a parrot's grasping print — two toes forward, two back, pressed into soft forest floor, accompanied by beak-pits where it hauled itself up. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four toes in an X arrangement, claw curves at each tip. Gait pattern: waddling walk, prints alternating wide apart, trail weaving between shrubs and ending at climbable trunks. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the beak-pit punctuation — little triangular beak dents beside the footprints wherever the slope got serious.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a soft round ball with a parrot's head — almost no neck, wings lost in the roundness. Proportions in words: body nearly spherical, head a rounding of the front, tail short. Key visual masses: the round body is everything. What reads at sprite size: roundness, green camouflage tones, owl-parrot face disc. Identifying negative space: very little — a small gap between the short legs under the ball.
species.statProfile: Slow, soft, and sturdy for its size — a gentle tank in miniature with no aerial game at all — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A spherical, moss-green, flightless parrot chick with a sweet expression and a honey-and-old-books aura the art must imply through warmth. Must-never-change: true flightlessness worn with pride, the round camouflage body, and climbing (not flying) as its way up the world.

species.name: Barrelboom
species.dexText: Barrelboom is a walking barrel of a bird whose booming call is felt in the ribs of everyone in the valley. On festival nights the region does not need drums. It has Barrelboom, holding the beat from its favourite hollow, and the whole valley keeping time.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-8 — a walking barrel of a bird whose booming call is felt in the ribs of everyone in the valley — the region's natural festival drum; the real animal is the kakapo (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Large — a walking barrel: the heavyweight of flightless parrots, broad, deep, and ground-shaking
species.temperament: Jovial, sociable, ceremonial; a creature that experiences rhythm as a public duty.
species.habitat: Valley forest floors and natural amphitheatre hollows in Region 4, where the boom carries best.
species.dietBehaviour: Browses the night forest in long circuits and returns to favoured booming hollows, where it inflates and delivers the valley's heartbeat; pairs, in the source's note, with the festival register without living in the festival region.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further. It never flew at any stage, and has never once minded.
species.discovery: Region 4 valley hollows and festival-adjacent forest; rarity class: rare; method: walk, night — located by sound long before sight; conditions: still nights carry the boom across the whole valley; level band in words: mid-to-high wild band; first-meeting note: the first meeting is physical: a boom lands in your ribs from the dark, and then the barrel of a bird steps into view, pleased to have an audience.
species.cry: Source character: the bucket's definitive cry spec — a deep, resonant *boom* produced by full-body inflation, felt as much as heard, in the ribs of everyone in the valley; between booms, warm parrot chatter and clicking. Pitch contour: the boom is very low, swelling and decaying slowly; chatter sits mid and friendly above it. Duration class: the boom is long; chatter is short-burst. Rhythm pattern: booms in slow, festival-drum cadence — measured pairs and rolls that a valley can dance to; chatter fills the rests. Variations — idle: contented chatter, occasional single practice boom; call: full booming sequence, valley-wide; hurt: a shocked squawk cutting a boom short; faint: a last deflating boom sighing out; affection: soft booms kept deliberately gentle, with happy chatter; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Massive round barrel torso that visibly inflates before a boom — the chest/throat expansion is the signature animation; wings small and flightless, used in display flourishes and balance; beak strong, face disc whiskered; feet powerful climbers; locomotion is a deliberate, rolling waddle — every step has festival weight.
species.paletteSeed: deep moss green, golden-green face, honey amber accents, dark bark brown
species.footprint: Print shape class: heavy grasping parrot prints — two toes forward, two back — pressed deep by the barrel's weight. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four toes in a broad X, strong claw curves. Gait pattern: rolling waddle, prints wide and alternating, trails converging on booming hollows from across the valley. Print size class: medium-to-large for a bird of the floor. Distinctive marker: the booming hollow itself — a swept, trampled arena of prints in a natural bowl, the valley's drum-stage, recognisable long before the bird arrives.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a walking barrel with a parrot head — the roundest large silhouette in the bucket. Proportions in words: torso a near-perfect barrel, head small by comparison, legs short columns. Key visual masses: the barrel, and its expansion when inflating. What reads at sprite size: barrel body, face disc, sheer round bulk. Identifying negative space: minimal — small leg gaps only; the silhouette is a drum and reads as one.
species.statProfile: Slow and very bulky with a booming presence that controls a space; offence modest and mostly ceremonial — its power is in being the valley's heartbeat — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A vast, round, moss-green barrel-parrot whose whole body is a drum, mid-inflation for a boom in its hero pose. Must-never-change: flightlessness as pride, the inflating barrel torso, and the festival-drum role — joy and ceremony, never a joke at the bird's expense.

species.name: Wombit
species.dexText: Wombit digs like a rumour spreads: everywhere, overnight, and impossible to trace to a single start. A garden left alone with a Wombit wakes up re-landscaped, with the pup asleep in the middle of the works.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-9 — a wombat pup that digs like a rumour spreads; the real animal is the wombat (✓ verified open), whose cube droppings are the line's seed (see stage 2).
species.sizeClass: Small — a compact, square-built pup, dense as a brick already
species.temperament: Determined, cheerful, stubborn in miniature; digging is not a behaviour, it is a worldview.
species.habitat: Diggable earth — banks, burrow slopes, and soft ground across Region 4's dry country.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes grasses and roots between digging bouts; excavates exploratory burrows constantly, backwards-kicking earth with total commitment; sleeps in whichever burrow is newest.
species.evolution: Evolves as the digging professionalises — from rumour-spread holes to architecture.
species.discovery: Region 4 dry banks and burrow slopes; rarity class: common in worked ground; method: walk, following fresh spoil heaps; conditions: soft, dry earth — after rain it digs with doubled enthusiasm; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: usually met rear-first, emerging backwards from a new hole in a shower of earth, blinking.
species.cry: Source character: short, gruff huffs and squeaky grunts, muffled when underground. Pitch contour: low-mid, flat, with indignant rises. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: single huffs while digging in effort rhythm; indignant grunt-series when a burrow is disturbed. Variations — idle: rhythmic digging huffs; call: a louder, square little grunt; hurt: sharp squeal-grunt; faint: a final huff as it slumps in its own excavation; affection: soft, fast, pleased grunting; evolution moment: the grunt drops and squares off — same voice, more brick.
species.anatomyNotes: Compact square body, very strong forelimbs with broad digging claws, short neck, blunt head used as a ram and a plug; hindquarters notably tough and flat-backed for burrow defence; locomotion is a rolling waddle above ground and powerful, earth-moving excavation below it — digging animation is this line's signature and must read as effortless volume-moving.
species.paletteSeed: dusty grey-brown, sand, darker paw brown, pale muzzle
species.footprint: Print shape class: broad, blunt prints — five toes with strong claw gouges fanned in front of a wide palm pad; the wombat track is a digger's signature. Toe/claw count and arrangement: five toes, claw marks long and parallel, often deeper than the pad itself. Gait pattern: waddling walk, prints close and straight-lined between burrow mouths. Print size class: small-to-medium, heavy for the size. Distinctive marker: prints rarely travel alone — they run between spoil heaps and burrow mouths, and the claw gouges score the earth even where the pad barely pressed.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low, square brick with a head — corners, not curves. Proportions in words: body long and flat-backed, legs very short, head blunt and wide. Key visual masses: the square torso block. What reads at sprite size: squareness, flat back, big front paws. Identifying negative space: tiny leg gaps only; the block is the identity, foreshadowing the adult's bricks.
species.statProfile: Slow above ground, strong and very sturdy for its stage — a compact wall that excavates — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A square, blunt, brick-dense wombat pup with oversized digging forepaws, mid-excavation in its hero pose. Must-never-change: the square build (the line's whole geometry), the digging claws as primary anatomy, and cheerful stubbornness in the face — never a mole or a badger read.

species.name: Burrowbrick
species.dexText: Burrowbrick is famous for the wombat's real party trick — perfect cube droppings — which it builds with: little brick walls, burrow doors, one-upmanship. The region's only architect whose bricks are also a punchline is played completely straight by everyone, including Burrowbrick, which is why it works.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-9 — famous for the wombat's real party trick, perfect cube droppings, which it builds with; the real animal is the wombat (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Medium — a massive, low, square stronghold of an animal, built like its own bricks
species.temperament: Deadpan, proud, territorial about its constructions; a master builder with no sense that anything is funny.
species.habitat: Established burrow complexes and worked earthworks across Region 4's dry country — recognisable by the little walls.
species.dietBehaviour: Grazes coarse grasses and roots on night rounds; devotes its days to construction — cube-stacked walls marking burrow doors, boundaries, and claims, rebuilt higher in answer to any neighbour's wall.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 established burrow complexes and earthwork slopes; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk — locate by the architecture (little cube walls) before the animal; conditions: dry, diggable country; building peaks in calm weather; level band in words: mid wild band; first-meeting note: you will be assessed from behind a small, perfect wall, by an animal that considers the wall the formal introduction.
species.cry: Source character: deep, square grunts and huffs, delivered with total deadpan; a harsh, grating call when a wall is threatened. Pitch contour: low and flat — expression lives in timing, not pitch. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: single grunts, widely spaced, like bricks being set down one at a time. Variations — idle: slow work-grunts in building rhythm; call: a flat, carrying grunt repeated at exact intervals; hurt: a shocked, barking grunt; faint: one last huff, face-down by its works; affection: soft rapid grunting, barely softer — the deadpan never fully drops; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Enormous square torso, flat armoured-feeling hindquarters (the burrow-door defence), forelimbs like excavation equipment; the cube production and stacking must be animatable as a dignified building behaviour — paws placing cubes with bricklayer care; locomotion is a slow, unstoppable waddle; nothing about this animal is quick except its digging.
species.paletteSeed: stone grey-brown, brick tan, dark earth, pale dry-grass accents
species.footprint: Print shape class: massive blunt five-toed prints, claw gouges ahead of deep palm pads — the adult wombat track at full weight. Toe/claw count and arrangement: five toes, long parallel claw scores in the earth. Gait pattern: deliberate waddle in dead-straight lines between burrow, grazing, and building sites. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: the trail's context — prints running alongside low cube-dropping walls, with single cubes placed at intervals along the path as markers; no other species signs its trail in architecture.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a living brick — long, low, flat-topped, flat-backed, squared at both ends. Proportions in words: torso a masonry block, legs mere courses at the corners, head a blunt front face. Key visual masses: the block. What reads at sprite size: squareness, flat top, huge front paws, and (in scene) its little walls echoing its own shape. Identifying negative space: almost none — this silhouette is a filled rectangle with intent.
species.statProfile: Very slow, very strong, and extremely sturdy — a wall that builds walls; the defensive profile is the headline — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A huge, square, deadpan wombat architect photographed beside its own cube-brick wall, the animal and the architecture sharing one geometry. Must-never-change: the perfect cubes and their building use, played completely straight (the design never winks), the square brick body, and the burrow-door hindquarters.

species.name: Narwhit
species.dexText: Narwhit is a small whale calf with a bud of a tusk, already listening to the water the way its elders taste it. It nudges ice, stories, and its mother's side with the same blunt curiosity.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-10 — a small whale calf with a bud of a tusk; the real animal is the narwhal (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a round, mottled calf, small as whales go and large as pups go
species.temperament: Gentle, dreamy, inquisitive; drawn to sounds and stories in the water.
species.habitat: Cold bays, ice-edge water, and slow northern channels of Region 4's Rift coast.
species.dietBehaviour: Feeds on small fish and soft prey in the cold shallows, staying close to the pod; practices tusk-sensing by touching the bud to ice, stones, and other calves, as if checking what things remember.
species.evolution: Evolves as the tusk spirals out and the sensing deepens into story-navigation.
species.discovery: Region 4 ice-edge bays and cold channels; rarity class: uncommon; method: water / surf-class travel along the ice edge, daytime; conditions: cold, clear water; pods are seasonal visitors to the bays; level band in words: early-to-mid wild band; first-meeting note: the calf will likely surface first, bud-tusk and all, to look at the boat or the Ranger with open, unhurried curiosity.
species.cry: Source character: bright whale-calf clicks, whistles, and soft pulsed calls, high and musical. Pitch contour: rising whistles, clicking descents. Duration class: short notes in musical series. Rhythm pattern: playful call-and-response with the pod; clicks in quick investigative bursts at new objects. Variations — idle: soft wandering whistles; call: a clear rising whistle repeated until answered; hurt: a sharp pulsed squeal; faint: whistles slowing and sinking; affection: gentle click-whistle exchanges at close range; evolution moment: the whistle deepens and gains a strange resonance, as if the new tusk were sounding with it.
species.anatomyNotes: True whale calf body — no legs, ever; small flippers, broad tail fluke, mottled skin; the tusk bud erupts from the upper left of the mouth line as a small spiral nub — animators must place it as a tooth, not a horn on the forehead; locomotion is full-body undulating swimming with fluke power.
species.paletteSeed: pale grey-blue, white mottling, ice white, soft pink mouth line
species.footprint: Water-trace instead of a print: a calf's wake — a small, smooth V with playful breaches in it; close to the surface, a pattern of soft exhalation bubbles and gentle fluke swirls; near ice, light exploratory tap-marks where the tusk bud has tested the edge. Distinctive marker: paired traces — the calf's small wake weaving in and out of a much larger, calmer adult wake.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a smooth, round torpedo with a nub at the front. Proportions in words: body plump and tapering to the fluke, head rounded into the body with no neck, tusk bud a tiny front point. Key visual masses: the plump mid-body. What reads at sprite size: mottled round whale, fluke, bud. Identifying negative space: the notch in the tail fluke and the crescent gaps at the flipper joints.
species.statProfile: Hardy in cold water, a strong swimmer, gentle in offence — senses and endurance lead the calf's profile — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A mottled, round narwhal calf with a small spiral tusk bud placed correctly as a tooth, mid-curious-nudge. Must-never-change: whale-first anatomy (no legs, no forehead horn), the bud's modest size, and dreamy curiosity as the resting expression.

species.name: Tuskicorn
species.dexText: Tuskicorn's spiral is a sense organ: it tastes the water's memories, and it navigates by stories other whales told the sea. The unicorn read is earned by the folklore, not the silhouette — it is a whale first, and a wonder second.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-10 — carrying the full spiral, which in this world is a sense organ: it tastes the water's memories and navigates by stories other whales told the sea; the real animal is the narwhal (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Large — a full, deep-water whale, its spiral tusk extending its great length further still
species.temperament: Serene, far-minded, generous with guidance; pods and lost travellers alike fall in behind it.
species.habitat: Deep cold channels, ice leads, and the open Rift sea of Region 4.
species.dietBehaviour: Feeds deep on fish and soft prey; travels immense, unerring routes read through the tusk from the water itself; in the travelling season, other species time their own journeys by its passing.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 deep cold channels and ice leads; rarity class: very rare; method: surf-class travel on deep cold water, often following pod routes; conditions: travelling season, open leads in the ice; level band in words: high wild band; first-meeting note: the tusk breaks the surface first, tasting the air-side of the world, and the whale rises to meet a Ranger the way a librarian approaches a question — it has been expecting something like you.
species.cry: Source character: deep, musical whale song-phrases — clicks, whistles, and long pulsed tones with an uncanny, story-like phrasing. Pitch contour: wide-ranging, rising whistles over low, slow pulses. Duration class: long phrases. Rhythm pattern: true sequences with repeats and variations, call-and-answer across distance — cries only, but structured like remembered tales. Variations — idle: low, slow song fragments while travelling; call: full carrying phrases answered by distant pods; hurt: a great pulsed blast; faint: song sinking note by note into the deep; affection: close, soft click-and-whistle exchanges, almost conversational in rhythm; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Full whale mass with mottled, lightening skin; the spiral tusk is the signature organ — long, left-sided, erupting through the mouth line, held forward when sensing, and it must move like a living, feeling limb (testing, tasting, recoiling from bad memories in the water); no dorsal fin — the back is smooth with a low ridge; fluke strokes are slow and immense.
species.paletteSeed: ice white and pale silver-blue, deep sea grey mottling, pearl tusk
species.footprint: Water-trace instead of a print: a great, calm wake in deep water — a long smooth V with slow fluke swirls, travelling in unnervingly straight story-lines between bays; at the surface, spiral-tasting traces: the tusk-tip dimpling the water in slow arcs as it reads. Distinctive marker: the wake's route itself — it follows lines that match old pod stories, passing places no current explains, and other whales' wakes join and leave it like tributaries.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a vast smooth whale line extended by a single forward spiral — the longest horizontal silhouette in the bucket. Proportions in words: tusk a major fraction of the visible length at the surface, body deep and smooth, fluke broad. Key visual masses: the body mass and the tusk as its exclamation. What reads at sprite size: spiral tusk first, then whale. Identifying negative space: the fluke notch and the clean gap between tusk line and waterline when it tastes the air.
species.statProfile: Very hardy, enduring, and sense-led — a navigator and guide whose offence is secondary to its role; defence is depth itself — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A true narwhal at full majesty: whale anatomy uncompromised, full spiral tusk carried as a tasting, feeling sense organ. Must-never-change: whale first, wonder second — no horn-on-forehead unicorn silhouette, no legs, no mane; the tusk's spiral direction and mouth placement stay biologically true to the narwhal seed.

species.name: Vitrel
species.dexText: Vitrel is a tadpole-clear froglet whose skin lets the light half-through, so that sitting on a leaf it becomes the leaf's own bright window. Up close, trusted and close, a tiny heart can be seen keeping time.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Frogs are Pokémon-crowded (Poliwag, Toxicroak, Bellibolt, …) — §5.4 flags the family. The seed here is transparency-as-trust, a mechanism none of them use (§5, C2-11). The design must lead with translucency or it falls back into the crowd.
species.lineConcept: C2-11 — a tadpole-clear froglet; the real animal is the glass frog (✓ verified open; see Flags — the seed is transparency-as-trust).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a leaf-sized froglet, small enough to vanish on the leaf it sits on
species.temperament: Shy, still, and quietly brave about being seen — by the right eyes, at the right distance.
species.habitat: Undersides and tops of broad leaves over slow streams in Region 4's wet forest.
species.dietBehaviour: Takes tiny insects on night rounds across the leaves; by day it flattens itself on a leaf and lets transparency do the hiding; it shows its underside only where it feels safe.
species.evolution: Evolves as the transparency completes and the trust it requires becomes the adult's defining gift.
species.discovery: Region 4 broad-leaf streamside forest; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, streamside leaves, night and early morning; conditions: humid, still air after rain; look for the leaf that has a window in it; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: the first meeting is an act of trust detection — if it does not flatten and vanish, and lets you see the leaf-light through it, you have already been assessed kindly.
species.cry: Source character: a tiny, clear, bell-like peep — a drop of sound, almost visible. Pitch contour: high, pure, with a quick fall. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: single peeps at long, irregular intervals; a soft series when calling across leaves. Variations — idle: rare single peeps; call: a clear repeating peep, slightly brighter; hurt: one sharp, startled peep and silence; faint: a peep that thins to nothing; affection: soft, rapid, lower peeps offered at close range; evolution moment: the peep gains a resonant, glassy ring, like a larger drop in a deeper pool.
species.anatomyNotes: Delicate froglet body with large, forward, golden eyes; toe pads for leaf-gripping on all four feet; the skin's translucency is the signature — animators must handle the belly's show-through (leaf-light, and faintly, the heart) as a layered effect, never as gore; locomotion is careful leaf-walking and short, precise hops.
species.paletteSeed: translucent leaf green, pale lime, glass-clear belly tones, gold eyes
species.footprint: Print shape class: a miniature leaf-print rather than a ground print — four toe-pad discs in a small splay, left as faint moisture marks on leaf surfaces, plus a soft belly sheen where it flattened. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four slim toes with round adhesive pads, no claws. Gait pattern: walk-and-hop across connected leaves, the trail readable only on the leaves themselves in dew or after rain. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the window — a leaf with a frog-shaped patch of slightly cleaner, brighter translucency where it rested and the light came through.
