species.silhouette: Outline class: a small, low dome of a frog on a leaf, ears absent, eyes as two bumps of gold. Proportions in words: body a flattened oval, legs folded tight, head merged into the body line. Key visual masses: the dome and the eye pair. What reads at sprite size: translucency, eye shine, leaf-perch. Identifying negative space: the thin gaps between the folded toes and the leaf edge; against backlight, the heart is a positive mark inside a negative-transparency field.
species.statProfile: Extremely frail and extremely hard to find — evasion and camouflage are the entire defensive profile; offence is negligible at this stage — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A tiny, translucent glass froglet flattened on a broad leaf, light coming through it, golden eyes forward. Must-never-change: transparency rendered as beauty and trust (never body-horror), the leaf-window camouflage idea, and delicate — never slimy — surfaces.

species.name: Clearibbit
species.dexText: Clearibbit's transparent belly shows its heart, beating, for anyone trusted enough to be shown. It hides by becoming the leaf's window — and chooses, sometimes, to let a friend look through the window at the heart of the matter.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Same §5.4 flag as Vitrel: frogs are Pokémon-crowded (Poliwag, Toxicroak, Bellibolt…). Clearibbit's seed — transparency-as-trust, the shown heart — is the mechanism none of them use. If a design reads as "another frog," it has failed the flag.
species.lineConcept: C2-11 — a glass frog whose transparent belly shows its heart, beating, for anyone trusted enough to be shown; the real animal is the glass frog (✓ verified open; see Flags).
species.sizeClass: Small — a palm-sized glass frog, still leaf-scaled, every proportion in service of the window it carries
species.temperament: Gentle, discerning, and brave in a very specific way: it decides who sees its heart, and the decision is the personality.
species.habitat: Canopy leaves and streamside branches over slow water in Region 4's wettest forest.
species.dietBehaviour: Night-hunts small insects along the leaves and low branches; guards its leaf territories quietly; the belly-showing is never casual — it is offered, held, and withdrawn with complete deliberateness.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further.
species.discovery: Region 4 streamside canopy and broad-leaf banks; rarity class: rare; method: walk, night, along stream leaves — found by backlight and patience; conditions: humid nights, moonlight or soft light behind leaves reveals the window; level band in words: mid wild band; first-meeting note: a true first meeting has two stages — finding the window in the leaf, and then, if trusted, being shown the heart beating inside it. Rangers remember which one they were given.
species.cry: Source character: a clear, glassy, bell-toned call — like a water drop struck on crystal — pure, carrying, and unafraid. Pitch contour: high and ringing, with a long pure fall. Duration class: short, but resonant — the ring outlasts the note. Rhythm pattern: deliberate singles; in chorus, staggered rings that answer each other leaf to leaf. Variations — idle: occasional single rings; call: full resonant sequence; hurt: a cracked, duller peep — the only graceless sound it makes; faint: a ring that fades rather than stops; affection: soft, low, repeated rings at very close range, synchronising — listeners swear — with the visible heartbeat; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Full glass-frog translucency across the belly with the heart visible and beating — the heartbeat is a core animation loop and must sync with the affection cry; large golden forward eyes; adhesive toe pads on long, delicate limbs; dorsal side remains leaf-green and opaque for camouflage — the transparency is ventral, and the flip between hidden and shown is a posture animation (flatten to hide, lift to show).
species.paletteSeed: vivid leaf green above, glass-clear and faint rose at the heart below, gold eyes, silver leaf-light edges
species.footprint: Print shape class: toe-pad moisture prints on leaves, larger and more deliberate than Vitrel's — four padded toes, no claws, arranged in a calm splay. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four toes per foot with round terminal pads. Gait pattern: slow leaf-to-leaf progression over streams, trails readable in dew as a dotted line of pad-marks and belly sheens. Print size class: tiny-to-small. Distinctive marker: beside favoured leaves, a repeated single resting-window — the same leaf used nightly, its frog-shaped bright patch polished by use.
species.silhouette: Outline class: an elegant low frog-dome, limbs longer and finer than the froglet's, eyes raised like two gold studs. Proportions in words: body a smooth oval lens, legs folded in clean lines beneath. Key visual masses: the lens body — posture decides whether it reads as leaf or as window. What reads at sprite size: translucency, gold eyes, the heart-glow in shown posture. Identifying negative space: the clear field of the belly itself is the negative space — a window cut in the silhouette, with the heart as the single mark inside it.
species.statProfile: Still frail, still elusive — a support-leaning, senses-and-evasion profile whose signature is trust, not force — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A glass frog of complete elegance: leaf-green above, crystal below, heart beating visibly in the window of its belly, offered — not exposed. Must-never-change: transparency-as-trust as the whole concept, the ventral-only window, and beauty without a trace of the grotesque (see Flags: this mechanism, not frog-ness, is the design).

species.name: Velvlet
species.dexText: Velvlet is a soft, many-legged velvet worm that hunts by firing twin strands of quick-setting slime — a living lasso in miniature. What the slime catches, dinner becomes; what it catches by accident, Velvlet patiently, apologetically frees.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-12 — a soft, many-legged velvet worm that hunts by firing twin strands of quick-setting slime — a living lasso; the real animal is the velvet worm (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a finger-length soft worm of a creature, all velvet and legs
species.temperament: Gentle, methodical, mildly apologetic; a predator with the manners of a rescuer already forming.
species.habitat: Damp leaf litter, rotting logs, and mossy undergrowth in Region 4's old forest floor.
species.dietBehaviour: Ambushes tiny insects from litter cover, firing its twin slime strands in a netting spray and reeling the catch in by eating through the strands; moves slowly and deliberately, feeling the way with its antennae.
species.evolution: Evolves without improving on the body plan — an ancient design (older than insects, older than fish stories) that never needed improving simply grows surer of itself.
species.discovery: Region 4 damp leaf litter and rotting-log country; rarity class: uncommon; method: walk, night and damp daytime, turning attention to log undersides and litter; conditions: wet weather brings it out hunting; level band in words: early wild band; first-meeting note: often met mid-rescue — a Velvlet freeing a beetle it caught by mistake is the region's favourite introduction to the line.
species.cry: Source character: an extremely soft, tiny, breathy squeak — barely a voice at all, mostly heard at close range in the litter. Pitch contour: mid-high, gentle, falling. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: singles, widely spaced; a faint rapid series while wrestling a slime-caught meal. Variations — idle: near-silence; call: a soft repeated squeak; hurt: a tiny sharp squeak; faint: a sighing squeak, subsiding into the litter; affection: warm, close, almost purring squeaks; evolution moment: the same small voice, steadier, as the strands fire in celebration and have to be apologised for.
species.anatomyNotes: Soft, unsegmented-looking velvet body on many pairs of short, stubby, clawed legs — the leg count is high and the gait is a slow, rippling caterpillar-like progression, but the body is a worm's, not an insect's: no hard shell, no wings, ever; two antennae feel the way; the signature organs are the paired slime glands beside the head, firing twin strands that oscillate into a net — animators must make the strands read as quick-setting and kind, not venomous.
species.paletteSeed: deep velvet blue-purple, soft violet, moss green accents, pale slime silver
species.footprint: Print shape class: no true footprint — a litter-trace: a soft, many-dotted disturbance, dozens of tiny leg ticks in rippling rows along a slow wandering line through damp litter. Toe/claw count and arrangement: each tiny leg ends in a minute claw tick; the rows are paired and numerous. Gait pattern: slow ripple-walk, the trace weaving under leaves and around logs. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: slime — spent strands dry into fine silver threads across the litter along its hunting lines, a lasso-artist's signature no other floor species leaves.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low, soft, velvet rope of a body on a fringe of legs. Proportions in words: body long and evenly thick, head barely distinct, antennae a gentle front pair. Key visual masses: the continuous velvet body. What reads at sprite size: velvet texture, leg fringe, antennae, and (in action) the twin slime arc. Identifying negative space: the tiny scalloped gaps between the many stub legs under the body line.
species.statProfile: Slow, soft, and frail in open ground — but with a capture mechanism that punches far above its size; a trapper's profile, not a fighter's — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A tiny, plush, deep-velvet worm on many stubby legs, twin slime strands mid-lasso in its hero pose. Must-never-change: the soft velvet worm body plan (ancient, shell-less, wingless), the twin-strand lasso as a kind tool, and gentleness in every expression — this is the gentlest predator in the making.

species.name: Slimelasso
species.dexText: Slimelasso is the region's gentlest predator and its best rescuer: the same slime that catches dinner catches falling climbers. An ancient body plan — older than insects, older than fish stories — that never needed improving, and has spent the ages becoming kind instead.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C2-12 — the region's gentlest predator and its best rescuer: the same slime that catches dinner catches falling climbers; the real animal is the velvet worm (✓ verified open).
species.sizeClass: Small — a long, soft, many-legged presence in the litter and low branches, large for a velvet worm and exactly the size a falling climber hopes for
species.temperament: Patient, capable, and profoundly gentle; rescues are performed with the same calm as hunts, and with more pride.
species.habitat: Forest floor, rotting logs, and the bases of climbed cliffs and great trees across Region 4 — anywhere things fall.
species.dietBehaviour: Hunts insects and small prey with wide, elegant twin-strand nets; stations itself, by long habit, beneath climbing routes and fruit trees, and fires upward without hesitation when anything — dinner or climber — comes down.
species.evolution: Final stage of the line; does not evolve further. R4's quietest flex: it never needed to.
species.discovery: Region 4 cliff bases, great-tree country, and old forest floor; rarity class: rare; method: walk — or be caught by one, which locals count as a meeting; conditions: climbing season and fruit-fall bring its rescues (and sightings) to their peak; level band in words: mid-to-high wild band; first-meeting note: the region's preferred first meeting is the famous one — a slip, a fall, a sudden gentle stop in a net of silver strands, and a soft, many-legged rescuer reeling you in with great care and no comment.
species.cry: Source character: a soft, low, breathy cry — still a small voice on a larger body, warm and unhurried, with a faint hum when working a lasso. Pitch contour: mid, level, reassuring falls at the end of phrases. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: calm singles; during a rescue, a steady, rhythmic series that climbers learn to breathe along with. Variations — idle: soft occasional cries from the litter; call: a gentle repeated cry that carries surprisingly well along the forest floor; hurt: a startled squeak, immediately followed by checking-on-others sounds; faint: a slow, sinking sigh-cry; affection: warm, close, purring squeaks while grooming a rescued friend's fright away; evolution moment: not applicable as final stage.
species.anatomyNotes: Long velvet body on many pairs of stubby clawed legs, rippling gait at surprising smoothness; antennae long and expressive; the slime glands are now expert instruments — twin strands fired in wide oscillating nets, strong enough to hold a falling Ranger, and the reel-in (eating/rawing the strands to draw the catch close) is the line's signature full-body animation; no shell, no armour, no weapons — softness is the whole engineering.
species.paletteSeed: rich velvet indigo, violet, deep moss green, bright silver slime
species.footprint: Print shape class: a litter-trace at full scale — long rippling rows of tiny leg ticks with minute claw marks, pressed in calm, unhurried lines. Toe/claw count and arrangement: many paired legs, each ticking the litter in sequence. Gait pattern: slow ripple progression that ranges widely — floor, logs, and the bases of cliffs in patient circuits. Print size class: small (the trace is long, not large). Distinctive marker: silver slime in its heroic form — anchored net-lines strung between log, branch, and cliff base, with the soft, Ranger-sized sag in the middle where someone was caught and lowered, gently, to the ground.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long, low velvet wave on a fringe of legs, antennae raised in attention. Proportions in words: body evenly thick and long, head a gentle thickening at the front, no hard angles anywhere. Key visual masses: the velvet body as one kind mass; in action, the twin slime arcs double the silhouette's width. What reads at sprite size: velvet darkness, leg fringe, antennae, silver strands. Identifying negative space: the scalloped under-body leg gaps, and the clean catenary curve of negative space inside a fired slime net.
species.statProfile: Slow and soft with modest direct offence, but an elite capture-and-rescue profile — control, reach, and reliability carry it — plus "⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design)".
species.designBrief: A large, plush, indigo velvet worm mid-rescue, twin silver slime nets spread wide and gentle, many legs braced with care. Must-never-change: the ancient, shell-less velvet-worm plan unchanged by evolution, slime as a rescue tool first in the visual hierarchy, and quiet, unshowy kindness as the expression — R4's quietest flex must look quiet.

species.name: Termight
species.dexText: Termight spend their whole lives building, carrying grains of earth one mouthful at a time toward a mound they will never see finished. A single Termight is shy and nearly colourless. Together, in their thousands, they raise chimneys, arches, and cool dark halls.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C3-1 Termight → Cathedrall — a pale termite worker; the line is a colony that builds cathedral mounds. Basis: termites (open as a designed animal; Pokémon has ants, not termites).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a fingertip-scale crawler, easy to cup in one palm alongside nestmates
species.temperament: Diligent, shy, colony-devoted; unsettled alone, calm and purposeful in a procession.
species.habitat: Warm earth at the edges of Region 4 clearings, always in or near the colony mound; scouts range only a short way over open ground.
species.dietBehaviour: Feeds on fallen wood fibre, dry leaves, and the earth itself as it tunnels. Works in single-file lines nose-to-tail; when the line is broken, the workers circle patiently until the scent of the route is found again.
species.evolution: Colony-formation — an individual Termight does not transform alone; when the colony it belongs to completes its cathedral mound and the mound gains a queen-heart, the colony-form Cathedrall is what the line has become (see Cathedrall).
species.discovery: Region 4 — mound country on warm, dry clearing edges. Rarity: common wherever a mound stands, effectively absent away from one. Method + conditions: follow a worker procession at ground level on a warm, still day; they do not hide, they simply hurry. Level band (in words): earliest band — among the first small crawlers a Ranger meets in mound country. First-meeting note: the Ranger meets a line, not an individual — one Termight stops, tastes the air with its antennae, and the whole line politely reroutes around the Ranger's boot.
species.cry: Source character: faint dry ticking and mandible clicks, barely louder than a fingernail on paper. Pitch contour: flat and very high, with tiny rising ticks when the line changes direction. Duration class: very short bursts. Rhythm pattern: rapid triple-ticks in step with the procession. Variations — idle: sparse single clicks while carrying; call: a quickened tick-run that travels down the line like a passed message; hurt: one sharp snap and silence; faint: clicks slow, space out, and stop mid-pattern; affection: a soft, fast antennal drumming against a nestmate or a trusted Ranger's fingertip; evolution moment: the whole colony ticks at once, a dry patter like first rain on a roof, as the mound's heart wakes.
species.anatomyNotes: Six short legs in a low, even gait; soft segmented abdomen carried behind a small head; two short antennae that do all the "looking." Manipulators: mandibles only — it carries in its mouth, so feeding, building, and attack-delivery all read through the head. Mouth/jaw: small chewing mandibles, no bite menace. Locomotion: steady scuttle, single-file. Signature feature: the pale, almost translucent worker body — animate it as one bead in a moving line, never as a lone hero pose.
species.paletteSeed: pale bone-cream, warm earth tan, soft clay red, dusty amber
species.footprint: Print shape class: paired pinpoint dots in two neat rows, six per stride, with a faint central drag line from the low abdomen. Toe/claw count and arrangement: no toes — each leg leaves a single needle-point dot, three per side per step. Gait pattern: alternating tripod gait, prints evenly spaced and almost always in single-file processions overprinted by hundreds of nestmates. Print size class: minute — individual prints need a crouch and good light; the procession trail is what reads first. Distinctive marker: the trail always curves toward the mound, and fresh grains of excavated earth are scattered along it like spilled sugar.
species.silhouette: Outline class: low, soft oval chain — three gently swelling segments in a row. Proportions in words: a small head, a slightly larger thorax, and a plump teardrop abdomen that makes up most of the read. Key visual masses: the pale abdomen is the single biggest mass; antennae are thin strokes in front. What reads at sprite size: the pale teardrop body and the two antenna strokes — one bead of a line. Identifying negative space: the small notch-gap under the raised abdomen between the back legs.
species.statProfile: Frail alone and slow to hurt anything; its real profile is endurance and numbers — tireless work rate, negligible individual threat, surprisingly stubborn when defending the mound. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a pale three-bead worker in a moving line; key features are the plump translucent abdomen, short antennae, and mouth-carried grain of earth. Must-never-change: never draw it alone as a monster — its identity is the procession and the mound; never give it a soldier's menace or weapons; the worker stays soft, pale, and unarmoured.

species.name: Cathedrall
species.dexText: When a Termight colony's mound gains its queen-heart, the whole building wakes as one creature, Cathedrall. Its chimneys breathe cool air over the region on hot days. Travellers steer by its tallest spire, and Termight processions move through its arches like blood through a heart.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C3-1 Termight → Cathedrall — the colony-mound itself gaining a queen-heart; the final "stage" is the colony as a building. Basis: termite cathedral mounds with chimneys, arches, and one tall spire the region navigates by. Design note from the source: R3's colony-promotion idea is social; this one is architectural — the evolution is a building.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a landmark, not a body: a mound tall enough to navigate by, read against the sky like a small hill with a spire
species.temperament: Patient, sheltering, and slow in every sense; protective of the colony within and oddly welcoming to travellers who rest in its shade without chipping at its walls.
species.habitat: It is its habitat — a fixed landmark in Region 4 mound country; a Cathedrall does not relocate.
species.dietBehaviour: The colony feeds it as it feeds the colony: workers bring wood fibre and earth, and the mound's slow inner life turns work into warmth, cool air, and new chambers. It "behaves" on a timescale of seasons — a new arch here, a sealed chimney there.
species.evolution: Colony-formation, completed — Cathedrall is the result, not a further stage; it does not evolve further. The trigger, in words: a mature Termight colony finishing its cathedral mound, and the mound gaining a queen-heart.
species.discovery: Region 4 — mound country; a Cathedrall is found by seeing it on the horizon, not by searching grass. Rarity: very rare as a waking colony-form, though large un-woken mounds are uncommon. Method + conditions: approach on foot on a clear day when the spire is visible from far off; the waking is recognised by warmth at the chimneys and the colony's single shared ticking. Level band (in words): late band — a landmark encounter, met when a Ranger is already seasoned in the region. First-meeting note: the Ranger shelters from noon heat in an arch that is cooler than any shade should be, and only later understands the building was breathing.
species.cry: Source character: the colony heard as one body — deep, slow ticking and earthen settling sounds carried through the mound's chimneys, with a low hollow resonance like wind in a bottle. Pitch contour: low and falling over long phrases, the reverse of the worker's tiny ticks. Duration class: long, widely spaced phrases. Rhythm pattern: a slow heartbeat spacing — tick, tick… long pause — quickening only in alarm or celebration. Variations — idle: sparse deep ticks and soft chimney sighs; call: a resonant pulse that every Termight in the colony answers at once; hurt: a groaning settle and falling dust from the arches when the mound is damaged; faint: not applicable as a battle faint in the ordinary sense — a threatened colony-form goes quiet and still, chimneys cooling, until it is safe; affection: a warm draught from the chimneys and a sheltered arch offered to a resting Ranger; evolution moment: it is an evolution — see Termight's evolution-moment cry (the colony ticking as one as the heart wakes).
species.anatomyNotes: No limbs, no mouth, no locomotion — do not animate it walking or striking. Manipulators: the Termight workers are its hands; any "action" is performed by processions streaming from its gates. Mouth/jaw: none — the chimney mouths breathe, they do not bite. Locomotion: none; its animation is breathing (warm shimmer at chimneys), dust settling, processions entering and leaving, and shadow moving over arches. Signature feature: the single tall navigation spire. Move animation must be environmental — a move from Cathedrall arrives as earth, dust, and worker swarms delivered from the mound.
species.paletteSeed: sun-baked clay, warm ochre, pale bone-cream, deep shade umber, dusty amber at the chimney mouths
species.footprint: It does not walk, so it leaves no footprints — the "track" a Ranger reads instead is the mound's sign: fresh fan-shaped aprons of excavated earth at its base, procession trails of minute paired dots converging on its gates from every direction, shed worker husks in dry drifts against the lee wall, and chimney warmth felt a step before the mound is seen. Distinctive marker: all trails in the area bend toward it — in mound country, every small road leads to Cathedrall.
species.silhouette: Outline class: architectural — an irregular mound mass crowned by one tall, clean spire, with smaller chimneys and arch openings breaking the base. Proportions in words: a broad, grounded base, a rising middle of stacked terraces, and the spire as a single vertical exclamation. Key visual masses: the mound body itself, then the spire — nothing else competes. What reads at sprite size: spire-over-mound, readable at map distance as a landmark icon. Identifying negative space: the dark arch openings at the base — the holes are part of the read, and the tallest arch is always left of the spire's fall line.
species.statProfile: A wall in the truest sense — immense staying power and sheltering presence, no speed, no pursuit; offense, where it exists at all, is the colony acting through it. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the mound-and-spire landmark; key features are the one tall navigation spire, breathing chimneys, arched gates with Termight processions, and the sense of a building that is alive. Must-never-change: never give it legs, a face on the mound, or a walking animation; never shrink it to creature scale; the queen-heart is felt (warmth, ticking, breath), not shown as a monster inside.

species.name: Silvlet
species.dexText: Silvlet lives between the pages and behind the shelves of old libraries, eating paste, dust, and the glue of old spines. It moves like a dropped bead of mercury — there, then not there. Librarians pretend to chase it and quietly leave the damaged bindings where it can reach them.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C3-2 Silvlet → Bookwyrm — a quicksilver sliver of a bug that lives in libraries. Basis: silverfish (open).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a sliver about as long as a bookmark is wide, gone before a hand comes down
species.temperament: Nervous, bright, and harmless; a startle-first creature that freezes in shadow and darts in light.
species.habitat: Region 4 institute libraries and archives — book stacks, binding shelves, and the warm dust under reading desks.
species.dietBehaviour: Paste, paper dust, shed skin, and the glue of old spines. Mostly nocturnal in habit even in lamplit stacks; it traces the edges of shelves in fast, wavering runs and vanishes down the gap behind a row of books.
species.evolution: In words: a Silvlet that has lived long in one archive, eaten deeply of its bindings, and learned its stacks by heart becomes Bookwyrm (see Bookwyrm). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — the institute's library and archive stacks. Rarity: uncommon — plentiful, but so fast and shy that sightings are brief. Method + conditions: search the stacks after closing, lamplight low, moving slowly; look along shelf edges and behind loose bindings, not on open floor. Level band (in words): early band — a small indoor encounter for a Ranger patient enough to look. First-meeting note: something silver crosses the margin of the book the Ranger is reading, and is gone; only a nibbled corner of the page proves it was there.
species.cry: Source character: a near-silent papery rustle with a faint metallic tick, more felt in a quiet room than heard across one. Pitch contour: very high and level, a whisker of sound. Duration class: extremely short. Rhythm pattern: single ticks, or a stutter of three when it changes direction mid-dart. Variations — idle: almost nothing — an occasional rustle-tick while feeding; call: a slightly longer silvery rasp that brings other Silvlet out of the same shelf-gap; hurt: one bright tick and a dart; faint: the rustle slows to a stop under cover — it plays dead in shadow until left alone; affection: a soft repeated ticking against the edge of a book it has been fed from; evolution moment: the ticking stretches into Bookwyrm's longer page-whisper as the body lengthens.
species.anatomyNotes: Long, low, many-legged sliver body; no manipulators — it pushes and tastes with two long antennae and three fine tail filaments. Mouth/jaw: tiny chewing mouthparts under the head, always nibbling when still. Locomotion: the signature — a swimming, side-to-side darting run, fish-like on land, with instant stops. Signature feature: the liquid-metal sheen; animate the run as a wiggle-dart, never as a steady scuttle.
species.paletteSeed: liquid silver, pale mercury grey, library dust beige, ink-shadow blue-grey
species.footprint: Print shape class: a fine sinuous drag-line with hair-thin leg ticks feathering both sides, like a stitch unpicked across dust. Toe/claw count and arrangement: no toes — dozens of minute leg points too small to count on a casual look, recorded as a feathered fringe. Gait pattern: wavering S-curves that stop dead at shadow edges and resume beyond them. Print size class: minute — visible only in undisturbed library dust or on a sunlit desk. Distinctive marker: the trail begins and ends at books — a shelf edge, a spine gap, a nibbled page corner.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a thin tapered sliver — pointed at both ends, widest just behind the head. Proportions in words: almost all body is length; antennae ahead and tail filaments behind extend the line further. Key visual masses: none large — it is a line, not a lump. What reads at sprite size: the bright silver dash and its wiggle. Identifying negative space: the forked split of the three tail filaments at the rear — the only "notch" in an otherwise smooth sliver.
species.statProfile: Extremely fast and extremely frail; a creature whose whole profile is not being there when anything lands. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a living silver dash; key features are the mercury sheen, long antennae, and triple tail filaments. Must-never-change: never bulk it up or armour it; never slow its darting, swimming gait; it stays a sliver that reads as motion first and body second.

species.name: Bookwyrm
species.dexText: Bookwyrm is the institute archive's pest and mascot in one long silver body. It has eaten the paste of a thousand bindings and, librarians swear, read everything it digested. It will not discuss endings, and goes pointedly still if asked.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C3-2 Silvlet → Bookwyrm — the archive's pest and mascot; it has read everything and will not discuss endings. Basis: silverfish, grown long on a life among books. Region fit from the source: Region 4's institute region needs an archive haunter; this is it.
species.sizeClass: Small — long rather than large: a forearm-length of silver sliver draped over a stack, still thin enough to slip behind a shelf
species.temperament: Dry, knowing, and unbothered; the calm of a creature that has lived in one quiet building longer than any of its keepers.
species.habitat: Deep archive stacks of the Region 4 institute — the oldest shelves, the restricted bindings, the warm top of the tallest bookcase.
species.dietBehaviour: The glue and paste of old spines, paper dust, and the occasional offered page-corner, which it accepts like a tribute. It drapes, reads the room, and relocates only when a shelf is moved — an event it treats as an earthquake and a personal insult.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Silvlet by a long archive life (see Silvlet).
species.discovery: Region 4 — the institute archive's oldest stacks. Rarity: rare — one established Bookwyrm per true archive is the usual story. Method + conditions: search after closing with a librarian's permission, in the restricted stacks, and wait rather than chase; it comes to inspect a reader who sits still long enough. Level band (in words): mid band — a quiet, late-library encounter. First-meeting note: it drapes itself over the spine of the very book the Ranger came for, regards them for a long moment, and slides aside — exactly one book's width.
species.cry: Source character: a long papery whisper-rustle, like a page turned very slowly, threaded with Silvlet's metallic tick grown lower and slower. Pitch contour: high but settled, falling gently at the end of each phrase, like a sigh over paper. Duration class: short phrases, longer than Silvlet's ticks. Rhythm pattern: unhurried single phrases with long reading pauses between. Variations — idle: slow page-whisper while draped and feeding; call: a drier, crisper rustle that settles every Silvlet in the stacks to stillness; hurt: a sharp page-snap sound and a silver uncoiling dart; faint: the whisper frays into separated ticks and stops, body flat in shadow; affection: a soft, continuous rustle while draping near a familiar librarian's or Ranger's reading place — its version of purring, in paper; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the moment is recorded under Silvlet).
species.anatomyNotes: Silvlet's plan, lengthened: many short legs under a long, low, flexible body that drapes over edges rather than standing. Manipulators: none — antennae taste and tap; the tail filaments have grown into three fine, expressive streamers. Mouth/jaw: small nibbling mouthparts; feeding is a head-down graze along a spine. Locomotion: the same swimming wiggle-dart as Silvlet, slower and more deliberate, with long still drapes between moves. Signature feature: the drape — it hangs over a book's edge in a soft catenary curve, and move delivery comes from the uncoiling dart, not from any limb strike.
species.paletteSeed: aged silver, parchment cream, library dust beige, faded ink blue, shelf-shadow grey
species.footprint: Print shape class: Silvlet's feathered stitch-trail grown bolder — a clear sinuous drag with paired leg-tick fringes, crossing open dust in long S-curves. Toe/claw count and arrangement: no toes; the fringe of minute leg points is denser and more even than Silvlet's. Gait pattern: unhurried waves with long gaps where it draped or rested — the trail pauses at books. Print size class: small — readable in archive dust without magnification. Distinctive marker: the trail visits bindings in order, shelf by shelf, like a reading list — and stops, always, one book before the end of a row.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long silver ribbon with a softly pointed head and a three-streamer tail. Proportions in words: length dominates completely; the body is a low, even ribbon with no large mass anywhere along it. Key visual masses: the draped middle curve is the read — a hanging arc between two shelf points. What reads at sprite size: the bright ribbon and its drape. Identifying negative space: the twin notches of the forked tail streamers, and the open curve under a drape where a book's edge shows through.
species.statProfile: Still fast, still frail, but seasoned — quicker to vanish, harder to corner, and far more accurate in its darting strikes than Silvlet; a veteran of one quiet building. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is a long silver ribbon draped over books; key features are the mercury sheen aged to a softer shine, the triple tail streamers, and the drape pose. Must-never-change: never make it a literal dragon or give it wings, legs of length, or a book for a body; it stays a silverfish grown long and knowing — and it never, ever discusses endings.

species.name: Stinklet
species.dexText: Stinklet carries the shield bug's famous scent glands, but the scent that comes out is lovely — green, sweet, and faintly floral. It releases a puff when startled, then seems faintly embarrassed about the mess. Other bugs follow it for the smell alone.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C3-3 Stinklet → Perfumarch — a shield bug whose scent glands make, against all expectation, perfume. Basis: shield / stink bugs (open).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a shield-shaped bug that sits comfortably on a thumbnail, broad for its length
species.temperament: Mild, startle-prone, and quietly pleased with itself whenever its perfume lands well.
species.habitat: Region 4 hedgerows, institute gardens, and the planted borders around Rift settlements — anywhere leaves are thick and the air is still.
species.dietBehaviour: Sips plant juices from stems and soft fruit skins. Spends long still hours flattened on the underside of a leaf; its defence is the perfume puff — beautiful, distracting, and just strong enough at close range to make anything chasing it stop and reconsider.
species.evolution: In words: a Stinklet whose glands mature and whose scent turns from lucky accident to craft becomes Perfumarch (see Perfumarch). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — institute gardens and hedgerow borders. Rarity: common in planted ground, uncommon in the wild Rift scrub. Method + conditions: search leaf undersides on a warm, still morning; follow the one unexpectedly pleasant smell in the hedge. Level band (in words): earliest band — a gentle garden encounter. First-meeting note: the Ranger's hand closes on leaves, a small sweet cloud blooms, and Stinklet is sitting in the middle of it, very still, hoping the perfume did the introductions.
species.cry: Source character: a soft leafy squeak with a faint fizzy edge, like a tiny cork easing out. Pitch contour: mid-high, popping up at the start of each note and settling. Duration class: very short. Rhythm pattern: single squeaks, or an apologetic double-squeak after a startle. Variations — idle: sparse soft squeaks while feeding; call: a slightly fizzier squeak that draws other Stinklet to the same leaf; hurt: a sharp squeak with the perfume puff released at the same instant; faint: squeaks thin out and the shield goes still and leaf-flat; affection: a mellow, bubbly little trill while perched on a familiar hand; evolution moment: the squeaks deepen and layer as the glands mature into Perfumarch's perfumed hum.
species.anatomyNotes: Six legs under a single broad shield shell; the body is the shield — there is no separate "back armour" piece. Manipulators: none; the piercing mouthparts are a fine rostrum folded under the head. Mouth/jaw: a sap-sipping beak, not a bite. Locomotion: slow, flat leaf-walking with short, neat steps; it flies only as a last resort, in a brief buzzy lift. Signature feature: the scent glands at the rear of the shield — any scent or Flora delivery animates from there, as a visible blooming puff, while the bug itself stays put.
species.paletteSeed: fresh leaf green, soft chartreuse, warm amber at the shield edge, pale cream belly
species.footprint: Print shape class: six tiny pinpricks in two staggered rows under a faint shield-shaped body-press where it rested. Toe/claw count and arrangement: one minute point per leg, three per side, the middle pair set widest. Gait pattern: slow, even, straight-line walking between leaves, prints widely spaced for so small a bug. Print size class: minute — found on dusty leaves and pale garden soil rather than open ground. Distinctive marker: a faint sweet-smelling damp spot at each rest point — the only print in the bucket a Ranger can follow by nose.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a clean geometric shield — broad rounded shoulders tapering to a soft point at the rear. Proportions in words: width is the story; the body is nearly as wide as it is long, low and flat. Key visual masses: the single shield mass, unbroken. What reads at sprite size: the shield shape itself, in green. Identifying negative space: the small triangular notch where the head tucks into the shield's front edge.
species.statProfile: Slow and soft-hitting, with staying power out of proportion to its size — the shield shrugs off glancing blows, and the perfume buys it room. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the living shield; key features are the unbroken shield shell, the folded sap-beak, and the perfume puff from the rear glands. Must-never-change: never make the scent a stink — the joke and the identity is that it is beautiful; never add horns, spikes, or menace to the shield; the puff is a bloom, not a gas attack.

species.name: Perfumarch
species.dexText: Perfumarch is the region's perfumer, and knows it. It processes through the gardens in a drifting cloud of its own finest scent, adjusting the blend leaf by leaf. Being near it is lovely for a moment, then a great deal — it has never once understood this.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C3-3 Stinklet → Perfumarch — the region's perfumer, processing in a cloud of its own best work. Basis: shield / stink bugs, grown grand. Temperament from the source: artist.
species.sizeClass: Small — a grand shield bug, about a palm across, carried high and proudly for a crawler
species.temperament: Artist — proud, meticulous, and generous with its work whether the audience asked or not; slightly hard to be near, entirely without malice.
species.habitat: Region 4's finest planted ground — institute gardens, festival flower rows, and the hedges around perfumers' and florists' doors, which it visits like a critic.
species.dietBehaviour: Plant juices chosen like ingredients — it feeds selectively, stem by stem, and its scent changes with its diet across the season. It processes slowly from flower bed to flower bed, trailing perfume, pausing to release a considered puff the way a painter steps back from a canvas.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Stinklet when accident became craft (see Stinklet).
species.discovery: Region 4 — institute gardens and festival flower ground. Rarity: uncommon — unmistakable when present, but it keeps a perfumer's hours and a critic's circuit. Method + conditions: search by nose on a still, warm afternoon; the encounter begins several garden rows before the creature is seen. Level band (in words): mid band — a garden encounter with some presence behind it. First-meeting note: the Ranger smells it long before they see it, follows the scent like a ribbon, and finds Perfumarch mid-procession, turning slowly to present its best side and its best blend.
species.cry: Source character: Stinklet's leafy squeak matured into a layered, perfumed hum-squeak — soft, round, and self-satisfied, with a faint chime at the end of phrases. Pitch contour: mid range, rising with pride at phrase ends. Duration class: short phrases, longer and more composed than Stinklet's pops. Rhythm pattern: deliberate singles with artist's pauses; a pleased triple-note when a blend comes out right. Variations — idle: low composed hum-squeaks while processing; call: a carrying, chime-ended phrase that gathers Stinklet from the hedge like apprentices; hurt: a startled squeak and an uncontrolled, overwhelming perfume burst — its embarrassment is audible; faint: phrases trail off into the cloud as it goes leaf-flat and still; affection: a warm, bubbly trill with a deliberately gentle puff, its version of a gift; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the moment is recorded under Stinklet).
species.anatomyNotes: The shield shell is now a grand, high-domed canopy carried on six deliberate legs; the body walks *under* its own masterpiece. Manipulators: none; the rostrum still sips, now with a connoisseur's selectivity. Mouth/jaw: fine sap-beak, never a bite. Locomotion: a slow procession — short steps, long pauses, the cloud moving with it. Signature feature: the perfume cloud itself, produced from the rear glands in visible, layered blooms; animate scent as its primary "action" language — puffs, trails, and the grand burst — while strikes, if any, are small and secondary.
species.paletteSeed: deep leaf green, gold-amber shield trim, blush-rose at the glands, cream, a haze of lilac in its cloud
species.footprint: Print shape class: six firm pinpricks in two rows with a broad shield body-press at each pause, bolder than Stinklet's. Toe/claw count and arrangement: one point per leg, three per side, evenly and proudly spaced. Gait pattern: a procession in prints — clusters of steps, then a rest-press, then steps again. Print size class: small — readable on garden paths and pale soil. Distinctive marker: each rest-press carries a lingering sweet damp ring, so the trail can be followed blindfold, by scent alone.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a grand domed shield on legs — a small walking canopy. Proportions in words: the shield is wider and higher than the body beneath it; legs read as a fringe below the dome. Key visual masses: the dome alone; everything else is detail at its edge. What reads at sprite size: dome-plus-cloud — the perfume haze is part of the silhouette and should be drawn as a soft halo mass. Identifying negative space: the arch of open air under the raised shield between the front and back legs, where the cloud drifts through.
species.statProfile: A slow, sturdy presence — hard to shift, harder to ignore; its strength is field control through scent, not damage. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the domed shield processing inside its own perfume cloud; key features are the high grand shield, the proud unhurried gait, and scent rendered as layered floral blooms. Must-never-change: never render the perfume as foul, green-stink cartoon gas — it is beautiful and merely too much; never slim the shield into an ordinary bug; the pride is in the posture, not in a face.

species.name: Bomblet
species.dexText: Bomblet carries two harmless sips in two separate tanks in its abdomen, and that is the whole trick: mixed, they pop — boiling, loud, and harmless at any range beyond a startle. It pops when surprised, when pleased, and occasionally when it has simply been saving one up.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Beetles are Pokémon-crowded — the seed is the two-chamber chemistry, which no Pokémon beetle uses (source §5). Carried line-wide.
species.lineConcept: C3-4 Bomblet → Chemcannon — a small beetle carrying two harmless sips in separate tanks; mixed, they pop. Basis: bombardier beetle (open as a mechanism — the two-chamber chemistry).
species.sizeClass: Small — a sturdy beetle about as long as a matchbox, low and dense
species.temperament: Cheerful, startle-happy, and entirely unaware of its own volume; a friendly firecracker.
species.habitat: Region 4 dry paths, festival-ground edges, and warm stony banks where it can bask and pop in peace.
species.dietBehaviour: Soft plant matter, fallen fruit, and small scavenged scraps. It grazes with its head down and its tanked abdomen up; anything sudden — a shadow, a shout, a friend arriving — earns a pop, after which it needs a little while to brew the next one.
species.evolution: In words: a Bomblet whose tanks grow deep and whose mixing chamber matures into true aim becomes Chemcannon (see Chemcannon). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — dry paths and festival-ground edges. Rarity: common in its ground, though more often heard than seen. Method + conditions: walk a warm stony bank at midday and listen for pops; approach openly — a sneaked-upon Bomblet simply pops earlier. Level band (in words): early band — a loud, harmless introduction to the region's crawlers. First-meeting note: the Ranger hears three pops getting closer, rounds a stone, and finds Bomblet popping at its own shadow — then, delighted to have company, at the Ranger.
species.cry: Source character: a round beetle chirr underneath its real voice — the pop itself, a bright percussive *thock* with a boiling hiss at its edge. Pitch contour: the chirr sits mid range; the pop has no pitch so much as a crack and a falling hiss. Duration class: the pop is instant; chirrs are short. Rhythm pattern: chirrs in loose singles; pops in startled singles, never in rapid fire — there is always a brewing pause. Variations — idle: soft grazing chirrs between long quiet stretches; call: a chirr-and-pop combination that other Bomblet answer down the bank, pop answering pop like distant festival drums; hurt: an immediate loud pop and a scuttle under cover; faint: a final small, sad fizzle — a pop that didn't quite — then quiet; affection: a deliberately tiny pop, its smallest, offered like a firework for one; evolution moment: the pops deepen and space out into Chemcannon's cannon rhythm as the chamber matures.
species.anatomyNotes: Six legs, a hard wing-case shell, and an abdomen visibly built around two rounded tanks with a mixing chamber at the rear tip. Manipulators: none — small mandibles handle food. Mouth/jaw: a grazer's mandibles at the front; all the drama is at the back. Locomotion: a low, dense beetle scuttle with a waddle from the tanked abdomen. Signature feature: the rear mixing nozzle — every pop, jet, or Flame delivery animates from the rear chamber as the beetle braces, tips its abdomen, and fires backward or upward; it must visibly brace and brew, never fire continuously.
species.paletteSeed: lacquered chestnut, brass-chrome tank bands, ember orange at the nozzle, cream belly
species.footprint: Print shape class: six stout claw-ticks in two rows with a low belly-drag between them from the heavy abdomen. Toe/claw count and arrangement: one firm tick per leg, three per side, the rear pair set widest to carry the tanks. Gait pattern: short dense strides, frequently interrupted. Print size class: small — clear in dust and path grit. Distinctive marker: the trail is punctuated by tiny paired scorch-dots and a faint boiled smell wherever it popped — a dotted line of small celebrations along the path.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low beetle oval with a swollen, twin-lobed rear. Proportions in words: the tanked abdomen is the biggest mass, ahead of a smaller head and a neat wing-case middle. Key visual masses: the two tank lobes at the back — the silhouette's whole point. What reads at sprite size: beetle oval plus double-bump rear. Identifying negative space: the narrow waist-notch between the wing case and the twin tanks.
species.statProfile: Small and sturdy with a loud trick — modest staying power, modest speed, and a pop that startles far above its weight; between pops, it is just a beetle. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the twin-tanked beetle; key features are the two visibly separate rear tanks, the bracing aim pose, and the pop rendered as boiling steam and noise, not explosion damage. Must-never-change: never merge the two tanks into one — the two-chamber chemistry is the seed; never make the pop a weapon of harm at range — it is loud, boiling, and harmless, a startle and a celebration.

species.name: Chemcannon
species.dexText: Chemcannon is the festival's noisemaker and the region's tiniest artillery, and it takes bookings — weddings are its favourite. It aims its boiling pop with great ceremony and greater pride. The pop has never hurt anyone. The bride's grandmother's hat is another matter.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Beetles are Pokémon-crowded — the seed is the two-chamber chemistry, which no Pokémon beetle uses (source §5).
species.lineConcept: C3-4 Chemcannon — the festival's noisemaker and the region's tiniest artillery, hired for weddings. Basis: bombardier beetle, grown into its mechanism — two chambers, mixed on aim.
species.sizeClass: Medium — still the tiniest artillery imaginable: a heavy beetle about as big as a kettle, all chamber and ceremony
species.temperament: Professional, proud, and ceremonious; a performer who treats every pop as a commission and every audience as a festival.
species.habitat: Region 4 festival grounds, wedding gardens, and warm banks near settlements — wherever it is within earshot of a celebration.
species.dietBehaviour: Fallen fruit, soft plant matter, and the festival scraps its admirers leave it. Between engagements it brews, basks, and practises its aim at stones; on the day, it arrives early, positions itself like a living cannon emplacement, and pops on cue.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Bomblet when the tanks deepened and the aim matured (see Bomblet).
species.discovery: Region 4 — festival grounds and celebration gardens. Rarity: uncommon in the wild, reliably present at festivals — an event-adjacent encounter. Method + conditions: attend a Region 4 festival or wedding and ask who is doing the popping; or find its practice bank on a quiet warm day and listen. Level band (in words): mid-to-late band — a seasoned Ranger's reward, met through the region's social life. First-meeting note: the Ranger is halfway through congratulating a wedding party when the ground itself seems to applaud — Chemcannon, emplaced behind the flower arch, taking its bow one pop at a time.
species.cry: Source character: a deep beetle chirr under a true cannon-pop — a rolling *boom-thock* with a long boiling hiss, pitched like a festival drum heard through steam. Pitch contour: chirrs sit low; the pop cracks high and falls away into hiss. Duration class: pops are instant with a long hiss tail; chirrs are short and formal. Rhythm pattern: ceremonial spacing — pop… pop… pop — with long brewing pauses it refuses to be hurried out of. Variations — idle: low practice chirrs and the occasional ranging pop at a stone; call: a formal three-pop salute that Bomblet down the bank answer raggedly; hurt: a startled, unaimed pop and a heavy scuttle into its emplacement hollow; faint: a grand final pop, a hiss that goes on too long, and then a tipped, steaming stillness; affection: a soft, precisely aimed pop that showers warm harmless steam over a favourite Ranger — its salute, at closest range; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the moment is recorded under Bomblet).
species.anatomyNotes: Bomblet's plan, fortified: a heavy wing-case, six braced legs that visibly plant before firing, and an abdomen that is now a true twin-chamber assembly with an aiming nozzle that can elevate and traverse. Manipulators: none. Mouth/jaw: grazing mandibles, irrelevant to its craft. Locomotion: a slow, heavy, deliberate beetle march — it positions like artillery, it does not chase. Signature feature: the aim — animate the whole body as the weapon: legs brace, abdomen lifts, nozzle lines up, pause for brewing, pop. The ceremony and the pause are part of every move delivery.
species.paletteSeed: dark lacquer brown, polished brass-chrome chambers, ember orange, wedding cream, festival red accent at the nozzle ring
species.footprint: Print shape class: six deep claw-ticks in two rows with a broad belly-and-tank drag, ending at each firing position in a braced star of dug-in prints. Toe/claw count and arrangement: one heavy tick per leg, three per side, the rear pair dug deepest. Gait pattern: slow march strides between emplacements; at each stop the prints cluster and deepen. Print size class: small-to-medium — unmistakable in festival dust. Distinctive marker: paired fan-shaped scorch-and-steam marks at every firing position, smelling faintly of boiled fruit — the only artillery range a Ranger can identify by smell.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low, heavy beetle mass dominated by a raised twin-chamber rear that reads as a small cannon on a living carriage. Proportions in words: fully half the read is chamber; head and legs are the supporting act. Key visual masses: the twin chambers and the nozzle above all. What reads at sprite size: beetle-plus-cannon — the elevated nozzle line against the low body. Identifying negative space: the gap under the elevated abdomen between the braced rear legs, where steam escapes.
species.statProfile: Slow, dense, and stubborn — a living emplacement with a loud, harmless-at-range signature and the staying power to hold its position through a whole festival. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the tiniest artillery: a kettle-heavy beetle whose raised twin chambers read as a ceremonial cannon. Key features are the separate chambers, the bracing ceremony, and steam-and-noise pops. Must-never-change: never merge the chambers, never make it military or menacing — it is hired for weddings; never let it fire without the brewing pause and the bow-like settle afterwards.

species.name: Hopbrella
species.dexText: Hopbrella hops out after rain on its single leg, finds whoever forgot their umbrella, and sticks out a very long tongue at them. It does not curse anyone. It lends itself, pointedly, holds the rain off beautifully — and expects to be returned.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-1 Hopbrella — a one-eyed, one-legged umbrella spirit that hops after rain and lends itself, pointedly. Basis: karakasa-obake (umbrella spirit — creature-shape only).
species.sizeClass: Medium — a full-sized umbrella come alive, canopy about as wide as a person's outstretched arms when open
species.temperament: Teasing, punctual, and deeply principled about being returned; kind underneath the pointedness.
species.habitat: Region 4 rainy lanes, institute doorways, bridge ends, and bus-stop-like shelters — wherever people get caught by weather.
species.dietBehaviour: It does not eat in any ordinary way; it seems to live on rain, lamplight, and the satisfaction of a debt properly repaid. Behaviour is the lending cycle: appear after rain, mock the umbrella-less, lend itself for exactly one journey, then hop the town until returned to the spot where it was borrowed.
species.evolution: Single-stage — does not evolve; some yokai arrive finished, and Hopbrella arrives finished.
species.discovery: Region 4 — rainy lanes, doorways, and shelters across the Rift settlements. Rarity: event-class in pattern though not in numbers — it appears after rain, to the person who needs it. Method + conditions: be caught without an umbrella in a Region 4 downpour and wait under a doorway; scolding it, chasing it, or carrying a spare umbrella all prevent the meeting. Level band (in words): any band — it chooses the meeting, not the Ranger's strength. First-meeting note: the rain starts, the doorway drips, and something hops around the corner, opens itself with a snap, sticks out its tongue — and then, pointedly, holds still to be taken up.
species.cry: Source character: a wet canvas *fwump*, a squeaking hop-spring, and a rude wet raspberry from the long tongue — percussion and canvas, not a voice. Pitch contour: the squeak rises with each hop and drops flat on landing; the raspberry has no pitch, only cheek. Duration class: short, one sound per hop. Rhythm pattern: hop… hop… fwump — an uneven, teasing rhythm that speeds up when it is showing off. Variations — idle: slow hop-squeaks and occasional canvas settles under a drip line; call: a loud snap-open fwump that other Hopbrella answer from doorways down the street; hurt: a squeak, a wobble, and a half-collapsed fwump; faint: the canopy folds with a long wet sigh and lies still until the rain stops; affection: a pleased little fwump-and-shake that sheds rain in a sparkling ring — then the tongue, because affection does not excuse anyone; evolution moment: not applicable — single-stage.
species.anatomyNotes: One leg, and the animator must honour it: all locomotion is hopping, with the canopy bobbing and tilting for balance. Manipulators: none — the tongue is its only "hand," used to point, mock, and tug at sleeves. Mouth/jaw: the long tongue emerges from under the canopy near the single large eye; the eye does the expressing — wide for mockery, soft for lending. Locomotion: springing hops, faster downhill, with a gliding half-open drift when the wind helps (its Gale side). Signature feature: the snap-open — canopy closed is a travelling form, canopy open is its whole personality; every move delivery starts from the open/closed beat.
species.paletteSeed: oiled-paper cream, indigo canopy ribs, vermilion eye accent, wet slate grey, tongue pink
species.footprint: Print shape class: a single round-toed print per landing — one foot only, ever — spaced in a hopping line, each print paired with a small wet tongue-dab mark just ahead of it where the tongue touched down for balance or emphasis. Toe/claw count and arrangement: the single foot leaves a soft three-pad press, no claws. Gait pattern: strictly alternating single prints in a bouncing arc, spacing widening downhill and after rain on slick stone. Print size class: small-to-medium — one print the size of a child's shoe, repeated. Distinctive marker: the tongue-dab — a small wet comma beside every second or third print, the signature no other hopper leaves.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a mushroom-cap dome on a single stem — canopy above, one leg below, nothing else. Proportions in words: the canopy is nearly all the width; the leg is a thin off-centre stem; the eye sits at the dome's front edge like a lamp. Key visual masses: canopy dome first, tongue second when out. What reads at sprite size: dome-plus-one-leg, instantly. Identifying negative space: the wide open air under the canopy on both sides of the single leg — the emptiness where a second leg should be is the recognition.
species.statProfile: Quick, springy, and surprisingly hard to hit mid-hop; fragile if pinned, but it is never where the weather — or the blow — lands. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the one-legged open umbrella with a single great eye and a very long tongue. Key features are the snap-open canopy, the hop, and the mock-lending manner. Must-never-change: never give it a second leg, a second eye, or a curse — it does not curse anyone; never make it sinister — its teasing is kind, and it always, always expects to be returned.

species.name: Boltcloth
species.dexText: Boltcloth flies at dusk over the roads between Region 4 settlements, looking — though it would never put it so grandly — for somebody cold. Folklore says its kind smothers; this one wraps. Lost travellers wake tucked into warm white cotton with one corner folded like a pillow.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-2 Boltcloth → Wraproll — a roll of living cotton cloth that flies at dusk and wraps rather than smothers. Basis: ittan-momen (flying cloth spirit — creature-shape only), re-toned to hospitality.
species.sizeClass: Small — a travelling bolt of cloth, about as long as a person is tall when it unrolls in flight, rolled tight to rucksack size at rest
species.temperament: Gentle, shy, and service-minded; it helps from a distance and is embarrassed to be thanked to its face — which makes its evolution a slow business.
species.habitat: Dusk skies over Region 4 roads, passes, and ferry landings — anywhere travellers can be caught out by dark and cold.
species.dietBehaviour: It does not eat; it gathers warmth — sunlit stones at noon, chimney thermals at evening — and spends it at night on strangers. By day it rests rolled in a warm, sheltered hollow; at dusk it unrolls, rises, and patrols the roads in long, quiet ribbons of flight.
species.evolution: Thankfulness-count — Boltcloth evolves by being thanked enough times. (Nobody has counted. It's a lot.) See Wraproll.
species.discovery: Region 4 — dusk roads and passes between settlements. Rarity: rare as a sighting, though many more travellers have met it asleep than awake. Method + conditions: travel a cold road at dusk, or be found by it — most encounters are discovered in the morning, in the wrapping. Level band (in words): mid band — a traveller's encounter, earned by being out in the region rather than by strength. First-meeting note: the Ranger wakes at dawn tucked into warm white cloth with one corner folded like a pillow, and just catches a white ribbon lifting away over the pass, too shy to stay for thanks.
species.cry: Source character: cloth in wind — soft flaps, billows, and a faint humming along its edge when it flies fast, like a flag remembering a tune. Pitch contour: the hum rises with speed and settles as it slows to wrap. Duration class: long, soft phrases while flying; near-silence when wrapping. Rhythm pattern: an uneven flap-flap-glide, matched to wingbeats it does not have. Variations — idle: slow soft flapping from its resting roll as breezes find it; call: a clearer edge-hum that other Boltcloth answer down the valley at dusk; hurt: a sharp snap-flap and a tumbling fold; faint: it settles out of the sky in slow spirals and lies folded and still; affection: the flapping gentles to almost nothing as it wraps — the quiet itself is the affection; evolution moment: thankfulness after thankfulness, the flaps deepen and broaden over years until one dusk the ribbon that rises is Wraproll, and the hum is a chorus of cloth.
species.anatomyNotes: No limbs, no head, no mouth — the body is the cloth, and the animator's whole vocabulary is fold, billow, wrap, and edge-tremble. Manipulators: its corners and edges, which fold with deliberate care (the pillow-fold is a two-corner manoeuvre). Mouth/jaw: none, ever — it never speaks and has no face to speak with; expression is in the cloth's tension. Locomotion: true flight by undulation, ribbon-style, plus a rolled resting form it drops into by folding. Signature feature: the wrap — any defensive or healing-flavoured delivery is the cloth arriving around a target; offensive delivery, where it exists, is a snapping edge, never a suffocation — it wraps, it does not smother.
species.paletteSeed: warm cotton white, dusk blue shadow, faint sunset rose at the edges, soft grey fold-lines
species.footprint: A flying cloth leaves no footprints; its trace is a NON-print sign — a long, soft rectangular press in road dust or frost where it settled over a sleeping traveller, edges crisp, one corner folded down in a neat triangular pillow-press. On grass: a pale, warmth-flattened patch that stays frost-free until mid-morning. Distinctive marker: the pillow-fold corner — no natural settling cloth folds its own corner.
species.silhouette: Outline class: in flight, a long ribbon with soft scalloped edges; at rest, a neat cylindrical roll. Proportions in words: all length and no thickness — a banner's body with a traveller's manners. Key visual masses: none solid; the read is the ribbon's wave itself, widest at its billowing middle. What reads at sprite size: the white S-curve against a dusk sky. Identifying negative space: the open loops of its flight-wave — the sky showing through the ribbon's curves is part of the shape.
species.statProfile: Light, evasive, and enduring rather than strong — hard to hold, impossible to hurry, with a traveller's stamina for long cold nights. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the flying white ribbon that becomes a blanket; key features are the billowing undulation, the shy distance, and the pillow-folded corner. Must-never-change: never give it a face, hands, or a smothering menace — the folklore menace is explicitly re-toned away; it wraps, warms, and leaves before thanks.

species.name: Wraproll
species.dexText: Wraproll is what Boltcloth becomes after being thanked more times than anyone has counted, and it is ten metres of flying hospitality. Whole lost parties wake under it on cold passes, tucked in, every corner folded. It still leaves before the thanks. Some things do not change.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-2 Boltcloth → Wraproll — ten metres of flying hospitality (source's own measure). Basis: ittan-momen, grown grand and kept gentle.
species.sizeClass: Large — a vast length of living cloth; when it settles over a campsite it covers the whole party like a marquee settling gently down
species.temperament: Warm, grand, and still shy — a great kindness that prefers to be discovered rather than witnessed.
species.habitat: High passes, ferry landings, and festival-eve roads across Region 4 — the places where many travellers, not just one, can be caught by the cold.
species.dietBehaviour: Warmth, gathered at scale: a day spread on a sunlit cliff, an evening riding chimney thermals over a town. At dusk it rises like a slow white sail and goes looking for camps that need it; by dawn it is always gone, leaving folded corners and an argument about whether anyone dreamed it.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Boltcloth by the thankfulness-count (see Boltcloth).
species.discovery: Region 4 — high passes and festival-eve roads. Rarity: very rare as a witnessed encounter; its work is uncommon-but-regular on the coldest routes. Method + conditions: camp exposed on a pass on a bitter night, in company — it comes to groups — and sleep; the meeting is confirmed at dawn by the wrapping. Level band (in words): late band — a high-country encounter for a Ranger whose road has taken them far. First-meeting note: the whole party wakes under one vast warm canopy of white cloth, corners folded like a made bed the size of a field, and the last of it is just lifting away into the dawn wind.
species.cry: Source character: great cloth in high wind — deep soft booms as the billows fill, a broad edge-hum like a distant choir of flags, and long kind silences when it settles. Pitch contour: low and broad, rising slowly as it climbs, falling to near-nothing as it wraps. Duration class: long phrases, minutes of weather rather than seconds of call. Rhythm pattern: boom… drift… boom, the slow breathing of a sail. Variations — idle: slow billow-booms while it rides a thermal; call: a carrying hum that Boltcloth across the valley answer and rise to; hurt: a tearing-snap flap and a shuddering fold — it retreats upward rather than fight; faint: it loses the wind in slow, grand spirals and settles folded over itself until left in peace; affection: the great quiet — it wraps a whole camp in near-silence, the softest sound it owns; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the moment is recorded under Boltcloth).
species.anatomyNotes: Boltcloth's plan at scale: a single vast cloth body, no limbs, no face, no mouth. Manipulators: corners and edges with the strength to lift its own folds and the delicacy to tuck a sleeping child in — animate both in the same gesture language. Mouth/jaw: none. Locomotion: slow sail-flight by great undulations; it travels as weather travels. Signature feature: the full-camp wrap — its grand delivery is arrival itself, a canopy descending; scale must read in every animation (folds take time, edges arrive after middles).
species.paletteSeed: warm cotton white, dawn gold at the edges, dusk blue in the deep folds, soft rose, high-sky grey
species.footprint: No footprints; its trace is a NON-print sign at campsite scale — a vast, soft rectangular warmth-press over an entire camp clearing, grass unfrosted and dew-free in a clean-edged field-sized patch, with folded-corner triangular presses at the margins. Distinctive marker: multiple pillow-folds — one per sleeper. A camp that wakes tucked wakes certain.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a slow white sail — a broad billowing rectangle in the sky, edges scalloped by wind. Proportions in words: length and breadth together, still no thickness; it is a field of cloth, not a creature-shaped creature. Key visual masses: the central billow, which swells and settles like breathing. What reads at sprite size: the great white S-curve, wider and slower than Boltcloth's ribbon. Identifying negative space: the deep U-curves of its undulation, sky showing through in slow rhythm.
species.statProfile: A gentle weather-system of a creature — immense endurance and presence, minimal offense; what it does to a battlefield is mostly make it warmer and calmer. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the vast flying blanket over a sleeping camp; key features are scale, slowness, and the folded corners at dawn. Must-never-change: never add a face or limbs, never stage it as a threat descending — its arrival is comfort, every time; the shyness survives the size.

species.name: Boneling
species.dexText: Boneling is a small bone-sprite that collects lost buttons and teeth, and keeps them sorted. It rattles softly when it walks, like a drawer of small precious things. Nothing it collects is ever thrown away; some of it, it is saving for someone.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-3 Boneling → Skelloss — a small bone-sprite that collects lost buttons and teeth. Basis: gashadokuro, re-toned small and gentle from the start.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a pocketable sprite, about as tall as a teacup, light enough to ride in a coat pocket among its finds
species.temperament: Melancholy, tidy, and hopeful; a little keeper of lost things, waiting in a patient way for the people the lost things belong to.
species.habitat: Region 4 forgotten meadows, old battlefield-turned-pasture edges (long at peace), churchyard-like memorial gardens, and the quiet corners of abandoned Rift cottages.
species.dietBehaviour: It does not eat; it collects. Behaviours are the collection rounds — meadow paths at dusk, turning over leaves for buttons, lining finds up in size order, and carrying the best of them home to a hollow it shares, eventually, with its greater self.
species.evolution: In words: a Boneling that has collected long enough — a forgotten place's worth of small lost things — gathers itself into the gentle giant Skelloss (see Skelloss). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — forgotten meadows and memorial gardens at dusk. Rarity: uncommon — present in any truly forgotten place, but quiet and pocket-small. Method + conditions: search at dusk along meadow paths, listening for a faint rattle; leave a lost button on a stone and wait at a kind distance. Level band (in words): early-to-mid band — a small, sad, gentle encounter. First-meeting note: a button the Ranger dropped an hour ago is placed, neatly, on the path in front of them — and a small pale shape is already retreating into the long grass, rattling softly.
species.cry: Source character: a gentle bone-rattle and a tiny hollow clink, like wind chimes made of buttons heard from another room — musical, never eerie. Pitch contour: high, hollow notes that fall in small descending runs, like something being put away in order. Duration class: short phrases. Rhythm pattern: rattle-clink… rattle-clink, in step with its walk; slower and sparser when it is sad, which is often. Variations — idle: sparse soft rattles while sorting its collection; call: a clear little clink-sequence that other Boneling answer across the meadow; hurt: one startled rattle-burst and a scatter-flat into the grass; faint: the rattles slow to single clinks and stop, body curled around its finds; affection: a pleased, quick rattle while offering its very best button — the highest honour it owns; evolution moment: years of collecting gather — rattle upon rattle joining, meadow by meadow, until the sound is bells (see Skelloss).
species.anatomyNotes: A small sprite body of smooth pale bone-like segments, simply jointed — arms, legs, and a rounded head, all miniature and unthreatening. Manipulators: two small hands, surprisingly dexterous, built for buttons; it carries finds cupped in both. Mouth/jaw: a small, still mouth; it does not bite — expression lives in the tilt of the head and the speed of the rattle. Locomotion: a toddling walk with a rattle at every step. Signature feature: the collection — it is almost never animated empty-handed; its moves, where it must deliver any, come from among its finds and its rattle, not from menace.
species.paletteSeed: warm bone white, meadow dusk green, faded button brass, soft mourning lilac
species.footprint: Print shape class: tiny two-lobed sprite prints, toe-light, in an earnest straight line. Toe/claw count and arrangement: three small toe-ticks per foot, no claws, prints close together. Gait pattern: a toddling alternating gait that detours, visibly, around every small object on the path — each detour ends with the object gone. Print size class: minute-to-small — needs dusk light and soft meadow earth. Distinctive marker: the trail is tidied — leaf litter along it is lined up, and small lost things are missing from it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a miniature rounded sprite — biggish head, small smooth body, short limbs, all in one pale piece. Proportions in words: head nearly a third of the height; hands nearly as big as the head when cupped together around a find. Key visual masses: the pale head and the cupped hands. What reads at sprite size: a small white shape bobbing through long grass, carrying something. Identifying negative space: the crescent gap between its cupped hands and its chest, where the collected treasure sits.
species.statProfile: Tiny and fragile, with a collector's patience — no threat at all until the meadow itself is threatened, and even then its answer is sorrow, not force. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the pocket bone-sprite carrying a button in both hands; key features are the smooth pale segments, the rattle-step, and the sorted collection. Must-never-change: never make it spooky, sharp, or skull-faced horror — it is a tidy little keeper; never empty its hands for long; the melancholy is gentle, like an unsent letter, never grim.

species.name: Skelloss
species.dexText: Skelloss is a gentle giant assembled from a forgotten meadow's worth of bones, and it rings faintly, like distant bells, when it walks. It wants exactly one thing: for somebody to remember the story of the place it came from. Rangers who learn the story and tell it back are followed, at a respectful distance, for days — in gratitude.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-3 Boneling → Skelloss — a gentle giant assembled from a forgotten meadow's worth of bones, who wants somebody to remember the story of the place it came from. Basis: gashadokuro, re-toned. Tone law from the source: melancholy, never horror.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a giant that stands over a meadow like a slow white tree, tall enough that its bells are heard before it is seen over the rise
species.temperament: Melancholy, patient, and kind; a giant whose whole heart is an act of remembrance. Never horror — its sadness is the sadness of an empty village green, not of a haunting.
species.habitat: The forgotten meadow it came from, and the paths around it in Region 4; it does not stray far from the place whose story it keeps.
