species.dietBehaviour: It does not eat. Its behaviour is keeping: standing in its meadow in all weathers, ringing faintly, gathering what Boneling bring, and listening — always listening — for anyone telling, singing, or half-remembering the story of its place.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Boneling by a meadow's worth of gathering (see Boneling).
species.discovery: Region 4 — a specific forgotten meadow; each Skelloss belongs to one place. Rarity: very rare — event-class in feeling: a Ranger finds *the* meadow, not *a* Skelloss. Method + conditions: learn that a meadow is forgotten (an abandoned settlement's green, a pasture no road reaches), go at dusk, listen for distant bells, and stay to listen rather than approach at once. Level band (in words): late band — a pilgrimage encounter, not a battle to stumble into. First-meeting note: bells, very faint, over the rise at dusk; then the giant standing in the long grass, quite still, facing the Ranger with the patience of something that has waited through everyone's forgetting.
species.cry: Source character: distant bells and a deep, soft bone-resonance — a slow tolling with a hollow warmth, like a village bell heard across water at evening. Pitch contour: low, falling phrases, each note left to ring out fully before the next. Duration class: long — single notes, long phrases, long silences. Rhythm pattern: a walking toll in step, irregular with its mood; when hopeful, the bells brighten into something almost like a tune. Variations — idle: sparse distant tolls while standing in the meadow; call: a fuller peal that Boneling across the meadow answer with their little rattles, a choir of the lost and kept; hurt: a cracked, sorrowful toll and a slow kneeling — it endures rather than retaliates; faint: the bells settle one by one into silence as it folds itself down into the grass like a hill remembering being flat; affection: the tune — when its story is told back to it, the bells find the melody of it, clear and unhurried, the happiest sound in Region 4; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the gathering is recorded under Boneling).
species.anatomyNotes: A giant humanoid frame of smooth, pale, bone-like segments — simply jointed at shoulder, elbow, hip, and knee, entirely without sharpness or gore; it is assembled the way a dry-stone wall is assembled, cleanly. Manipulators: two great gentle hands, fingers long and careful, used for gathering and for placing — never for grasping in anger. Mouth/jaw: a still, small mouth in a smooth, plain face; expression is posture and bells. Locomotion: a very slow, rolling walk, each step placed like a decision, bells sounding from the frame's movement. Signature feature: the bells-in-motion — its whole sound and half its silhouette come from the ringing frame; any move delivery is a slow, deliberate gesture of the great hands, at walking pace, telegraphed by a toll.
species.paletteSeed: warm bone white, meadow green, dusk gold in the bell-light, soft lilac shadow, faded brass
species.footprint: Print shape class: huge, soft, five-lobed foot-presses, shallow for their size — it walks as if apologising to the ground. Toe/claw count and arrangement: five rounded toe-presses per foot, no claw marks, ever. Gait pattern: a very slow alternating amble with long stride spacing, bell-tolls in the earth as much as the air — Rangers feel the step in a mug of tea before they see the print. Print size class: huge — unmistakable, and always in meadow ground, circling the forgotten place. Distinctive marker: Boneling trails converge on every Skelloss print, and small lost things are left placed neatly at the print's edge, like offerings at a gate.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a tall, spare, gently stooped humanoid — a white trellis of a figure over a meadow. Proportions in words: long limbs, a modest torso, a head carried slightly forward in a listening tilt. Key visual masses: the shoulders and the great hands; the body is open framework, not bulk. What reads at sprite size: the stooped white giant against the sky, bells implied by the sway. Identifying negative space: sky shows *through* it — between the ribs of the frame, under the arms, between the legs; it is partly a shape made of gaps, like memory itself.
species.statProfile: Immense staying power and great gentle strength, at a pace nothing can hurry; a wall that would rather kneel than harm. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the stooped bone-white giant in its meadow, sky through its frame, bells in its walk. Key features are the listening tilt, the careful great hands, and the distant-bell sound made visible as sway. Must-never-change: never horror — no gore, no menace, no nightmare staging, ever; never fill in the frame into a solid monster; its want stays singular and legible: to have its place remembered.

species.name: Nuelet
species.dexText: Nuelet is a patchwork pup — monkey face, tanuki body, tiger legs, and a snake for a tail, which has opinions of its own. Its cry is a night-bird's cry, strange and sweet, and it practises it at dusk. Nobody agrees on what it will grow into, least of all its tail.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Pokémon's Silvally is an artificial chimera — this is a natural folklore one, and the mechanics are opposite (born, not built) (source §5). Carried line-wide.
species.lineConcept: C4-4 Nuelet → Chimerune — a patchwork pup: monkey face, tanuki body, tiger legs, a snake for a tail, and a night-bird's cry. Basis: nue (folklore chimera — creature-shape only; a natural folklore chimera, born, not built).
species.sizeClass: Small — a pup-sized bundle of mismatched parts, none of which quite agree on how big the animal is
species.temperament: Curious, changeable, and affectionate in four different ways at once; each part seems to bring its own mood to the day.
species.habitat: Region 4 woodland edges, shrine-like groves, and the brushy ground under storm-coming skies.
species.dietBehaviour: An omnivore by committee — fruit for the monkey, roots for the body, a hunter's patience in the legs. It plays by pouncing and then apologising with its face; the tail hunts sunbeams independently and must be negotiated with at mealtimes.
species.evolution: In words: a Nuelet grown through enough weather — of the sky and of feeling — settles its patchwork into Chimerune (see Chimerune). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — woodland edges and grove clearings at dusk. Rarity: rare — few, shy, and mostly heard. Method + conditions: go at dusk before changeable weather, sit quiet in a grove, and listen for a night-bird crying out of season from ground level. Level band (in words): mid band — an elusive evening encounter. First-meeting note: a night-bird cries from a bush; the bush rustles; and out comes a pup that is four animals agreeing to travel together, its tail arriving a moment later, separately interested in the Ranger's shadow.
species.cry: Source character: a night-bird's cry — a soft, eerie-sweet whistled note, like a thrush calling in the dark — with small monkey chitters underneath when excited and, occasionally, a faint hiss of commentary from the tail. Pitch contour: the bird-note falls in a long, lovely slide; chitters sit high and quick beneath it. Duration class: the bird-note is long for so small a creature; chitters are short bursts. Rhythm pattern: note… note… then chatter, as if the face answers the voice. Variations — idle: sparse practice notes at dusk, tail hissing softly at moths; call: a full three-note bird phrase that carries oddly far and makes other Nuelet answer in chorus; hurt: the note breaks into chitters and a startled hiss; faint: the cry slides down and away like a bird leaving at nightfall, and all four parts go still at slightly different moments; affection: a soft, low version of the bird-note with the tail curled in — its whole patchwork at peace at once, rare and brief; evolution moment: the dusk cry deepens over seasons into Chimerune's weather-telling voice.
species.anatomyNotes: The anatomy *is* the brief — four builds in one body, and the animator must keep them distinct: monkey face with mobile features and small hands in the forepaws' manner; a round tanuki body, low and plush; tiger legs, striped, built for a pounce the body rarely commits to; and a living snake tail with its own head-end behaviour and reaction timing. Manipulators: the face-end forepaws and the tail, which can point, poke, and disagree. Mouth/jaw: two expressive ends — the monkey mouth (chitter, grin) and the snake tail's small mouth (hiss, tongue-flick); neither bites in earnest. Locomotion: a pup's trot with a tiger's crouch available and a tanuki's waddle as the default compromise. Signature feature: disagreement animation — parts reacting a beat apart (tail startles after body, face last) is its character in motion.
species.paletteSeed: monkey cream face, tanuki russet-brown, tiger amber with dark striping, snake-tail moss green, night-blue shadow
species.footprint: Print shape class: a committee in the dust — no two prints in a stride quite match: a hand-like forepaw print on one side, round tanuki pads behind, tiger-paw presses with the stride of something bigger, and a sinuous tail-drag weaving through all of it. Toe/claw count and arrangement: forepaw five finger-ticks; tiger paws four toe-presses with claw ticks only when it pounced; tail leaves no toes at all. Gait pattern: an irregular trot whose spacing keeps changing its mind. Print size class: small overall, with individual tiger prints suspiciously large for the pup. Distinctive marker: the tail-drag — a thin S-line crossing its own trail, sometimes looping back as if the tail went to look at something.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low pup body that breaks its own outline in four places — pricked face, round middle, striped legs, and a raised snake-tail curve. Proportions in words: the body is tanuki-round; the legs are a size too grand; the tail is a second small creature's worth of length. Key visual masses: the round body first, the tail's S second. What reads at sprite size: round pup plus upcurved living tail. Identifying negative space: the open loop between the tail's curve and the back — a window the creature carries everywhere.
species.statProfile: A scrappy all-rounder in miniature — nothing exceptional, everything available, and a tail that occasionally contributes an idea of its own. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the four-animal pup travelling as one; key features are the monkey face's expressiveness, the round body, the grand striped legs, and the independently-minded snake tail. Must-never-change: never blend the parts into a smooth single animal — the seams are the design; never make it artificial, stitched, or built — it was born this way (see Flags); never silence the tail's separate reactions.

species.name: Chimerune
species.dexText: Chimerune appears before storms of feeling — arguments, festivals, reunions — and its cry tells Rangers which kind is coming. A rising cry means joy is gathering somewhere near. A falling one sends wise Rangers to make tea and be kind on purpose.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Pokémon's Silvally is an artificial chimera — this is a natural folklore one, and the mechanics are opposite (born, not built) (source §5).
species.lineConcept: C4-4 Nuelet → Chimerune — it appears before storms of feeling, and its cry tells Rangers which kind is coming. Basis: nue, grown into its weather-sense.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a large, long-bodied presence, about the size of a big dog grown strange, arriving and departing like weather
species.temperament: Perceptive, grave, and compassionate; a creature that feels weather other creatures make, and bears it without blame.
species.habitat: Region 4 groves, hilltops, and the edges of settlements — high, listening places within earshot of people's lives.
species.dietBehaviour: As Nuelet, by committee, but slower and more deliberate. Its true behaviour is attendance: it comes, uninvited and unblamed, to the edge of gatherings where feeling is about to break, cries once or twice, and is gone before the storm it foretold.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Nuelet through weather of sky and feeling (see Nuelet).
species.discovery: Region 4 — grove hilltops and settlement edges, before gatherings. Rarity: very rare — event-class: it is met before festivals, arguments, and reunions, or not at all. Method + conditions: be present where feeling is gathering — a festival being set up, a household on the edge of news — and listen at dusk for the night-bird cry at ground level. Level band (in words): late band — an omen encounter for a Ranger the region has learned to trust. First-meeting note: the evening before the festival, every conversation in the village keeps almost becoming an argument — and from the grove above, a long falling cry, then a rising one, and everyone, somehow, decides to be glad instead.
species.cry: Source character: the night-bird's cry grown deep and carrying — a long whistled note with weather in it, underlaid by a low monkey murmur and, rarely, the tail's soft hiss keeping time. Pitch contour: contour *is* the message — rising contours foretell joy and gathering, falling contours foretell quarrels and partings; Rangers read it like a barometer. Duration class: long, single, unhurried notes. Rhythm pattern: one note, a silence in which everyone listens, then — sometimes — the answering note that settles the forecast. Variations — idle: sparse low notes from a hilltop at dusk, forecasting nothing in particular, or nothing it will share; call: a full rising phrase that Nuelet answer from the groves in patchwork chorus; hurt: the note breaks downward — itself a small bad omen it seems embarrassed by; faint: the cry withdraws like a bird into deepening dark, parts going quiet in sequence, tail last; affection: a warm rising note, given privately, that Rangers treasure — it means something good is coming for *you*; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the deepening is recorded under Nuelet).
species.anatomyNotes: Nuelet's four-part plan at full size and full poise: monkey face grown wise and mobile; tanuki body deepened and steady; tiger legs carrying real, quiet power; snake tail long, expressive, and now perfectly in step — except in omens, when it moves a breath *before* the rest, and that asynchrony is a signal animators must preserve. Manipulators: forepaws and tail, both deliberate. Mouth/jaw: as Nuelet — expression over bite, at both ends. Locomotion: a slow, placed, almost ceremonial walk; it does not hurry and is never seen running. Signature feature: the cry-pose — it stops, lifts the monkey face to the weather it can feel, the tail rises in counterpoint, and the note is delivered like a report.
species.paletteSeed: deep russet, storm amber, moss-green tail, cream face, slate night-blue in the striping and shadow
species.footprint: Print shape class: Nuelet's committee trail grown certain — hand-like forepaw, round body-pads, deep tiger-paw presses, and a bold tail S-line, all in one confident stride. Toe/claw count and arrangement: five forepaw finger-ticks; four tiger toe-presses, claws sheathed in walking, ticked only on hilltop stone where it stood to cry. Gait pattern: slow and even, approaching a settlement's edge and — characteristically — stopping at listening distance; the trail often ends at a vantage, not a den. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: the trail appears before gatherings — Rangers check for Chimerune prints the way they check a sky.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long, low, four-textured silhouette under a raised tail-curve — part beast, part banner. Proportions in words: length over height; the tiger legs give it stance, the tail gives it punctuation. Key visual masses: the deep round body and the tail's high S. What reads at sprite size: patchwork beast plus living tail, with the lifted listening head. Identifying negative space: the tail-loop window, now large enough to frame a moon — and in show staging, it should.
species.statProfile: A balanced, enduring presence with a weather-sense no stat sheet holds — its forecast is its true power; in a straight contest it is solid everywhere and supreme nowhere. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the grave patchwork beast in listening pose, tail raised in counterpoint. Key features are the four kept-distinct body sources, the cry-contour as visible posture, and the tail's omen-asynchrony. Must-never-change: never homogenise the parts, never make it artificial or built — born, not built (see Flags); never stage its omens as doom-horror — its storms are feelings, and its manner toward them is compassion.

species.name: Amabit
species.dexText: Amabit is a shining-scaled sea sprite with three tail-fins and kind eyes, seen where the Region 4 coast goes calm and bright. It comes close out of plain friendliness, which old sailors say is rarer in the sea than any storm. It has nothing to announce yet. It is learning the water.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-5 Amabit → Prophescale — a shining-scaled sea sprite with three tail-fins and kind eyes. Basis: amabie (sea spirit — creature-shape only), kept gentle and helpful.
species.sizeClass: Small — a child-sized sea sprite, about as long as a paddling toddler is tall, all gleam and fins
species.temperament: Kind, curious, and unhurried; a friendly face in calm water.
species.habitat: Calm, bright inshore water along the Region 4 Rift coast — harbour mouths, lagoon edges, and sunlit shallows.
species.dietBehaviour: Small sea plants and whatever plankton-rich water it filters as it swims. It investigates boats gently, keeps pace with swimmers at a polite distance, and practises — if the old sailors are right — being noticeable: surfacing where it can be seen, shining on purpose.
species.evolution: In words: an Amabit grown wise in the coast's weather, that has something true to say, becomes Prophescale (see Prophescale). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — calm inshore water, harbour mouths, and lagoons. Rarity: rare — a calm-water sighting, brief and bright. Method + conditions: be on still, sunlit water in the morning; look for a gleam that moves against the light. Level band (in words): mid band — a coast encounter for a Ranger who has learned to be quiet on water. First-meeting note: something shines under the boat, rises, and looks at the Ranger with unmistakable kind intent — then slides away, leaving the water brighter where it was.
species.cry: Source character: a clear, bell-like chiming from the water — notes struck on a glass rim, with a soft bubbling underneath. Pitch contour: rising, questioning phrases, like a child about to speak. Duration class: short phrases. Rhythm pattern: chime-chime… pause… chime, in the rhythm of a swim alongside. Variations — idle: sparse single chimes while cruising the shallows; call: a brighter run of notes that other Amabit answer gleam for gleam down the coast; hurt: one cracked chime and a dive; faint: the chimes sink in pitch and spacing as it slips into deep water to rest; affection: a soft, rapid chiming while keeping pace with a favourite boat — a sprite's way of walking someone home; evolution moment: the chimes slow and deepen across seasons into Prophescale's single, weighty surfacing note.
species.anatomyNotes: A sleek sea-sprite body: a rounded torso, small arms, and a tail that divides into three distinct fins — the signature, always three, always fanning separately. Manipulators: small hands, more for touching and greeting than grasping. Mouth/jaw: a small, kind mouth; expression is in the large, kind eyes, which the animator must keep front and centre. Locomotion: gentle undulating swimming, unhurried, with a shining surface-roll as its characteristic move. Signature feature: the shining scales — light behaviour is part of the anatomy; it gleams on purpose, brightest at the moment of surfacing.
species.paletteSeed: shining sea-green, pearl white, soft gold scale-light, kind deep-teal eyes
species.footprint: A sea sprite leaves no footprints; its trace is a NON-print sign — a three-finned wake: three fine parallel ripple-lines braided into one shining trail on calm water, plus, occasionally, a single shining scale left on a harbour step or a boat's waterline like a visiting card. Distinctive marker: the wake braids in threes, and the water stays a moment brighter along it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a small, sleek sprite-shape — round head and torso flowing into a triple-finned tail. Proportions in words: the tail is half the length, the eyes are the face's whole story, the fins are a fan wider than the body. Key visual masses: the shining torso and the three-fin fan. What reads at sprite size: gleam-plus-triple-fin, even as a shape under water. Identifying negative space: the two notches between the three tail-fins — count the fins by the gaps.
species.statProfile: Quick in its own water, frail out of it, with a coast-wise awareness that reads as luck; its strength is brightness and goodwill. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the shining small sprite with the three-fin fan; key features are the gleaming scales, the kind oversized eyes, and surfacing-on-purpose. Must-never-change: never reduce the tail-fins from three, never make it eerie or oracular in this stage — it announces nothing yet; it is a kind child of the coast learning the water.

species.name: Prophescale
species.dexText: Prophescale surfaces once, delivers one true and useful sentence, and leaves before anyone can ask a second question. Rangers keep a book of its sentences. Most pages are weather; the other pages are the reason the book is kept locked, and read aloud only when needed.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-5 Amabit → Prophescale — it surfaces once, delivers one true and useful sentence, and leaves before anyone can ask a second question. Basis: amabie, grown into its one announcement.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a graceful sea presence about as long as a small boat, seen mostly as gleam, eyes, and fins at the surface
species.temperament: Serene, certain, and brief; kind in the way of a lighthouse — it exists to be useful at exactly the right moment, and not to be company.
species.habitat: The Region 4 Rift coast, offshore of harbours and fishing villages — it belongs to the whole coast, and to no harbour.
species.dietBehaviour: As Amabit, at scale and at distance. Its behaviour is the surfacing: it rises where it will be seen and heard, delivers its sentence as the source frames it — one true and useful sentence, a delivered truth, not a conversation — and is gone down the shining water before a second question can form. It never explains, repeats, or stays.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Amabit when the sprite grew wise enough to have something true to say (see Amabit).
species.discovery: Region 4 — offshore harbour water and fishing-village coasts. Rarity: event-class, strictly — it surfaces once, on its own occasion; Rangers do not find Prophescale, they attend it. Method + conditions: be on the water or the harbour wall when the coast goes calm and bright without warning; have the Ranger's book ready — sentences are recorded, never requested. Level band (in words): any band — truth does not check a Ranger's strength, though late-band Rangers are likelier to be believed afterwards. First-meeting note: the harbour goes bright and still; it rises, shining, at exactly the distance of clear hearing; the sentence is short and entirely practical; and the water closes over the gleam while everyone is still deciding what to ask.
species.cry: Source character: Amabit's glass chimes deepened into a single resonant surfacing note — and then the sentence, which is not a cry and not ordinary speech: as the source frames it, one true and useful sentence, delivered once, in a voice like calm water over a bell. Pitch contour: the note rises as it surfaces and settles to level for the sentence, which is spoken plainly, without ornament. Duration class: the note is long; the sentence is exactly as long as a sentence. Rhythm pattern: note… sentence… silence… gone; there is no second phrase, ever. Variations — idle: it is not heard idling; a distant single chime on bright calm days is the most the coast gets; call: the surfacing note itself is the call, and harbours answer by going quiet; hurt: it does not stay to be hurt — a bright dive and the sentence, if there was one, is lost with it, which harbours count as warning enough; faint: it withdraws below any contest — a sinking fall of pitch and the water closing; a Prophescale that fades does so offstage, in deep water; affection: the nearest thing on record is a sentence delivered *gently* — the book notes the tone twice, both times beside weather that would have killed someone; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the deepening is recorded under Amabit).
species.anatomyNotes: Amabit's plan, graced: sleek shining body, small arms now mostly folded in composure, and the three tail-fins at full splendid fan — still exactly three. Manipulators: small hands, rarely used; it gestures, when at all, with a tilt of the shining head. Mouth/jaw: the mouth matters — it must be animated simply and clearly for the one sentence, then close; no second mouth movement, no murmur, no elaboration (cries-only discipline holds for every other sound it makes: chimes, never chatter). Locomotion: a slow, level rise and a bright, unhurried dive; it never thrashes. Signature feature: the surfacing itself — gleam, eyes, level gaze, delivery, departure, staged as one continuous ceremonial beat.
species.paletteSeed: deep shining sea-green, bright pearl, old gold scale-light, calm harbour teal, white water at the surfacing line
species.footprint: No footprints; its trace is a NON-print sign of record — a broad three-braided shining wake that appears, runs straight for the harbour, and ends where it rose; and afterwards, an entry: the sentence, written in the Rangers' book in the witness's hand. Distinctive marker: the wake exists only once per surfacing, and locals can date old stories by it — "the year of the bright water."
species.silhouette: Outline class: a sleek rising arc — head, eyes, and shoulders above the waterline, the triple-fin fan flaring once at the surface before the dive. Proportions in words: longer and calmer than Amabit; the fins are a sail of three at the rear, the face is small and level and kind. Key visual masses: the gleaming back at the surface and the fin-fan. What reads at sprite size: gleam, eyes, three fins — in that order. Identifying negative space: the two clean notches between the three fins, visible against the light at the moment of the dive.
species.statProfile: Elusive beyond contest — its profile is that it cannot be kept, cornered, or questioned; what strength it has is the strength of being exactly once, and entirely believed. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the shining surfacing, eyes level, fins fanned, against a suddenly calm harbour. Key features are the triple fins, the gleam, and the absolute brevity of the visit. Must-never-change: never give it a second sentence, an explanation, or a Q-and-A staging — one true and useful sentence, then gone; never convert its delivery into ordinary creature speech or chatter in any other scene; never darken it into a doom-prophet — most pages are weather, and even the other pages are *useful*.

species.name: Smoothsea
species.dexText: Smoothsea is first noticed as a smoothness: a black dome in a flat-calm sea, where the water has gone mirror-still around it. It rises when the sea is calm, and it makes the sea calmer. Sailors slow down near it the way people lower their voices in a library.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-6 Smoothsea → Monkalm — a smooth black dome in a flat-calm sea. Basis: umibozu (sea-monk spirit — creature-shape only), re-toned into a riddle and a ferry.
species.sizeClass: Large — a dome like a small island's shoulder rising from still water, wide enough that boats give it room without knowing why
species.temperament: Serene, watchful, and unfinished — a presence that seems to be waiting to become something, politely.
species.habitat: Open Region 4 Rift sea, on mirror-calm days; ferry routes and the quiet water between islands.
species.dietBehaviour: It does not eat. It rises, it is still, it sinks again — and the water around it holds its flat calm a long while after, which small boats use as a resting place. Panic near it — splashing, shouting — is the one thing that disturbs its stillness.
species.evolution: In words: the dome gains the face — Smoothsea becomes Monkalm when the dome is *plus the face*, which is worse and better (see Monkalm). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — open sea on mirror-calm days. Rarity: rare — a condition encounter: no calm, no dome. Method + conditions: sail a ferry route on a flat-calm morning and watch for water that is *too* still, a black dome where the chart says open sea. Level band (in words): mid-to-late band — open-water work for a steady Ranger. First-meeting note: the sea goes mirror-still mile by mile, the boat slows in water like glass, and the dome is simply there, black and smooth and patient, taking up the view like a held breath.
species.cry: Source character: a low water-resonance — a deep, round hum felt in a boat's hull, with slow dripping at its waterline; almost a silence with a pitch. Pitch contour: very low, very level, falling almost imperceptibly as it sinks. Duration class: long, continuous phrases while surfaced. Rhythm pattern: the hum breathes — slow swells, matched to the tiny rise and fall of the dome. Variations — idle: the faintest hull-hum on calm water, often logged as "engine trouble, except there was no engine"; call: a deeper swell that stills nearby water visibly, and other Smoothsea answer as faint hums at the edge of hearing; hurt: the hum stumbles, ripples break outward, and it sinks at once — it answers disturbance by leaving; faint: no struggle, no sound almost — the hum thins to nothing as the dome settles under, leaving troubled water; affection: the hum warms a fraction and the calm widens — small boats resting in its lee report the water feeling *looked after*; evolution moment: the hum gathers and deepens until the surface of the dome breaks differently — a face is coming (see Monkalm).
species.anatomyNotes: A dome and nothing else — that is the stage's whole discipline: no limbs, no face, no visible mouth. Manipulators: none; it acts on the water around it (calming, and by stillness, refusing). Mouth/jaw: none visible — any sound comes from the whole dome as resonance. Locomotion: a near-imperceptible rising, sinking, and drift; it does not swim in view. Signature feature: the mirror ring — the flat-calm disc of water it carries around itself; animate the water as part of the creature.
species.paletteSeed: wet black, mirror silver, deep sea green at the waterline, flat-calm pearl grey
species.footprint: No footprints; its trace is a NON-print sign — a perfect circular ring of mirror-calm water persisting after it sinks, glassy inside the ring and ordinary sea outside it, sometimes with a single black gleam still turning slowly at the centre. Distinctive marker: the ring's edge is *too* round — sailors draw it in logs as a compass circle.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a clean hemisphere on a flat line — half a black moon sitting on the sea. Proportions in words: all dome; height is half of width, the waterline does the composing. Key visual masses: the dome alone, doubled by its mirror reflection into a full dark circle. What reads at sprite size: the black half-disc and the still ring — readable across a whole seascape panel. Identifying negative space: none on the creature; the negative space is the emptied, flattened sea around it.
species.statProfile: Immense calm as a statistic — hard to harm chiefly because it declines to be present for harm; slow, vast, and entirely without aggression. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the black dome and its mirror ring on glass water. Key features are the perfect smoothness, the doubled reflection, and stillness as presence. Must-never-change: never add a face, limbs, or menace in this stage — the face is the evolution; never stage it as a sea-monster attack — disturbance near it is the visitor's doing, and its answer is to sink away.

species.name: Monkalm
species.dexText: Monkalm is the dome plus the face — a bald sea-monk the size of weather, which is worse and better. Panic brings waves; a calm answer to its one low riddle earns a ferry ride on its back. The riddle is never hard. That is the test: it is asking whether you can be calm, not whether you are clever.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C4-6 Smoothsea → Monkalm — the dome plus the face: a bald sea-monk the size of weather, posing one low riddle, ferrying the calm. Basis: umibozu, re-toned.
species.sizeClass: Huge — the size of weather: a head and shoulders over the sea like a small black hill with a face, a back broad enough to ferry on
species.temperament: Serene, grave, and quietly kind; a examiner of calm whose ferry is a reward for the steady-hearted.
species.habitat: Open Region 4 Rift sea on mirror-calm days — the same water as Smoothsea, fulfilled.
species.dietBehaviour: It does not eat. Its behaviour is the encounter: it rises on mirror-calm water, regards the vessel, poses its one low riddle in a voice like a hull-hum given words *only for the riddle* in the encounter's framing as the source gives it — one riddle, calmly answered or calmly failed — and ferries the calm across whatever water they need to cross. Those who panic get waves and a sinking-away giant, and a long swim of a lesson.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Smoothsea when the dome gained the face (see Smoothsea).
species.discovery: Region 4 — open sea, mirror-calm, on ferry routes between the Rift islands. Rarity: event-class — it rises when the water goes mirror-still, for a vessel ready to be calm. Method + conditions: be on calm water, keep the boat calm, and wait; shouting, rowing at it, or panic all end the meeting before it begins. Level band (in words): late band — the open sea's own examination, taken when it is offered. First-meeting note: the dome rises, and rises, and the face comes with it — worse, because it is looking at you; better, because it is looking *kindly* — and the whole sea waits while it asks its one low riddle.
species.cry: Source character: Smoothsea's hull-hum become a presence — a very low, round resonance with slow water-sounds at the shoulders, and the riddle delivered as the source frames it: one low riddle, a single calm question, not a conversation. Pitch contour: the hum is level and deep; the riddle is spoken at the bottom of the voice, evenly, with a long pause after it that is part of the asking. Duration class: hum phrases are long; the riddle is one unhurried sentence of a question. Rhythm pattern: hum… silence… riddle… a silence as long as it takes. Variations — idle: a distant hull-hum under mirror-calm water, felt rather than heard; call: the hum swells as the face rises — other Smoothsea hums still themselves, as if listening; hurt: it does not cry out; the hum breaks, waves come up with its displeasure at panic, and it sinks — the sea's noise is the whole report; faint: withdrawal, not defeat — a sinking fall of resonance and a long troubled settling of water; affection: after a calm answer, the hum warms and steadies under the ferry ride the whole way across — passengers describe it as being hummed *to*, very low, by the sea; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the face's coming is recorded under Smoothsea).
species.anatomyNotes: The dome fulfilled: a vast smooth head — bald as a monk's, in the source's image — with a calm, plain face, broad shoulders at the waterline, and a back that serves as the ferry deck. Manipulators: none in view; the ferrying is the back and the steadiness. Mouth/jaw: a small, still mouth in the huge face, animated sparingly — open for the riddle, closed for everything else; all other sound is whole-body resonance, cries in hum form, never chatter. Locomotion: rising, sinking, and a slow ferry-glide that barely ripples. Signature feature: scale-with-stillness — it moves like weather changing its mind, and any delivery it makes is a swell, a settling, or the gift of flat water.
species.paletteSeed: wet black, mirror silver, deep sea green, dawn pearl on the face, flat grey calm
species.footprint: No footprints; its trace is a NON-print sign — a ferry wake of impossible geometry: a straight, glassy calm lane across otherwise ordinary sea, the width of its back, persisting after it has gone, with the circular mirror-ring at the place where it rose. Distinctive marker: the lane ends mid-sea, at the far shore of need — locals navigate by old Monkalm lanes on still mornings.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a black hill with a face — dome, shoulders, and waterline, doubled in reflection into a dark medallion on the sea. Proportions in words: the face is small in the dome the way a face is small in a mountain, and it is the whole read anyway. Key visual masses: the head-dome and the shoulder line at the water. What reads at sprite size: black dome, calm face, mirror doubling — instantly a presence, never a monster shape. Identifying negative space: the clean arc of sky between its shoulders and any land — it takes the horizon's place.
species.statProfile: A weather-scale wall of calm — beyond ordinary contest; encounters with it are examinations, not battles, and its "strength" is the sea itself agreeing with it. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the dome plus the face on mirror water, back offered as a ferry. Key features are the bald monk-like head, the small kind face at vast scale, and the riddle-silence staging. Must-never-change: never stage it as a capsizing sea-horror — panic brings waves, the creature brings a question; never give it a hard riddle, a cruel price, or a second demand; the ferry is earned by calm, and given kindly.

species.name: Barrelimp
species.dexText: Barrelimp is a thumb-high imp that lives in sake barrels, where it keeps warm, keeps out of the way, and keeps — brewers insist — the brew honest. A barrel with an imp in it never goes off. A barrel without one is just a barrel, and everyone can tell the difference at a festival.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Double flag, carried line-wide (see §5; full text on Festivoni): Pokémon's Ogerpon occupies the oni chair, and R3 already holds the owner-directed Volcano Oni anchor — if the owner wants only one oni in the world, this concept is the first cut.
species.lineConcept: C4-7 Barrelimp → Festivoni — a thumb-high imp that lives in sake barrels. Basis: oni, in miniature and in good humour (creature-shape only).
species.sizeClass: Tiny — thumb-high in the source's own words: it lives inside a sake barrel and treats the bung-hole as a front door
species.temperament: Mischievous, warm-natured, and fiercely loyal to its barrel and its brewer; a tiny guardian with a great festival's heart in miniature.
species.habitat: Region 4 brewery sheds, festival store-tents, and cellar-cool barrel rows — wherever sake is kept for celebrations.
species.dietBehaviour: Thimblefuls of sake, festival crumbs, and the warmth of the barrel itself. It drums on the inside of the staves when the brew is ready — brewers knock back, politely — and at festivals it rides its barrel like a chariot, rolling in small triumphant circles.
species.evolution: In words: a Barrelimp that has kept many barrels through many festivals, grown great on warmth and thunder, becomes Festivoni (see Festivoni). No level is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 — brewery sheds and festival barrel rows. Rarity: uncommon — every good brewery has one, and none of them advertise it. Method + conditions: visit a brewery before a festival, knock twice on a likely barrel, and wait to be knocked back at. Level band (in words): early-to-mid band — a small warm encounter in the region's social heart. First-meeting note: the Ranger knocks, something knocks back from inside the barrel — once, in unmistakable rhythm — and a thumb-high imp leans out of the bung-hole to inspect them like a landlord inspecting a tenant.
species.cry: Source character: a tiny, throaty chuckle-drumming — little *tok-tok* knocks on barrel wood with a squeaky, sake-warmed giggle threaded through. Pitch contour: high and round, giggles rising, knocks flat and woody. Duration class: very short phrases. Rhythm pattern: tok-tok… giggle — the knock always first, like a signature. Variations — idle: sparse contented toks while the brew settles; call: a rolling drum-phrase on the staves that other Barrelimp answer barrel to barrel down the row; hurt: a startled squeak and a slammed-shut silence from inside the barrel; faint: toks slow and soften as it retreats to the bottom of the barrel to sleep it off among the warmth; affection: a pleased drum-roll and the bung-hole leaned out of, beaming — its highest sociability; evolution moment: across many festivals the toks deepen into a drum the size of weather (see Festivoni).
species.anatomyNotes: A thumb-high imp: round belly, short limbs, a small horned head with a brewer's expression, and hands made for drumming staves. Manipulators: two quick hands and a grip that can hold a barrel hoop while riding. Mouth/jaw: a small, wide, expressive mouth — giggles, never speeches; expression is grin and eyebrow. Locomotion: scurrying climbs, barrel-rolls ridden from inside, and triumphant circuits on foot at festival scale. Signature feature: the barrel as body-extension — it is animated *with* its barrel (drumming it, leaning from it, rolling in it); alone and barrel-less it is only half the read.
species.paletteSeed: warm sake-amber, barrel oak brown, small ember red, cream belly, brass hoop glint
species.footprint: Print shape class: tiny four-toed imp prints, round-heeled, in busy scurrying arcs around a barrel's base. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four small toe-ticks per foot, no claw gouges — it runs on tiptoe when pleased, which is often. Gait pattern: short quick alternating steps interrupted by long barrel-roll arcs (a smooth curved groove, not prints) where it rode the barrel around. Print size class: minute — found in brewery dust and festival sawdust. Distinctive marker: the prints circle barrels and stop at the staves, going straight up — it climbs home.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a tiny round imp, usually composed with its barrel — a small figure on, in, or beside a great round stave-body. Proportions in words: belly first, head second, limbs as punctuation; the barrel dwarfs it and completes it. Key visual masses: the barrel, then the imp's round head at the bung-hole. What reads at sprite size: barrel-plus-imp — the pair is the sprite. Identifying negative space: the dark round bung-hole with the imp leaning out of it — a hole with a face.
species.statProfile: Tiny, quick, and warm — negligible force, remarkable nerve; its real statistic is morale, its own and everyone else's. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the thumb-high imp with its sake barrel; key features are the drumming hands, the bung-hole doorway, and the festival grin. Must-never-change: never separate the design from the barrel, never make the imp sly or sinister — it is a warm little guardian of good brews; never enlarge this stage — thumb-high is the charm and the law of the stage.

species.name: Festivoni
species.dexText: Festivoni is a big red oni who brews thunder-sake — it pops and rumbles faintly in the cup — and judges the region's festivals on volume. Between festivals it arm-wrestles storms for practice, and lets them win just often enough to keep them coming back. A festival Festivoni calls loud enough is loud enough.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Double flag (see §5): Pokémon's Ogerpon occupies the oni chair (a masked ogre child with type-changing masks — this is a grown festival brewer, a different design entirely); and R3 already holds the owner-directed Volcano Oni anchor — Festivoni is a *different* oni for a different region, a drinker where the anchor is a volcano. If the owner wants only one oni in the world, this is the concept to cut first — it's flagged, not hidden.
species.lineConcept: C4-7 Barrelimp → Festivoni — a big red oni who brews thunder-sake, arm-wrestles storms for practice, and judges the region's festivals on volume. Basis: oni (creature-shape only), grown festival-grand and kept good-humoured.
species.sizeClass: Large — a big oni in the source's words: taller than the festival gate it judges under, broad enough to carry a sake barrel under each arm
species.temperament: Boisterous, generous, and exacting about exactly one thing — volume; a judge whose heart is a drum.
species.habitat: Region 4 festival grounds, brewery yards, and storm-facing hilltops in the off-season — wherever noise is made properly.
species.dietBehaviour: Festival food in festival quantities, and its own thunder-sake, which it shares with weather and winners. Its behaviour is the circuit: brew, judge, celebrate the winners by drumming until the lanterns swing, then carry the barrels home and start the next brew.
species.evolution: Final stage — does not evolve further. It arrived here from Barrelimp through many festivals of warmth and thunder (see Barrelimp).
species.discovery: Region 4 — festival grounds and brewery yards, in festival season. Rarity: event-class — it is met by attending the festival properly; off-season it keeps to its hilltop and its storms. Method + conditions: be at a Region 4 festival at full volume; the meeting usually takes the form of being judged — a hush as it listens, then the verdict drum. Level band (in words): late band — a pillar-of-the-region encounter. First-meeting note: the festival noise peaks, falters — because the big red shape under the gate has raised one hand — and then its laugh rolls out over the grounds like friendly thunder, and every drum in the place answers at once.
species.cry: Source character: a great rolling laugh with a drum in it — Barrelimp's tok-toks become festival taiko booms from its own chest and palms, sake-warmed and enormous. Pitch contour: low and rising when pleased; verdicts fall like a struck drum. Duration class: long phrases; laughs roll for as long as they need. Rhythm pattern: boom… boom-boom… LAUGH — drumming first, voice as the resolution. Variations — idle: contented low drumming while brewing, thunder answering distantly like an old sparring partner; call: a full chest-drum phrase that every Barrelimp in every barrel answers in miniature, a storm of tiny toks inside the big rhythm; hurt: a startled boom and a laugh at itself — it is almost impossible to offend; faint: the drumming slows, the laugh softens to a rumble, and it sits down among the barrels like a hill deciding to be a hill for a while; affection: a deliberately gentle single drum-note and a cup of thunder-sake held out at Ranger scale — the highest honour of the festival circuit; evolution moment: not applicable — final stage (the deepening is recorded under Barrelimp).
species.anatomyNotes: A big oni build: broad shoulders, great arms made for drumming and arm-wrestling weather, sturdy legs in a festival stance, a horned head with a wide expressive face, red-skinned in the source's image. Manipulators: two huge hands — drums, cups, barrels, and verdicts all live in them; finger articulation matters (the raised-hand hush is a signature beat). Mouth/jaw: a big, laugh-built mouth — expressions are grin, laugh, and the judge's listening stillness; it makes cries, laughs, and drum-sounds, never speeches. Locomotion: a rolling, grounded stride that the ground comments on; it plants like a gate-post when judging. Signature feature: the drum-body — chest, palms, and barrels as one percussion system; every significant delivery (Flame included, as thunder-sake steam and pop) is timed to a drum beat the animator must hit.
species.paletteSeed: festival red, sake-amber, storm indigo, lantern gold, barrel oak brown
species.footprint: Print shape class: broad four-toed oni prints, deep and round-heeled, in grounded festival strides. Toe/claw count and arrangement: four strong toe-presses per foot, no claw tears — its weight, not its claws, marks the ground. Gait pattern: a rolling alternating stride, spacing wide and even, characteristically circling festival grounds and ending at the gate. Print size class: large — a child could stand in one, and at festivals, does. Distinctive marker: barrel-ring presses beside the prints wherever it set a barrel down to judge — the prints conduct an invisible orchestra of circles.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a broad gate-post of an oni — wide shoulders, horned head, arms like drum-beaters, stance like a festival gate. Proportions in words: breadth over height; hands and head are the largest features after the shoulders. Key visual masses: the shoulder-and-chest block, then the horns against the sky. What reads at sprite size: red breadth plus horns plus a barrel under one arm. Identifying negative space: the arch between its planted legs — at festival scale, small creatures and children shelter in it from rain, and staging should let them.
species.statProfile: A festival pillar — great strength, great endurance, a storm's sparring partner; not fast, never sneaky, and dangerous only to silence. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: Silhouette is the big red oni under the festival gate, barrel under one arm, hand raised for the hush. Key features are the drum-body percussion, the thunder-sake, and boisterous kind authority. Must-never-change: never make it a villain, a brute, or a horror oni — it judges festivals and lets storms win sometimes; never remove the brewing (a drinker and brewer, not a brawler who happens to be big); never shrink the warmth — the laugh is the design.

species.name: Tsuchlet
species.dexText: Tsuchlet is a snake that is mostly belly, with a head at one end and a thin, apologetic tail at the other. It is already practising the family arts: looking innocent, looking elsewhere, and being somewhere else by the time anyone looks back.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ HARD FLAG (carried from §5, applies to the whole C5-1 line): Pokémon's Dunsparce / Dudunsparce IS the tsuchinoko — but theirs is a silent drill-tailed burrower; every folklore trait that makes the tsuchinoko itself (speech, lying, sake, the double jump) is the part they did not use, and it is exactly this concept's design seed. Included because the owner named the tsuchinoko class himself; the flag rides with it.
species.lineConcept: C5-1 — the young of the fat snake of legend; cryptid basis: the tsuchinoko, Japan's barrel-bodied snake that folklore insists nobody can quite catch.
species.sizeClass: Small — a plump coil about the size of a well-fed household cushion, most of it middle.
species.temperament: Cheeky, unbothered, and quietly pleased with itself; a born escape artist who treats being chased as a compliment.
species.habitat: Warm grass banks, rice-field edges, and sunlit stone walls around Region 4 villages; anywhere with good hiding grass and better gossip.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats small field fare and fallen fruit, and is drawn — long before it should be — to the smell of sake breweries and festival stalls. When followed, it leads pursuers in confident circles and leaves them with excellent directions to somewhere it is not.
species.evolution: Evolves into Sakebelly after a long, well-fed life of narrow escapes, tall tales, and being believed in by exactly enough people.
species.discovery: Region 4 grass banks and brewery lanes near the Rift's settled edges. Rarity class: rare — glimpsed far more often than met. Method + conditions: warm afternoons after festivals, when spilled festival drink sweetens the grass; follow the giggling-shaped gap in the grass, not a trail. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will watch the Ranger first, from inside a coil that looks, at a glance, like a dropped cushion.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a squeaky, rubbery hiss with a round pop at the end, like a cork thinking about leaving a bottle. Pitch contour: starts low in the belly, wobbles up, pops. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: single pops when content, a quick patter when startled. Variations — idle: soft pop-hiss at long intervals; call: a braver, squeakier pop repeated toward another Tsuchlet; hurt: a flat deflated squeak; faint: a slow sigh-hiss as it coils tight; affection: a warm, muffled purring pop against a trusted hand; evolution moment: the pops deepen and round out, one after the other, like a story finding its voice.
species.anatomyNotes: No limbs and no manipulators; all expression is belly, head tilt, and tail. Mouth is a small, sly slit that opens wide only for food and yawns. Locomotion is a side-to-side undulation made comic by the wide middle — the belly lags half a beat behind the head. Signature feature for animators: the mid-body bulge, which must squash and rebound with every turn; even this young, a startled Tsuchlet can manage one small, surprising hop.
species.paletteSeed: dusty olive, warm sake-amber, cream belly, leaf green
species.footprint: No feet, ever. A tracker finds a wide, smooth belly-drag: a broad central groove pressed into dust or mud, with soft side undulations rippling off it where the body pushed, and the groove briefly vanishing altogether where a startled hop lifted the whole belly clear of the ground. Print size class: small but absurdly wide for a snake. Distinctive marker: the groove is fattest in the middle of each undulation, as if whatever made it was carrying its lunch in its waistband.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low, horizontal barrel. Proportions in words: a very wide middle tapering quickly to a small head and a thin tail. Key visual masses: the great round belly is nearly the whole creature; head and tail read as punctuation. What reads at sprite size: the fat coil and the smug little head raised at one end. Identifying negative space: almost none — the coil closes its own loop, and the small triangular gap inside a tight coil is the tell.
species.statProfile: Slippery rather than strong — hard to hit, hard to hold, modest in a straight contest and already better at leaving than fighting. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A fat, low snake coiled like a dropped cushion, small sly head, thin tail, cream belly showing at the coil's edge. Must-never-change: the belly is the silhouette; no limbs, no horns, no drill or burrower tail — this is not a digging snake; the expression stays charming, never sinister.

species.name: Sakebelly
species.dexText: Sakebelly has never been caught, and has excellent directions to prove it. Travellers who pursue it somehow arrive exactly where they needed to be, holding a story nobody believes and a fondness they cannot explain.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ HARD FLAG (see §5): Pokémon's Dunsparce / Dudunsparce IS Pokémon's tsuchinoko, and this concept's seed is exactly the folklore traits Pokémon did not use — speech (kept ambiguous, above), lying, sake, and the double jump. The flag rides with the concept by the owner's own direction.
species.lineConcept: C5-1 — the fat snake of legend in full possession of its folklore: it lies charmingly, it loves sake, and it can jump twice in the air, which is one more jump than is fair; cryptid basis: the tsuchinoko.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a travelling barrel of a snake, broad enough across the middle that two Rangers would argue about whether it could possibly be a snake at all.
species.temperament: Charming, evasive, and generous in the way of all great liars — it would rather bribe a pursuer with perfect directions than ever be rude about escaping.
species.habitat: Festival roads, brewery storehouses, and the warm grass country of Region 4 where travellers pass and tales travel faster.
species.dietBehaviour: A devoted sake connoisseur that accepts a saucer as tribute and repays it in guidance; otherwise eats heartily from fields and festival leavings. Its defence is never a bite: it talks its way — in cries — around every pursuer, then leaves by air, twice.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 festival roads and sake-brewing hamlets on the Rift's gentler fringe. Rarity class: event — nobody has ever caught one, and an encounter is a story, not a farming spot. Method + conditions: festival evenings, a saucer left out in the open, and the patience to be lied to politely; sightings spike wherever a good tale is being told outdoors. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: the first meeting is always also the farewell — it will be mid-anecdote, mid-bow, and then, impossibly, mid-air.
species.cry: Cries only — with the owner's own seed kept exactly as ambiguous as written: it talks (in cries nobody can prove weren't words). Source character: a round, rolling, sake-warm burble with the cadence of conversation and the content of pure snake. Pitch contour: rises and falls in long, anecdote-shaped swells, with a conspiratorial dip before the best part. Duration class: long — it holds forth. Rhythm pattern: patter, pause, punchline pop; repeat until the audience has forgotten why they came. Variations — idle: a contented burbling monologue to no one; call: a carrying, storytelling roll that other Sakebelly answer from far grass; hurt: an offended, spluttering pop; faint: a trailing burble that ends, suspiciously, like a punchline; affection: a soft, confidential murmur at very close range; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — its arrival in a scene is announced by the burble starting up somewhere it was not a moment ago.
species.anatomyNotes: No limbs; the whole performance is belly, head, and nerve. Mouth is mobile and expressive far beyond a normal snake's — it must be able to look like it is mid-sentence without ever speaking. Locomotion is undulation on the ground and, signature of the species, a double jump in the air: a first leap, a visible second kick off nothing, and a landing that pretends nothing happened. Animators must stage the second jump as a deliberate cheat — a little mid-air coil-and-spring — never as ordinary leaping.
species.paletteSeed: deep olive, polished sake-amber, cream belly, festival red
species.footprint: A tracker finds the famous trail and then loses it, which is the point. A broad belly-drag with strong side undulations, fatter and more confident than Tsuchlet's, that simply stops — then resumes a good leap away, then stops and resumes again, the gaps marking the double jump's launch and landing. At each landing: a deep, round belly-print, like a barrel set down firmly. Distinctive marker: the trail of a creature that leaves by air and wants credit for it.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a grand horizontal barrel with pretensions. Proportions in words: an enormous middle, a head carried high and knowingly, a tail too thin for the rest of it. Key visual masses: belly first, head second, tail as an afterthought. What reads at sprite size: the barrel body and the raised, storyteller's head. Identifying negative space: the clear air under the body in the double jump — a Sakebelly silhouette is the only snake silhouette routinely found off the ground.
species.statProfile: Elusive above all — defence by absence, offence by misdirection, with a sturdier body than its comedy suggests. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A magnificent barrel-bodied snake, head up like a raconteur at a festival table, cream belly, thin tail curled like a footnote. Must-never-change: the folklore kit is the design — charming liar's expression, sake association, and the double jump; no drill tail, no burrower read, no menace; it is a beloved fraud, not a monster.

species.name: Mothlet
species.dexText: Mothlet gathers wherever light gathers before a storm, turning its great lamp eyes to the sky. It cannot yet fly far, so it warns from fence posts and window ledges, blinking at weather nobody else has noticed.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Flag (see §5): moths are a Pokémon-crowded family — carried here for the owner's eye; the crowding is answered in the Omenmoth sheet, whose seed no moth in that crowd holds.
species.lineConcept: C5-2 — a grey moth-cub with lamp eyes; cryptid basis: Mothman, the winged omen of bridges and bad weather, re-read here from the beginning as a warner, not a threat.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a plump handful of fluff that fits in the crook of a street lamp.
species.temperament: Earnest, anxious, and devoted; a small creature with a large sense of responsibility and no way yet to carry it.
species.habitat: Bridge ends, lamp posts, and eaves around Region 4's river towns; always somewhere high enough to watch the sky.
species.dietBehaviour: Sips nectar and rainwater and basks in lamplight, which it seems to store in its eyes. On still, heavy evenings it gathers with others of its line and stares in one direction — old Rangers check the sky when the Mothlet do.
species.evolution: Evolves into Omenmoth after many storm seasons spent watching, warning, and being — slowly, finally — believed.
species.discovery: Region 4 river towns and their bridges. Rarity class: uncommon. Method + conditions: dusk on still, heavy evenings before bad weather; look for paired lights on posts that blink together. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will not flee — it will turn both lamp eyes on the Ranger, then pointedly back at the sky, as if filing a report.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a soft, fuzzy chirr, muffled by its own fluff, with a faint glassy ring underneath like a lamp humming. Pitch contour: a low, worried level line that lifts sharply when the sky changes. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: single chirrs while calm; a rapid, repeated chirr-chirr-chirr when a storm is coming. Variations — idle: barely-there fluff-muffled chirrs; call: the rapid storm pattern, aimed at the sky; hurt: a thin, startled squeak-chirr; faint: the hum in the cry dies out first, then the sound; affection: a gentle, warm hum-chirr against a trusted shoulder; evolution moment: the chirr stretches thin and silent, and the hum carries on alone for a breath.
species.anatomyNotes: Small round body with stubby legs, short arms held close, and wings still too small for real flight — it glides down from posts and flaps hard to regain them. Mouth is a tiny, serious line, rarely open. Head is mostly eyes: the lamp eyes are the face. Signature feature: antennae that curl toward approaching weather. Animators: its movement is perch, lean, stare, flutter — never darting insect panic.
species.paletteSeed: lamp grey, soft moth-dust cream, ember amber (eyes), dusk blue
species.footprint: A tracker finds almost nothing, and the almost is the identification: faint, brushed dust prints from stubby feet in a wandering perch-to-perch line, each print smudged soft by wing-powder, with a pale dusting of moth scales scattered between them. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the smudge — no other print in the region is deliberately this blurred, as if the creature walked through its own fog.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a round puff with antennae. Proportions in words: a head that is mostly eyes on a body that is mostly fluff, wings folded like a small cape. Key visual masses: the eye-pair dominates; the body is a soft ball beneath. What reads at sprite size: two lamp eyes in a grey puff. Identifying negative space: the curl of clear air inside each antenna's spiral.
species.statProfile: Fragile and quick-eyed — a scout's profile, all warning and no weight behind it. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A grey fluff-ball moth-cub with enormous lamp eyes, curled antennae, and a cape of folded wings, perched like it pays rent on the post. Must-never-change: the lamp eyes are the face; the read is earnest warner, never creepy insect; fluff stays soft, colours stay dusk-muted.

species.name: Omenmoth
species.dexText: Omenmoth appears on bridges in the still hour before great storms, wings folded, saying nothing, being blamed for everything. River towns that have learned to read it move indoors at its arrival and leave a lamp lit for it afterwards, in apology.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Flag (see §5): moths are Pokémon-crowded — none of them is a bipedal omen with a grievance, which is this concept's seed and distinction. The flag rides with it for the owner's eye.
species.lineConcept: C5-2 — tall, silent, red-eyed, and seen on bridges before storms; it does not cause the storm, it is warning about the storm, and it is tired of the misunderstanding; cryptid basis: Mothman.
species.sizeClass: Large — taller than the Rangers it warns, mostly wing and patience.
species.temperament: Grave, silent, and long-suffering; devoted to a duty that earns it suspicion, and too tired of the misunderstanding to perform innocence.
species.habitat: Bridges, towers, and high girders over Region 4's rivers, in the hours before severe weather; it roosts far from towns between storms.
species.dietBehaviour: It eats little and late — night blossoms and rain — and spends its true energy on station-keeping: choosing the bridge, taking the stance, holding the warning until the weather itself arrives to relieve it. It never approaches people; the warning is the whole relationship.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's great river bridges. Rarity class: event — a sighting belongs to a specific storm, not a map routine. Method + conditions: the still, heavy hour before a major storm, from the far bank, at a respectful distance; it is already there when the wind drops. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: there is no approach — the Ranger stops, the Omenmoth turns its head, and both of them look at the sky.
species.cry: Cries only — and barely: its famous register is silence. Source character: a very low, felt-more-than-heard hum with a dry wing-chirr at its edge, produced rarely and only at close range. Pitch contour: flat and low, dropping lower still before it falls silent. Duration class: brief, when it comes at all. Rhythm pattern: none in the wild — a single sustained hum at most; its call is its presence. Variations — idle: silence, with wing-settling sounds only; call: the low hum, once, toward its own kind ahead of a storm front; hurt: a sharp, dry chirr — the loudest sound it makes, and a sign something has gone very wrong; faint: a slow folding silence as the wings come down; affection: a barely audible softening of the hum near the one lamp-keeper it trusts; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — witnesses describe its arrival as the moment the bridge's ordinary sounds quietly stop.
species.anatomyNotes: Tall and bipedal — the family break from Mothlet's cub body. Long legs, long arms held folded into the wing-cape, and great wings that wrap the body like a cloak when closed and span wide only in departure. Mouth is effectively invisible; it does not open for cries in any visible way. Eyes are the whole face: two red lamps in a smooth, dark head, no other features to animate. Locomotion on the ground is a slow, upright stride; flight is a single deep wingbeat and a glide. Signature feature: the stance — motionless, head slightly bowed, wings closed — which animators must hold far longer than feels natural; the warning is a stillness, not a gesture.
species.paletteSeed: bridge grey, storm charcoal, warning red (eyes), rain silver
species.footprint: A tracker after a storm finds tall bipedal prints in the bridge dust: narrow, long-toed prints in a slow, even stride, planted flat with no hurry in them, flanked at the first and last print by great brushed arcs where the wings swept the ground powder aside. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the prints begin and end in open air at the bridge's edge — it arrived on the wing, stood a while, and left the same way.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a cloaked standing figure. Proportions in words: very tall, narrow through the body, the wing-cape widening the outline at the shoulders and closing to a point below. Key visual masses: the folded wings are the body; the head is a small smooth dome carrying the eyes. What reads at sprite size: a tall dark figure with two red eyes — nothing else is needed, and nothing else should compete. Identifying negative space: the long clear gap between its striding legs, and the notch where the wing-cape parts at the front.
species.statProfile: A sentinel's profile — enduring, hard to move, quick to be gone; it endures weather and blame alike and fights, if ever, only to leave. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A tall, grey, wing-cloaked biped with a smooth featureless head and two red lamp eyes, standing on a bridge like a monument that chose its spot. Must-never-change: bipedal omen, not an insect on all fours; the eyes are the only face; it warns and never menaces — no fangs, no claws held out, no horror read; the grievance is in the posture, a tired slump inside the grandeur.

species.name: Spikid
species.dexText: Spikid trails farm herds it was never invited to join, practising guard duty on butterflies and its own shadow. Farmers who find its spiky tracks around the pen in the morning have started leaving out a saucer, just in case it is hereditary.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C5-3 — a spiky pup, "kid" doing double duty and it knows it; cryptid basis: the chupacabra, re-seeded from the first stage as a guardian in training, never a goat-sucker.
species.sizeClass: Small — a goat-kid-sized pup, all bounce and back-spikes.
species.temperament: Bold, bristly, and heroically over-serious about a job nobody has given it yet.
species.habitat: Farm edges, scrub pasture, and goat country around Region 4's rural settlements, wherever a herd needs — or tolerates — an apprentice guardian.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats farm scraps and wild pasture fare, and has developed a famous fondness for the goat's milk farmers leave out — tribute it accepts with grave ceremony. It sleeps within sight of the herd and startles awake at any night sound, spikes first.
species.evolution: Evolves into Capraguard after seasons of accepted service — the turning point is the first night a herd sleeps soundly because it is there.
species.discovery: Region 4 pasture country. Rarity class: uncommon. Method + conditions: dawn rounds of goat pens and scrub fences; its patrol tracks circle the pen before the farmer's own tracks do. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will plant itself between the Ranger and the goats, at a size where the gesture is mostly symbolic, and mean it completely.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a yappy, bristly bark with a goat-kid bleat folded through it — the two sounds arrive together and neither wins. Pitch contour: sharp upward yap, wobbling bleat on the way down. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: single challenge-yaps at strangers; a rolling yap-bleat patter when the herd is moving. Variations — idle: occasional practice yaps at nothing, immediately looked-around-after; call: the rolling yap-bleat, answered by other Spikid across the pasture; hurt: a high, offended squeal-yap; faint: yaps trailing into a bleated sigh; affection: a soft, snuffly bleat with the bark entirely dropped; evolution moment: the yap deepens mid-cry and the bleat steadies under it, guard-voice arriving before guard-size does.
species.anatomyNotes: Quadruped pup body: four sturdy legs, a blunt pup muzzle with a strong little jaw, and ears that swivel toward herd sounds. Manipulators: none — it nudges, herds, and carries with its mouth and chest. Locomotion is a springy trot that breaks into sideways, crabwise guard-hops when excited. Signature feature: the row of back spikes, still soft-tipped at this stage, which rise and bristle with emotion — animators should treat the spike-row as its eyebrow: it does the expressing.
species.paletteSeed: scrub tan, bramble brown, milk cream, thorn green
species.footprint: A tracker finds busy pup prints with a bodyguard's itinerary: small padded prints, each showing short claw marks at the front, in a trotting gait that keeps circling back on itself — patrol loops around pen and pasture rather than a traveller's straight line. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: beside the prints, shallow pricked rows in the dust where the back spikes brushed low ground during a guard-crouch.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a round pup with a sawtooth back. Proportions in words: a compact body, legs short enough to keep the belly low, head large and earnest. Key visual masses: the spike row along the spine is the second-largest read after the head. What reads at sprite size: pup shape, spike row, ears up. Identifying negative space: the sharp triangular notches between the back spikes — a picket-fence skyline no other pup in the region carries.
species.statProfile: Scrappy and brave past its size — quick to engage, quick to tire, built on nerve more than power. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A goat-kid pup with a bristling row of back spikes, big ears, and a chest-out guardian stance several sizes too small for it. Must-never-change: the re-seed starts here — no fangs-for-draining, no sinister night-prowler read at any stage; the spikes are armour and expression, never menace; the kid/pup double nature stays in the silhouette.

species.name: Capraguard
species.dexText: Capraguard walks the night pasture so the herd does not have to think about it. Old farmers insist the terrible stories were the goats' own invention: a guardian rumoured to be a monster is a guardian nothing tests twice.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C5-3 — the goat-sucker of legend re-read as the goat-keeper: the cryptid was a bodyguard all along, and the goats started the rumour as advertising; cryptid basis: the chupacabra, re-seeded as guardian.
species.sizeClass: Large — a pen-gate presence, taller at the shoulder than the goats it guards and broader than the rumours about it.
species.temperament: Fierce on duty and mild off it; a professional. Its loyalty is to the herd as an institution, and it keeps professional hours.
species.habitat: Goat pasture, high scrub, and farm country across Region 4's rural Rift fringe, ranging a nightly circuit of pens and grazing ground.
species.dietBehaviour: Accepts the traditional tribute — goat's milk, left out at the pen gate — and earns it nightly: patrolling, scent-marking the fence line, and placing itself, unhurried, between the herd and anything that arrives after dark. It does not chase glory or strays far; the herd is the territory.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4 goat country. Rarity class: rare — it is on duty when people are asleep, and it prefers the arrangement. Method + conditions: night pasture, approached openly and announced, never snuck up on; the correct protocol is a saucer of milk and a Ranger willing to be inspected first. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: it will inspect the Ranger the way it inspects everything — thoroughly, from the front, at its own pace — and the goats will keep grazing through the whole interview, which is the real reference letter.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a deep, carrying guard-bark with a steady bleat under it, the pup's double sound grown into a patrol horn. Pitch contour: a level, declarative bark that settles into the bleat's calm register. Duration class: medium — an announcement, not a conversation. Rhythm pattern: single barks at intervals on patrol; a rapid, rising sequence only when the herd is genuinely threatened. Variations — idle: low, occasional patrol barks that the herd sleeps through; call: fence-line answering barks with neighbouring Capraguard, territory confirmed in turn; hurt: a short, furious bark-bleat, mostly outrage; faint: barks slowing into a heavy, seated sigh; affection: the soft snuffle-bleat it gives the herd's newborns, bark entirely retired; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — its presence on a new farm is announced by one deep bark at dusk on the first night.
species.anatomyNotes: Powerful quadruped: four column-sturdy legs, a deep chest, and a broad, strong jaw kept — pointedly — unhurried; it guards by placement and display far more than by biting. No manipulators; herding is done with shoulder, chest, and stance. Locomotion is a deliberate patrol walk and a ground-covering surge when it must arrive. Signature features: the full spike ridge along the back, now true armour, which rises as a warning display; and the stand — broadside, head high, between the threat and the herd — which animators should treat as its signature move in every encounter.
species.paletteSeed: deep pasture brown, iron thorn-grey, milk cream, dusk green
species.footprint: A tracker finds a night watchman's round done properly: large padded prints with clear, short claw marks, in an unhurried walking gait that makes a complete circuit — pen gate, fence line, water trough, and back — with wider, deeper prints at the spots where it stood broadside for a long while. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: the circuit itself — a closed loop of prints around a herd, fresh every morning, is a Capraguard signature no wandering predator leaves.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a broad quadruped fortress with a spiked skyline. Proportions in words: long and deep through the body, legs like gateposts, head carried high and level.
