Key visual masses: chest and spike ridge share the read; the head is a watchtower above them. What reads at sprite size: the sawtooth ridge and the tall, level head over a herd of smaller shapes. Identifying negative space: the clean arch under the deep chest, and the regular triangular gaps along the spike ridge.
species.statProfile: A wall with a patrol route — bulky, enduring, and strong in defence of a position; not built for pursuit and never asked to be. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A large, deep-chested herd guardian with a full armour ridge of back spikes, standing broadside between the viewer and an unseen herd. Must-never-change: the guardian re-read is the whole concept — no blood-draining, no horror-cryptid staging, nothing that makes the goats' protector read as their predator; fierceness is protective display, and the resting read is a calm professional at its post.

species.name: Bunyiplet
species.dexText: Bunyiplet haunts the edges of billabongs, surfacing to object — loudly, in cries — to rain, boats, frogs, and the general direction of the weather. Old hands at the river read its moods the way they read the clouds, and trust it about as much.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C5-4 — a billabong tadpole-thing with too many opinions; cryptid basis: the bunyip of Australian billabongs, re-read here as the swamp's young and very vocal — in cries — flood-watcher.
species.sizeClass: Small — a round, wet armful, mostly head and tail.
species.temperament: Opinionated, splashy, and deeply certain; a small swamp creature with the confidence of a weather service.
species.habitat: Billabongs, backwaters, and reed-choked bends of Region 4's rivers; always at the muddy margin between water and land.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats water plants, insects, and whatever the current delivers, and spends the rest of its time holding forth from a half-submerged log. When the river is about to rise, its complaining changes key — locals who know the line learn that key early.
species.evolution: Evolves into Bunyawn after long residence in one billabong, when the swamp's moods and its own have thoroughly become the same thing.
species.discovery: Region 4 billabongs and backwaters. Rarity class: uncommon — heard constantly, seen at its own convenience. Method + conditions: still mornings at the water's edge; sit, wait, and let it surface to object to the Ranger personally. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: the first meeting begins as an argument — it will surface, look the Ranger over, and file its opinion at volume.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a wet, booming-for-its-size bellow-bubble — part frog croak, part blown-across-a-bottle, all complaint. Pitch contour: starts in the throat, rises with indignation, and ends in bubbles. Duration class: medium. Rhythm pattern: emphatic single bellows, answered by itself from a second spot, giving the impression of a committee. Variations — idle: muttering bubble-croaks at the surface; call: the full bellow, carrying across the whole billabong; hurt: a spluttering, offended squawk; faint: bellows sinking into a slow bubble-trail; affection: a soft, private burbling reserved for its own log and favoured Rangers; evolution moment: the bellow drops, deepens, and slows — opinion mellowing, against its will, into omen.
species.anatomyNotes: A tadpole plan grown ambitious: a big round head-body, a long paddling tail, and small stub limbs that gesture more than they grip. Mouth is wide and built for bellowing — the jaw drops impressively for the cry. No true manipulators; it splashes, points with its whole body, and thumps its tail for emphasis. Locomotion is swimming and mud-wriggling; on land it hauls itself short distances and objects throughout. Signature feature: the throat sac that inflates ahead of every opinion.
species.paletteSeed: billabong green, mud brown, reed gold, deep water teal
species.footprint: A tracker finds a muddy margin well argued with: webbed stub-limb prints in a waddling, irregular gait, trailed through by a long central tail-drag, and the whole trackway wandering between water and log in loops — out, around, back — like a creature that kept remembering one more thing to say. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the tail-drag never runs straight; a Bunyiplet trail is a paragraph, not a line.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a round tadpole with pretensions. Proportions in words: head and body one wet circle, tail long and tapering behind, limbs barely interrupting the outline. Key visual masses: the circle first, the inflated throat second when calling. What reads at sprite size: a big round shape half out of the water with a tail behind it. Identifying negative space: the crescent of clear water between its chin and the surface when it surfaces to object.
species.statProfile: A loud small tank of a swimmer — sturdier than it looks, slow on land, and with a voice entirely out of proportion to its body. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A round billabong tadpole-thing on a favourite log, throat sac inflated, mid-objection, tail trailing in dark water. Must-never-change: comedic and swampy, never a horror swamp-monster; the wide bellowing mouth and throat sac are the signature; it lives at the muddy margin, half in and half out of the water, in every pose.

species.name: Bunyawn
species.dexText: Bunyawn sleeps beneath its billabong for seasons at a time, and its waking yawn — vast, unhurried, and carrying for miles — is the region's most trusted flood warning. It accepts no ceremony for this. It was asleep. It would like to go back to sleep.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C5-4 — the swamp's yawning spirit, whose yawn is a flood-warning siren: when Bunyawn yawns, river towns move the furniture upstairs; it has never once been wrong and resents being thanked (it was asleep; it would like to go back to sleep); cryptid basis: the bunyip.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a billabong unto itself; when it surfaces, the waterline of the whole pool rearranges around it.
species.temperament: Majestic, sleepy, and faintly resentful; a public utility with the soul of a creature whose nap keeps being interrupted by hydrology.
species.habitat: The deepest billabongs and slow black-water bends of Region 4; a true Bunyawn pool is a landmark, known by name in the river towns.
species.dietBehaviour: Wakes rarely and eats accordingly — a slow, enormous grazing of the whole pool's abundance when it does — and otherwise sleeps under the mud in a stillness the local wildlife treats as furniture. Its one public act is the yawn: a response to pressure changes in the river that no instrument in the region has ever beaten.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's named billabongs. Rarity class: event — a Bunyawn sighting is a flood-warning sighting, and the correct response is furniture, not field notes. Method + conditions: the heavy, rising-water days of the wet season, at a known Bunyawn pool, observed from high ground. Level band (in words): very high wild band. First-meeting note: the first meeting is a sound before it is a sight — a yawn arriving across the water — and the Ranger's first duty in it is to carry the warning, not complete the interview.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: the yawn itself — a vast, slow, resonant opening of sound, part bellow, part foghorn, part a whole swamp exhaling, that resolves at its peak into a carrying siren tone river towns are built to hear. Pitch contour: begins below hearing, swells slowly upward as the jaw opens, holds the siren peak, and subsides in a long, drowsy fall. Duration class: very long — a town has time to act inside one cry. Rhythm pattern: single, unhurried, and never repeated in a hurry; a second yawn means a second, worse rise. Variations — idle: deep, slow sleep-bubbling from beneath the mud, felt in the bank; call: the full flood-warning yawn, as above; hurt: a startled, cut-short bellow-yawn of mostly surprise; faint: the yawn failing to finish, sinking into a settling rumble as it submerges; affection: a small — for it — private yawn-bubble offered to a long-known river keeper; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — its seasonal waking is the performance, and it begins underwater.
species.anatomyNotes: A vast, low, swamp-body: broad back awash at the surface, heavy limbs mostly for anchoring in mud, and a head that is principally a jaw. No manipulators; its agency is presence, appetite, and the yawn. Locomotion is slow swimming and slower mud-hauling; it almost never fully leaves the water. Signature feature, above all others: the yawn — a jaw that opens beyond any reasonable gape, throat and mouth becoming the whole frame, which animators must stage in unhurried stages: the stir, the rise, the gape, the siren, the drowsy close.
species.paletteSeed: black-water teal, deep mud brown, algae green, warning amber
species.footprint: A tracker finds geography, not tracks: a broad belly-and-body drag through bank mud where it hauled itself at the pool's edge, heavy webbed prints planted deep and far apart in a slow wading gait, and — unmistakably — a wide, smoothed crater in the mud of its sleeping pool where it settled. Print size class: huge. Distinctive marker: the mud at a Bunyawn landing holds the print of the great jaw at rest, a single crescent scoop where the chin came down.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a low island with a jaw. Proportions in words: immense breadth, very little height above the waterline, the back a long mud-coloured horizon. Key visual masses: the body is a landscape; the open jaw, when it comes, out-reads everything. What reads at sprite size: a dark pool-shape and, in the yawn, a vast pale gape. Identifying negative space: the huge arch of the open mouth — the largest single negative space in this whole file.
species.statProfile: An immovable swamp wall — immense endurance and presence, near-zero interest in pursuit, and a warning worth more than its strength. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A huge, low billabong spirit surfacing in dark water, back awash like a mud island, caught at the peak of the great yawn. Must-never-change: sleepy and put-upon, never a lurking swamp horror; the yawn is a kindness it performs half-asleep and must always read as warning, not threat; it stays half-submerged — the waterline is part of the design.

species.name: Pooklet
species.dexText: Pooklet practises being a horse on weekdays with enormous commitment and uneven results. When dignity is required it becomes a rabbit, stands very tall for a rabbit, and waits to be taken seriously, which is the one thing that has never once happened.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C6-1 — a soot-black shapeshifter, horse-shaped on weekdays, rabbit-shaped when it wants to be taken seriously (it is wrong about which is which); folklore basis: the Irish póoka, kept to the creature-type only.
species.sizeClass: Small — pony-small in one shape, lap-small in the other, and never quite certain which it currently is.
species.temperament: Mischievous, theatrical, and entirely sincere in both shapes; a trickster whose tricks are mostly on itself.
species.habitat: Lane ends, stone walls, and dusk meadows around Region 4's Irish-flavoured settlements; anywhere a traveller might accept company for the road.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats meadow fare in either shape and accepts apples as stage payment. It is already practising the family offer — the ride — though at its size the offer is mostly symbolic, and the destinations it manages are only mildly more interesting than intended.
species.evolution: Evolves into Pooknight when its rides have carried enough travellers somewhere better than they planned, and the shapeshifting has settled into craftsmanship.
species.discovery: Region 4 lane country at dusk. Rarity class: uncommon. Method + conditions: twilight lanes and meadow walls; accept the company of any soot-black animal that seems unusually pleased to meet the Ranger. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will introduce itself twice — once in each shape — and watch carefully to see which introduction landed better.
species.cry: Cries only, in both shapes. Source character: a sooty, soft-edged whinny in horse shape that comes out at rabbit scale, and a squeaky, self-important thump-call in rabbit shape pitched far below its size — the cries, like the creature, are in the wrong forms. Pitch contour: whinny-cry rises and breaks playfully; rabbit-cry is a low, deliberate boom-squeak. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: single offered cries, then attentive silence to judge the review. Variations — idle: practice whinnies at meadow volume; call: the full wrong-sized cry, aimed at travellers; hurt: a startled squeak in whichever pitch it was not using; faint: a dwindling whinny-squeak as it deflates into the grass; affection: a warm, rumbling nicker at close range, shape briefly forgotten; evolution moment: the two cries braid together — whinny over boom-squeak — as the shapes stop being costumes and become craft.
species.anatomyNotes: A shapeshifter with two complete body plans at this stage: a small soot-black pony (four legs, mane, tail, a rideable-in-theory back) and a soot-black rabbit (long ears, hind-leg locomotion, sitting-posture dignity). No manipulators in either shape; expression lives in ears in both. The shift between shapes is a sooty swirl-and-settle, quick and a little showy. Locomotion is a trot or a bound according to shape. Signature feature for animators: the wrongness — the pony is slightly too poised, the rabbit slightly too grand; play the confidence, not the comedy, and the comedy takes care of itself.
species.paletteSeed: soot black, peat brown, dusk violet, lantern cream (eyes)
species.footprint: A tracker finds the most confusing short trail in the region: small unshod hoofprints in a neat trotting gait that stop mid-stride and continue, without any gap, as paired rabbit prints in a bounding pattern — back pair landing ahead of the front pair — then switch back again at a wall. Print size class: small in both sets. Distinctive marker: the changeover print itself, one trackway half-hoof, half-paw, where the shift happened mid-step.
species.silhouette: Outline class (pony): a small, neat horse silhouette, mane and tail plumed with soot-soft edges. Outline class (rabbit): a tall-eared sitting silhouette of absurd dignity. Proportions in words: both shapes are compact; the ears and the mane respectively carry the read. What reads at sprite size: soot-black shape, upright ears or plumed mane, cream eyes. Identifying negative space: between the rabbit's long ears, and under the pony's arched neck — the two notches by which a tracker of silhouettes tells which promise it is currently making.
species.statProfile: Quick, evasive, and unpredictable in either shape — a trickster's profile, light on power and heavy on leaving arrangements confused. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A soot-black young shapeshifter shown mid-shift between its pony and rabbit shapes, one end of the swirl in each, cream eyes bright with self-importance. Must-never-change: both shapes stay soot-black and stay its own — no borrowed creature features; the dignity error (rabbit for serious, horse for ordinary days) is the character and must be playable in the design; no malice anywhere in the read.

species.name: Pooknight
species.dexText: Pooknight waits at lane ends after dark and offers, with perfect courtesy, to carry travellers home. It has never once gone home by the road home. Riders dismount at dawn somewhere more interesting, slightly changed, and unable to make the creature sound frightening no matter how they tell it.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C6-1 — it offers rides; the rides end somewhere more interesting than the destination; no one has ever been harmed, and several people have been improved; folklore basis: the Irish póoka, creature-type only.
species.sizeClass: Large — a full riding-horse presence in one shape, and a rabbit the size of a standing stone's shadow in the other, each equally sure it is the impressive one.
species.temperament: Courteous, mysterious, and benevolent in the roundabout way of all true detours; a shapeshifter whose mischief is a form of guidance.
species.habitat: Night lanes, crossroads, and old stone country across Region 4; it ranges wherever someone is travelling too directly toward their own good.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats roadside meadow fare and the traditional apple at journey's end. Its behaviour is a ritual: the offer, the mounting, the long night road that unspools wrong in the right way, and the dawn arrival. It chooses riders, never cargo, and it never explains the route.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's night lanes and crossroads. Rarity class: rare — it finds the Ranger more often than the reverse. Method + conditions: travelling alone after dark with a fixed destination and a troubled mind appears to be the entire summoning rite; it will be waiting at the next lane end. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: the first meeting is an offer, made in cries and posture at the roadside — and the sheet's advice, like the region's, is to consider accepting.
species.cry: Cries only, in both shapes. Source character: in horse shape, a deep, soot-soft whinny with night air in it, courteous as an opened gate; in rabbit shape, an improbably deep, slow boom-call that travellers feel in the road. Pitch contour: the whinny rises in an arc and settles like a decision; the boom-call stays low and level, a promise rather than a question. Duration class: medium. Rhythm pattern: single offered cries with long, listening silences between — it asks once and waits. Variations — idle: a low nicker to the empty lane; call: the full offer-cry at a crossroads; hurt: a sharp, startled whinny-boom in both registers at once; faint: the cry folding into soot and silence as it slips its shape; affection: a warm, private nicker offered to a returned rider it remembers; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — a first full ride, witnesses say, is accompanied by its cries alternating shape by shape down the dark road.
species.anatomyNotes: Two complete, masterful body plans. Horse shape: a tall, soot-black riding horse, four legs in a ground-covering night gait, mane and tail plumed, back offered bare — there is no saddle, there has never been a saddle. Rabbit shape: a huge, long-eared form that moves in ground-eating bounds and sits, in stillness, like a monument to being taken seriously. No manipulators in either shape. The shift is now a smooth soot-swirl, deployed mid-stride for effect. Signature feature for animators: courtesy in motion — every approach is a small bow of the head, in whichever shape currently has one worth bowing.
species.paletteSeed: soot black, midnight violet, moon silver, cream (eyes)
species.footprint: A tracker finds a night's whole story: large unshod hoofprints in a travelling gait that leaves the lane entirely, crosses country no road crosses, and — at the strangest stretches — becomes the paired bounding prints of an enormous rabbit without breaking stride, before returning to hooves at a dawn crossroads far from where the lane was going. Print size class: large in both sets. Distinctive marker: the trackway never passes a single landmark twice, and it always ends somewhere better than the road did.
species.silhouette: Outline class (horse): a tall, elegant night-horse, mane plumed, head bowed in offer. Outline class (rabbit): a towering long-eared silhouette seated at a crossroads like a toll-keeper of the dark. Proportions in words: both shapes are long-limbed and unhurried; soot softens every edge. What reads at sprite size: black shape, cream eyes, and the ears-or-mane signature. Identifying negative space: the tall slot between the rabbit's ears, and the arched gap under the horse's neck as it bows — negative spaces shaped like doorways.
species.statProfile: A night traveller's profile — fast over country, evasive, and enduring; its strength is in the journey, not the contest at the end of it. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A great soot-black horse at a night crossroads, head bowed in courteous offer, with its rabbit shape's long-eared shadow falling across the road beside it. Must-never-change: benevolent detour, never a kidnapper or a horror of the lanes — no one has ever been harmed; no rider gear, no saddle, no bridle; the two shapes stay equally dignified in design even though the creature's own ranking of them is wrong.

species.name: Hatchlet
species.dexText: Hatchlet comes from an egg laid under a star, and hatches already wearing the bud of a comb like a chick wearing a crown two sizes early. Things it looks at for too long go briefly, softly strange — pebbles turn pliant under its stare, and it falls over trying to eat one.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C6-2 — a serpent chick hatched from an egg laid under a star; folklore basis: the basilisk / cockatrice, re-toned from the first stage into the gentle register the line's tone law requires.
species.sizeClass: Tiny — a fistful of down, scales, and consequence.
species.temperament: Regal in intention, helpless in practice; a tiny sovereign whose kingdom is the nest and whose decrees are naps.
species.habitat: Warm, high, dry nesting places around Region 4's rocky Rift edges, where eggs are laid where the stars can see them.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats chick fare and small ground fare, cheeps for service, and practises its gaze on stones, beetles, and its own feet — the softening it manages lasts moments at this age and mostly happens to lunch.
species.evolution: Evolves into Gazewyrm after its gaze has ripened through long starlit seasons — the comb comes in first, then the crown of it, then the consequences.
species.discovery: Region 4 rocky nesting country. Rarity class: rare — an egg laid under a star is an event before it is a species. Method + conditions: clear, star-heavy nights above dry rock; the nest is found by the small ring of oddly softened stones around it. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will attempt the gaze on the Ranger, achieve nothing worse than making a bootlace briefly pliant, and expect to have won.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a bright, imperious cheep with a serpentine hiss braided under it — chick and wyrm in one small throat. Pitch contour: cheeps spike high and certain; the hiss slides underneath, level and patient. Duration class: short. Rhythm pattern: demanding single cheeps, then a burst when service is slow. Variations — idle: sleepy cheep-hisses from the nest; call: the full imperious burst, answered faintly by other Hatchlet on the ridge; hurt: a thin, shocked cheep with the hiss gone; faint: cheeps spacing out into a soft, hissing sigh; affection: a low, contented cheep-purr against a warm hand; evolution moment: the cheep thins away over one long cry and the hiss comes forward alone, crowned by a new, bell-clear note.
species.anatomyNotes: A chick's front on a serpent's plan: downy chest and small clawed legs, a beaked little head under a budding comb, and behind it a long scaled tail that has not agreed to be dignified yet. Short wing-stubs that flap for balance and emphasis. Mouth is a small beak that opens for cheeps and attempted decrees. Locomotion is a waddling walk constantly interrupted by the tail's contrary steering. Signature feature: the eyes — oversized, star-bright, and already capable of the softening gaze; animators should mark gaze-moments with a held, too-long stare and a visible wobble in the target, never with beams or menace.
species.paletteSeed: eggshell cream, dawn gold, soft scale green, star silver
species.footprint: A tracker finds a chick's errand with a serpent's signature: small three-toed clawed prints in a waddling, alternating gait, trailed through and over by a sinuous tail-drag that keeps knocking the prints sideways, the whole trackway circling a nest ringed with oddly softened, thumb-pressed-looking stones. Print size class: tiny. Distinctive marker: the softened stones — in Hatchlet country, the ground itself shows where the gaze has been practising.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a round chick with a long tail and a crown bud. Proportions in words: head and downy body one plump shape, comb a small crest on top, tail extending the outline well behind. Key visual masses: the downy body dominates; the comb is small but placed like a signature. What reads at sprite size: plump chick, comb crest, trailing tail. Identifying negative space: the curl of clear air inside the tail's resting loop beside the body.
species.statProfile: A fragile hatchling with one extraordinary habit — no power to speak of yet, all of it in the eyes. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A downy serpent-chick fresh from a starlit egg, comb bud like an early crown, tail looped beside it, staring with total sovereignty at a pebble it has just softened. Must-never-change: the re-tone starts here — the gaze softens, briefly and harmlessly, and never harms; no horror-chick, no death-stare staging; the comb-as-crown read and the beak-plus-tail plan are the silhouette.

species.name: Gazewyrm
species.dexText: Gazewyrm's stare turns the world briefly to soft stone, and by morning everything has forgiven it and sprung back. Local sculptors compete to hold poses under its gaze, and local duellists learn, once, that a sword gone pliant settles most arguments peacefully.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C6-2 — it wears a comb like a crown, and its gaze turns things to soft stone — soft, and only until morning, which makes it the region's most surprising sculptor and its worst duellist; folklore basis: the basilisk / cockatrice, re-toned.
species.sizeClass: Large — a long, low royal progress of a serpent, longer than the garden paths it refuses to hurry along.
species.temperament: Serene, vain, and fundamentally kind beneath the royalty; a sculptor who works in temporary stone and strong opinions about posture.
species.habitat: Dry, high, star-open country and sculpture gardens around Region 4's Rift settlements, where it is part resident, part institution.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats ground fare and garden fare at royal leisure. Its days are processions between sunny stones; its art is incidental — it looks at things, things soften into poses, and the region has learned to leave interesting objects, volunteers, and occasionally picnics in its line of sight.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's dry high country and sculpture gardens. Rarity class: rare — but a public rare; its processions are in the local almanac. Method + conditions: bright mornings along its known sunny routes; the soft-stone statues, all mid-pose and all temporary, mark the way. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: it will regard the Ranger the way it regards all material — appraisingly — and the correct etiquette is to hold a good pose until morning, at worst.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a clear, bell-toned hiss-song, serene and carrying, with the faintest chick-cheep ghost still audible in it at moments of surprise. Pitch contour: long level phrases that rise, crown-like, at the end of each — a sound that finishes its sentences higher than it began them. Duration class: long and unhurried. Rhythm pattern: slow single phrases with processional pauses; it does not repeat itself for anyone. Variations — idle: a soft, sunny hiss-song from the warm stones; call: the full bell-phrase, answered across the dry hills by its own kind; hurt: a sharp, cracked-bell hiss of pure indignation; faint: the phrases lowering and slowing into a coiled silence; affection: a low, warm hiss-purr with the cheep-ghost surfacing, briefly, for old keepers; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — dawn after a sculpting night is its recurring performance, the soft stone of its works springing back to life around it.
species.anatomyNotes: A full serpent plan, refined: a long scaled body, small clawed forelimbs kept folded in royal disuse, a beaked head crowned by the great comb, and vestigial wing-ridges along the back that stir only for display. Mouth is a fine beak, mostly closed; the face is the eyes. Locomotion is a slow, level undulation that never hurries and never climbs down. Signature feature: the gaze — held, level, and long — and animators must sell its effect entirely through the target: a held pose, a pliant wobble, a soft-stone sheen that lifts at morning. No beams, no rays, no petrifying blast; the folk tale is told gently, in the staging as in the lore.
species.paletteSeed: crown gold, warm scale green, soft stone grey, star silver
species.footprint: A tracker finds a royal road in the dust: a broad, smooth serpent drag with shallow side undulations, flanked at intervals by the faint paired scratches of forelimbs it deigned to use, and punctuated — unmistakably — by softened patches where pebbles and dust along the trail have been pressed pliant under a resting stare. Print size class: large, and mostly trail rather than print. Distinctive marker: sections of the trail go oddly smooth and sculpted-looking, as if the ground itself had been posed.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a long, low serpent with a crowned head. Proportions in words: the body is one extended line; the head rises at the front, comb high; the tail resolves the line to a point. Key visual masses: the comb-crown is the vertical event of the whole silhouette; everything else is procession. What reads at sprite size: crowned serpent, level stare, unhurried coil. Identifying negative space: the arch of clear air under the raised, crowned head — a gateway shape the body passes through as it advances.
species.statProfile: A strange, serene specialist — modest as a fighter, which the source itself records (its worst-duellist reputation is canon to the concept), and unmatched at ending a contest by softening it. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A long, crowned serpent in royal procession across sunny stones, comb held like a coronet, gaze level, with a freshly softened, mid-pose statue of a garden chair softening behind it. Must-never-change: TONE LAW — the gaze turns things to SOFT stone, only until morning; nobody stays stone, nobody is harmed, and the creature is never staged as a deadly basilisk; the comb is a crown, the manner is serene sculpture, and the comedy of the worst duellist in the region stays in the posture.

species.name: Hutlet
species.dexText: Hutlet is a small living den on chicken legs, and it follows its family everywhere with the whole-hearted waddle of a duckling many times its proper size. Families in its country learn to walk at a pace a house can keep, and to leave the little door unlatched, because it worries.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Inspiration note (carried from the source, binding): the source figure of the walking-hut folklore (the witch of the hut) is NOT named, used, or carried — only the hut itself, which was always the interesting part.
species.lineConcept: C6-3 — a den with chicken legs; the small Hutlet follows its family like a duckling; folklore basis: the walking hut of Slavic folklore — the hut only.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a doghouse that got up; knee-high shelter on tall, busy legs.
species.temperament: Devoted, anxious, and homely; a creature whose entire personality is wanting to be where its people are, with a roof over them.
species.habitat: Forest-edge homesteads and village lanes in Region 4's wooded Rift country; it lives, definitionally, wherever its family currently is.
species.dietBehaviour: It grazes moss, mushrooms, and garden scraps with the underside of its floor, and is visibly nourished by occupancy — a lived-in Hutlet has warm windows. Its behaviour is following: it trails the family to fields, markets, and picnics, and settles at night as close to the house as it can politely be a second, smaller house.
species.evolution: Evolves into Wanderhut after years of following, when the family it trails becomes a road it walks — the den outgrows one household and takes up the forest roads for all of them.
species.discovery: Region 4 forest-edge villages. Rarity class: uncommon — but never wild in any useful sense; a Hutlet is always somebody's. Method + conditions: morning in a homestead yard; the small second house that was not there at supper is the encounter. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will follow the Ranger home if the Ranger is kind to it, and this must be treated, by everyone, as the serious commitment it is.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a warm arrangement of timber sounds — soft creaks, a low clucking chirr from under the floor, and a tiny chimney-puff whistle when pleased; the cry of a house clearing its throat. Pitch contour: creaks rise and settle like a rocking chair finding its rhythm; the whistle lifts at the end. Duration class: short to medium. Rhythm pattern: settle-creaks in a row when it stops walking; a single pleased whistle for guests. Variations — idle: slow, sleepy creaking and underfloor cluck-mutters; call: a carrying creak-and-whistle that its family recognises from the fields; hurt: a sharp splintery creak and a startled cluck; faint: the legs fold, the creaks slow, and the windows dim to embers; affection: a deep, warm creak-chirr with the door swinging gently open; evolution moment: the creaks deepen into a house-sized register and the legs answer with the first long, road-going stride.
species.anatomyNotes: The body is the den: a small timber hut — walls, pitched roof, a door, a round window, a stub chimney — carried on tall, scaly chicken legs with three-toed feet. There are no arms and no face; expression is door, window-glow, chimney puffs, and posture of the whole house. The door is a door, opening on a cosy interior; it is not a mouth, and animators must never stage it as one. Locomotion is a waddling, duckling-follow gait, legs working harder than the body's dignity suggests. Signature feature: the settle — when it stops, it lowers itself on folded legs like a hen, roof dipping in a small, relieved bow.
species.paletteSeed: warm timber brown, moss green, thatch gold, window amber
species.footprint: A tracker finds chicken prints at house scale, and must be told straight, as the source tells it: the absurdity is the identification. Three-toed chicken feet — three long toes forward, one short spur mark behind — each print far too large for any bird, pressed deep by a den's weight, in a waddling alternating gait that follows, print for print, the human trackway of its family beside it. Print size class: medium, at small-house scale. Distinctive marker: where it settled for the night, a square of flattened grass ringed by the folded-leg scuffs, exactly where no building stood the day before.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a small house on legs. Proportions in words: a compact square den, a pitched roof above, and legs long enough to put clear daylight under the floor. Key visual masses: roof and walls are the body; the legs are punctuation that moves. What reads at sprite size: hut shape, glowing window, busy legs. Identifying negative space: the bright arch of open air beneath the floor between the legs — the signature gap that says this house walks.
species.statProfile: A shelter's profile — no offence to speak of, a heartening sturdiness, and a defence that consists of being a building. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A small timber den on tall chicken legs, mid-waddle behind an unseen family, window glowing warm, chimney puffing once with pleasure. Must-never-change: only the hut is carried — no occupant figure, witch or otherwise, is named, shown, or implied anywhere in the design; the door is a door and never a mouth; the read is devotion and home, never haunted-house menace.

species.name: Wanderhut
species.dexText: Wanderhut walks the forest roads of the region on great chicken legs, and stops only for polite guests. Travellers who knock properly are fed — inside is bigger than the walls allow, and there is always soup — and travellers who do not are simply carried a mile in the wrong direction by the simple act of the house leaving without them.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: Inspiration note (carried from the source, binding): the source figure of the walking-hut folklore (the witch of the hut) is NOT named, used, or carried — only the hut itself, which was always the interesting part.
species.lineConcept: C6-3 — the grown walking hut walks the forest roads and stops only for polite guests; inside is bigger, and there is always soup; folklore basis: the walking hut of Slavic folklore — the hut only.
species.sizeClass: Huge — a full cottage in motion, roof-tree high, with a stride that clears fences the polite way: over them.
species.temperament: Hospitable, particular, and serenely unbothered; a landlord of the roads with one house rule, which is manners.
species.habitat: The deep forest roads of Region 4's wooded Rift country, on routes known to guides and grandmothers and recorded in no atlas, because they move.
species.dietBehaviour: It grazes whole clearings slowly — moss, windfall, and mushrooms — and gathers something less nameable from occupancy and good conversation, which keep its windows bright. Its behaviour is the rounds: walking the roads, pausing at knock and courtesy, opening the door on warmth and soup, and settling at night wherever the road was kindest.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's deep forest roads. Rarity class: rare — an encounter is arranged by politeness more than by searching. Method + conditions: walking the old forest roads at dusk, knocking — on a gatepost, a stone, the air — and introducing oneself properly appears to be the working method; guides insist the manners are the map. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: the first meeting is an inspection the Ranger does not conduct — the house stops, the window considers them, and the door decides.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a great house settling its timbers — deep structural creaks in slow sequence, a low underfloor cluck-chirr at cottage scale, and a long, contented chimney sigh when the soup is on. Pitch contour: low and architectural, rising slightly as it prepares to move, sighing down as it settles. Duration class: long — a Wanderhut sound takes its time the way the house does. Rhythm pattern: stride-creaks in walking rhythm, door-creak punctuation, then stillness. Variations — idle: the slow tick and creak of a sleeping building, felt through the road; call: a deep creak-and-chime of the door latch that carries through forest, an invitation in the grammar of houses; hurt: a groaning splinter-creak of genuine alarm — the rarest sound it makes; faint: legs folding in sequence, timbers sighing down storey by storey, windows going ember by ember; affection: for a returning polite guest, a warm all-over creak-chirr and the door opening before the knock is finished; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — its arrival on a new road is announced by creaks in a forest that, a moment before, had no house in it.
species.anatomyNotes: A full cottage body: timber walls, a broad pitched roof with moss along the ridge, a proper door with a lit round window beside it, a smoking chimney — carried on immense, scaly chicken legs with three-toed feet that place themselves with unexpected delicacy. No arms, no face; all expression is window-glow, door, chimney, and the posture of the whole architecture. The interior is bigger than the exterior in a way animation should treat as simple hospitality physics: through the door, more room, a table, soup. Locomotion is a stately, long-strided walk with a gentle building-sway; running is never shown and, by all accounts, never happens. Signature feature: the stop — legs halting in sequence, house settling with a deep creak, door opening on lamplight: the region's most complete sentence in creature animation.
species.paletteSeed: deep timber brown, roof moss green, hearth amber, forest dusk blue
species.footprint: A tracker finds chicken prints at house scale, and the file states it plainly because the truth is the joke and the identification both: enormous three-toed chicken prints — three long toes splayed forward, one short spur mark behind — each print deep enough to hold rain, spaced at the stride of a walking cottage, crossing fences at the points where the prints simply continue on the other side. Print size class: huge, at full-house scale. Distinctive marker: where it received a guest, the prints stop in a neat pair, a square of trampled clearing beside them, and the faint ring of a settled house that stood there one night and never again.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a cottage on stilts that happen to be legs. Proportions in words: a broad, high house-body, roof and chimney above, and legs long enough to stride a fence, with a room's worth of daylight beneath the floor. Key visual masses: roof first, glowing windows second, legs as moving architecture. What reads at sprite size: house, legs, lamplight — the region's most unmistakable moving landmark. Identifying negative space: the great arch beneath the floor, tall enough to walk under, which frames whatever forest stands behind it.
species.statProfile: A fortress of hospitality — immense endurance and defence, negligible pursuit, and a strength best measured in weather withstood and travellers sheltered. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A full forest cottage striding gently down a dusk road on great chicken legs, windows warm, chimney smoking, door just opening for a polite guest. Must-never-change: only the hut is carried — no occupant figure, witch or otherwise, is named, shown, or implied; inside is bigger and there is always soup, and those two facts are the design's heart; hospitality, never haunted-house horror; the legs are chicken legs at house scale and stay proudly so.

species.name: Naggin
species.dexText: Naggin is a coach-horse colt with a head it carries like a lantern already — high, steady, and slightly ahead of the rest of it. It practises night roads at a trot the moment the light goes, rehearsing for a keeper it has not met and a route it already seems to know.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Flag (carried from §5, applies to the whole C6-4 line): Pokémon's Spectrier is a ghost horse — the design here is the rider and the lantern, not the horse; that distinction is the line's seed and is carried in full on the Dullaride sheet.
species.lineConcept: C6-4 — a sturdy coach-horse colt; "nag" plus "noggin," and the noggin is the point; folklore basis: the Irish dullahan, re-read from the first stage around the keeper and the lantern, not the horse alone.
species.sizeClass: Small — a compact, sturdy colt, built like a small coach and twice as proud of its head.
species.temperament: Sturdy, earnest, and night-brave; a young professional of the dark roads, serious about the noggin's responsibilities.
species.habitat: Coach roads, stable yards, and the lantern-lit lanes of Region 4's settlements; it prefers the hours when the roads belong to its kind.
species.dietBehaviour: Eats stable fare and roadside grazing with a working horse's appetite. Its behaviour is rehearsal: walking routes at dusk, standing steady at sudden sounds, and carrying its head at exactly the height a lantern would hang — keepers in its country call that carriage the sign of the line.
species.evolution: Evolves into Dullaride when its keeper finds it — the bond, not the body, is the trigger: a colt that has carried its head like a lantern meets the gentle keeper who needs a horse that knows the night roads.
species.discovery: Region 4 coach roads and stable country. Rarity class: uncommon. Method + conditions: dusk at stable yards and lane ends; the colt standing head-high in the last light, practising stillness, is the sighting. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: it will present the noggin first — head high, ears forward — and wait to be admired at the correct altitude.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a bright, sturdy whinny with a coach-bell's clarity in it, and a snort that lands like a punctuation mark. Pitch contour: the whinny rises in a clean arc and cuts off neatly, stable-trained. Duration class: short to medium. Rhythm pattern: single whinnies at route landmarks — it announces corners to itself; double snorts when pleased with its own stillness. Variations — idle: soft nickering and hoof-shift sounds in the dusk yard; call: the full bell-clear whinny down the lane, answered by other Naggin at their posts; hurt: a sharp, startled whinny-snort; faint: whinnies lowering into a heavy, kneeling sigh; affection: a warm, rumbling nicker with the head bowed to keeper height; evolution moment: the whinny carries, steadies, and is answered — for the first time — by the soft chime of a lantern taking up its light.
species.anatomyNotes: A sturdy quadruped colt: four strong legs, a compact coach body, and a head-and-neck unit that is the design's whole argument — carried high, level, and steady, with large, calm eyes and ears that swivel to road sounds. Mouth is a soft horse muzzle; the jaw works cud and commentary-snorts. No manipulators. Locomotion is an even, road-eating trot with a notably level top line: the noggin does not bob. Signature feature for animators: that steadiness — animate the body around a head that stays lantern-still at lantern height.
species.paletteSeed: coach black, stable brown, brass amber, dusk cream
species.footprint: A tracker finds the print of the horse body, as this line's record always keeps it: small, neat, round unshod hoofprints in an even trotting gait — four prints in a steady, level rhythm with no drag and no scatter, the trackway of a colt that practises. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: at corners and lane ends the prints gather into a small, patient standing cluster, where it stood head-high, rehearsing the wait.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a compact colt with a flagpole neck. Proportions in words: body sturdy and short-coupled, legs strong, neck and head carried high above the body's line. Key visual masses: the noggin, held high, out-reads everything but the body itself. What reads at sprite size: sturdy colt, head up like a lamp being carried into dusk. Identifying negative space: the tall, clear triangle under the raised neck and jaw — the space a lantern will one day occupy in the line's read.
species.statProfile: A steady all-rounder in the making — sturdy, enduring, and unflashy, built for roads and hours rather than moments. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A sturdy soot-dark colt at dusk, head carried high and lantern-steady, ears to the road, in a stable yard gone violet with evening. Must-never-change: the noggin carriage is the concept — head high, level, and steady at every moment; no headless imagery at this stage, no spookiness; it is a young professional, earnest and calm, and the night in its design is a workplace, not a haunting.

species.name: Dullaride
species.dexText: Dullaride walks the Rift's roads after dark with its gentle keeper, whose lantern-head — carried under one arm, smiling its soft light at corners — is lit for everyone travelling late. Nothing on those roads fears it twice: the first night is a story, and every night after is a service.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
notes: ⚠ Flag (see §5): Pokémon's Spectrier is a ghost horse — the design here is the rider and the lantern, not the horse. The horse body is the vehicle of the concept only in the creature-bond sense; the sheet, brief, and silhouette all centre the keeper and the carried lantern-head.
species.lineConcept: C6-4 — ridden by a gentle headless keeper who carries their own lantern-head under one arm and lights the Rift's roads at night; folklore basis: the Irish dullahan, creature-type only, re-read around the rider and the lantern.
species.sizeClass: Large — a full coach-horse in body, with a keeper above it and a lantern's glow completing a silhouette taller than any cart on the night roads.
species.temperament: Gentle, punctual, and devoted to the route; a keeper and horse in complete agreement that the night roads should be lit, guided, and kind.
species.habitat: The night roads of Region 4 — Rift crossings, forest lanes, and the long unlit stretches between settlements — walked nightly, in all weathers, on a roundsman's schedule.
species.dietBehaviour: The horse grazes the verges at rest stops with a working animal's good sense; the pair's behaviour is the rounds themselves: walking the route, pausing where travellers lose the way, lending light at fords and crossroads, and moving on when the road is safe again. The keeper speaks to no one in words — guidance is given in light, pace, and presence, and it has always been enough.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's unlit roads at night. Rarity class: rare — but a scheduled rare; regular night travellers plan around its rounds with gratitude. Method + conditions: deep night on the Rift roads, at a ford or crossroads where the way is uncertain; wait, and watch for a lantern's glow carried at arm's height, approaching at a walking horse's pace. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: the glow arrives before the shapes do — light first, then the kind, unhurried silhouette — and the correct response, per everyone who uses those roads, is thanks.
species.cry: Cries only — the keeper gives no words, ever, and the pair's voice is the horse's, accompanied. Source character: a deep, steady whinny with a coach-bell's calm in it, layered with the soft chime and hum of the carried lantern as it swings. Pitch contour: the whinny rises gently and settles like a light being set down; the lantern-chime keeps a level undertone. Duration class: medium. Rhythm pattern: single whinnies at landmarks, lantern-chime marking the stride between; the two sounds answer each other down the road. Variations — idle: soft nickering, hoof sounds, and the lantern's low hum at a rest stop; call: the full whinny-and-chime down a dark stretch, a service announcement to travellers ahead; hurt: a sharp horse cry and the lantern's alarmed flare, instantly steadied by the keeper's hand; faint: the whinny failing as the horse sinks, the lantern light lowering with it, keeper kneeling in the same motion; affection: a warm, low nicker from the horse and a soft, brightening glow — the pair's whole vocabulary of fondness in two registers; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — its taking up a new road is marked, witnesses say, by one whinny and one new light where the map shows none.
species.anatomyNotes: Two bonded figures staged as one species-entry, and animators must keep the division of labour exact. The horse body: a strong, dark coach-horse, four legs in an unhurried road gait, head carried high and steady in the family carriage. The keeper: a headless rider seated calmly, one arm crooked around their own lantern-head — a softly glowing, gentle-faced lantern carried at the side like a travelling light — and the other hand resting easy on the reins it barely needs. The lantern-head is a lantern: warm light, soft features in its glow, carried, never worn, never floating free. Locomotion is entirely the horse's; guidance is entirely light and pace. Signature features: the glow at arm's height moving at a horse's walking rhythm, and the synchrony — horse and keeper settle, turn, and pause as one creature, which is what, for animation purposes, they are.
species.paletteSeed: coach black, lantern amber, night-road blue, brass cream
species.footprint: A tracker finds the print of the horse body, and only the horse body, as this line's record keeps it: large, round, unshod hoofprints in a level walking gait, four prints to the stride, unhurried and evenly deep, in a trackway that follows the road's hardest stretches — fords, crossroads, unlit bends — and pauses, in small patient standing clusters, exactly where a traveller would need light. Print size class: large. Distinctive marker: at the standing clusters, a faint round scorch-pale ring in the dust where the lantern was set down a moment — the only trace the keeper ever leaves, and it is a trace of the light, not of a foot.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a horse, a rider, and a carried light. Proportions in words: the horse is long and level; the keeper sits tall and headless above the saddle line, shoulders calm; the lantern-head hangs glowing in the crook of one arm at the silhouette's side. Key visual masses: horse body first, rider second, lantern-glow the brightest and smallest mass — and the one the eye finishes on. What reads at sprite size: dark horse, rider with no head, one warm light carried low — readable instantly, and kindlier the longer it is looked at. Identifying negative space: the clean, deliberate gap where the keeper's head is not — a space the lantern's glow, carried below, answers; and the arch under the horse's steady neck.
species.statProfile: An enduring road-guardian's profile — steady defence, long stamina, and strength spent on presence and guidance rather than contest. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A dark coach-horse walking a night road, a gentle headless keeper in the saddle carrying a softly glowing lantern-head under one arm, light spilling on the ford ahead. Must-never-change: the design is the RIDER AND THE LANTERN, not the horse (see Flags); the keeper is gentle — no menace, no doom-herald staging, no gore anywhere in the headlessness, which is played as calm fact and warm light; the lantern-head is carried under the arm, never worn, never floating; cries and light are the pair's only language.

species.name: Talitot
species.dexText: Talitot sleeps so deeply and so stiffly that walking has been given up as impractical, and it gets about by hopping, seal fluttering, in a slow commute between naps. The paper seal on its forehead is a bedtime note in the region's careful hand: do not wake, hopping.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C6-5 — a stiff little sleeper with a paper seal on its forehead (the seal is a bedtime note: do not wake, hopping); it hops because it is too stiff with sleep to walk; folklore basis: the Chinese jiangshi, re-toned as a sleepy dream-deliverer, not a horror vampire.
species.sizeClass: Small — a knee-high, cushion-stiff little figure that travels upright and entirely asleep.
species.temperament: Sleepy, mild, and entirely unbothered; the calmest creature in any room it slowly crosses.
species.habitat: Quiet lanes, temple steps, and the dusk edges of Region 4's villages — the soft, safe routes between wherever it fell asleep and wherever it is apparently expected.
species.dietBehaviour: It gathers stray dreams and sleep-mist the way other creatures gather berries, nibbling dusk light and the warmth of sleeping houses, and delivers nothing yet — at this stage the dreams it collects are mostly its own, carried carefully in both stiff arms. It does not drink, bite, or haunt; it naps, hops, and is late in the gentlest way.
species.evolution: Evolves into Hopshroud after long service in the small hours — when the dreams it carries are no longer only its own, and the night roads have learned its hop by sound.
species.discovery: Region 4 village lanes at dusk. Rarity class: uncommon. Method + conditions: the quiet hour after lamps are lit; listen for a slow, even hop where no one should be awake, and step aside for it — it will not step aside for the Ranger, being asleep. Level band (in words): low wild band. First-meeting note: the first meeting is a near-miss conducted at hopping pace — it arrives with its eyes closed, acknowledges the Ranger with one sleepy sway, and hops on.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a soft, drowsy murmur-hum broken by the paper flutter of its seal and a small, round snore-note at the bottom of each breath — a lullaby sung by its own sleeping. Pitch contour: low, level, and sinking; every phrase ends lower and nearer sleep than it began. Duration class: medium, but unhurried to the point of comedy. Rhythm pattern: one murmur per hop, in hop rhythm — the cry and the locomotion share a metronome. Variations — idle: continuous soft snore-murmurs, seal fluttering at each breath; call: a slightly more awake murmur repeated toward another Talitot on the lane, answered in the same tempo; hurt: a startled, squeaky yawn-cry, more woken than injured, followed by immediate attempts to re-sleep; faint: the murmurs spacing out into one long, settled snore as it tips gently over, still stiff; affection: a warm, close murmur-hum with the seal pressed trustingly against a keeper's hand; evolution moment: the murmur deepens into a road-carrying hum without ever waking — the tempo stays, the purpose arrives.
species.anatomyNotes: A small, upright, stiff-bodied sleeper: body held straight as a board, arms held out or folded stiffly with sleep, legs that do not bend separately in any useful way. The paper seal on the forehead is a permanent feature — a small hanging note that flutters with every hop and breath, and animators should treat it as the creature's eyelid: its movement is how its sleep reads. Mouth is a small, soft line that opens for yawns and murmurs. No gripping manipulators; carried things are balanced on the stiff arms. Locomotion is the hop and only the hop — both feet together, body upright, landing with a small whole-body bob — because it is too stiff with sleep to walk, and this must never be animated as menace, pursuit, or a lunge.
species.paletteSeed: dusk indigo, seal-paper cream, sleepy rose, lamp amber
species.footprint: A tracker finds the hop, exactly as the expansion of this line promises: paired prints, both feet together, side by side in a single neat impression, then a clean gap of untouched ground, then the pair again — an even, drowsy rhythm of landings down the lane, with a faint paper-drag tick at the edge of some prints where the seal swung low. Print size class: small. Distinctive marker: the pairs never alternate and never hurry; a Talitot trackway can be identified by its tempo alone, and it sometimes stops entirely at a doorstep, pairs stacking, where it fell properly asleep mid-route.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a small upright figure with a flag on its forehead. Proportions in words: body straight and board-stiff, head high, arms held stiffly forward or folded, seal a small rectangle hanging over the face. Key visual masses: the stiff vertical body is the whole read; the seal is its punctuation. What reads at sprite size: upright little sleeper, fluttering seal, mid-hop. Identifying negative space: the clean slot of air beneath both feet at the top of every hop — the hop's held breath, and the shape by which the silhouette is known at distance.
species.statProfile: A soft, slow, surprisingly sturdy sleeper — no speed, no malice, and a constitution that treats most trouble as weather to nap through. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A small, board-stiff sleeper mid-hop down a dusk lane, eyes closed, paper bedtime seal fluttering on its forehead, arms held out with the solemnity of a creature carrying its own nap. Must-never-change: TONE — this is a sleepy dream-deliverer in training, never a horror vampire: no fangs, no blood, no hopping pursuit played for fear; the seal is a bedtime note and stays legible as care, not a ward against evil; the stiffness is sleep, always sleep.

species.name: Hopshroud
species.dexText: Hopshroud keeps the region's night post of dreams, hopping the dark roads with its stiff arms full of other people's sleeping, and delivering each dream — by scent, by house, by long practice — to the right pillow. The record of errors stands at two, both famous, both forgiven by breakfast.
species.provenance: mochichao-design lane wave 1 — FUTURE CONSIDERED, not canon
species.lineConcept: C6-5 — it hops the night roads delivering the region's dreams to the right houses, and has only mixed them up twice; folklore basis: the Chinese jiangshi, re-toned as a sleepy dream-deliverer, not a horror vampire.
species.sizeClass: Medium — a tall, straight, muffled figure, person-height in the way a postman is person-height: as a fact of the route, not a presence in the room.
species.temperament: Dutiful, drowsy, and quietly proud of the route; a public servant of the small hours whose entire menace is the possibility of being woken fully, which no one has ever risked.
species.habitat: The night roads and sleeping lanes of Region 4, between the dream-gathering dusk fields and the villages on its rounds; it is a creature of routes, thresholds, and doorsteps.
species.dietBehaviour: It sustains itself on sleep-mist, dusk light, and the warmth of well-kept houses, and its work is collection and delivery: gathering the day's stray dreams at dusk, sorting them — in its sleep, without error worth mentioning — and hopping the rounds until every house has its own night back. It never enters uninvited; dreams are left at thresholds, and drift the rest of the way on their own.
species.evolution: Final stage of its line; no further evolution is recorded.
species.discovery: Region 4's village roads at deep night. Rarity class: rare — it works while the region sleeps, and being seen at work is a small breach of the service it quietly forgives. Method + conditions: the small hours on a known delivery lane; stand at a threshold, be still, and let the even hop pass — a Ranger who follows it will simply be delivered, eventually, to their own door. Level band (in words): high wild band. First-meeting note: it will pause, regard the Ranger with closed eyes, re-sort something invisible in its stiff arms, and hop on — as if the Ranger, too, were a parcel it had correctly routed.
species.cry: Cries only. Source character: a low, carrying murmur-hum in hop tempo, deeper and more purposeful than Talitot's, with the soft paper rustle of its larger seal riding over it and a faint, many-layered whispering underneath that is the sound of carried dreams settling — never voices, never words, only the hush of other people's sleep in transit. Pitch contour: low and level on the road, with a gentle lift at each doorstep as a delivery is made, sinking back to route tempo between houses. Duration class: long — it murmurs for the length of a round. Rhythm pattern: one phrase per hop, doorstep phrases marked by a small, satisfied settling-note. Variations — idle: at rest between rounds, a deep, slow snore-murmur with the seal rising and falling; call: the route-hum pitched to carry down a lane to another Hopshroud, rounds acknowledged in turn; hurt: a startled, wide-awake squeak-yawn — the closest it comes to alarm — followed by visible, heroic efforts to return to working sleep; faint: the hum unspooling into one long exhale as it settles, stiff and upright, against a gatepost, deliveries paused but unspilled; affection: a warm, private murmur offered at the threshold of a house it has served for years; evolution moment: not applicable as a final stage — the start of each night's round is its recurring ceremony, the murmur taking up the tempo as the first hop leaves the dusk field.
species.anatomyNotes: A tall, board-stiff upright body in a soft shroud-like wrap, arms held forward and full — the carried dreams are staged as soft, dim, shifting bundles of mist-light cradled in the stiff arms, handled with postman's care. Legs move only together; locomotion is the hop alone, both feet leaving and landing as one, body upright, seal fluttering — stately, drowsy, and entirely without spring or menace. The seal on the forehead is larger now, a proper route-note in the same bedtime hand, and remains the face's main moving part: eyes beneath it stay closed in nearly every key pose. Mouth opens for yawns of continental patience. Signature features for animators: the doorstep pause — hop, stop, the small lift of the arms as a dream is released to drift the last of the way itself, the satisfied settling-note, hop on.
species.paletteSeed: deep night indigo, shroud cream, seal red (accent), dream silver
species.footprint: A tracker in the morning finds the round completed: paired prints, both feet together, in a single impression per hop, evenly spaced down the night lanes in unbroken drowsy tempo, with the pairs gathering into small standing clusters at doorstep after doorstep — the delivery pauses — and never once breaking into a run, a chase, or a stray from the route. Print size class: medium. Distinctive marker: at certain thresholds the pair of prints faces the door a long while, and a faint drift of dream-mist silvering on the step is the only receipt the service leaves.
species.silhouette: Outline class: a tall, straight figure with a banner on its forehead, arms full. Proportions in words: body one unbent vertical, head high under the hanging seal, arms a stiff shelf across the front carrying soft, dim shapes. Key visual masses: the vertical body and the bundle-shelf of the arms share the read; the seal is the crest. What reads at sprite size: upright hopper, fluttering seal, arms full of faint light. Identifying negative space: the clean slot beneath both feet at the hop's peak, taller now — a held breath the length of a doorstep — and the notch between the seal's lower edge and the closed eyes.
species.statProfile: A night-service profile — enduring, unhurried, and far sturdier asleep than most creatures awake; it does not fight for routes, it simply cannot be kept from completing them. ⚑ numbers unassigned (owner/game-design).
species.designBrief: A tall, stiff, shrouded figure mid-hop on a night road, eyes closed, great bedtime seal fluttering, stiff arms full of soft dream-light, passing a sleeping village's doorsteps like the last post of the day. Must-never-change: TONE LAW — a sleepy dream-deliverer, never a horror vampire: no fangs, no blood, no predation, and the hop is drowsy duty, never pursuit; the seal is a bedtime / route note, an instrument of care; its errors are two, famous, and forgiven — the design's expression stays mild enough to deserve that forgiveness.
